Use to swap a template_id, change a subject/body, adjust delay, or A/B variant. Subject/body/body_html support merge-tag fallbacks ({{first_name|there}}) and spintax ({Hi|Hey|Hello}) for inbox-fingerprint variation.

tools.name: customer_avatar_create
tools.description: Create a customer avatar (ICP). Accepts the full ICP spec EITHER flat at top level OR inside `avatar_data`. Flat fields: name (required), description, summary, age_range, gender, location, occupation, income_range, education_level, lifestyle, aspirations, typical_quote, background_story, avatar_image_url, background_story_image_url; arrays: values, interests, personality_traits, primary_goals, motivations, pain_points, challenges, frustrations, content_preferences, preferred_channels, tags. **Canonical buying_behavior shape** (rendered in the dashboard avatar editor's Behaviors tab): { trigger: string, // what event finally pushes them to buy decision_cycle: string, // how long the decision takes, with patterns stakeholders: string[], // who's involved (CFO sign-off, spouse, head of ops) preferred_intake: string, // demo / deck / sandbox / case study, etc. budget_range: string, // what they're willing to spend objections: string[] // common pushbacks ('takes too long', 'too expensive') } **Canonical online_behavior shape** (also rendered in the same tab): { social_platforms: string[], // LinkedIn, TikTok, Reddit, etc. device_preference: string, // mobile-first / desktop / mixed content_habits: string, // short vs long-form, video vs text, time-of-day information_sources: string[], // trusted newsletters / podcasts / forums daily_hours_online: string // free-form time estimate } Unknown keys on either object round-trip but don't render. populate_status is server-managed and hidden from responses.

tools.name: customer_avatar_delete
tools.description: Delete a customer avatar. Accepts `id` or `avatar_id`.

tools.name: customer_avatar_get
tools.description: Fetch one customer avatar. Accepts `id` or `avatar_id`.

tools.name: customer_avatar_list
tools.description: List customer avatars (ICPs).

tools.name: customer_avatar_populate
tools.description: LLM-enrich a sparse customer_avatar with GROUNDED context (Firecrawl scrapes + agent notes + brand guide). Refuses with `code: 'context_insufficient'` (400) if the account has no brand_style_guide AND no urls_to_scrape / search_queries / agent_notes are supplied. See entity_populate for the full contract — this is the same tool with entity_type='avatar' hardcoded. Enriches 20+ ICP columns: summary, age_range, gender, location, occupation, income_range, lifestyle, values[], interests[], primary_goals[], motivations[], pain_points[], frustrations[], aspirations, typical_quote, background_story, online_behavior{}, buying_behavior{}, content_preferences[], preferred_channels[]. Flips populate_status to 'populated' on success.

tools.name: customer_avatar_update
tools.description: Update a customer avatar. Accepts `id` or `avatar_id`. Fields can be passed flat or inside `avatar_data`. 5xx responses now name the offending field (e.g. P2000 'value too long for column "X"').

tools.name: customer_avatar_version_create
tools.description: Snapshot a customer avatar's CURRENT PERSISTED row into version history before an ICP rewrite. Returns 201 {data: version} with the allocated version_number (previous max + 1) and the captured avatar_data. The snapshot is read from the database, never from this call's body: change_message is the ONLY field the handler reads, so name, pain_points, buying_behavior or any other key sent here is accepted at 201 and silently dropped, and unsaved edits are NOT captured. Persist with customer_avatar_update first, then snapshot. Usually you do not need this tool at all: customer_avatar_update already writes an 'Auto-snapshot before update' version of the pre-edit row whenever a substantive field changes, so calling this first just adds a duplicate history entry; use it for a deliberately labelled checkpoint. The stored version `name` is copied off the avatar row. Concurrent snapshots contend on the [avatar_id, version_number] unique; the handler retries 5 times and then returns 503 'Failed to allocate version_number after retries', which is retryable rather than a bad request.

tools.name: customer_avatar_version_get
tools.description: Fetch one avatar snapshot in full, including the avatar_data blob that makes paging the list view expensive. Returns {data: {id, avatar_id, version_number, name, avatar_data, change_message, created_by, created_at}}. version_id is the snapshot ROW UUID from customer_avatar_version_list, NOT the integer version_number: passing 3 does not 404, it fails the uuid cast on the id column and comes back as a 500 'Failed to get avatar version'. A real UUID belonging to a different avatar does 404 'Version not found', because the lookup is scoped by avatar_id. avatar_data is the whole avatar row as it stood, including the id, account_id, created_at and updated_at of that moment plus operational columns like populate_status and lock_version; a restore strips exactly those first four and writes every other key back, so read this first to see exactly what customer_avatar_version_restore would overwrite.

tools.name: customer_avatar_version_list
tools.description: List saved snapshots of one customer avatar (ICP), newest version_number first. Returns {data: [{id, avatar_id, version_number, name, avatar_data, change_message, created_by, created_at}], pagination: {page, limit, total, total_pages}}. Every row carries the FULL avatar_data blob (no column selection), so a page of 20 is a heavy payload: take ids here and pull detail with customer_avatar_version_get. Traps: limit defaults to 20 and is silently clamped to 50, so asking for 200 returns 50 with no error, and page is floored to 1. The row's `id` (a UUID) is what version_get and version_restore take, NOT version_number. created_by is nullable and no route on this surface ever writes it, so it is always null. Most rows here are automatic; customer_avatar_update snapshots the pre-edit row by itself on any substantive change unless it was called with snapshot false. An avatar_id from another account returns 404 'Customer avatar not found', not 403; a non-UUID avatar_id fails the uuid cast and comes back 500.

tools.name: customer_avatar_version_restore
tools.description: OVERWRITES the live customer avatar with a snapshot. Every key stored in that version's avatar_data except id, account_id, created_at and updated_at is written straight back onto the row, so pain_points, buying_behavior, online_behavior, tags and any edit made since that snapshot are replaced, and operational columns captured in the blob (is_active, metadata, populate_status, populate_error, populated_at, lock_version) are rewound with them. There is NO confirm parameter and no body is parsed: the first call performs the restore. It is normally recoverable because the handler auto-snapshots the current state first and returns {data: restored avatar, restored_from_version, auto_snapshot_version}, and restoring auto_snapshot_version undoes it. TRAP ONE: if that auto-snapshot loses the version_number race 5 times it is abandoned and the restore proceeds ANYWAY while auto_snapshot_version still reports the number it was trying to use, so confirm the row with customer_avatar_version_list before treating it as your undo. TRAP TWO, wider than this avatar: the restore then nulls icp_matched_at on EVERY visitor row in the account, not only visitors matched to this ICP, forcing an account-wide re-match while each visitor's matched_icp_id is left pointing at its old ICP; that write is wrapped in a catch that only logs, so if it fails the route still returns 200 and stale ICP match timestamps silently survive the persona change. version_id is the snapshot ROW UUID; a version_number passed here fails the uuid cast and returns 500, not 404.

tools.name: customer_journey_avatar_link
tools.description: Attach a customer avatar (ICP) to a journey map and return the full refreshed link list. Writes customer_journey_avatars, the many-to-many table, NOT the legacy customer_journey_maps.target_avatar_id that customer_journey_link_to_avatar sets. Three behaviours worth knowing before you call it: the FIRST avatar linked to a journey is made primary whatever you pass, because a journey must have one; passing is_primary true DEMOTES the current primary in the same transaction; and the write is an upsert on (journey_id, avatar_id), so re-linking an avatar already attached is not an error and changes only is_primary. The avatar must belong to the same account or the call is a 400 'Avatar not found in this account'. Every row written through an API key is stamped added_by_agent true, which is how the dashboard distinguishes agent links from human ones.

tools.name: customer_journey_avatar_list
tools.description: List every customer avatar (ICP) linked to one journey map, as {data: [{id, avatar_id, is_primary, sort_order, added_by_agent, avatar: {name, avatar_image_url, occupation, summary}}]}. READ THIS BEFORE customer_journey_link_to_avatar: there are TWO avatar relationships on a journey and they are not the same thing. customer_journey_maps.target_avatar_id is the legacy single-persona column and is what customer_journey_link_to_avatar and customer_journey_update write; customer_journey_avatars is the many-to-many table with a primary and an explicit order, and this trio is the only way to reach it. This GET is not purely a read: it first backfills the legacy target_avatar_id into the link table, so on a journey that has only ever used the old column the first call materialises that link and returns it. `avatar` is null when the linked avatar row has since been deleted.

tools.name: customer_journey_avatar_unlink
tools.description: Detach one customer avatar from a journey map and return the refreshed link list. Removes the customer_journey_avatars row only; it does NOT clear the legacy customer_journey_maps.target_avatar_id, so a journey can still report a target persona through customer_journey_get after this call, and the next customer_journey_avatar_list will BACKFILL that legacy value straight back into the link table. To detach a persona completely, unlink here and also set target_avatar_id to null with customer_journey_link_to_avatar. An avatar that is not linked is a 404, not a silent success.

tools.name: customer_journey_create
tools.description: Create a customer journey map. Accepts fields flat OR inside `journey_data`. Fields: name (required), description, summary, stages (array of stage objects), metadata, tags, is_active. **Canonical stage shape** (the dashboard UI renders these keys; common synonyms are normalized server-side, but the canonical names are preferred): { name: string, // stage heading. Synonyms: stage, title description: string, emotions: string[], // chip pills. Synonym (singular): emotion pain_points: string[], // chip pills touchpoints: string[], // chip pills. Synonym: channels content_types: string[], opportunities: string[], // chip pills. Synonym: actions images?: [{id, url, prompt}] } Unknown keys are preserved but not rendered.

tools.name: customer_journey_delete
tools.description: Delete a customer journey map. Accepts `id` or `journey_id`.

tools.name: customer_journey_get
tools.description: Fetch one customer journey map. Accepts `id` or `journey_id`.

tools.name: customer_journey_link_to_avatar
tools.description: Link a customer journey map to a customer_avatar by setting target_avatar_id. Convenience wrapper around customer_journey_update — uses the canonical 'this journey is for THIS persona' relationship column. Pass null (or empty string) to unlink. The avatar must belong to the same account; cross-account UUIDs return 400. Mirror of before_after_grid_link_to_avatar.

tools.name: customer_journey_list
tools.description: List customer journey maps.

tools.name: customer_journey_populate
tools.description: LLM-enrich a sparse customer_journey_map with GROUNDED context. Same contract as entity_populate with entity_type='journey' hardcoded. Enriches: summary + stages[] with each stage having {name, description, emotions[], pain_points[], touchpoints[], content_types[], opportunities[]}. Flips populate_status to 'populated' on success.

tools.name: customer_journey_update
tools.description: Update a customer journey map. Accepts `id` or `journey_id`. Fields flat or inside `journey_data`.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_available_filters
tools.description: Here you will find all the necessary information about filters that can be used with DataForSEO Labs API endpoints. Please, keep in mind that filters are associated with a certain object in the result array, and should be specified accordingly.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_bulk_keyword_difficulty
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with the Keyword Difficulty metric for a maximum of 1,000 keywords in one API request. Keyword Difficulty stands for the relative difficulty of ranking in the first top-10 organic results for the related keyword. Keyword Difficulty in DataForSEO API responses indicates the chance of getting in top-10 organic results for a keyword on a logarithmic scale from 0 to 100.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_bulk_traffic_estimation
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with estimated monthly traffic volumes for up to 1,000 domains, subdomains, or webpages. Along with organic search traffic estimations, you will also get separate values for paid search, featured snippet, and local pack results.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_competitors_domain
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with a full overview of ranking and traffic data of the competitor domains from organic and paid search. In addition to that, you will get the metrics specific to the keywords both competitor domains and your domain rank for within the same SERP.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_domain_intersection
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with the keywords for which both specified domains rank within the same SERP. You will get search volume, competition, cost-per-click and impressions data on each intersecting keyword. Along with that, you will get data on the first and second domain's SERP element discovered for this keyword, as well as the estimated traffic volume and cost of ad traffic.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_domain_rank_overview
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with ranking and traffic data from organic and paid search for the specified domain. You will be able to review the domain ranking distribution in SERPs as well as estimated monthly traffic volume for both organic and paid results.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_historical_keyword_data
tools.description: This endpoint provides Google historical keyword data for specified keywords, including search volume, cost-per-click, competition values for paid search, monthly searches, and search volume trends. You can get historical keyword data since August, 2021, depending on keywords along with location and language combination

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_historical_rank_overview
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with historical data on rankings and traffic of the specified domain, such as domain ranking distribution in SERPs and estimated monthly traffic volume for both organic and paid results

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_historical_serp
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with Google SERPs collected within the specified time frame. You will also receive a complete overview of featured snippets and other extra elements that were present within the specified dates. The data will allow you to analyze the dynamics of keyword rankings over time for the specified keyword and location.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_keyword_ideas
tools.description: The Keyword Ideas provides search terms that are relevant to the product or service categories of the specified keywords. The algorithm selects the keywords which fall into the same categories as the seed keywords specified in a POST array. As a result, you will get a list of relevant keyword ideas for up to 200 seed keywords. Along with each keyword idea, you will get its search volume rate for the last month, search volume trend for the previous 12 months, as well as current cost-per-click and competition values. Moreover, this endpoint supplies minimum, maximum and average values of daily impressions, clicks and CPC for each result.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_keyword_overview
tools.description: This endpoint provides Google keyword data for specified keywords. For each keyword, you will receive current cost-per-click, competition values for paid search, search volume, search intent, monthly searches

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_keyword_suggestions
tools.description: The Keyword Suggestions provides search queries that include the specified seed keyword. The algorithm is based on the full-text search for the specified keyword and therefore returns only those search terms that contain the keyword you set in the POST array with additional words before, after, or within the specified key phrase. Returned keyword suggestions can contain the words from the specified key phrase in a sequence different from the one you specify. As a result, you will get a list of long-tail keywords with each keyword in the list matching the specified search term. Along with each suggested keyword, you will get its search volume rate for the last month, search volume trend for the previous 12 months, as well as current cost-per-click and competition values. Moreover, this endpoint supplies minimum, maximum and average values of daily impressions, clicks and CPC for each result.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_keywords_for_site
tools.description: The Keywords For Site endpoint will provide you with a list of keywords relevant to the target domain. Each keyword is supplied with relevant, search volume data for the last month, cost-per-click, competition

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_page_intersection
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with the keywords for which specified pages rank within the same SERP. You will get search volume, competition, cost-per-click and impressions data on each intersecting keyword. Along with that, you will get data on SERP elements that specified pages rank for in search results, as well as the estimated traffic volume and cost of ad traffic. Page Intersection endpoint supports organic, paid, local pack and featured snippet results. Find keywords several webpages rank for: If you would like to get the keywords several pages rank for, you need to specify webpages only in the pages object. This way, you will receive intersected ranked keywords for the specified URLs. Find keywords your competitors rank for but you do not: If you would like to receive all keywords several pages rank for, but particular pages do not, you need to use the exclude_pages array as well. This way you will receive the keywords for which the URLs from the pages object rank for, but the URLs from the exclude_pages array do not

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_ranked_keywords
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with the list of keywords that any domain or webpage is ranking for. You will also get SERP elements related to the keyword position, as well as impressions, monthly searches and other data relevant to the returned keywords.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_related_keywords
tools.description: The Related Keywords endpoint provides keywords appearing in the "searches related to" SERP element You can get up to 4680 keyword ideas by specifying the search depth. Each related keyword comes with the list of relevant product categories, search volume rate for the last month, search volume trend for the previous 12 months, as well as current cost-per-click and competition values. Moreover, this endpoint supplies minimum, maximum and average values of daily impressions, clicks and CPC for each result. Datasource: DataForSEO SERPs Database Search algorithm: depth-first search for queries appearing in the "search related to" element of SERP for the specified seed keyword.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_serp_competitors
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with a list of domains ranking for the keywords you specify. You will also get SERP rankings, rating, estimated traffic volume, and visibility values the provided domains gain from the specified keywords.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_subdomains
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with a list of subdomains of the specified domain, along with the ranking distribution across organic and paid search. In addition to that, you will also get the estimated traffic volume of subdomains based on search volume.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_top_searches
tools.description: The Top Searches endpoint of DataForSEO Labs API can provide you with over 7 billion keywords from the DataForSEO Keyword Database. Each keyword in the API response is provided with a set of relevant keyword data with Google Ads metrics

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_search_intent
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with search intent data for up to 1,000 keywords. For each keyword that you specify when setting a task, the API will return the keyword's search intent and intent probability. Besides the highest probable search intent, the results will also provide you with other likely search intent(s) and their probability. Based on keyword data and search results data, our system has been trained to detect four types of search intent: informational, navigational, commercial, transactional.

tools.name: delete_task
tools.description: Delete a task by ID

tools.name: deploy_changes
tools.description: List the files that have changed since the last deploy of the specified tier (dev-preview / staging / production).

tools.name: deploy_diff
tools.description: PREVIEW what a deploy will change — the exact file + route diff between what a deploy WOULD ship and what is currently live on a tier. Read-only; never deploys. Call this before deploy_site to answer 'is it safe to deploy / what am I about to change?'. Sides of the diff: • to-ship (left): omit `local` → the DB is_current text set (exactly what deploy_site ships). Pass `local: [{path,sha256}]` → preview a push you have NOT saved yet. • deployed (right): resolved newest-wins from the exact version manifest of the last deploy, else the post-deploy checkpoint, else a timestamp proxy, else never_deployed. THE CONTRACT — data.has_changes is TRUE | FALSE | null: • false → a CONFIDENT all-clear: exact baseline AND code AND assets all match. Safe to skip the deploy. • true → a concrete change was found (never_deployed ⇒ everything is new ⇒ true). • null → we CANNOT prove no-change: approximate/timestamp basis, GitHub-source project, or an unknown asset baseline. Do NOT treat an empty diff as 'nothing will change' — read data.confidence + data.basis + data.warnings. Returns data.{basis, confidence, source_of_truth, summary{changed,added,deleted,unchanged,total_to_ship}, files{changed,added,deleted}, assets{changed,added,deleted,confidence}, routes{added,modified,removed,details,non_route_file_changes}, warnings}. Routes are a STATIC heuristic from changed src/app files; shared component/lib changes land under non_route_file_changes, not invented routes. warnings may include reserved_cdn_prefix_page_collision — a shipping PAGE sits under a reserved CDN asset prefix (videos/, media/, images/, ...) and will 403 on the deployed URL; rename the route.

tools.name: deploy_doctor
tools.description: DIAGNOSE a deployed environment that isn't serving correctly — 403/404 on the live URL, blank pages, 'deploy said ready but the site is broken'. Read-only; checks the FULL serving path that you cannot see from other tools: • CloudFront wiring — is the default behavior pointing at the right origin kind for this project (Lambda for framework apps, S3 for static)? Leftover static config on an SSR distribution? • The attached CloudFront Function — a static-era function rewriting page paths against a Lambda origin is the classic 'every route 404s but /_next/* chunks work' signature. • Serving diff — the same routes requested through the CDN AND directly against the origin. origin-200/CDN-broken = CloudFront problem; both-broken = build/artifact problem. This distinction is the single most valuable diagnostic: it tells you whether to fix the project or escalate the platform. • Project-tree red flags — framework source without package.json (deploys misclassify as static), reserved-prefix page collisions, suspiciously fast 'builds'. Returns { healthy, findings: [{severity, code, detail, fix}], serving: {cdn, origin_direct}, distribution, recent_deployments }. Relay CRITICAL findings' fix text verbatim — each names the exact next action. Use this INSTEAD of guessing when a deployed URL misbehaves; do not propose deleting/recreating infrastructure without running it first.

tools.name: deploy_get
tools.description: Get one deployment by ID, including URL, status, error, build_logs, and timing. The id slot accepts BOTH forms the deployment row carries: • UUID `id` (what deploy_site / deploy_run return as `deploy_id`) • String `deployment_id` (e.g. 'olympus-1779590857819-6joz6p' — what deploy_history / deploy_status surface) Pass either to `deployment_id`; the route resolves whichever matches. Returns both fields in the response so downstream calls have whatever form they need. Response shape: `{ data: Deployment }` where Deployment is `{ id, deploy_id, deployment_id, environment, status, url, preview_url (===url), error, build_logs, build_time_ms, environment_vars, branch, commit_hash, commit_message, author, triggered_by, started_at, completed_at, created_at }`. `data.status` is always present (column has default='queued'); read it directly. The same per-deployment field set is emitted by deploy_status (under data[] and most_recent) and deploy_site (under data) — one parser handles all three.

tools.name: deploy_history
tools.description: List a project's deployment history with optional filters (environment / status / triggered_by).

tools.name: deploy_run
tools.description: Trigger a deploy. environment=dev-preview hits the dev preview pipeline (fast). environment=production goes through the heavyweight production pipeline. agent_codename is an optional label that shows up in the deployment record.

tools.name: deploy_site
tools.description: Deploy the project to one of the three AWS serverless (Lambda + CloudFront) environments. **GitHub is NOT required** — this pulls files straight from builder_code_versions (the same DB that project_file_save writes to). Works on every project, GitHub-connected or not. Environments — each routes to a distinct deployment service: • development (default, SAFE) — fast turn-around for low-risk experiments. Use this first. • staging — must be enabled per project in the hosting dashboard first; calling this on a project where staging_enabled=false returns 412 with code "staging_not_enabled". • production — full CodeBuild → CloudFront. Slowest path; reserve for go-live. NEVER pick this just to "test the deploy flow" — use development for that. END-TO-END LIFECYCLE (preview → production): 1. Edit. project_file_save({sync_preview:true}) or project_files_bulk_save updates the live PREVIEW (Fly container, instant) AND builder_code_versions. 2. Eyeball. preview_screenshot({path:"/..."}) → check the rendered UI before any Lambda spend. 3. Iterate on development. deploy_site({environment:"development"}). Lives at *.development.hiveku-app.com. 4. (Optional) Promote to staging. deploy_site({environment:"staging"}) — requires staging_enabled=true. 5. Go to production. deploy_site({environment:"production"}). This builds a SEPARATE Lambda artifact — production and development DO NOT share code. **Every file change you want in production (including middleware.ts, next.config.js, env-driven changes) requires its own deploy_site({environment:"production"}) call.** There is no auto-promote from development or staging to production. project_file_save reaches the preview INSTANTLY but does NOT touch any of the Lambda environments — those only update when you deploy_site. 6. Custom domain. After the first production deploy succeeds, call project_domains_add({project_id, domain, tier:"production"}) and surface the returned DNS records to the user. Until DNS verifies and SSL issues, the *.hiveku-app.com URL is the only live production address. NOT this tool: the LIVE PREVIEW (Fly container at hvk-<hash>.preview.hiveku.com) is updated INSTANTLY via project_file_save({sync_preview: true}) or preview_sync. That is a separate surface — instant, no build, no Lambda. Use preview_sync for "see my edit live"; use deploy_site only when you want a real Lambda artifact behind one of the three environment subdomains. Returns deployment_id; poll deploy_get({project_id, deployment_id}) for status. READ data.warnings[] when present — e.g. reserved_cdn_prefix_page_collision means a shipping PAGE sits under a reserved CDN asset prefix (videos/, media/, images/, ...) and WILL 403 on the deployed URL; rename the route (see hiveku_docs "Reserved CDN Asset Path Prefixes"). POST-DEPLOY SMOKE VERIFICATION: after the build, the pipeline itself requests the live URL (homepage + sample routes) through the CDN and FAILS the deploy if they return 403/404/5xx — a deploy that reports success is verified actually serving. If a deploy fails with 'live site FAILS verification', the artifacts deployed but the serving path is broken: run deploy_doctor({project_id, environment}) for the diagnosis instead of blindly retrying.

tools.name: deploy_status
tools.description: List recent deployments for a project, newest first. To check 'what is the status of MY latest deploy', read `most_recent.status` — a singleton convenience that mirrors deploy_get's shape and avoids the data-is-array-not-object trap. Response shape (consistent across calls — same field names as deploy_get + deploy_site): { data: Deployment[] // history, newest first (max 20 by default) most_recent: Deployment|null // === data[0]; null if no deploys ever pagination: { page, limit, total, pages } } Each Deployment object: { id, deploy_id (===id), deployment_id, environment, status, url, preview_url (===url), error, branch, commit_hash, author, triggered_by, started_at, completed_at, created_at }. Use deploy_get when you already have a specific deployment_id (from deploy_site's `deploy_id`). Use deploy_status when polling 'is my latest deploy done?'. Both return the same per-deployment shape so you can write one parser.

tools.name: deploy_subscribe
tools.description: Subscribe to live deploy + build-log events via Server-Sent Events. Returns text/event-stream the client reads as long-poll. Avoids burning a deploy_status poll every 15s. EVENT TYPES: • event: status — fires on every builder_deployments status transition. Carries id, deployment_id, deployment_type, status, url, error, timestamp. • event: log — fires per build-log line WHEN include_log_lines=true (verbose; usually leave off). • event: ping — heartbeat every heartbeat_ms; no payload. • event: end — final event before close. payload.reason = 'deployment_terminal' | 'max_seconds' | 'server_shutdown'. Pinning to one deployment (deployment_id arg): stream auto-closes as soon as the deployment reaches a terminal status (completed / failed / cancelled / etc.). Without it: streams all deployments for the project until max_seconds elapses. max_seconds caps the connection at 10 min (default) — reconnect for longer subscriptions. Some MCP runtimes can't hold SSE; fall back to polling deploy_get every 5-10s when this fails.

tools.name: design_comment_resolve
tools.description: Mark one review comment on a Creative Studio design as resolved (sets is_resolved true and stamps resolved_at now). Returns only { success: true } - not the comment, not its text, not its new state - so read the thread back with GET /api/olympus/marketing/design/:id/comments if you need to see the result. ONE WAY: no route anywhere un-resolves a comment, and the design canvas renders only unresolved pins and counts only unresolved comments, so a comment resolved by mistake vanishes from the designer's view and can be restored only by direct database access. SILENT NO-OP ON A REPLY: any comment row on the project is accepted, including a reply (one with parent_comment_id set), but the thread read returns isResolved for TOP-LEVEL comments only, so resolving a reply reports success and changes nothing anyone can observe - resolve the parent comment instead. Re-resolving an already-resolved comment also succeeds and overwrites resolved_at with the new time, losing the original resolution time. resolved_by is written NULL for API-key callers, so the row records that it was resolved and when but can never name who did it. A design project that is missing or owned by another account returns 404 'Project not found'; a commentId that is not on that project returns 404 'Comment not found'; an id or commentId that is not a UUID is not guarded here and surfaces as a 500 rather than a 404. Costs nothing: no money, no outbound call, no queued job, no notification, one row update. The handler reads no body and no query string, so anything else sent with the call is ignored.

tools.name: design_comments_list
tools.description: Read the review thread pinned to one Creative Studio design project. Returns { comments: [{ id, commentText, position: { x, y }, userId, isResolved, createdAt, replies: [{ id, commentText, userId, createdAt }] }] }, oldest first, with each top-level comment's replies nested inline, so there is no second call. `position` is the percentage pin on the canvas and reads { x: 50, y: 50 } for any comment stored without one. RESOLVED COMMENTS ARE INCLUDED: the designer's canvas renders only unresolved pins, so filter on `isResolved` yourself or your count will disagree with the 'N unresolved' badge the human is looking at. No filters and no pagination - the entire thread comes back every call. A malformed, unknown or other-tenant id returns 404 'Design project not found', which is NOT the same answer as 200 with an empty comments array. READ ONLY, and no create tool exists or can: design_comments.user_id is NOT NULL and an API key has no user behind it, so posting a comment stays a human action in the dashboard. Resolving is a separate POST to /api/olympus/marketing/design/:id/comments/:commentId/resolve and is one-way - no route un-resolves a comment.

tools.name: design_create
tools.description: Create a new design project. The agent typically provides initialCanvasData (full Fabric.js JSON: { version, objects:[...], background }) and an artboard size — anything created here is immediately editable in the dashboard. Returns id + dashboardUrl so the agent can hand off to the user.

tools.name: design_export_image
tools.description: Flatten a design to a PNG so the user can see the result. Renders one frame of the canvas via the Remotion worker — same CanvasComposition the MP4 path uses, so frame=0 matches what `canvas.toDataURL` would produce in the dashboard editor. For motion designs, set `frame` to capture a specific moment (e.g. frame=60 at fps=30 = 2s in). The agent should: (1) design_update with the canvas, (2) design_export_image to get an S3 PNG URL, (3) include the URL in the chat reply so the user sees the design inline; meanwhile the user can also click design.dashboardUrl to edit. Refuses early if the canvas is empty. Sync poll, ~5-15s typical, 90s budget.

tools.name: design_export_mp4
tools.description: Render a motion-graphic design to MP4 (or GIF) via the Remotion worker. Pass the full canvas_json snapshot the user has been editing (layered Fabric JSON with per-layer `animation` metadata) — the worker uses the same animation vocabulary as the editor so the output matches the in-browser preview exactly. SYNCHRONOUS: blocks for up to 240s while the worker renders. Refuses early if the canvas has no objects. Returns mp4Url + jobId. The MP4 is hosted publicly so it can be embedded directly; after this call, also PATCH the design with `previewVideoUrl` so the dashboard gallery shows an autoplay thumbnail.

tools.name: design_from_testimonial
tools.description: Open a Creative Studio draft on an APPROVED video testimonial's published recording, so the clip can be trimmed, captioned or branded before it is sent back through the testimonial replace-media route. Mints a design_projects row of design_type motion_graphic whose canvas is ONE unmuted HivekuVideo layer sized to the recording (1080x1920 and a black artboard when the row never got its dimensions), plus a media_assets row registering that SAME already-published object BY URL and tagged 'testimonial': no bytes are fetched, copied or re-uploaded, no render is queued, nothing is billed. Returns {ok, created, design_project_id, editor_url (relative /dashboard/marketing/design/<id>), dashboard_url (the absolute, clickable form)} plus asset_id ONLY when created is true. Idempotent: created:false means the draft already existed and came back untouched, and a draft the operator deleted is quietly re-minted. Continue with design_state_get to read the canvas, design_update to edit it, design_export_mp4 to render. APPROVED-ONLY, and it cannot be talked around: status rejected or spam is 409 media_deleted (those rows keep their url columns after the S3 delete, so they LOOK editable while the bytes are gone), any other non-approved status is 409 not_approved, a testimonial whose consent was withdrawn is 409 revoked, and the final linking UPDATE re-checks status approved AND consent not revoked, so approve the testimonial first rather than looking for a way in. Also refused: a written testimonial is 400 not_media, a recording hosted on an external platform is 400 offsite_media, a row with no published recording yet is 409 no_media, and an unknown, malformed or other-account id is a flat 404 not_found. 409 state_changed is a REAL OUTCOME, not a transient error: the testimonial was revoked or unapproved mid-flight, the draft and the asset this call had just written were both deleted again, nothing is attached and nothing leaked, so re-read the testimonial instead of retrying blind. The request body is never read, so the id is the only thing that steers this.

tools.name: design_get
tools.description: Fetch a single design project including full Fabric.js canvasData. Use this for round-tripping: read → mutate → design_update. For an AI-friendly summary instead of raw JSON, use design_state_get.

tools.name: design_list
tools.description: List the account's design projects (graphics + motion graphics) ordered by most-recently-edited. Returns id / title / designType / status / featuredImageUrl / previewVideoUrl / tags. Pair with design_dashboard_url to give the user a click-through link.

tools.name: design_publish_to_library
tools.description: Publish a saved design as a flat PNG into the account's Media Library. Reads the design's canvas STRAIGHT FROM THE DB (send no canvas_json), renders one settled frame on the Remotion worker, uploads the PNG to the account's S3 media path and creates a media_assets row tagged creative-studio + published. Returns { success, fileUrl, mediaAssetId, width, height }: fileUrl is the permanent public URL of the PNG, mediaAssetId is the new library row. TREAT THIS AS CREATE, NEVER AS SYNC: nothing dedupes, the filename carries Date.now() and the insert is a plain create with no unique key, so publishing the same design twice leaves TWO S3 objects and TWO library entries, and a retry after a timeout duplicates the same way. Synchronous, polled for up to 90s; on timeout it returns 504 with no job handle to poll while the worker may still finish and orphan a still that never reaches the library, so never loop or auto-retry it. Costs one real still-render job plus one permanent S3 object and one DB row per call; no customer-facing send and no card charge. For a throwaway preview PNG that registers nothing in the library, use design_export_image instead (it also lets you choose the frame; this tool always publishes the settled frame, after enter animations finish, which is frame 0 only for a design with no animation). To register an already-hosted URL without rendering, use media_library_register_external_url. Body is optional in full: with no arguments beyond id it publishes the first page under the design's own title. Failures: 404 unknown design or another account's, 400 empty canvas or an unresolvable page_id (the error lists the available page ids and names), 422 the render itself failed, 502 the worker rejected the job or the rendered PNG could not be downloaded, 504 render timed out, 500 REMOTION_RENDER_URL unset on this environment or the S3 upload failed. PM-task linking and custom tags are deliberately not exposed here.

tools.name: design_render_job_get
tools.description: Poll one durable video render job by id and return {jobId, status, progress, progressMessage, url, assetId, width, height, durationSeconds, warnings, error}. This is the recovery path for a paid render whose originating request died: marketing_generate_video and marketing_video_pipeline_retry_scene both reserve a design_render_jobs row and hand back its id, and a 504 or a dropped connection loses the response but NOT the job. Calling this does not just read the row, it ADVANCES it: the handler runs the same pollAndAdvance the reconcile cron uses, so the clip finishes and registers in the media library through this call. Status is one of the RenderJobStatus values and only completed, failed and abandoned are terminal, so keep polling on anything else. The lookup is account-scoped before anything else happens, so another tenant's job id is a plain 404 rather than a leak. `url` and `assetId` stay null until the job reaches completed.

tools.name: design_state_get
tools.description: Get a human-readable + structured summary of a design's canvas — element-by-element position/size/style/text/animation plus a one-line text summary. Use this before issuing design_update so the agent reasons over a compact view instead of the raw Fabric JSON. Returns featuredImageUrl if a preview thumbnail exists.

tools.name: design_templates_list
tools.description: List the design templates available to the agent. Returns the rich 52-template library brand-substituted with the account's active brand guide (orange for Locus, purple for Hiveku, etc.) plus artboard size presets grouped by category (Social Media / Presentation / Print / Ads / Email). Each template carries a ready-to-use canvasData payload — pipe it into design_create's initialCanvasData.

tools.name: design_update
tools.description: Save canvas state on a design. Pass `canvasData` (full Fabric.js JSON) to overwrite the canvas — this is the primary write path. The dashboard editor reads from the same column, so user edits later are preserved on next save. Other fields (title/description/status/tags/featuredImageUrl/artboard) update independently. `previewVideoUrl` sets the autoplay-thumbnail URL without touching the rest of canvasData (only fires when canvasData is omitted). Body capped at 10MB. For full design freedom: arbitrary shapes (rect/circle/triangle/polygon/path/line), text (textbox/i-text with fontFamily/fontSize/fontWeight/lineHeight/charSpacing), images (type:image, src), groups, layer ordering (via objects[] order), positions (left/top/angle/scaleX/scaleY), styling (fill/stroke/strokeWidth/opacity), and per-layer motion via `animation` on the object. THE FIELD NAMES BELOW ARE EXACT: the renderer reads them literally, and an unrecognized key is ignored in silence, so a design saved with the wrong names renders completely static while every tool reports success. This description previously documented `{ preset, delay_ms, duration_ms }`, none of which the renderer reads. `animation: { enter?: 'fade-in'|'fade-up'|'fade-down'|'fade-left'|'fade-right'|'scale-in'|'pop'|'slide-up'|'slide-down'|'slide-left'|'slide-right'|'wipe-up'|'wipe-down'|'blur-in'|'rotate-in', enter_delay_ms?: number (default 0), enter_duration_ms?: number (default 800), enter_distance_px?: number (default 60, for the directional fades and slides), easing?: 'cubic-out'|'quart-out'|'expo-out'|'back-out'|'ease-in-out'|'elastic', exit?: same preset list, exit_at_ms?: number, exit_duration_ms?: number (default 600), loop?: 'pulse'|'wiggle'|'rotate-slow'|'breathe'|'float'|'shimmer' }`. NOTE that `loop` is a SEPARATE FIELD from `enter`, not another preset value: pulse, wiggle, rotate-slow and breathe were previously listed among the entry presets, so putting one in `enter` produces no entry animation at all. Omitting `enter` leaves the layer visible from t=0; omitting `exit` leaves it visible to the end. Canvas-level motion: set `_animation: { duration_ms, fps, loop }` on the root.

tools.name: design_version_create
tools.description: Snapshot the current canvas state into design_versions. Call this BEFORE making large destructive edits so the user can roll back from the dashboard's Version History panel. Mark `isMilestone: true` for named save-points (e.g. 'final approved version').

tools.name: design_version_get
tools.description: Read ONE design version snapshot, including its frozen canvas blob. Returns id, versionNumber, versionName, changeSummary, title, isMilestone, createdAt, plus the two blobs the listing does NOT carry: canvasData (design_versions.sections - the full Fabric.js JSON frozen at snapshot time: objects[] with per-layer geometry, style, text, image src and animation, plus the canvas-level _animation block and any _preview_video_url) and artboard (design_versions.global_settings - width, height, background, gridEnabled, gridSize, snapEnabled, rulerEnabled). Call design_versions_list FIRST: it returns every field here EXCEPT canvasData and artboard, so come here only when the blob is actually needed. SIZE IS THE TRAP: unlike design_state_get, which rewrites an embedded image src to '[embedded image]', this hands back the raw blob, so a canvas carrying base64 data: URIs returns at multiple MB and swamps the agent's context. canvasData is sections || {} over a column that defaults to [], so it can arrive as an object, an empty array, or {} - check before reading .objects. Reading a version does NOT restore it and does not touch design_projects. Restoring is a separate destructive write: send this canvasData to design_update (PATCH on the design), which overwrites design_projects.sections wholesale and increments sections_version - pass expectedSectionsVersion on that call or a human editing the same design loses their unsaved canvas with no error to either side. design_update MERGES artboard rather than replacing it, so pushing this snapshot's artboard back restores the keys it holds and leaves any newer key in place. Costs nothing: two indexed reads, no write, no queued job, no money. Every miss is a 404 - a versionId that belongs to another account, or to a different design in this account, is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

tools.name: design_versions_list
tools.description: List all version snapshots for a design (most recent first).

tools.name: design_video_capabilities_get
tools.description: Pre-flight for AI video: can this account generate a clip right now, asked BEFORE marketing_generate_video reserves a paid (~$1) render. Returns {videoEnabled} on every outcome, plus {plan, used, limit} once the plan gate runs, plus {reason, message} when blocked. reason is one of not_configured (REMOTION_RENDER_URL is unset on this environment), render_service_unavailable (the render worker did not answer /health within 2s), plan_upgrade_required (the effective plan is not premium), monthly_cap_reached (20 clips per account per calendar month, UTC) or cap_check_unavailable. SILENT FAILURE: all five of those are HTTP 200. There is no error status to branch on, so read videoEnabled and never the status code. cap_check_unavailable is a transient database error and is RETRYABLE, not a real block - do not tell anyone to upgrade or that they are out of clips on it. used and limit are OMITTED on not_configured, render_service_unavailable, plan_upgrade_required and cap_check_unavailable; they appear only on monthly_cap_reached and on success. videoEnabled true is not a guarantee either: worker health is cached process-wide for 60 seconds in BOTH directions, so a worker that just died still reads reachable for up to a minute (the render then fails) and one that just recovered still reads unavailable. used counts only clips already registered in the Media Library after a render finishes, and the cap takes no lock, so an in-flight generation is uncounted and concurrent calls near the boundary can land a clip or two over. Use this rather than marketing_generate_video with dry_run:true as the pre-flight: dry_run reports the same plan and cap gate but runs before the REMOTION_RENDER_URL check and never probes the worker, so it cannot see not_configured or render_service_unavailable, and it still requires a prompt. Free and read-only: nothing is reserved, billed or enqueued. Takes no arguments and always reports the calling key's own account.

tools.name: design_video_rerender
tools.description: Re-render a single Remotion-template video clip with new prop values. Used when a design contains a video element backed by a Remotion template — the user (or agent) edits a slot, this re-runs the render, and the resulting MP4 swaps in place. Canvas position/scale/rotation are preserved by the caller on update. Blocks up to 240s.

tools.name: design_voiceover_create
tools.description: SPENDS MONEY: renders the script through Cartesia, stores the MP3 and writes a billing row. Run design_voiceover_estimate first - that is what it is for - and read too_long, billable and remaining_seconds before calling this. Returns asset_id, url, duration_ms, characters, cost_cents, cached, voice_id and script, and registers the clip in the Media Library. cached: true means an identical (script, voice) render already existed on this account, so nothing new was spent, cost_cents is 0 and no allowance was consumed. asset_id can come back null while url is real audio that has ALREADY been billed, because the library row is best-effort - never treat a null asset_id as a failed render and never retry on it. voice_id must be a Cartesia UUID from design_voices_list: this surface refuses anything else with 400 voice_not_recognised, unlike the browser route, where the shared library silently substitutes the default voice and only writes a server log, turning an unknown id into a paid render in the wrong voice reported as success. voice_id is checked for UUID shape, not catalog membership, so a well-formed id Cartesia does not know still reaches the provider and comes back provider_rejected. Failures carry a machine `error` code plus a human `message`: empty_script and script_too_long are 400, plan_upgrade_required (the plan includes no voiceover) and monthly_cap_reached (ten times the allowance) are 402, and provider_rejected, provider_timeout or upload_failed mean no ledger row was written.

tools.name: design_voiceover_estimate
tools.description: Prices a voiceover script before anything is rendered, and spends nothing: returns characters, max_characters (800), estimated_seconds, too_long, plan, included_minutes, used_seconds, remaining_seconds, billable, overage_cents_per_minute and cost_cents. characters counts the NORMALIZED script - markdown is stripped before it reaches the provider, so a bolded word does not inflate it - and estimated_seconds is a flat 15.5-characters-per-second heuristic, not a measurement. cost_cents is the gross per-character figure the render ledger records (12 cents per 1,000 characters); the monthly invoice bills only whole minutes past included_minutes at overage_cents_per_minute, so cost_cents is not by itself what the customer pays. billable is true when estimated_seconds exceeds remaining_seconds. included_minutes of 0 means the plan (free or hosting) has no voiceover allowance at all and design_voiceover_create will 402 plan_upgrade_required, so check it before writing a script. Omit script to read the allowance on its own.

tools.name: design_voices_list
tools.description: Narrator catalog for Design Studio voiceovers, with a server-scored shortlist on top. Returns { voices: [{ id, name, gender, description, suggested }], suggested_count }, sorted suggested-first then alphabetically, and a voice id here is the value a storyboard or a video render takes. Read brand_guide_voiceovers_get FIRST: that returns the account's APPROVED narrators with the human usage notes on each, and this wider catalog is only for deliberately picking outside that set. Not voice_tts_voices_list, which is the IVR catalog behind the paid phone-plan gate and answers 402 for exactly the marketing-only accounts this one serves. The failure that reads as data: when CARTESIA_API_KEY is unset or the upstream call fails or times out, the response is HTTP 503 carrying voices: [] plus error 'not_configured' or 'voices_unavailable', so an empty array is a broken environment and never an account with no voices - read error before reporting that there are none, and note a failure is not cached so every call retries upstream. suggested_count is the hardcoded constant 8, not a count of the rows returned, and fewer than 8 can carry suggested: true. Takes no arguments at all: no search, no filter, no paging, and the upstream read is one un-paginated page of 100 rows then filtered to non-archived English voices, so this is a slice of the Cartesia catalog and not the whole of it. Costs nothing: it generates no TTS, writes no row, and a successful catalog is cached 10 minutes per process.

tools.name: email_audience_create
tools.description: Create an audience. kind='dynamic' (default) re-evaluates filter_json at send time; 'static' is a manually-maintained list. filter_json vocabulary — the WHOLE list the engine honours (AUDIENCE_FILTER_KEYS in the builder's src/lib/marketing/audience-materializer.ts, which both the send and email_audience_preview resolve through): has_email, include_tags, any_tags, exclude_tags, lifecycle_stages, lead_sources, utm_campaigns, lead_statuses, min_lead_score, max_lead_score, created_after, created_before, has_deal, deal_status, deal_pipeline_id, deal_stage_ids, custom_fields, icp_matched_ids, min_icp_confidence, visited_pages, last_seen_within_days, in_journey_stage, engaged_campaign_ids, not_engaged_campaign_ids, has_shopify_order, min_shopify_total_spent_cents, max_shopify_total_spent_cents, min_shopify_order_count, shopify_last_order_after, shopify_last_order_before. AN UNKNOWN KEY IS NOT REJECTED — it is stored and then ignored. This route validates no key names, so an invented name (min_score, icp_tiers, company_ids, owner_ids, deal_stages, has_open_deal, opened_campaign_ids, clicked_campaign_ids, shopify_min_orders, shopify_min_spend, shopify_ordered_after, unsubscribed, suppressed, groups, filter_version, …) saves with a 201 and then narrows NOTHING: the campaign reaches everyone the remaining keys allow, including the people the operator meant to exclude. Type the names above exactly and read filter_json back before attaching the audience to a campaign. THE ONLY REFUSAL (400, with a contradictions[] body) is a filter no contact can satisfy: a tag both required and excluded, every any_tags value also excluded, an inverted lead-score / shopify-spend / created / last-order range, has_shopify_order=false alongside min_shopify_order_count>=1, the same campaign id in both engaged_campaign_ids and not_engaged_campaign_ids, or conflicting custom_fields predicates. It also fires on email_audience_update when a static audience is flipped to dynamic. Every predicate AND-intersects; there is no OR. Bounds are min_lead_score / max_lead_score (0-100; a NULL lead_score matches neither). has_deal is 'any' | 'open' | 'won' | 'none'; deal_status is ignored under 'open'/'won'. visited_pages and last_seen_within_days resolve against ClickHouse and ARE sized by email_audience_preview — if ClickHouse is unreachable the resolver throws and the preview answers 'Audience not found'. lead_sources and utm_campaigns each match the CURRENT or the FIRST-TOUCH column (lead_source OR original_lead_source, utm_campaign OR original_utm_campaign), by exact case-sensitive equality.

tools.description: Generate an OAuth authorization URL so the user can connect their Gmail / Outlook (and Google Calendar + Google Meet on the same flow) to this Hiveku account. Returns a `setup_url` you HAND TO THE USER (don't open it on their behalf — they need to be in their own browser session to grant Google consent). The URL is valid for 5 minutes; after they finish, the OAuth callback writes an email_connections row and the CRM email/calendar surface starts working immediately. Default scope_label = `modify_with_calendar` (Gmail read/send/modify + Google Calendar events + Meet read-only). Other options: - readonly: read email only (no calendar) - send: send email only (no read, no calendar) - modify: read/send/modify email (no calendar) User resolution: passes through to whichever Hiveku user OWNS the connection. Solo-account agents can omit user_email/user_id (auto-picks the only user). Multi-user accounts must specify which user the connection belongs to. Prereq: the account needs a Google OAuth Client registered with `product='crm_email_calendar'`. If the agent gets `code: 'no_oauth_app'`, surface the hint that the account owner needs to register one at /dashboard/settings/oauth-apps first. After the user finishes: poll `email_connections_list` (filter platform=gmail) and look for `connection_status: 'connected'`. Once that lands, crm_calendar_list and friends will return real data.

The recipient is ALWAYS the AWS mailbox simulator (success@simulator.amazonses.com): full pipeline exercised, ZERO reputation impact, no human recipient — NEVER invent your own test addresses (example.com test sends caused the 08-07 account suspension). verdict sent_but_no_delivery_event means the send path works but the event webhook pipeline is broken. tools.name: email_service_status
tools.description: Account's email-service health for the TRANSACTIONAL lane (hk_ API keys, smtp.hiveku.com, /api/v1/email/send). READ sending_enabled FIRST: when false, a `suspension` block carries the reason/timestamp and ALL sending is blocked (SMTP 450s at DATA, /api/v1/email/send refuses) regardless of the healthy-looking reputation numbers below it — domain reputation reflects history, not current sendability. Also returns verified domains, API-key previews, SMTP connection details and code snippets. Suspensions are lifted by Hiveku staff, not by any tool. sending_enabled is a KILL SWITCH, not a readiness check: true means only "not suspended". It does NOT assert a verified domain or an active API key (read `domains` and `api_keys` for those), and it says NOTHING about marketing campaigns, which are provisioned separately. So sending_enabled: true here alongside ready_to_send: false / ses_provisioned: false from marketing_setup_status is normal and both are correct: they measure different lanes. The one thing they share is the suspension gate, evaluated from the same predicate in both, so sending_enabled: false also blocks every campaign send. For campaign sendability use marketing_setup_status; for an end-to-end transactional proof use email_deliverability_check.

tools.name: entity_populate
tools.description: LLM-enrich a sparse marketing entity (customer_avatar / customer_journey / before_after_grid) with GROUNDED context. The agent supplies research — URLs to scrape, web search queries, free-form notes — and the marketing agent server's populate_entity.py merges that with the account's brand_style_guide (if any), calls DeepSeek V4 Pro, and writes the enriched JSON back to the row. **HALLUCINATION GUARDS** (this is not a fancy autocomplete): 1. If the account has no brand_style_guide AND the agent supplies no urls_to_scrape / search_queries / agent_notes / related_research, the script REFUSES to call the LLM and returns `code: 'context_insufficient'` (400). The agent must gather context first. 2. The LLM is instructed to LEAVE FIELDS NULL (strings) or EMPTY [] (arrays) when the context doesn't ground a confident answer. Refusal > fabrication. 3. Response includes a `_meta` block: `{requires_human_review, fields_with_low_confidence[], sources_used[], notes}` — the agent should surface this to the user when populating fresh / sparse accounts. **Recommended grounding pattern for a FRESH account** (no brand guide, no prior research): 1. Get the account's primary website URL (from website_projects.domain or ask the user). 2. Call entity_populate with `urls_to_scrape: ['https://acme.com', 'https://acme.com/about', 'https://acme.com/services']` — Firecrawl scrapes them and the LLM reads the page content. 3. Optionally add `search_queries: ['acme corp business model', 'acme corp customer reviews']` for outside signals. 4. Optionally add `agent_notes: 'B2B SaaS for HVAC contractors, ICP is shop owners with 5-20 trucks'` if you already know something concrete. For a MATURE account: brand_style_guide alone is usually enough. Pass urls_to_scrape only if you want the LLM to lean on specific page copy (a new product page, etc.). Enrichment shape per entity: avatar → 20+ ICP columns: summary, age_range, gender, location, occupation, income_range, lifestyle, values[], interests[], primary_goals[], motivations[], pain_points[], frustrations[], aspirations, typical_quote, background_story, online_behavior{social_platforms[], device_preference, content_habits, information_sources[], daily_hours_online}, buying_behavior{trigger, decision_cycle, stakeholders[], preferred_intake, budget_range, objections[]}, content_preferences[], preferred_channels[] journey → summary + stages[] with each stage having {name, description, emotions[], pain_points[], touchpoints[], content_types[], opportunities[]} grid → transformation_story, key_benefits[], measurable_results[], audience_context, grid_items[] with each item {before:{title, description, pain_points[]}, after:{title, description, benefits[]}, transformation_details} Side effects: UPDATEs the row in place (caller's existing fields are preserved when LLM doesn't return them); flips populate_status to 'populated' / 'failed' / 'context_insufficient'. Takes ~10-60s when scrapes/searches are requested (one Firecrawl scrape ~2-5s; LLM call ~5-20s). Costs ~$0.001-0.005 per call (DeepSeek + Firecrawl combined). Response shape on success: `{ entity_type, entity_id, entity_name, rows_updated, fields_set[], model, enriched, _meta, context_used: {brand_guide, agent_notes, related_research, scrapes_attempted, scrapes_succeeded, searches_attempted, searches_succeeded} }`. On context_insufficient: 400 with a clear hint to gather research first.

tools.name: execute_js
tools.description: 🕷️ CRAWL4AI: Execute JavaScript before scraping (Firecrawl-backed via actions)

tools.name: fetch_url
tools.description: Fetch a public URL and return its body (HTML/JSON/text). Use after web_search to read a specific page, to pull docs, or to inspect a customer-supplied link. SSRF-safe: refuses private/loopback/link-local hosts and non-http(s) schemes. Body capped at 200KB. For structured scraping (markdown extraction, link discovery), prefer the future scrape_url tool when available; fetch_url returns the raw response.

tools.name: gallery_apply_jsx
tools.description: Generate ready-to-paste JSX for a responsive image grid. images is [{ src, alt?, caption? }]. Splice the returned JSX into a component file via project_commit.

tools.name: gallery_apply_to_cms
tools.description: Scaffold a CMS gallery collection and write one entry per image (image, alt, caption, order fields). User can then edit/reorder via the CMS panel.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generate a brand-aligned image from a text prompt. Output is a hosted PNG URL AND a media_assets row with `source_type='ai_generated'` so the asset shows up in the Hiveku media library (listable via media_library_list with source_type=ai_generated, taggable, attachable to blogs/emails/etc). The response includes `media_asset_id` so the agent can chain into media_update / media_usage_get / etc. Before calling: ALWAYS load `account_context_get` first so the prompt can reference the account's brand voice + visual style. A prompt like "hero image for our blog about X" without brand context produces generic stock-photo output that does not match the rest of the site. Charges against the account's image-generation quota; returns `budget_exceeded` (429) when the plan limit is hit. For multiple images in one onboarding/composition pass (avatar + hero + before + after), use `generate_image_set` instead — same quota, same auto-registration, but one round-trip and parallel execution.

tools.name: generate_image_set
tools.description: Batch image generation — generate up to 10 brand-aligned images in one call. Common onboarding pattern: avatar/persona portrait + landing-page hero + transformation-before + transformation-after, composed against the same brand context. Each prompt can carry its own role, style, aspect_ratio, and (optionally) per-prompt model override; a top-level `model` provides the default. All successes are auto-registered as media_assets rows (source_type='ai_generated'), so they show up immediately in media_library_list and can be filtered by `tags`/`role` (role is saved into ai_metadata). Per-prompt error handling: one bad prompt does not fail the whole batch — failures land in `errors[]` with the index, role, and code. The account's image quota is debited per successful generation (atomic per-call reservation). Budget exhaustion mid-batch yields `code:'budget_exceeded'` on the remaining entries while the earlier successes still land. Before calling: ALWAYS load `account_context_get` so the prompts reference the account's brand voice + visual style. Compose the prompts up-front from the same context for visual consistency across the set.

tools.name: get_account_info

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Get one PM project (pm_projects table) with its recent tasks and any linked website. ⚠️ THIS IS A PM-PROJECTS TOOL. The id slot wants a pm_projects.id — NOT a website_projects.id. For BUILDER / WEBSITE project details (preview URLs, GitHub state, environments, container status) call `project_get` (single-project) or `sites_list` (all). Calling get_project with a website_projects UUID returns 404 because the row lives in a different table.

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Get a single PM task by ID. Response `data` includes the task fields plus `annotations` — the browser annotations reviewers dropped on the live preview, each with its SCREENSHOT. Per annotation: { id, annotation_type, priority, annotation_text, page_url, page_title, coordinates, screenshot_url, screenshot_key, screenshot_status, capture_method, viewport_size, created_by_name, created_by_email, created_at, resolved_at }. `screenshot_url` is a directly-fetchable public PNG (no signing/auth needed). `screenshot_status` is ready | capturing | failed | none — a null screenshot_url with status="capturing" means the async capture hasn't finished yet (re-fetch shortly), NOT that it's broken. `annotation_count` gives the total.

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_delete
tools.description: Delete a queue. Cascades members. Tickets keep their queue_id pointer (orphaned) — reassign them before deleting.

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_get

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_list
tools.description: List queues with member + ticket counts. A queue is a group of agents with a routing strategy (round_robin | least_busy | fixed_user). Tickets can be routed to a queue and the dispatcher picks the assignee per strategy. Filter by is_active to hide retired queues.

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_remove_member
tools.description: Remove a user from a queue. Doesn't affect existing ticket assignments — those stay with the user even after they leave the queue.

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_update
