tools.name: helpdesk_sla_history
tools.description: SLA attainment over a window — the historical complement to helpdesk_tickets_overdue. Includes ALL ticket statuses (a ticket that breached and was later resolved still counts as a breach; overdue only shows live breaches). Window is over created_at: from/to ISO datetimes, default trailing 30 days, max 92 days. Optional scoping by assigned_to_id or queue_id; group_by=assignee|queue adds per-group breakdowns. Each ticket is classified twice — first_response (first_response_at vs first_response_due_at) and resolve (resolved_at vs resolve_due_at) — as met | breached | pending | no_sla. HONESTY CONTRACT: attainment_pct = met/(met+breached); no_sla tickets (no SLA policy applied) and pending tickets (deadline not yet expired) are EXCLUDED from that denominator, and both counts are reported alongside the percentage so the exclusion is visible, never silent. median_first_response_minutes / median_resolution_minutes are computed only from tickets carrying the real timestamps — never imputed. Counts are whole-window, not page-limited.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_add_message
tools.description: Add a message to a ticket. direction defaults to "internal" (internal note). Use helpdesk_ticket_send_reply for customer-visible outbound replies.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_assign
tools.description: Assign a ticket to a human (assigned_to_id) or a queue (queue_id).

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_create
tools.description: Create a new helpdesk ticket. Contact resolution precedence: crm_contact_id → contact_email → contact_phone (one is required). If the email/phone isn't on file, a contact is lazy-created with lead_source='helpdesk' (a phone-created contact has no email). Phones are normalized to E.164 before lookup; multiple contacts can legitimately share a phone (shared office lines — there is deliberately NO unique index), so a multi-match resolves to the OLDEST contact and the 201 body includes contact_resolution { matched_by: 'phone', ambiguous: true } — use crm_contact_merge to heal the split rather than ignoring it. Two simultaneous tickets from the same unknown phone can race into twin contacts (same race the email branch has). The ticket fires the helpdesk_ticket_created workflow trigger and runs the account's auto-acknowledge / auto-assign / SLA automations. Optional first_message attaches the customer's initial message in one call (direction defaults to 'inbound'). Channel still defaults to 'email' even when resolving by contact_phone — pass channel: 'sms' when ticketing a texter. Priority defaults to normal. tags are free-form labels.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_escalate_to_human
tools.description: Escalate a ticket: bumps to priority=urgent, optionally assigns to a human/queue, adds "escalated" tag.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_get
tools.description: Fetch one ticket. Pass include=messages to get the inline message log.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_list
tools.description: List support tickets with filters (status, priority, channel, queue, assignee, contact, company).

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_list_for_company
tools.description: List a company's tickets.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_list_for_contact
tools.description: List a contact's tickets (shorthand for helpdesk_ticket_list with contact_id).

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_merge
tools.description: Merge this ticket into another (moves messages; this ticket is closed with a merge note).

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_messages
tools.description: Convenience: fetch a ticket with its message log inline.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_send_reply
tools.description: Send a customer-visible reply to a ticket (direction=outbound). Sets first_response_at if not set.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_set_priority
tools.description: Update ticket priority.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_set_status
tools.description: Update ticket status. Auto-sets resolved_at / closed_at when status flips to resolved or closed.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_transfer_to_voice
tools.description: Annotate the ticket for a voice transfer. The actual outbound dial is picked up by voice_server.

tools.name: helpdesk_tickets_overdue
tools.description: Surface tickets that have breached SLA — first_response_due_at or resolve_due_at is in the past AND the corresponding actual timestamp is missing. Excludes resolved/closed tickets. Use kind=first_response to focus on missed reply windows, kind=resolve for missed resolutions, kind=both (default) for either.

tools.name: helpdesk_workload
tools.description: Per-agent staffing snapshot — the quantity read beside helpdesk_csat_stats (quality per assignee). For every assignee plus the unassigned bucket: open/pending counts, currently-breached SLA counts (same predicates as helpdesk_tickets_overdue: due date passed, actual timestamp missing, ticket still open/pending), and oldest_open_at. Counts are whole-table grouped aggregates, never page-limited. The unassigned bucket is the null-assignee view the ticket-list API cannot filter for. Assignees whose user record is outside this account return name: null with the id. Optional queue_id scopes every count to one queue.

tools.name: history_cancel_preview_restore
tools.description: Destroy the isolated preview app spawned by history_preview_restore. Pass the preview_session_id from the spawn response. Idempotent — calling against an already-torn-down session returns ok=true + already_torn_down=true. Cleanup is best-effort: per-step failures (Fly destroy / S3 sweep) are reported in the response's `errors` field and the orphan-sweeper cron retries any partial teardown after 1h. If you don't have the preview_session_id, call history_list_preview_sessions first to find active sessions for the project.

tools.name: history_list_preview_sessions
tools.description: List ephemeral preview-restore sessions for a project. Returns active sessions by default (status NOT IN destroyed/failed); pass include_finished='true' for the full history. Use this to (a) find a preview_session_id for an existing session before tearing it down, (b) audit abandoned sessions, or (c) hand a still-running preview_url back to the user mid-conversation.

tools.name: history_preview_restore
tools.description: Spawn an ISOLATED ephemeral preview app for a checkpoint or point-in-time snapshot. The canonical project container is never touched — a broken snapshot can't break the user's working dev environment. Returns { preview_session_id, preview_url } the user can open in a browser / iframe. When done, call history_cancel_preview_restore({preview_session_id}) to destroy the isolated app. Spawn takes 30-90s (snapshot upload + Fly app create + machine boot + health poll). On health-check failure the route auto-destroys the half-spawned app and returns 504 with code='preview_unhealthy'. To COMMIT the previewed state to the canonical project, call history_restore_to_time OR project_checkpoint_restore — those write to the canonical DB and container, separate from the isolated preview app. Tearing down the preview session is independent of (and not required before) committing. Exactly one of as_of OR checkpoint_id is required.

tools.name: history_restore_to_time
tools.description: Restore the project to its state at an arbitrary timestamp (point-in-time restore). Unlike project_checkpoint_restore, this works even when no snapshot was taken at the target time — it reconstructs by querying per-row created_at trails and matching the right S3 object versions. Files that exist now but didn't exist at the target time are NOT removed (same semantics as the checkpoint restore). For strict point-in-time recreation, follow with project_files_bulk_save + delete_missing=true using the snapshot from project_state_at. Pairs with history_preview_restore for try-before-commit workflows.

tools.name: hiveboard_connect
tools.description: Wire arrows between elements that already exist, by id, with the geometry solved for you. A connector needs two things and they do different jobs. The stored coordinates are what gets DRAWN; the bindings are what keeps the endpoints attached when a human later drags one of the boxes. Building it by hand means resolving each id to a box, which lives in a different field per element type, then picking the right pair of edge anchors. That is why the old way to draw a diagram was two calls with an id-zipping step in between, where one invalid row shifted every id after it and the arrows attached to the wrong boxes. Each connection picks the anchor pair the relationship implies: side to side when the two boxes are mostly apart horizontally, bottom to top otherwise, matching what the editor's own connection mode does. A text element has no stored width or height anywhere, so its box can only be estimated server-side; connecting to one is the case you cannot do correctly from outside. Connecting TO an arrow or line is refused. Returns connector_ids and a `skipped` list with the reason for each. Additive.

tools.name: hiveboard_create
tools.description: Create a new Hiveboard (Miro-style canvas). Optionally attach to a project. Use this for sitemaps, brainstorms, sales flows, customer journey maps, etc. After creating, add content via hiveboard_element_create / hiveboard_elements_bulk_create, OR call hiveboard_sitemap_scaffold to auto-place a tree of pages, OR call hiveboard_import_miro to ingest an existing Miro JSON export.

tools.name: hiveboard_delete
tools.description: Delete a Hiveboard. Cascades to every element on the board.

tools.name: hiveboard_duplicate
tools.description: Clone a Hiveboard + every element into a new board (same account, optionally renamed).

tools.name: hiveboard_element_create
tools.description: Add a single element to a Hiveboard. Element types: "rectangle", "circle", "diamond", "triangle", "hexagon", "text", "sticky-note", "frame", "arrow", "line", "pen", "image". Position {x, y} is the element's TOP-LEFT corner, not its centre: the builder sets start={x,y} and end={x+width,y+height} (hiveku_builder/src/lib/hiveboards/element-builder.ts:130-135). This description previously said "center-origin", which put every generated element off by half its size (80x50 at the default 160x100) and left connector arrows pointing at corners instead of edges. To centre a shape on a point, subtract half the width and height yourself. element_data is type-specific (e.g. {text, width, height} for shapes; {points: [...]} for pen; {startConnection, endConnection} for arrow). Sticky notes are the exception to colour: element_data.color must be one of yellow, blue, green, pink, purple, orange. Anything else (a hex, most obviously) is coerced to yellow, because the renderer looks the name up in a table and used to CRASH the whole board on a miss. Additive - does NOT touch other elements on the board. For many elements use hiveboard_elements_bulk_create.

tools.name: hiveboard_element_delete
tools.description: Remove one element by id.

tools.name: hiveboard_element_update
tools.description: Patch ONE element. Allow-listed: element_type, element_data, position, z_index, rotation, color, fill_color, stroke_width, font_size, locked, hidden. element_data is REPLACED wholesale, never merged, and the renderer needs the complete typed element: sending {label: 'New name'} strips start/end and breaks that element on the canvas. Read the element first (hiveboard_elements_find with include_data), change the one field, send the whole object back. For a MERGE, and for a move that also drags the attached connectors along, use hiveboard_elements_patch instead. Style fields are now mirrored into element_data for you, so color/z_index/locked and friends take effect. They previously wrote a column the renderer never reads, which returned 200 and changed nothing on screen. `hidden` is still read by no renderer at all.

tools.name: hiveboard_elements_bulk_create
tools.description: Add up to 5000 elements in one call. Each element is the same shape as hiveboard_element_create. Additive — does NOT delete existing content. Returns {created, invalid, errors[]}.

tools.name: hiveboard_elements_find
tools.description: Find elements on a board by type, by the text they show, or by the region they sit in, without pulling the whole board. Returns a projection: id, element_type, z_index, box {x,y,w,h}, and the text. Text matching is one field whatever the type keeps it in: a shape shows its `label`, a text element and a sticky show their `content`. Getting that distinction wrong by hand is why a search for a card by its caption used to come back empty. Set include_data true when you are about to call hiveboard_elements_patch: that tool merges into the stored element_data, so you need to see what is already there. Leave it off otherwise; raw element_data is what makes a board read expensive. Region is JSON {x, y, w, h} and matches anything OVERLAPPING it, not only what is fully inside. Read-only.

tools.name: hiveboard_elements_patch
tools.description: Update many elements at once, and the ONLY correct way to move something on a board. Three things separate it from hiveboard_element_update. (1) element_data MERGES here instead of being replaced, so changing one label cannot strip an element's geometry and break it on the canvas. (2) A move is a real move: shapes carry their position in start/end, stickies and text and images carry it in position, a pen carries every point, and patching the position column alone moves nothing. (3) Connectors follow: every arrow bound to something that moved has its endpoints translated by the same delta, across the WHOLE board, because the arrows that break are exactly the ones you did not name. Use `text` rather than guessing the field: it writes `label` on a shape and `content` on a text or sticky. Style fields are mirrored into element_data so they take effect. Returns updated, connectors_repaired, skipped (with reasons) and not_found. An id belonging to another board simply does not resolve and comes back in not_found.

tools.name: hiveboard_elements_prune
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Remove many elements from a board at once, by ids, by type, by region, or the whole canvas. The board itself survives; use hiveboard_delete for that. This is what makes a generated board fixable. Every scaffold is additive, so re-running one stacks a second copy on the first, and until this existed cleanup was one call per element: a 200-element mistake cost 200 calls to undo. It snapshots the board into version history first and returns snapshot_version_id. If that comes back NULL the delete was NOT recoverable, and you should say so rather than assume a rollback exists. confirm: true is required. An empty filter is never treated as 'everything': clearing the canvas has to be asked for with all: true, by name. Returns deleted, the recomputed element_count, and any requested ids that were not on this board.

tools.name: hiveboard_flow_scaffold
tools.description: Build a directed flow diagram in one call from nodes and edges: a process map, a user flow, an onboarding flow, or a swimlane handoff map. Those are one drawing with different nouns, so this is one tool. YOU PASS RELATIONSHIPS, IT DERIVES THE LAYOUT. Each node is ranked one layer after its latest predecessor, so the flow reads in dependency order however you listed it, and within a layer nodes are ordered by their predecessors' positions to stop the arrows crossing. A node with TWO parents works here, which is the thing hiveboard_sitemap_scaffold structurally cannot express. Cycles are fine. A rework loop ('failed review' back to 'draft') is drawn dashed and curved and does not flatten the layout; the response lists back_edges so you can see which ones it treated that way. Node types map to the shapes readers actually parse: start/end become terminator circles, decision becomes a diamond, handoff becomes a hexagon, step becomes a card. Label a decision as a question and label both edges leaving it. Pass `lanes` to draw swimlanes. The lane then decides the cross axis instead of the crossing-minimised order, because a swimlane diagram exists to say WHO does each step. A frame is a visual grouping only: it contains nothing in any data sense. An edge naming an unknown node is a 400, not a silently missing branch. Additive. Returns node_to_element_id and node_ranks.

tools.name: hiveboard_funnel_scaffold
tools.description: Build a whole conversion funnel in one call: a card per stage, its metric beside it, a connector carrying the conversion rate, and a drop-off callout beside every leak. The stage that loses the most is highlighted automatically. YOU PASS COUNTS, IT DERIVES THE RATES. Step conversion, step drop-off in both percent and absolute contacts, overall top-to-bottom conversion, and the single biggest leak all come back in the response, so you can quote the same numbers you just drew. Pull the counts from crm_pipeline_stage_summary or the analytics tools rather than inventing them; a funnel with unattributed numbers is a liability. A missing count is not a zero: the connector says 'no data' rather than drawing a confident 0% that reads as a catastrophe. width_mode 'proportional' tapers each card by its share of the top stage, which is what makes a funnel look like a funnel. Widths are floored so a 2% stage stays readable. Additive: it never deletes existing content, so a second call stacks on the first unless you move the origin. Returns stage_to_element_id and the full conversion table.

tools.name: hiveboard_get
tools.description: Fetch a Hiveboard's metadata + every element (z-indexed). Returns elements: [{id, element_type, element_data, position, z_index, color, fill_color, ...}] plus workshop_state, which carries the live dot-vote ledger ({active, budget, frozen, votes:[{elementId, userId}]}) and the session timer. A frozen tally is what a facilitated workshop leaves behind, so that field is how you report what the room actually chose. This returns EVERY element with its full element_data and takes no filters, so on a large board it is expensive. To read a board as a diagram use hiveboard_outline; to find specific elements use hiveboard_elements_find.

tools.name: hiveboard_grid_scaffold
tools.description: Build any board that is content binned on two axes: a customer journey map (stages across, facets down), a retro, a kanban snapshot, a SWOT, a RACI, an affinity wall. One drawing, different nouns, one tool. IT SIZES ITSELF TO THE CONTENT. A sticky note is the only element whose text wraps, and text past its box scrolls INTERNALLY, so the overflow is invisible until someone clicks the note. Each row is therefore sized from its longest cell, and any cell still too long comes back in `truncated` rather than being silently swallowed. Shorten or split those; do not assume they rendered. A row typed 'scores' is drawn as a curve with a dot and a reading per column, auto-scaled to its own range, which is how an emotion line gets onto a journey map without you picking a scale. It is a line, never a filled area: the canvas has no fill primitive outside its six shapes, so there are no pie or area charts here at all. Every row's cells array must be exactly as long as columns, in column order, with null for an empty cell. A length mismatch is a 400 naming both counts, because padding it would slide every later cell one column left and look plausible. Sticky colour is a NAME (yellow, blue, green, pink, purple, orange), never a hex. Additive. Returns cell_to_element_id keyed '<row> <column>'.

tools.name: hiveboard_import_miro
tools.description: Import a Miro board export into Hiveku. Accepts the raw JSON from Miro's REST API (GET /v2/boards/<id>/items) — the {board, items: [...]} shape. Mapping handles shape/sticky_note/text/frame/image/paint; unsupported types (mindmap_node, card, kanban, etc.) are skipped with warnings. Miro's items endpoint doesn't include connectors, so imported boards have content but no arrows. Use hiveboard_element_create afterward to wire connections, or hiveboard_sitemap_scaffold if the import was a sitemap. Either creates a NEW board (omit board_id; name defaults to the Miro board's name) or APPENDS to an existing one (pass board_id). Returns {board_id, created, inserted, summary: {by_type, converted, skipped}, warnings}.

tools.name: hiveboard_list
tools.description: List Hiveboards in the account, newest-edited first. Returns summary cards: id, name, project_id, background_type, element_count, created/edited timestamps. Use `search` to find a board by name rather than listing and matching yourself: the list is capped at 200 and truncates silently, so on an account with many boards a client-side match can miss the one you want.

tools.name: hiveboard_outline
tools.description: Read a board as a STRUCTURE rather than a pile of elements: nodes with their labels and boxes, plus the edge list joining them. The edge list is the point, because it exists nowhere in the data. A connector is a row whose element_data names two other element ids, and nothing joins them back up, so without this the only way to learn what is connected to what is to pull every element through hiveboard_get and rebuild the graph yourself. On a large board that is tens of thousands of tokens for one question. unbound_connectors is the diagnostic worth reading: an arrow drawn between two boxes with no bindings only LOOKS like a relationship. It does not survive a human dragging either box and it is invisible to any structural read. A board full of them needs re-wiring with hiveboard_connect. Read-only. Also returns orphan_count and the board's extent, which is what you need to pick an origin that does not land a new diagram on top of the old one.

tools.name: hiveboard_sequence_scaffold
tools.description: Build an outreach sequence or cadence board in one call: a card per touch, the wait carried on the connector between them, a decision diamond wherever the path forks on a reply, and a goal terminator at the end. YOU PASS WAITS, IT DERIVES THE CALENDAR. Per-step waits are accumulated into an absolute day offset and stamped on every card, and the schedule comes back in the response. Nobody reading a cadence wants 'wait 3 days' five times; they want to know the last touch lands on day 21. The wait on a step is the gap BEFORE it, which is how every sequence tool on the platform models it, so the input maps straight onto email_sequence_get's step list. This is deliberately not hiveboard_flow_scaffold with different words: that one takes a graph and has no time semantics, and using it here would mean building the nodes, the edges and the day arithmetic yourself. on_reply forks the path: a diamond goes on the main line, the outcome card sits on its own row above it clear of everything, and the sequence resumes from the fork. Additive. Returns step_to_element_id, the derived schedule, and total_span_days.

tools.name: hiveboard_sitemap_scaffold
tools.description: Build a whole tree on a Hiveboard in one call: a sitemap, an org chart, a taxonomy, a decision tree. Pass `pages` either as a flat list with `parent` refs OR as a nested tree with `children`; the server detects which shape you sent. Each node becomes a frame labelled with its title, with `path` rendered as a caption underneath it. Parent-to-child arrows are wired automatically with real connections, not floating lines. SET pack_subtrees: true FOR ANYTHING UNBALANCED. The default layout groups nodes by depth and orders each depth by sibling index, so at depth 2 with several parents the subtrees interleave and the arrows cross. pack_subtrees runs a tidy layout instead: every subtree gets a contiguous band and a parent sits centred over its own children. It is off by default only so existing boards do not change shape. Additive: it never deletes existing content, so a second call STACKS another tree on the first unless you pass a different origin. Returns title_to_element_id, which is the only cheap way to patch one node later. Duplicate titles are a hard 400 and nothing is created, because titles are the join key. A parent naming a title that does not exist is silently treated as a root, so check arrows_created against the number of nodes that had a parent. Example flat input: {pages: [{title:"Home",path:"/"}, {title:"About",parent:"Home"}, {title:"Team",parent:"About"}]}

tools.name: hiveboard_update
tools.description: Update a Hiveboard's metadata. Allow-listed: name, description, background_type, background_color, is_public, project_id. Never touches elements. is_public does NOT mean public to the internet. The board is already scoped to its account, so it means any member of THIS account may open it without being granted access to it individually. Pass project_id to attach the board to a project after the fact, or null to detach it. A project_id from another account is a 404, not a silent re-home.

tools.name: hiveku_docs_get
tools.description: Get full documentation for a single Hiveku/Olympus endpoint — path params, query params, request body schema, response example, and notes (gotchas, duplicate detection, workflow triggers). Use this AFTER hiveku_docs_search has narrowed you down to a candidate endpoint, before you call the corresponding MCP tool.

tools.name: hiveku_docs_search
tools.description: Search the Hiveku/Olympus API documentation. Returns matching endpoint summaries (path, methods, description, category, tags). Use this BEFORE guessing — it covers every CRM, marketing, SEO, helpdesk, PM, voice, and integration endpoint. Filter by keyword (search) or category (crm, marketing, seo, helpdesk, pm, voice, integrations, etc.). Call hiveku_docs_get with a specific path to see request/response shapes.

tools.name: hiveku_playbook_get
tools.description: Get full detail for a single playbook by id — every step, sample arguments, prerequisites, related endpoints, and gotchas. Use this when hiveku_playbooks_list surfaced a candidate and you want the actual sequence to execute.

tools.name: hiveku_playbooks_list
tools.description: List Hiveku how-to PLAYBOOKS — named chained-workflow recipes. Each playbook bundles 3-7 tool calls into a complete task: "edit a file and ship it", "estimate → invoice", "rollback a project", "debug a failed deploy", etc. Use playbooks BEFORE composing your own multi-step flow — they encode the canonical Hiveku sequence and call out the right tools in the right order. Beats stitching things together from `hiveku_docs_search` results. Categories: sites, files, deployments, preview, crm, content. Filter with `category` if you only want one bucket.

tools.name: html
tools.description: 🕷️ CRAWL4AI: Extract rendered HTML (Firecrawl-backed)

tools.name: ice_score
tools.description: ICE prioritization scoring (Impact × Confidence × Ease) — pure math, no persistence. Use to rank growth experiments, findings, SEO action items, pm_tasks, etc. against a consistent framework instead of inventing per-call scoring. Two modes: 1. Single — pass {impact, confidence, ease} → {score (1-1000), normalized_score (0-1), components} 2. Batch — pass {items: [{label, impact, confidence, ease, ...passthrough}]} → {items: [{...passthrough, score, rank, input_index}], summary: {count, top_score, mean_score}} Batch mode preserves every input field on each item (notes, evidence, action_url, etc.) so you can round-trip a list through the scorer without losing context. Sorted by score desc, stable tiebreak on input order. Each component clamped to [1,10] with a per-item warning when out of range. Formula: score = impact * confidence * ease. Range 1-1000. Normalized: score/1000.

tools.name: integration_create
tools.description: Create an integration. Only API-KEY providers (bing_webmaster, dataforseo) can be created from CLI/MCP — OAuth providers return 422 with a dashboard URL the user must visit. Idempotent: re-running with the same provider returns the existing row updated with the new credentials and existed:true.

tools.name: integration_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an integration (sets is_active=false). The row is preserved for audit history; downstream tools that look up by provider_slug + active will stop finding it. Accepts `integration_id` or `id`.

tools.name: integration_get
tools.description: Get one integration by id, including masked credentials_preview and last_synced_at. Accepts `integration_id` or `id`.

tools.name: integration_list
tools.description: List all account integrations (Google + marketing/sales connections). Filter by provider_slug or is_active. Returns credentials_preview (masked tokens) for confirmation only; never returns raw secrets.

tools.name: integration_oauth_check
tools.description: Poll the status of a CLI-driven OAuth flow started by integration_oauth_initiate. Status values: pending (user hasn't completed consent yet), completed (integration_id is the new connection), failed (see error field), expired (15 min timeout — call initiate again). Recommended polling interval: 5 seconds; bail after ~15 minutes.

tools.name: integration_oauth_initiate
tools.description: Start an OAuth flow for google_ads / google_search_console / google_business_profile / google_analytics. Returns setup_url, setup_token (for polling), oauth_app_id, and (for ads/gsc/gbp) connection_id. ⚠️ DO NOT USE FOR GMAIL OR CALENDAR. Use `email_connect_start` instead — Gmail + Calendar + Meet share a single consent flow that writes to email_connections (the table CRM calendar/inbox/triage tools read). This route will return code='wrong_tool_for_provider' if you pass google_gmail or google_calendar. THREE PATHS: 1) FIRST-TIME SETUP (recommended for agents driving setup end-to-end). For google_ads pass {provider_slug, customer_id, manager_id?, developer_token} — the route creates the ppc_connections row with those bindings populated, then OAuth fills in refresh_token and status auto-promotes to 'connected'. The agent collects the three Google Ads fields from the user in conversation (developer_token from the MCC's API Center, customer_id of the client account, manager_id of the MCC), calls this tool ONCE, hands the setup_url to the user. Same for google_search_console (pass site_url) and google_business_profile (pass gbp_account_id + gbp_location_id) — but those bindings are usually discovered POST-OAuth via seo_gsc_discover_sites / seo_gbp_discover_locations, so omit them and discover later. 2) RE-AUTH (dead refresh_token). Pass target_connection_id pointing at the existing ppc_connections / seo_connections row. Credentials get replaced in place, bindings are preserved, status auto-promotes back to 'connected'. Symptom that triggers this: integration_test reports 'Account has been deleted', or sync starts failing with OAuth errors. 3) BARE INITIATE (no pre-bindings). For google_analytics, or when you want to bind fields later via seo_connection_update / ppc_connection_update. OAuth app resolution (per-account only — no platform-shared credentials): 1. body.oauth_app_id (if supplied) — validates account ownership + product match 2. First per-account oauth_apps row matching (provider=google, product=<the product for provider_slug>) If neither resolves, returns 412 code='integration_not_configured'. Fix by calling oauth_app_create with the customer's Google Cloud OAuth credentials. After setup_url is opened + consent completed: poll integration_oauth_check until status='completed'. Then verify with integration_test (oauth/api) or ppc_connection_test (google_ads specifically) + run the sync to populate cached data.

tools.name: integration_providers_list
tools.description: List available integration providers. Returns slug, name, description, auth_type ("oauth" or "api_key"), and can_create_from_cli. Use this BEFORE integration_create to discover valid slugs and check whether OAuth-required.

tools.name: integration_test
tools.description: Live-test an integration. For OAuth providers (Google *), runs an actual token refresh — success means refresh_token is still valid and the access_token gets rotated. For API-key providers, sanity-checks that credentials are present. Updates last_synced_at on success. Accepts `integration_id` or `id`.

tools.name: integration_update
tools.description: Update an integration's settings, identifier, or is_active flag. Credentials cannot be updated here — rotate via OAuth (dashboard) or re-POST for API-key providers. Accepts `integration_id` or `id`.

tools.name: job_cancel
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight async job. Idempotent on terminal jobs (returns 409 with the current status). v1 handlers don't poll for cancellation — they finish whatever they were doing — so this is best treated as 'stop charging me for this future polling round-trip' rather than a hard kill switch. For long-running jobs that haven't fully started yet (status='queued'), cancel is immediate. Once status flips to 'running', the in-process handler completes regardless.

tools.name: job_status_get
tools.description: Check any Olympus async job. PREFER LONG-POLLING: pass wait_seconds (max 25) and the server holds the request, returning the moment the job goes terminal — ONE call replaces a client-side sleep-and-poll loop (MCP calls are rate-limited; poll loops are the #1 budget burner). Typical pattern: job_status_get({ job_id, wait_seconds: 20 }) in a loop until `terminal` is true. Returns status / progress / progress_message / result / error / elapsed_ms / terminal. Large string fields in the echoed `input` are replaced with <field>_bytes stubs (you already have what you sent). The `terminal` flag is the canonical 'stop polling' signal — true when status is succeeded / failed / cancelled / timed_out. Retention: rows are kept ~90 days. After that, polling a stale job_id returns 404. To cancel a queued/running job, call job_cancel({ job_id }).

tools.name: kb_create
tools.description: Create a new knowledge base for storing documents and AI context

tools.name: kb_delete
tools.description: Delete a knowledge base (cascades to its documents).

tools.name: kb_documents_delete
tools.description: Remove a document from a KB.

tools.name: kb_documents_get
tools.description: Fetch one knowledge-base document by id. Returns `data` with the full row: content, metadata, created_at, updated_at. It does NOT return chunks, despite what this tool used to claim. The stored vectors live in Qdrant keyed by metadata.upload_id and are reachable through kb_search, not here. The `embedding` column is a pgvector type Prisma cannot select, so it is absent from the response whether or not the document was embedded; absence is NOT evidence it is unindexed. Scoped through the KB: a document_id that exists under a DIFFERENT knowledge base 404s rather than leaking, so pass the kb_id the document actually belongs to.

tools.name: kb_documents_index_text
tools.description: Index a raw text document into a KB. Server chunks + embeds.

tools.name: kb_documents_list
tools.description: List documents in a knowledge base.

tools.name: kb_get
tools.description: Get a knowledge base by ID with its documents and sources

tools.name: kb_list
tools.description: List knowledge bases with optional type and search filters

tools.name: kb_search
tools.description: Search across knowledge base documents using semantic search

tools.name: kb_stats
tools.description: Size and freshness of one knowledge base: document_count, artifact_count, source_count, sources_by_status, first_indexed_at, last_indexed_at, plus the KB row itself (name, context_type, is_archived, is_default, version). There is NO chunk count and this tool will never return one: chunking happens on the way into Qdrant and the vectors are addressed there by metadata.upload_id, while Postgres holds one row per indexed document. document_count is that row count, NOT a chunk count. Read sources_by_status before concluding a KB is small. A KB that looks under-populated is usually one whose sources are stuck 'pending' or 'failed' rather than one nobody fed, and document_count alone cannot tell those apart. last_indexed_at is the newest DOCUMENT created_at, so it stops moving the moment ingest stalls even while sources keep arriving.

tools.name: kb_update

tools.name: keywords_data_dataforseo_trends_subregion_interests

tools.name: list_departments
tools.description: List the departments this Hiveku account can chat with. Each department has its own identity (custom name, voice, personality), skills, rules, and memory configured by the account in the Hiveku dashboard. Call this first to discover what domains are available before using talk_to_department. Returns domain, label, identity_name, and has_identity flag per accessible department.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List PROJECT-MANAGEMENT projects (pm_projects) for the account — tasks, owners, status, priority. NOT the buildable code projects. If you need to EDIT CODE / DEPLOY / SCREENSHOT a website, call `sites_list` instead — that returns website_projects with all three environments (development / staging / production), GitHub connection state from builder_project_settings, and container status. The `github_repo_full_name` field on pm_projects is usually null even when GitHub IS connected on the website side — sites_list reads the canonical GitHub state.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: List project tasks with rich filtering — by project, status, priority, assignee, type, due date, tags, and more

tools.name: marketing_agent_actions_list
tools.description: List every script and read action marketing_agent_read can run, with a total count. Call this before guessing a script or action name. Read-only.

tools.name: marketing_agent_read
tools.description: Run one READ action from the marketing agent's own Python implementations — 131 actions across 24 scripts covering PPC (Google, Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft, Amazon), SEO (GSC, Bing Webmaster, GBP, audits, keywords, local) and Social. WHEN TO USE: reach for the cross-platform ppc_*, seo_* and social_* tools FIRST — they work from a connection id regardless of platform, and are the only surface with social calendar/hashtags/pillars/comments and connection lifecycle. Use this when you need per-platform DEPTH they cannot express (asset groups, experiments, split tests, lead forms, targeting facets, auction insights). DISCOVER: GET this endpoint (no body) returns every script and its allowed actions. Pass { script, action, connection_id?, args? }, e.g. { script: 'ppc_google_ads', action: 'search-terms', connection_id: '…', args: { 'date-range': 'LAST_30_DAYS' } }. READ-ONLY, and not an oversight: writes spend money or mutate platform state, and the marketing agent wraps them in a daily-budget ceiling, paused-on-create and staged approval that live ABOVE these CLIs. For writes use the ppc_*/seo_*/social_* write tools or talk_to_department({ domain: 'marketing' }).

tools.name: marketing_call_attribution_breakdown
tools.description: The same question for CALLS, which are most of a local-services advertiser's conversions. Groups this account's calls by source/medium/campaign and by day, the way a PPC platform aggregates, so the two can be laid side by side. AND IT REPORTS CALL QUALITY, WHICH THE PLATFORM STRUCTURALLY CANNOT. Google Ads counts a call as a conversion once it passes a minimum duration, regardless of whether it was a lead — so a 12-second wrong number is a conversion. This returns the duration distribution against THIS ACCOUNT'S own configured threshold, the disposition mix, and how many calls reached voicemail, were missed or were abandoned. Learning that 18 of 40 'conversions' were under 30 seconds is the point. Returns no call rows and no transcripts. ALWAYS read the caveats in the response before reporting a discrepancy: this is OUR record, not the platform's record of a conversion, and the two legitimately differ — view-through conversions have no click and can never appear here, cross-device joins are invisible to us, the platform dates by CLICK while we date by the event, and the platform also counts conversions that are not this type at all.

tools.name: marketing_call_attribution_list
tools.description: The breakdown from marketing_call_attribution_breakdown PLUS a page of individual calls. Each carries its source/medium/campaign, the tracking DID that rang and the pool session that credited it (dynamic-number insertion attributes through both), its duration bucket, whether it meets the account's own conversion policy, and has_transcript / has_summary. Returns NO transcripts and never touches storage — use marketing_call_transcript_get for a specific call. include_summaries inlines each AI summary; leave it off for a wide sweep. Breakdown percentages cover up to 5000 scanned calls: totals.truncated says when the window is larger, and totals.calls_matching is the uncapped count.

tools.name: marketing_call_transcript_get
tools.description: Read ONE call's verbatim transcript and AI summary by call id (the id field from marketing_call_attribution_list). DELIBERATELY A SEPARATE, COSTLIER STEP: the transcript is an object in the encrypted recordings bucket, so this pays a storage round trip a list sweep must never pay implicitly. Call it for calls you have a specific question about, not across a result set. THE TEXT IS VERBATIM AND UNREDACTED. A transcript contains whatever was said aloud, including card numbers, dates of birth and health details. Treat it as the most sensitive class of customer data and do not paste it anywhere it would outlive the question. When there is no transcript, transcript_state says WHICH of five situations it is, and none of them means 'empty': never_recorded (no recording ever existed, so nothing failed), pending (still processing), failed (the retry window has closed and nothing will retry it), purged (it WAS transcribed and retention later deleted it — the ai_summary is the surviving record), unreadable (the stored object is missing or will not read).

tools.name: marketing_content_get
tools.description: Fetch one marketing content item.

tools.name: marketing_content_list
tools.description: List marketing content (campaigns, ads, copy).

tools.name: marketing_content_templates
tools.description: List marketing content templates available for use.

tools.name: marketing_design_export_image
tools.description: Render one frame of a design canvas to a flat PNG via the Remotion render worker (synchronous — polls up to ~90s). Send the full Fabric.js canvas_json plus artboard width/height; the canvas must contain at least one layer. Matches what the dashboard editor would export, so use it to show the user a preview of agent-made designs.

tools.name: marketing_design_export_mp4
tools.description: Render an animated design (per-layer keyframes) to MP4 or GIF via the Remotion render worker (synchronous — polls up to ~240s). Send the full Fabric.js canvas_json plus width/height and duration_seconds; the canvas must contain at least one layer.

tools.name: marketing_design_get
tools.description: Get one Creative Studio design project by ID — returns the full Fabric.js canvasData, artboard settings, metadata, and a dashboardUrl for the user to open it in the editor.

tools.name: marketing_design_list
tools.description: List Creative Studio design projects (design_projects) with title, type, status, featured image, and preview video URL. Filter by design_type and status.

tools.name: marketing_form_conversion_audit
tools.description: Answer 'the platform says 40 conversions, the CRM shows 22 — where did the other 18 go?' for FORM fills. Returns submissions with their source attribution (UTMs, click ids, channel, landing page), aggregated the way a platform aggregates (source/medium/campaign, and by day in the ad-account timezone), plus named discrepancy buckets that SUM TO THE TOTAL: deleted, duplicate, spam, archived, workflow_failed, no_attribution, unpaid_attribution, counted. Use buckets.counted as OUR number and explain the gap with the rest — '40 vs 22, and here are 11 spam, 4 duplicates, 3 with no UTMs' answers the question; a bare number does not. Unlike the dashboard Forms tab this INCLUDES spam, deleted and duplicate rows and labels them, because they ARE the answer. has_click_id isolates submissions tied to a paid click, recovered from utm_params OR the landing-page URL — which catches real paid clicks the CRM recorded as organic. Defaults to the last 30 days, UTC days, and NO field data. ALWAYS read the caveats in the response before reporting a discrepancy: this is OUR record, not the platform's record of a conversion, and the two legitimately differ — view-through conversions have no click and can never appear here, cross-device joins are invisible to us, the platform dates by CLICK while we date by the event, and the platform also counts conversions that are not this type at all. CLICK TIMING splits into what is KNOWN and what is guessed — read `click_window` before quoting either. `click_window.click_dated` is how many counted rows carry the REAL click instant (embed v3.4+). Of those, `clicks_before_range` provably clicked before the range, so the platform credited them to an EARLIER period — that is a FINDING explaining part of the gap, not a hedge. `boundary_risk` covers only rows with no dated click. A row is never in both. CRITICAL: if `click_dated` is 0, then `clicks_before_range: 0` means NOT MEASURABLE, not zero — never report it as 'no clicks fell outside the window'. Each submission also carries `attribution.first_touch_at` with `click_time_is_exact`; only an exact one dates a click, the rest merely bound it. Compare against ppc_campaign_metrics.conversions or a conversion action's total.

tools.name: marketing_frequency_cap_get
tools.description: The 7-day rolling per-contact send cap. Recipients already emailed this many times in the last week are SILENTLY SKIPPED at dispatch (skipped_frequency_cap) — this is usually why a send under-delivers. 0 = unlimited.

tools.name: marketing_frequency_cap_set
tools.description: Set the 7-day rolling per-contact send cap (0 = unlimited). Useful as a blast-radius limiter while testing.

tools.name: marketing_funnel_appearance_get
tools.description: Read one review funnel's fully resolved look and feel, what each field falls back to, and whether anything is actually overridden. Returns appearance (logo_url, primary_color, background, background_color, background_image_url, surface_color, text_color, muted_text_color, corners, layout, font_heading, font_body, headline, subhead, show_attribution), inherited_from_brand (the brand-guide value behind primary_color, text_color, background_color, logo_url, font_heading, font_body, plus logo_url_source 'brand_guide' | 'account' | null), is_inherited, share_url, status, font_choices, contrast_ratio, rating_style and rating_styles. CALL THIS BEFORE marketing_funnel_appearance_update: that write REPLACES the whole appearance object rather than merging, so this response is the base you must edit and send back. appearance is the account brand guide (with accounts.logo_url as the logo backstop) merged UNDER the funnel's own overrides, so most fields are values nobody chose for this funnel; is_inherited true means surveys.settings.appearance does not exist at all and a reset would be a no-op. contrast_ratio is the WCAG ratio of the auto-picked black-or-white button label against primary_color ONLY, rounded to one decimal; it says nothing about text_color on background_color, and below 4.5 those buttons are unreadable. Nothing enforces it, so a funnel can already be live and failing. share_url is RELATIVE ('/s/' + share_token) and is a PUBLIC capability link: anyone holding it can submit to this funnel, and that page 404s unless status is 'active'. survey_get returns the same link absolute, so the two tools disagree on the string by design. rating_style is null when the funnel's first scoring step is not a star step (an nps, csat or scale step, or no scoring step at all), which is also exactly the case where the update tool silently ignores rating_style. Find funnel_id with survey_list, which returns review funnels as type 'review' alongside nps and csat surveys. 400 invalid_id for a non-UUID, 404 for an id outside the calling account or for a survey that is not type 'review'.

tools.name: marketing_funnel_appearance_update
tools.description: Restyles a LIVE PUBLIC PAGE: no draft, no preview, no publish step, so what this writes is what a visitor on /s/<share_token> sees next. It spends no money and queues no job. Returns { ok, appearance (sanitised, as stored), rating_style }, plus contrast_ratio on every path EXCEPT reset:true. THE TRAP: appearance is a WHOLE-OBJECT REPLACE, not a merge. Every key you OMIT silently reverts to the brand value or the product default instead of keeping what was stored, so read marketing_funnel_appearance_get first and send its appearance back edited. SILENT SUBSTITUTION: nothing invalid is rejected. A colour that is not #rgb or #rrggbb, a font outside font_choices and a url that is not http(s) all fall back with no error, and headline/subhead are trimmed to 200/400 chars; compare the returned appearance against what you sent. show_attribution:false strips 'Powered by Hiveku' from that public page; documented as a higher-plan unlock but NO plan gate exists here, so it works on any account. reset:true DELETES the override so the funnel follows the brand guide again including future edits; it ignores any appearance sent with it and does not reset rating_style, though a rating_style in the same body is still applied. rating_style is NOT part of appearance: it writes survey_questions.config.display and changes what the funnel ASKS. SILENT NO-OP: it applies only when the funnel's first scoring step is a 'star' step, so on an nps, csat or scale funnel it is accepted, ignored and answered ok:true with rating_style null. LOSSY: 'faces' and 'thumbs' force star_count to 5 and switching back to 'stars' does not restore a 10-star scale. An unrecognised value is a 422 naming the allowed set; a body naming none of reset, appearance or rating_style is a 422 nothing_to_update. surveys.settings is read-modify-written WHOLE, so a concurrent survey_update landing between this read and write is lost. Archived funnels are NOT excluded and can still be restyled. 400 invalid_id for a non-UUID; 404 outside the account or for a survey that is not type 'review'.

tools.name: marketing_generate_video
tools.description: Generate a short AI video clip (~10s, 720p, Gemini Omni Flash) from a text prompt — for social posts, Reels/Shorts, and ad creative. Optionally image-to-video via reference_image_url or reference_media_asset_id (a Media Library image; pair with generate_image for a still → "animate this" flow). The clip is auto-registered in the Media Library (tags ai_generated + creative-studio) and the returned asset_id attaches straight to posts via media_asset_ids. COST + LIMITS — treat clips as expensive: each generation is PAID (~$1 per clip), Premium-plan only, capped at 20 clips/account/month, and platform capacity is limited (429 video_quota_exhausted = try again after the overnight reset). ALWAYS call with dry_run:true FIRST to check {allowed, used, limit} before promising a video, prefer reusing existing assets (marketing_media_list), and NEVER retry a generation that succeeded. Brand-aware by default (the account brand guide is appended to the model prompt; use_brand:false to opt out). aspect_ratio: 9:16 (default, Stories/Reels/TikTok) or 16:9 (YouTube/X/LinkedIn). Platform duration ceilings still apply at post time (X 140s, Reels 90s, Shorts 60s). Errors: 402 plan_upgrade_required | monthly_cap_reached (with used/limit), 429 video_quota_exhausted, 501 video_generation_not_configured, 504 timeout. Generation takes ~30-90s — this call blocks until done.

tools.name: marketing_knowledge_bases_list
tools.description: List marketing-specific knowledge bases (separate from general kb_*).

tools.name: marketing_knowledge_bases_search
tools.description: Semantic search across marketing knowledge bases.

tools.name: marketing_mailing_address_get
tools.description: The account's physical postal address + `can_spam_complete`. CAN-SPAM requires a real mailing address in every marketing email; footer validation FAILS without one, so no campaign can send until this is set.

tools.name: marketing_mailing_address_set
tools.description: Set the account's physical postal address (CAN-SPAM). ALL of address, city, state, zip_code, country must be present or every send is refused at footer validation. Confirm the address with the owner — it appears in the footer of every marketing email they send.

tools.name: marketing_media_folders
tools.description: List folders in the marketing Media Library (media_assets folders) with asset and child-folder counts. Pass parent_id="root" for top-level folders. NOT related to website builder-project assets_* paths.

tools.name: marketing_media_get
tools.description: Get one marketing Media Library asset (media_assets) by ID, including its folder, collections, and recent usage tracking. This is the media library used by social posts and designs — NOT the website builder-project assets_* tools (use assets_info for project files).

tools.name: marketing_media_list
tools.description: List assets in the marketing Media Library (media_assets) — the account-level library that social posts and designs pull images/videos from. NOT the website builder-project assets_* tools (those are per-project files on S3); for website project files use assets_list/assets_upload. Filters: folder_id ("root" for top level), media_type, tags (comma-separated), search (title/filename), ai_generated, collection_id. Paginated.

tools.name: marketing_media_register_external_url
tools.description: Register an existing http(s) URL as a marketing Media Library asset (media_assets) without uploading bytes — for AI-generated S3 URLs, CDN/stock URLs, or bulk imports. This is the library social posts and designs use — NOT the website builder-project assets_* tools. media_type and mime_type are inferred from the URL extension when omitted; title falls back to the filename in the URL.

tools.name: marketing_media_upload_base64
tools.description: Upload a file (base64 bytes, max 50MB) into the marketing Media Library (media_assets) — S3-backed, account-level, used by social posts and designs. NOT the website builder-project asset store; to ship an image into a website project use assets_upload instead. mime_type is inferred from the file extension when omitted; a data: URI prefix on content is stripped automatically.

tools.name: marketing_qr_style_get
tools.description: Read the account-wide QR appearance that every reputation surface draws with. Returns style (the stored values merged over the defaults, i.e. the thing to draw), defaults, stored (ONLY the fields this account has actually chosen, so a client can label a field 'inherited' instead of inferring it from equality), warnings, and account_logo_url (accounts.logo_url, so logo_mode 'account' can be previewed without a second call). warnings is the half an agent can act on and is reachable no other way: inverted_colors, low_contrast_margin (under 7:1), large_logo (a logo over 0.25 of the width), detached_modules. Reading is deliberately TOLERANT and never fails on a bad row: each invalid stored value falls back to its own default silently, so a value in style may be a fallback rather than what is on the row, and stored is the field that tells the two apart. A colour pair below the 3:1 write floor can therefore sit here quietly while it blocks every write (see marketing_qr_style_update). SETTINGS ONLY: there is no server-side QR renderer anywhere in the product, so no tool can render, download or eyeball a QR image; the code only exists once a human opens the funnel QR studio in a browser. Takes no arguments, costs nothing, two point reads.

tools.name: marketing_qr_style_update
tools.description: Merge a partial QR style into the account's reputation settings. Returns ok, style (the full merged result), defaults, stored, warnings and dropped; it does NOT return account_logo_url, unlike marketing_qr_style_get. SETS STYLE ONLY: there is no server-side QR renderer, so this cannot produce, preview or verify a QR image - a code is drawn only when a human opens the funnel QR studio in a browser. SILENT PARTIAL WRITE, the trap that bites: any key outside the eight below is DROPPED rather than rejected, and as long as one recognised key is present the call still returns 200 ok:true with the misspelling visible only in dropped, so always read dropped back. (A body whose keys are ALL unrecognised is a 400 no_changes instead, never a 200 that stored nothing.) logo_size is CLAMPED into 0.05 to 0.35 rather than rejected, so 0.9 returns 200 with 0.35 stored; read the echoed style. Every other field errors instead, and a blank-string logo_size is an error rather than zero. Cross-field validation runs on the MERGED RESULT, not on your patch, so a row already under the 3:1 contrast floor, or in logo_mode 'url' with no usable logo_url, rejects EVERY patch with 400 invalid_qr_style - including patches that never mention those fields - until one call carries the fix as well. Account-wide with no per-funnel override: one call restyles the whole fleet, and these values end up printed on counter cards and van doors where a print run cannot be patched. No money, no outbound call, no queued job. Known dead ends today: the studio hydrates the module colour from a 'dot_color' key this API never returns, so dots_color is stored and drawn by nothing, and logo_url is stored but the studio takes its logo from the funnel brand, leaving dot_style, corner_square_style, corner_dot_style, background_color, logo_size and logo_mode as the only fields that currently change what a human sees. Call marketing_qr_style_get first for the current values, what is inherited, and the warnings.

tools.name: marketing_report_create
tools.description: Create a scheduled CLIENT REPORT — the shareable, branded results page the client opens (marketing report: leads, deals won, traffic, spend, SEO, rankings movement, search-term wins, AEO, local, work log; social report: posts, impressions, engagement). Returns the row including its public_token: marketing reports are PUBLIC BY DEFAULT (the share link is the point) and next_scheduled_at is stamped so the scheduler cron actually delivers on cadence. delivery_config.recipients (email addresses) is who marketing_report_send emails. After creating, call marketing_report_regenerate to populate the numbers, then marketing_report_share_link for the URL.

tools.name: marketing_report_pdf
tools.description: Download a client MARKETING report as a PDF, rendered server-side from the STORED last_report_data blob — the exact numbers the public share page and the report email show (marketing_report_regenerate is the only way they change). Returns { filename, content_type, size_bytes, generated_at, data_base64 } — decode data_base64 to get the PDF bytes. 409 when the report has never been generated: call marketing_report_regenerate first, then retry. Social reports are not supported (400) — share their public link instead. A plain browser GET on the same route (no format param) streams raw application/pdf with a download filename.

tools.name: marketing_report_regenerate
tools.description: Rebuild the report's numbers NOW and store them (last_report_data) — the public page and the emailed summary render this stored blob verbatim, so regenerate is the only way numbers change. Does NOT email anyone and does NOT advance the schedule (the cron owns cadence). Marketing reports accept days: 7 or 30 (window). Can take a while: the marketing assembly includes live Google Ads pulls (search terms, change history). Run this after create and before send/share.

tools.name: marketing_report_send
tools.description: Email the report to its recipients — REAL MAIL LANDS IN THE CLIENT'S INBOX, so this is confirm-gated. First call WITHOUT confirm: you get a preview (report title + the exact recipient list + the public URL that will be mailed) — show it to the user. Re-call with confirm: true (strict boolean) to actually send. Marketing reports email the CURRENT stored numbers (regenerate first if stale) and require an existing public link. Pass recipients to replace delivery_config.recipients before sending. Never advances the cron schedule.

tools.name: marketing_report_share_link
tools.description: Fetch the report's public share URL (/public/marketing-report/[token] or /public/social-report/[token]) — the link the client opens, no login required. Returns url: null with a fix-it note when the report is not public (use marketing_report_update with is_public: true to mint the link). Read-only; never mints.

tools.name: marketing_report_update
tools.description: Update a client report's config: rename, change cadence (schedule change re-stamps next_scheduled_at so the cron stays in sync), section list, recipients (delivery_config), active flag, or the share link. is_public: true mints a public_token when the row has none; is_public: false on a marketing report REVOKES the link outright (social keeps its token so re-enabling restores the same URL).

tools.name: marketing_setup_status
tools.description: RUN THIS FIRST, before building anything. One call listing every condition that SILENTLY blocks a MARKETING CAMPAIGN send: marketing enabled, not paused, not suspended, SES tenant provisioned, a VERIFIED sending domain, and the CAN-SPAM mailing address. Returns ready_to_send + blockers[], with a `fix` on each FAILING check (passing checks carry no fix text). Skipping it is how agents build a perfect campaign and then discover it can never send. Scope: campaign and sequence dispatch through the account's SES tenant. It is NOT the transactional lane, which email_service_status reports as sending_enabled (hk_ API keys, smtp.hiveku.com, /api/v1/email/send). The two are provisioned independently, so ready_to_send: false here with sending_enabled: true there is normal and both are correct. The only shared gate is not_suspended, read from the same predicate in both, so a suspension shows up as false on both sides.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_create
tools.description: Draft a storyboard for a multi-scene marketing video and park it awaiting the user's approval. Use this instead of one-off marketing_generate_video whenever the ask is "make me a video" (Reel/TikTok/promo/explainer/testimonial/listing tour), not just one clip. FREE AND FAST — it validates, prices, and stores; NOTHING is reserved, billed, or enqueued until a human approves. Pass EXACTLY ONE of: `storyboard` (a full hiveku.storyboard.v1 document you authored) OR `template_id` (a genre template the builder renders server-side: social-short, product-promo, explainer, testimonial, listing-tour, event-promo). With a template, fill `substitutions` ({slot: value}); optionally set style_id (clean-professional, bold-social, premium-minimal, warm-documentary), profile_id (tiktok, instagram_reels, youtube_shorts, youtube_landscape, linkedin_feed, linkedin_square, website_hero), voice_id (a Cartesia voice UUID), music (generate|stock|none), and model (auto|kling-2.5-turbo|veo-3.1-fast|veo-3.1-lite|omni-flash). A hand-authored `storyboard` may carry the look fields inline: board-level style_id, transition (none|fade|slide-left|slide-up), transition_ms, brand, captions.style, and per-scene camera. There is no `look` block on create — nothing to patch yet; to restyle a template-built board, create it and then call marketing_storyboard_set_look. On a validation failure the response carries validation.errors naming the exact bad field per scene — fix those with marketing_storyboard_update. THE AGENT CANNOT APPROVE: after creating, submit for approval and stop.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_delete
tools.description: Delete a storyboard that never ran. IRREVERSIBLE. For cleaning up a board the user rejected or a duplicate created by mistake — in practice only two boards delete: one still in draft/awaiting_approval that was never approved, and a canceled/failed one that never reserved a clip. THIS IS NOT HOW YOU STOP A RUN — marketing_video_pipeline_cancel is. An approved or mid-run board returns 409 pipeline_running: cancel it first (that releases its reserved clips), then delete. A board that generated anything returns 409 pipeline_has_render_jobs — those render jobs carry the billing record and the platform keeps them on purpose, so that board is permanent. Neither refusal is something to work around; a 404 usually means it was already deleted.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_get
tools.description: Read one storyboard/pipeline row: status, the document, per-scene generation state, and the final result when ready. Same row and snapshot as marketing_video_pipeline_status — the storyboard artifact and the run record are one row.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_set_look
tools.description: Change a storyboard's LOOK by name — style, brand, captions, transition, music, per-scene camera — WITHOUT resending the document. PREFER THIS over marketing_storyboard_update for any appearance change: a full replace makes you restate every field you are not changing, and a field you forget is a field you silently delete. IT IS NOT A LIGHTER-WEIGHT WRITE. It bumps the storyboard version, recomputes the checksum, and CLEARS EVERY APPROVAL STAMP exactly like a full replace — a one-colour change re-drafts an approved board and the user must approve again. That is the gate working. Only a draft/awaiting_approval board is editable (else 409 pipeline_already_started). The agent still cannot approve. submit defaults true — the revision goes straight back to awaiting_approval so the user sees the re-priced card; pass submit=false only to park a draft you are not ready to show. Every `look` key is optional: absent = leave alone, a value = set, and null = DELETE that field ON THE KEYS THAT ACCEPT NULL. Null is NOT universal — three fields are required on the board and reject null with a 400: `captions.enabled`, `music.mode`, and `scenes[].on_screen_text` (clear on-screen text with the empty string "", which is its no-text value). Unknown keys are REJECTED (400 invalid_look), not ignored, so a misspelled knob is reported instead of silently doing nothing. - style_id: clean-professional | bold-social | premium-minimal | warm-documentary | null. Applied FIRST, so an explicit knob in the same call overrides the playbook for that field. - brand: {primary_color, accent_color, font_family, logo_url, inherit_account_brand} with #rrggbb colours, or null to remove the block. PRECEDENCE, PER FIELD: (1) inherit_account_brand=false means the account brand guide is not read at all, for any field; (2) a field set here always wins; (3) a field left unset is filled from the account brand guide at compile time. Set ONLY the field being overridden — restating the account's own colours freezes them and the board stops following the brand guide when it changes. - captions: {enabled (required on the board, no null form), style|null merged key-by-key}. Style keys: emphasis (bold|medium|light), placement (lower-third|centered|upper-third), highlight (fill|scale|underline|none), uppercase, font_family, font_weight 100-900, font_scale 0.02-0.12, position (top|center|bottom), fill/color, accent/highlight_fill, stroke (#rrggbb), stroke_width 0-20. Renderer keys (font_weight/position/fill) win over playbook keys (emphasis/placement). - transition: {kind: none|fade|slide-left|slide-up|null, transition_ms: 0-2000|null}. "none" forces 0ms. - music: {mode: generate|stock|none (required on the board, no null form), brief, stock_track_id, duck_under_vo_db -60..0}. - scenes: [{id, camera, transition_out, on_screen_text}], max 20, matched BY SCENE ID and never by index — an unknown id is a 400 listing the ids that DO exist. on_screen_text is a string up to 500 chars with NO null form: pass "" to clear it. camera = {zoom_from 1-3, zoom_to 1-3, pan_x_pct -50..50, pan_y_pct -50..50, origin: center|top|bottom|left|right|top-left|top-right|bottom-left|bottom-right}; setting it opts that scene OUT of the automatic move entirely (omitted axes become no-move, so a lone zoom_from is a hold at that scale), and camera=null restores the automatic move. A non-zero pan requires zoom headroom (max zoom > 1) or it is a 400. House-safe motion is a 0.08-0.20 zoom delta; keep |pan_pct| under (max_zoom - 1) x 50 or the frame slides past its own edge.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_submit_for_approval
tools.description: Put the storyboard's approval card in front of the user — THE HAND-OFF, then STOP. It parks the board in awaiting_approval and surfaces the approval card (storyboard table, pre-viz, itemized cost). THE AGENT CANNOT APPROVE OR START THE RUN — only a signed-in human clicking Approve does. After this, tell the user what was built (scenes, runtime, estimated cost), ask them to review and approve, and end the turn. Do NOT then generate scenes one at a time to work around the gate.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_update
tools.description: Replace a storyboard's document (PRE-APPROVAL ONLY) and re-validate. A FULL REPLACE — whatever the document omits is gone; use it when the SCENES change (add/remove/reorder a scene, rewrite a prompt, vo_line, or duration). For an appearance change (style, brand, captions, transition, music, a scene's camera or on-screen text) use marketing_storyboard_set_look instead, which edits by name so a field you did not restate cannot be silently dropped. ANY edit VOIDS a prior approval and re-prices — that is the checksum gate working; the user must approve again after a change. submit defaults true (send it back to awaiting_approval); pass submit=false to park a draft. A 409 pipeline_already_started means it is past approval and can no longer be edited (cancel and re-create, or retry a failed scene). The agent still cannot approve.

tools.name: marketing_template_archive
tools.description: Archive a marketing template (soft — campaigns keep their reference; never hard-deleted).

tools.name: marketing_template_create
tools.description: Create a template a CAMPAIGN can use (marketing_template). Author it EITHER way: 1. `layout_json` — the visual builder's block tree. Compiled to HTML/text server-side via MJML, so the template stays EDITABLE in the Hiveku visual builder afterwards. Prefer this. Shape: { version: 1, styles: {...}, blocks: [ { type, ...props } ] }. Block types: heading | text | image | button | divider | spacer | hero | social | columns | footer | quote | card | list | stats. 2. `compiled_html` (+ optional `compiled_text`) — paste-in raw HTML. Faster, but NOT editable in the visual builder. The body MUST carry an unsubscribe link and the account's physical address to pass CAN-SPAM footer validation at send time ({{unsubscribe_link}} is substituted per-recipient). Run marketing_setup_status first if unsure. ⚠️ Do NOT use email_template_create for campaigns — that writes the TRANSACTIONAL template store (/api/v1 send API) and a campaign cannot reference it.

tools.name: marketing_template_get
tools.description: Fetch one marketing template, including its layout_json block tree and compiled HTML/text.

tools.name: marketing_template_list
tools.description: List MARKETING templates — the ones a campaign's template_id can reference, and what the Templates tab shows. NOT the same store as email_template_list (that's transactional templates for the /api/v1 send API, which a campaign cannot use).

tools.name: marketing_template_update
tools.description: Update a marketing template. Passing layout_json recompiles the HTML/text from the block tree; passing compiled_html/compiled_text alone edits the raw body without touching the tree.

tools.name: marketing_testimonial_media_replace
tools.description: OUTWARD FACING AND IRREVERSIBLE. On success the new video is live on every public Hiveku surface (widgets, testimonial galleries, share pages) instantly: there is no staging step and no undo in this call. It promotes a COMPLETED Creative Studio MP4 render to be an APPROVED testimonial's published video by server-side copying the whole file (can be ~100 MB) to a new public immutable key and then repointing the row. Get render_job_id from design_export_mp4 (its jobId) and confirm the job reads status completed with design_render_job_get BEFORE calling: a job that is unfinished, is a still image, is not an .mp4, or belongs to another account is render_job_invalid (400). Returns { ok, public_video_url, quote_needs_re_review, cms, note }. quote_needs_re_review true means the published quote was lifted from an AI snippet of the OLD recording, so a trim may have cut the exact words the quote claims were said; the row is stamped body_source snippet_stale and a human must re-check it. That is an FTC 16 CFR Part 255 exposure, so report the flag to the operator and never swallow it. SILENT FAILURE on the site half: cms is null when the row has no CMS projection, and even cms.ok true can mean the site never got the new video - cms.reason unchanged, or videoUrl listed in cms.droppedFields, means the target collection does not declare the video field. A clean site write is still NOT live: the customer's site keeps serving the old video until a deploy runs. COSTS every call: the S3 copy, one more public object that nothing ever cleans up (the old keys are only parked in import_meta.replaced_media for a future sweep), and a fresh Deepgram transcription plus AI snippet, sentiment and topic regeneration. NOT IDEMPOTENT: a second call with the same render_job_id mints a second live key and a second transcription. Approved media testimonials only - text is not_media (400), pending or rejected is not_approved (409), withdrawn consent is revoked (409), and state_changed (409) means a takedown landed during the copy and nothing was replaced; none of those are retryable. Right after success the transcript, ai_snippets, ai_sentiment and ai_topics fields read empty, poster_url is null and processing_status is back to submitted - that is the deliberate reset, not a second bug to chase.

tools.name: marketing_testimonial_widget_archive
tools.description: Take one testimonial proof widget off the air. This is a SOFT ARCHIVE: it writes status 'archived' on the reputation_widgets row and destroys nothing - the row, its configuration and its public_token all survive, and marketing_testimonial_widget_update with status 'active' republishes at the SAME token. Never report it as a deletion or as unrecoverable; there is no hard delete for a widget on this API. Returns { ok: true, archived: true, widget } with the archived row. OUTWARD-FACING and immediate: the iframe /embed/testimonials/<token> and the hosted wall /t/<token> stop serving the moment this returns (a not-available notice and a 404 respectively), so anything embedded on a third-party page goes blank - confirm with the operator before archiving a widget that is live. The JSON feed /api/public/testimonials/wall/<token> is edge-cached (s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=60) and can keep answering with content for up to about six minutes; calling this again does not speed that up, since it is idempotent and an already-archived widget still answers ok. FAILURES: 400 invalid_id on a non-UUID; 404 not_found means no such widget IN THIS ACCOUNT, covering both not-yours and does-not-exist, and never that it was already deleted. Costs nothing: one UPDATE, no money, no outbound call, no queued job.

tools.name: marketing_testimonial_widget_create
tools.description: Creates one embeddable testimonial gallery and returns { widget }: the new row including its freshly minted public_token (24 random bytes as hex, permanent, and the entire embed snippet). IT PUBLISHES NOTHING. status is always 'draft' and all three public readers require 'active', so the widget serves nothing anywhere until a separate PATCH to /api/olympus/marketing/reputation/widgets/[id] sets status 'active'. This call is step one of two; telling an operator their gallery is live after it is false. kind is 'wall' when omitted and must be one of wall, grid, carousel, single, badge, popup, collector, otherwise 400 invalid_kind with the allowed list. 'collector' is the leave-a-testimonial launcher rather than a gallery: it needs collector.survey_id pointing at a review funnel in this same account that is active and not archived or the frame shows a not-configured notice, and it renders as a collector only when the frame is opened with ?mode=collector, falling back to a wall on a direct open. name IS PUBLIC COPY, not an internal label: /t/<public_token> renders it as the heading of a deliberately indexable page, so a widget called 'test 3' publishes that heading to search engines. It becomes 'Testimonials' when omitted and is silently TRUNCATED at 120 characters rather than rejected. filters decides whether a live wall is full or nearly empty: filters.include is the source picker over testimonial, google, facebook, yelp, trustpilot, tripadvisor and an absent or empty include means ALL of them; with no filters.min_rating, synced reviews are floored at 4 stars while first-party testimonials have no floor; featured_only true, or a kinds list that omits 'text', excludes every synced review; filters.limit defaults to 30 and is clamped to 1-100; filters.order and filters.languages appear in the schema comment but no reader implements them. style keys that are actually read: accent_color (hex), card_radius (0-32), columns (1-4), show_rating, show_company, show_video, show_avatar, show_date. allowed_origins IS NOT ACCESS CONTROL: it is an anti-leech Referer check enforced only on the iframe page, an absent Referer fails OPEN, the JSON feed ignores it entirely, and an omitted or empty list means embeddable anywhere. filters, style and collector must be JSON objects; a string or an array is silently replaced with {} and still answers 200. No money, no outbound call, no queued job, but there is NO UNDO: the sibling DELETE only archives and public_token can never be rotated, so every call permanently adds a row and permanently burns a token. Do not loop on this to retry.

tools.name: marketing_testimonial_widget_update
tools.description: Reshape one testimonial proof widget (a reputation_widgets row) and, when status is sent, publish or unpublish it. Returns { ok: true, widget }: the FULL row AFTER the write, so the status just set is readable without a second call. OUTWARD-FACING: status 'active' starts serving testimonials and synced platform reviews immediately, with no further confirmation anywhere, on every page already carrying this widget's public_token - the iframe /embed/testimonials/<token>, the search-indexable hosted wall /t/<token>, and the JSON feed /api/public/testimonials/wall/<token>. 'draft' or 'archived' takes it down; the two pages flip at once, but the JSON feed is edge-cached (s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=60) and can keep serving for up to about six minutes, so wait rather than re-flipping. WHOLESALE REPLACEMENT is the trap that empties live walls: filters, style, collector and allowed_origins each overwrite the stored object entirely and are never merged. Read the current row first (GET /api/olympus/marketing/reputation/widgets returns full rows) and send the complete object back - a partial filters silently drops the operator's include source picker, which decides whether the wall shows synced Google reviews as well as first-party testimonials, the difference between a full wall and an empty one on a customer's site.
