An EMPTY allowed_origins means ALLOW EVERYWHERE, not block everything; entries are trimmed and lowercased, and only the iframe page enforces them (a Referer check that fails OPEN on an absent Referer, so it is anti-leech, not access control), so a wrong hostname list turns an already-live embed into a refusal notice. kind and public_token are NOT settable and are ignored without error if sent: rotating the token would break embeds nobody can reach. FAILURES: an empty patch is 400 no_fields and writes nothing; a non-UUID id is 400 invalid_id; an unrecognised status, a name over 120 chars, more than 20 origins, or a non-object filters/style/collector is 422 invalid_body with issues - rejected, never truncated or silently dropped. 404 not_found means no such widget IN THIS ACCOUNT, never that one was deleted. Costs nothing: one UPDATE, no money, no outbound call, no queued job.

tools.name: marketing_testimonial_widgets_list
tools.description: Returns { widgets: [...] }: this account's embeddable testimonial widgets as full reputation_widgets rows (id, name, kind, status, public_token, filters, style, collector, allowed_origins, created_at), newest created_at first. HARD-CAPPED AT 100 with no cursor, no offset and no filter argument of any kind, so widget 101 is invisible here while still serving publicly on customer sites. Never report this list as the account's complete set. Only status 'active' widgets serve anything: 'draft' and 'archived' rows render a not-available page on /embed/testimonials/<public_token> and /t/<public_token> and answer 404 on the public JSON feed, so a row appearing here is not evidence that anything is live. public_token is returned in full and that is correct, because it is the public embed id the snippet carries rather than a credential, but it is also all anyone needs to read /api/public/testimonials/wall/<public_token>, which applies NO origin check at all, so share it exactly as freely as the embed code and no more freely. Read-only: no writes, no money, no queued job. To publish, rename or retarget a widget, PATCH /api/olympus/marketing/reputation/widgets/[id]; that route's DELETE only archives, it destroys nothing.

tools.name: marketing_testimonials_list
tools.description: The testimonial moderation queue for the account, newest first, keyset-paginated. Returns { testimonials, next_before }; each row carries id, kind (video|audio|text), status (pending|approved|rejected|spam|archived), collected_via, rating, headline, body, body_source, author { name, role, company, name_public }, transcript, ai_snippets, ai_sentiment, ai_topics, processing_status, processing_error, media { playable, url, poster_url, mime_type, duration_seconds, width, height, unavailable_reason }, is_public, featured, tags, created_at. This is the ONLY way to obtain a testimonial id: the id feeds the two testimonial tools that take one, over POST /api/olympus/marketing/reputation/testimonials/:id/edit-in-studio (opens a Creative Studio draft of an approved clip) and POST .../:id/replace-media (publishes a rendered clip back over it). NO MEDIA URL FOR ANYTHING UNAPPROVED, EVER. Unlike the moderation UI this tool does not return preview_url (a six-hour AWS presigned GET for the private, unapproved original recording) and never mints a signed poster either, because a presigned string is a bearer capability and a tool response lands in a transcript, a prompt cache and a log line. media.playable is only 'live' or 'none' here, never 'signed'; media.url and media.poster_url are non-null only for an approved, consented, published row. Otherwise unavailable_reason is 'text_only', 'media_deleted' or 'no_permission', and 'no_permission' is PERMANENT on this surface rather than a grant that could be widened, so do not retry, do not treat it as a transient error, and do not go looking for another media URL: there is none to find. Also deliberately absent: author.email (a PRIVATE column that is never projected off the server) and the consent record (consent_granted / consent_at / consent_revoked_at). is_public is the stored derivation of (approved AND consent granted AND not revoked), so is_public plus status fully answers 'may I publish this' without the legal evidence trail. author.name is the display-safe name: a customer who set name_public false reads as 'Sarah K.' here, and that shortened string is what may be published. transcript, body, rating and headline ARE returned for pending rows. That is unreviewed third-party speech about the tenant: summarise it, but do not republish any of it until status is 'approved'. PAGINATION TRAP: next_before is the last row's created_at whenever the page came back full, so an exact-fit final page hands back a cursor that fetches an empty page; stop on an empty testimonials array, not on next_before being null. The cursor is created_at-only with a strict less-than, so any row sharing the exact created_at of a page's last row is SKIPPED. Bad filters fail loudly rather than returning a misleading empty page: an unknown status or kind is a 400 (invalid_status / invalid_kind) listing the allowed values, a non-UUID survey_id is a 400 (invalid_survey_id) instead of a 500, and an unparseable before is a 400 (invalid_before) instead of silently serving page 1 forever. Costs nothing: one indexed Postgres read capped at 100 rows, no S3 request, no outbound call, no spend.

tools.name: marketing_video_pipeline_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a run. Unsubmitted clips release their monthly-cap slots; a clip already generating was already paid for and is left to finalize (its asset is kept — paid work is never discarded). A run that already finished/failed/was canceled returns 409 pipeline_already_terminal.

tools.name: marketing_video_pipeline_retry_scene
tools.description: Re-generate EXACTLY ONE failed clip scene (0-based index from marketing_video_pipeline_status). Only a clip whose latest attempt FAILED can be retried; completed scenes keep their paid-for assets and are never regenerated — the route refuses a retry on a scene that already landed rather than double-billing it. A 402 monthly_cap_reached means the single retry clip will not fit the remaining allowance.

tools.name: marketing_video_pipeline_start
tools.description: Resume an ALREADY-APPROVED run that went idle. This does NOT approve or bypass the gate — approval already starts the run automatically; this is a manual re-kick for the rare stall (a per-minute reconcile cron is the automatic backstop). Against a board the user has not approved it returns 409 storyboard_not_approved, the correct answer — call marketing_storyboard_submit_for_approval and wait for the user.

tools.name: marketing_video_pipeline_status
tools.description: Snapshot an approved run: status, per-scene state (static/pending/reserved/generating/completed/failed), quota pauses (paused_until — the run resumes itself; not a failure), and the final media asset once compositing finishes. Returns immediately — check in, do NOT poll in a tight loop; a full board takes minutes and the platform drives it on its own.

tools.name: marketing_workspace_get
tools.description: Fetch the marketing workspace (active sub-departments, persona configs, dashboards).

tools.name: mc_decision_check
tools.description: Cheap polling endpoint for agents waiting on a HITL decision. Returns a tiny payload — just status, resolved (true if status=done OR decision_answer is set), the structured answer if any, who decided, and a `retry_after_seconds` hint derived from priority (P0=30s, P1=2m, P2=15m, P3=6h). Honor the hint so we don't get hammered. Prefer this over mc_task_get when all you need is 'did the human answer yet?'. Agent workflow: 1. Create card via mc_task_create with decision_options. 2. Loop: call mc_decision_check, if !resolved sleep retry_after_seconds. 3. On resolve: read answer.chosen_key (and answer.text when chosen_key='OTHER') and continue.

tools.name: mc_decision_to_memory
tools.description: Promote a resolved Mission Control card's decision into the account's durable memory. Closes the HITL loop — instead of the answer disappearing into card history, it lives in account_ai_memory where future agents working that account inherit the call. Card must be resolved (decision_answer set); returns 412 with code='not_resolved' otherwise. By default composes a memory entry from card.title + chosen option label + answer.text + decider + date. Supply `summary` to override. Returns the memory_entry_id so callers can link further. The card's meta.memory_links grows with each promotion; a `memory_promoted` event is emitted for the audit trail.

tools.name: mc_decisions_pending
tools.description: Convenience query for digest jobs: returns cards with status='awaiting_human', grouped by priority (P0/P1/P2/P3 buckets). Cheaper than mc_tasks_list + client-side filter; the grouped response shape is ready to feed straight into a digest template.

tools.name: mc_intake_classify
tools.description: Server-side LLM classifier for a Mission Control intake. Given title + body + source, returns suggested {account_slug, type, priority, assignee, estimate_min, reasoning} with a confidence score. Use this standalone to pre-classify a request before deciding whether to call mc_intake_external (or to enrich an existing card via mc_task_update). If you want intake to be atomic-with-classification, just call mc_intake_external with `auto_route_above` set instead of two calls. Model: Sonnet 4.6 via OpenRouter (more conservative about confidence than Haiku, which matters when account_confidence drives auto_route_above). Returns 503 with code='llm_unavailable' if OPENROUTER_API_KEY isn't configured.

tools.name: mc_intake_external
tools.description: Generic external intake — Slack, email, webhook, anything. Creates a card with a source chip and source_ref so the original context is traceable. OPTIONAL LLM AUTO-TRIAGE: pass `auto_route_above` (a confidence threshold 0-1) to call the classifier inline. If the LLM's account_confidence >= threshold, the new card lands in the Doing lane with the suggested priority + assignee applied. Below threshold (or if the classifier fails) it lands in Intake unchanged — the classification still gets stamped in meta so the human sees what the LLM thought during triage. Recommended threshold: 0.8 for auto-routing, 0.0 to always classify-but-keep-in-inbox.

tools.name: mc_lane_create
tools.description: Create a new Kanban column for the account. Name must be unique within the account; conflicts return 409 with code='duplicate_name'. display_order is auto-appended after the current max if omitted.

tools.name: mc_lane_delete
tools.description: Hard-delete a lane. Cards in the lane have their lane_id set to NULL (no card is lost — they appear as 'Uncategorized' on the board). Prefer mc_lane_update { archived: true } if you want the lane label to remain in event history.

tools.name: mc_lane_update
tools.description: Rename, recolor, reorder, or archive a lane. Pass { archived: true } to soft-hide a lane from the default board view (cards in it keep their lane_id; archived lanes appear in the lane editor for un-archiving).

tools.name: mc_lanes_list
tools.description: List the account's Mission Control Kanban columns (lanes), ordered by display_order. Each lane: { id, name, description, color, display_order, archived, counts: { open, in_progress, awaiting_human, awaiting_agent, done } }. First read seeds the default lanes (Intake, Decisions, Discoveries, Doing, Done) if the account has never used Mission Control before. The response also includes `uncategorized_counts` for cards with no lane_id.

tools.name: mc_schedule_create
tools.description: Create a recurring-card schedule. The cron worker ticks the table and fires matches; each fire spawns one card per matching account from the named template. Example: cron='0 9 1 * *', timezone='America/New_York', template_name='ppc.monthly_review', defaults={priority:'P2', assignee:'pi-ppc'} — on the 1st of every month at 9am ET, spawn a P2 'Monthly PPC review' card assigned to pi-ppc using the ppc.monthly_review template. target_account_filter supports: { account_ids: [...] }, { tag: 'cb-google-ads' } (saas-admin only), { all: true }. Per-account olympus path scopes to the schedule's own account.

tools.name: mc_schedule_delete
tools.description: Delete a schedule. Spawned cards are unaffected.

tools.name: mc_schedule_fire
tools.description: Manually fire a schedule now — spawn cards for the matching accounts using its template. The cron worker auto-calls this when the cron matches; use it for backfills, replays, or to verify a new schedule's plan before letting the cron drive it. Dry-run mode previews the plan without spawning. Pass accounts_override to fire against an explicit list of account ids (bypasses target_account_filter — useful when you want to backfill just one account).

tools.name: mc_schedule_get
tools.description: Fetch one schedule by id with its current state (last_fired_at, last_fire_summary).

tools.name: mc_schedule_update
tools.description: Update a schedule. Pass only the fields to change. enabled=false pauses; flipping it back resumes.

tools.name: mc_schedules_list
tools.description: List recurring-card schedules for the account. Each schedule pairs a cron expression with a template_name; the cron worker fires them on cadence and spawns cards for each matching account using mc_template render.

tools.name: mc_sla_breached
tools.description: Cards past their priority-derived SLA. Default SLAs (overridable per call): P0 = 1h (urgent revenue/SLA blocker) P1 = 4h (blocking a cadence) P2 = 24h (can wait a day) P3 = 168h (FYI / weekly) Excludes resolved/archived cards and those snoozed via auto_confirm_until in the future. Response carries age_hours, sla_hours, and over_by_hours per card so digests can render 'P0 alert created 6h ago — 5h over SLA.' Override per call with sla_P0_hours / sla_P1_hours / sla_P2_hours / sla_P3_hours if a tenant runs a different escalation rhythm.

tools.name: mc_task_comment
tools.description: Append a comment to a Mission Control card. Comments are append-only; the conversation between agents and the human stays linear and auditable. Author is free-form (agent slug or user id). THREADING: pass `parent_comment_id` to reply in-thread to a specific prior comment (fetch comments via mc_task_get to find the id). The server validates the parent belongs to this task and refuses 400 with code='parent_not_on_task' otherwise. Omit the field to leave a new top-level comment. The UI indents replies under their parent so an agent's nested back-and-forth with the user reads as a thread instead of an interleaved log.

tools.name: mc_task_comments_list
tools.description: List the comment thread on one Mission Control card, oldest first. Returns every comment with its free-form author, which may be an agent slug or a user id, so do not assume a human wrote any given line. Pair with mc_task_comment to append. The card id must be a UUID or the route 400s before touching the database. A card belonging to another account is a 404, not an empty list, so an empty array genuinely means the card exists on this account and nobody has commented.

tools.name: mc_task_create
tools.description: Create a Mission Control card. Common patterns: • Decision needed: status='awaiting_human', priority='P1', body uses a decision template (what was I doing / where I'm stuck / what I need / options / my recommendation / next steps). • Discovery (FYI, non-blocking): status='open', priority='P3', body describes what was found. • Hand-off to another agent: assignee=<agent slug>, status='awaiting_agent'. lane_id is optional — if omitted, the card lands as uncategorized; the UI surfaces these so the human can route them. Use mc_lanes_list to see the account's columns first if you want to drop into a specific one. Body is free-form markdown; Hiveku doesn't enforce a template, but agents should be consistent within their org so the human always finds the right info in the right place. DECISION OPTIONS: pass `decision_options: [{key, label, description?}]` to give the human structured radio choices. The UI auto-appends an OTHER row so the human can always type a custom answer. When the human submits, the answer is stamped on the card as { chosen_key, text? } — readable via mc_task_get or the cheaper mc_decision_check. The 'OTHER' key is reserved (don't send it as your own option key). Best practice: ≤6 options, short labels, longer description for the trade-off.

tools.name: mc_task_decide
tools.description: Submit a structured decision answer on a Mission Control card. Use this when the agent is the courier for a human's choice — Slack reply parsed into an option, Telegram quick-action, in-chat 'I pick A' reply, an auto_confirm policy firing. Validates chosen_key against the card's decision_options (or accepts 'OTHER' + text). By default transitions to status='done' and stamps decided_by_user_id with the human you're acting as. ACCOUNTABILITY: • Pass acting_as_user_id (a public_users.id from the task's account, NOT a Clerk id) to attribute the decision to a real human. That value becomes decided_by_user_id — identical to a human answering via the Mission Control UI. • Omit acting_as_user_id only for non-human auto-confirms (auto_confirm_until policy firing, scheduled escalation). The card resolves with decided_by_user_id=null; the event log captures the agent slug and notes "agent_relay: true" so audits can see the agent acted unilaterally. CLAIM CONTENTION: if the card is claimed by a user other than acting_as_user_id, returns 409 with code='claim_held_by_other' unless force=true. Forced takeovers are audit-logged in meta. MULTI-STEP DECISIONS: set also_resolve=false to record the answer without flipping to done — useful when the choice unblocks the agent but the larger workflow isn't finished. Auto-posts a comment '✅ Decision: <label>' on the card unless you supply your own via the `comment` field.

tools.name: mc_task_get
tools.description: Fetch one Mission Control card by id with full body, comments timeline, recent events, and the lane it sits in. Use this before mc_task_transition, mc_task_update, or mc_task_comment so you know the current state. COMMENTS shape — each entry: { id, author, body, parent_comment_id, created_at }. parent_comment_id=null is a top-level comment; non-null points to the parent comment in the same task and forms a reply thread. To reply in-thread, pass that id back to mc_task_comment as parent_comment_id. The events array carries claim / decision / status_changed / linked / spawned_pm_task / memory_promoted rows for the audit timeline. Decision audit fields (claim_by, decided_by) are included when set so an agent can see 'human X is on it' or 'human X resolved with answer Y' before acting.

tools.name: mc_task_link_pm
tools.description: Link a Mission Control card to an existing pm_task. The MC card represents the decision/intake; the pm_task is the actual work on the project board. After linking, mc_task_get shows related_account_task_id and pm_task_get_mc_link shows the reverse. Idempotent on the same link — if the card is already linked to that pm_task, returns 200 with was_already_linked: true. If linked to a DIFFERENT pm_task, returns 409 unless { force: true }. force replaces the link and emits both an unlinked and linked event.

tools.name: mc_task_mirror_from_pm
tools.description: Sync the MC card's status from its linked pm_task. Mapping: pm.queued → mc.open pm.in_progress → mc.in_progress pm.qa | pm.ready_for_review | pm.blocked → mc.awaiting_human pm.done → mc.done pm.cancelled → mc.archived Idempotent — if the MC status already matches the derived target, returns no_change: true with no event emitted. Returns 412 if the MC card has no linked pm_task. Use after any pm_task status change to keep the kanban view consistent without per-pm-task-change webhooks.

tools.name: mc_task_spawn_pm
tools.description: One-shot: create a NEW pm_task from a Mission Control card and link them. Use this when you need the MC decision-context PLUS a trackable work item on the project board. Defaults: title and description carry over from the MC card; priority maps P0→urgent, P1→high, P2→medium, P3→low; task_type defaults to 'marketing'; status starts at 'queued'. Override any field via the body. The new pm_task carries an ai_metadata.spawned_from { kind: 'mission_control', mc_task_id } back-reference so a later agent picking up the pm_task can pull the decision context via pm_task_get_mc_link. Refuses with 409 if the MC card is already linked to a pm_task; pass { force: true } to replace.

tools.name: mc_task_transition
tools.description: Ergonomic status push — single call to move a card forward with optional comment. Equivalent to mc_task_update with just { status, comment } but cheaper and clearer. Use this when an agent is reporting 'I picked it up' (open → in_progress), 'I need human input' (in_progress → awaiting_human), or 'I'm done' (* → done). Setting status='done' also stamps resolved_at automatically. IMPORTANT: if the card has decision_options (a structured-choice request) and the human's answer is what's closing it, use mc_task_decide instead — that captures the chosen key + free-form text into decision_answer and stamps decided_by_user_id correctly. Using mc_task_transition(done) on a decision card silently discards the structured-answer slot and leaves polling agents (mc_decision_check) seeing answer: null.

tools.name: mc_task_unlink_pm
tools.description: Clear the pm_task link from a Mission Control card. Idempotent — if the card isn't linked, returns 200 with was_linked: false. The pm_task itself is untouched.

tools.name: mc_task_update
tools.description: Patch a Mission Control card. Send only the fields you want to change — anything omitted is untouched. Changes to status, priority, lane_id, and assignee emit audit events so the digest jobs and UI can render a clean 'what moved today' trail. When to prefer something else: • Simple status push → mc_task_transition (lighter contract, optional comment in one call) • Closing a card with a structured human answer → mc_task_decide (captures decision_answer + decided_by_user_id; this PATCH cannot write either field) • Linking to a PM task → mc_task_link_pm (validates the pm_task exists in the same account) • Claim ownership → /workspaces claim flow (human-only; agents can read claimed_by_user_id but not write it) related_account_task_id IS settable here for back-compat, but mc_task_link_pm gives you validation + audit-event semantics.

tools.name: mc_tasks_aged
tools.description: Find Mission Control cards that have been in a status for too long — the canonical 'what got forgotten' signal. Default behavior: status='awaiting_human' older than 24h. Aging is measured against updated_at so a card that recently got a comment or status nudge doesn't keep flagging. Perfect for the morning digest's 'stalled decisions' section.

tools.name: mc_tasks_list
tools.description: List Mission Control cards for the account. Filterable by status, priority, assignee, lane_id; supports free-text search across title + body. Cards are the universal HITL surface — agents drop decisions / discoveries / hand-offs here so a human sees them in one spot. Status vocabulary is fixed (open | in_progress | awaiting_human | awaiting_agent | done | archived); lanes are the per-account customizable Kanban columns. Use mc_tasks_next instead if you're an autonomous agent polling for work — that endpoint pre-filters to ready-to-work statuses and orders by priority.

tools.name: mc_tasks_next
tools.description: Polling endpoint for autonomous agents — 'what should I work on next?'. Returns up to `limit` cards in priority order that are ready to work (status in open / awaiting_agent / in_progress). Filter by assignee (recommended; otherwise you'll see everything in the account, which is rarely useful). Optional lane filter by name or UUID. Designed for cron-driven pollers running every N minutes — cheap, indexed, no side effects.

tools.name: mc_tasks_stalled
tools.description: Cards with NO activity (events: status changes, comments, claim ops) in N hours. Stricter than mc_tasks_aged — that one measures task.updated_at which gets bumped by any mutation. This one inspects the event log, so a card whose only update was an agent claim counts as stalled if no human has acted since. Returns hours_since_last_event so digests can sort by 'most stale first'. Pair with a status filter for finer queries ('all in_progress cards with no events in 72h').

tools.name: mc_template_create
tools.description: Create a tenant template. Name is lowercase a-z 0-9 with . _ - separators (e.g. 'wct_intake', 'ppc.monthly_review'). Body is markdown with {{var}} markers — variables can be nested ({{account.name}}, {{today}}). If `variables` isn't passed, it's auto-extracted from the {{...}} markers in body. Cannot create platform built-ins from olympus — those are saas-admin-only.

tools.name: mc_template_delete
tools.description: Delete a tenant template. Platform built-ins are untouched. After deletion, mc_templates_get for that name falls back to the built-in if one exists.

tools.name: mc_template_update
tools.description: Update a tenant template. Cannot mutate platform built-ins — use mc_template_create to shadow them with a tenant copy first.

tools.name: mc_templates_get
tools.description: Fetch one template by name. Returns the tenant override if one exists, otherwise the platform built-in.

tools.name: mc_templates_list
tools.description: List Mission Control templates visible to the account. Templates are reusable markdown bodies with {{var}} markers — define a 'wct_intake' or 'decision_required' template once and every card created from it stays consistent. Returns both account-owned templates and platform-wide built-ins; when both define the same name, the tenant version wins (is_tenant_override: true).

tools.name: mc_templates_render
tools.description: Server-side render a template's body with the provided variables. Resolves tenant override > built-in. Lenient by default — missing variables stay as literal {{markers}} in the output and are reported in the `missing` array. Pass strict=true to error on missing. Typical agent flow: render the template, pipe the rendered markdown straight into mc_task_create's body. Saves having to do string formatting in the agent's language.

tools.name: md
tools.description: 🕷️ CRAWL4AI: Generate markdown from web content (Firecrawl-backed)

tools.name: media_ai_enhance_prompt
tools.description: Turns a rough social post idea into one image-generation prompt. Returns { success, enhancedPrompt, originalContext }: enhancedPrompt is 1-2 sentences of plain prose meant to be passed straight to generate_image or generate_image_set, originalContext echoes the first 100 characters of the trimmed postContent so a caller enhancing many posts can match responses to requests. It WRITES NOTHING of its own - no media_assets row, no social post, no CRM change - so whatever you generate from the prompt still has to be registered separately. COSTS MONEY ON EVERY CALL: it runs a full tool-enabled social department agent turn (hydrated with the account's memory, rules and brand voice, minted into turn history and metered against the account's AI spend), so budget a few cents and several seconds to tens of seconds of latency; it returns 504 if the turn passes 120s and 500 'No prompt generated' if the agent streams back an empty string. Brand context is hydrated server side, so account_context_get is not a prerequisite here. SILENT FAILURE: the anti-repetition block (image prompts read from the 30 newest ai_generated social_posts, at most 15 shown to the model) sits in its own try/catch that only logs a warning, so a 200 does NOT prove fatigue avoidance ran and you can get back a near copy of last week's image prompt. Only the first 500 characters of postContent steer the prompt. tone is matched against a fixed table (professional, friendly, witty, inspirational, educational, conversational, bold, empathetic, humorous, authoritative); any other value is accepted with no error and simply drops the tone guidance block, though the raw string is still shown to the model.

tools.name: media_bulk_move
tools.description: Reassign the folder of 1 to 200 media library assets in one filtered updateMany. Returns { result: { success, updatedCount, movedAssets, targetFolderId }, skipped_asset_ids }: movedAssets and updatedCount cover ONLY the ids that belong to this account, and every id you sent that does not is returned in skipped_asset_ids, so a 200 carrying a short updatedCount is a PARTIAL move and skipped_asset_ids is the only field that names what was dropped - always read it. targetFolderId separates a missing key from an explicit null: OMITTING the key is a 400, an explicit null moves the assets to the library root, and a uuid must name a folder in this account or the call 404s having moved nothing. Nothing is written unless the whole input validates: a non-uuid entry, an empty array, or more than 200 ids is a 422, and if none of the ids exist in this account it is a 404. Get a real destination id from media_folders_list first. Cheap and reversible: no money, no queued job, no file is touched, and moving them back undoes it. This is pinned to the move operation and cannot delete; removing an asset is media_delete, one at a time. For a single asset media_update with folder_id is fewer moving parts, but that route does NOT verify the destination folder is yours.

tools.name: media_collection_add_item
tools.description: Add an asset to a collection. Idempotent — duplicate add returns the existing row.

tools.name: media_collection_create
tools.description: Create a collection. cover_asset_id is the thumbnail shown in the UI.

tools.name: media_collection_delete
tools.description: Delete a collection. Cascade-removes membership rows (does NOT delete the underlying assets).

tools.name: media_collection_get
tools.description: Fetch one collection by id with every asset it contains (in sort_order).

tools.name: media_collection_items_list
tools.description: List just the membership rows of one media collection, ordered by sort_order asc. Returns { data: [{ id, sort_order, added_at, asset }], total }. media_collection_get returns the same items plus the collection row and its cover asset, so use that when you also want the collection metadata and this when you only want the contents. The row-level `id` is the MEMBERSHIP row id, NOT the asset id: pass asset.id to media_collection_remove_item or media_library_get, because an item id matches no asset and comes back 'Asset not in collection' 404. The embedded asset is a PARTIAL projection (id, filename, original_filename, file_url, file_size, mime_type, media_type, width, height, title, alt_text, tags, created_at); description, caption, duration, folder_id, source_type, ai_generated and usage_count are absent, so call media_library_get for full metadata rather than concluding those fields are empty. Traps: this route reads no query params at all, so there is no pagination and a large collection returns every row in one payload; and media_collection_add_item writes sort_order 0 by default, so a collection that was never explicitly ordered comes back in arbitrary order despite the orderBy. An unknown collection id, or one owned by another account, returns 404 'Collection not found', which is a different signal from an empty collection: empty is 200 with data: [] and total: 0.

tools.name: media_collection_remove_item
tools.description: Remove an asset from a collection. Doesn't delete the asset itself.

tools.name: media_collection_update
tools.description: Rename a collection / change its cover / toggle is_public. Use add/remove tools for asset membership.

tools.name: media_collections_list
tools.description: List curated media collections (album-style groupings of assets, distinct from folders). Each collection has a cover_asset_id + sort_order. Multiple collections can include the same asset.

tools.name: media_create
tools.description: Register an already-hosted file as a media_assets row. Pure INSERT: uploads no bytes, never touches S3, never fetches file_url. Returns 201 { data: <new asset row> } with file_size coerced from BigInt to a number. Prefer media_library_register_external_url for ordinary imports (only file_url required, media_type inferred); use this to set every column yourself. filename, file_url and media_type are required together, else 400 'filename, file_url, and media_type are required'. Traps: a dead, private or expired file_url persists as a healthy-looking row that renders a broken thumbnail wherever it is later attached; folder_id is NOT checked against the account here (the multipart upload route does check it), so a bogus or foreign folder UUID trips an FK violation the catch swallows into a bare 500 'Failed to create media asset' naming no field; the same opaque 500 is all you get for an out-of-enum media_type or source_type, or a non-integer file_size (BigInt() throws). ai_generated and is_public go through Boolean(), so any non-empty string, including the string 'false', stores as true. file_size 0 is falsy and stores as NULL. No unique index and no dedupe on file_url: calling twice creates two rows. This route also skips the updateMediaStorageUsed call the upload routes make, so the storage meter does not move.

tools.name: media_delete
tools.description: Delete an asset (hard-delete + S3 purge). Refuses with 409 in_use if the asset has any media_usage_tracking rows (i.e. it's referenced by an email, page section, CMS entry, etc.) — pass force=true to delete anyway and accept the orphan. Call media_usage_get first to see exactly what would break.

tools.name: media_folder_create
tools.description: Create a media folder. Optional parent_id makes it a sub-folder. Slug + name unique per (account, parent). description / color / icon are UI hints only.

tools.name: media_folder_delete
tools.description: Delete an empty folder. Refuses with 409 if the folder contains assets or subfolders — move them first via media_update (folder_id) and media_folder_update (parent_id).

tools.name: media_folder_get
tools.description: Fetch one media folder with parent_folder {id, name, folder_path}, child_folders [{id, name, slug, color, icon}] in sort_order, and the derived asset_count + child_folder_count. It returns NO assets: those are counts only, so list the contents with media_library_list(folder_id). Both counts are DIRECT children only, so asset_count 0 does not mean the subtree is empty and is not a safe green light for deletion: DELETE on this same route does NOT refuse a non-empty folder the way the media_folder_delete description claims. It updateMany-unparents every child folder (parent_id null) and every asset (folder_id null) to root, then deletes, so the assets survive but the organisation is gone with no undo and no 409. Unknown id and another account's folder are indistinguishable here: both return 404 'Folder not found'. Note also that a rename through media_folder_update recomputes slug and folder_path on this folder alone, so descendants can report a stale folder_path until they are reparented.

tools.name: media_folder_update
tools.description: Rename / reparent / restyle a folder. Allow-listed fields: name, slug, parent_id, description, color, icon.

tools.name: media_folders_list
tools.description: List media folders with hierarchy + asset count per folder.

tools.name: media_library_get
tools.description: Fetch one media asset by UUID. Returns full metadata + folder + collections + usage_count.

tools.name: media_library_list
tools.description: List media library assets in the account. Filters: media_type (image|video|audio|document|archive|other), tags (comma-separated), folder_id, collection_id, source_type (upload|pexels|ai_generated|import|url), ai_generated, search (free-text against title/filename/alt). Account-scoped; account-wide library shared across all projects.

tools.name: media_library_register_external_url
tools.description: Register a pre-hosted URL (S3, CDN, third-party) as a media_assets row WITHOUT uploading bytes. Useful for: (1) backfilling older generate_image outputs that weren't auto-registered, (2) importing a list of pre-existing image URLs in bulk (cheap INSERT — no round-trip), (3) tracking external CDN assets so they show up in media_library_list / are taggable / searchable. Body: file_url (required), title, source_type (ai_generated|upload|pexels|import|url — default 'url'), media_type (auto-inferred from extension), mime_type (auto-inferred), tags[], description, alt_text, caption, ai_generated, ai_metadata, external_id, width/height/duration if known. Returns the new asset row.

tools.name: media_library_register_external_url_batch
tools.description: Batch variant of media_library_register_external_url — register N pre-hosted URLs as media_assets rows in a single call. Up to 100 per batch; chunk client-side for larger imports. Per-row error handling: one bad URL doesn't fail the whole batch — successful rows come back in `asset_ids[]` and failures in `errors[{index, file_url, error}]`. Same field contract per asset as the solo endpoint: file_url required; title / source_type / media_type / mime_type / tags[] / ai_metadata{} / alt_text / caption / description / ai_generated / external_id / folder_id / width / height / duration / is_public all optional with the same defaults.

tools.name: media_stock_video_search
tools.description: The only stock FOOTAGE search on this surface: free video from Pexels and Pixabay, the picker behind a `stock` storyboard scene. Returns { success, results, providerErrors, licenses: { pexels, pixabay } }. Each result carries id (the provider-prefixed handle, e.g. "pexels:13736675", which is what a storyboard scene stores in stock_video_id), provider, providerVideoId, previewUrl, downloadUrl (the mp4 the render worker fetches), width, height, durationS, attribution, author, pageUrl, license, and sizeBytes when the provider reports it. READ providerErrors ON EVERY CALL. A provider whose API key is unset or whose call failed is listed there, contributes zero rows, and the response is still 200 with success:true, so half a catalogue looks like the whole catalogue. An unrecognised provider value is IGNORED rather than rejected: the search silently widens to both providers, so check the provider field on the rows you actually got. width and height are the storyboard FRAME the footage will fill, not a post-filter, but they do shape the search: they set the orientation hint sent to Pexels and a minimum-dimension floor for Pixabay, they order results by aspect fit, and they pick the mp4 rendition closest to that frame instead of the largest file. The route defaults them to 1080x1920 and caps each at 4096. min_duration and max_duration are SECONDS and are silently dropped unless they parse as positive numbers; min_duration also cannot exclude a clip whose provider reports a duration of 0. per_page defaults to 15, is capped at 50 and floored at 3. A missing or blank query is a 400. Costs nothing: no render job, no monthly clip-cap slot, no database write, and nothing lands in the media library (results are catalogue handles only). It does make one outbound call per provider. For STILLS use stock_photos_search, which searches Unsplash and Pexels over a different route and cannot return video.

tools.name: media_update
tools.description: Update an asset's metadata. Allow-listed: title, alt_text, caption, description, tags (replaces the array), folder_id. Doesn't change the underlying file — use media_delete + media_upload for that.

tools.name: media_upload
tools.description: Upload an image/video/audio/document to the Media Library. Pass file bytes as base64 in `content`. Up to 50MB per upload. mime_type is inferred from file_name extension if omitted. Optional folder_id + tags + title + alt_text + description. Returns the new asset row with its S3 URL. For multiple files in one shot, call this tool repeatedly — each upload is independent (don't batch via this endpoint; the underlying multipart route handles batch uploads from the dashboard UI instead).

tools.name: media_usage_get
tools.description: Return every place an asset is currently used (from media_usage_tracking). Use this BEFORE deleting to know whether orphaning would break live content. Response: { usage_count, usage: [{usage_type, usage_id, usage_context, created_at}] }.

tools.name: memory_bulk_create
tools.description: Batch memory entry creation — one call beats 20 sequential POSTs during new-account onboarding. Pass entries as [{ type|domain, name?, content }, ...]. Either { domain: '_skill:foo', content } or { type: 'skill', name: 'foo', content } per entry. Upfront validation refuses the whole batch on any malformed row (matches per-row 400). Per-row write failures (e.g. duplicate domain) come back in results[] with ok=false; the rest still land. Cap 100 entries per batch.

tools.name: memory_create
tools.description: Create a new memory entry. Use {type, name} (e.g. type="skill", name="discovery-call-prep") OR pass an explicit domain (e.g. "_skill:discovery-call-prep" or "seo"). Returns 409 if the (domain, project_id) pair already exists — use memory_update to modify.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete a memory entry by UUID. The entry is snapshotted into the version history before deletion (changed_by="olympus_agent_delete"), so it remains recoverable via memory_restore_version.

tools.name: memory_get
tools.description: Fetch one memory entry by UUID, including its content, version, and metadata.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List AI agent memory entries. ONE unified surface for skills, rules, commands, agent personas, identity entries, and plain memory documents (e.g. "seo", "branding"). All stored in account_ai_memory; type is inferred from the domain prefix (_skill:, _rule:, _command:, _agent:, _identity:, or no prefix).

tools.name: memory_list_versions
tools.description: List the version history for one memory entry. Each row is a snapshot taken before a PUT or DELETE, with `changed_by` recording the source. Versions persist after the entry is deleted, so this works for recovering deleted entries too.

tools.name: memory_restore_version
tools.description: Restore a memory entry from a specific version snapshot. If the entry still exists, its content is updated. If it was deleted, it is re-inserted with its original UUID. Version number monotonically increments — restore is forward, not backward, preserving a clean audit chain.

tools.name: memory_update
tools.description: Update the content of a memory entry by UUID. The prior content is automatically snapshotted into the version history before being overwritten, so the change is recoverable via memory_restore_version.

tools.name: oauth_app_create
tools.description: Register a per-account OAuth client. Required for any OAuth flow — Hiveku has no platform-shared credentials, every account brings its own client_id + client_secret. Walk the user through obtaining client_id + client_secret from the provider's developer console (Google Cloud Console / Azure AD / Meta for Developers). Required Google Cloud setup BEFORE calling this: 1. Create or pick a Google Cloud project 2. Enable the API for the product (e.g., Search Console API) 3. OAuth consent screen → External, add scopes the product needs, add the user as a test user OR publish 4. Credentials → Create OAuth client ID → Web application → Authorized redirect URI must include https://app.hiveku.com/api/oauth/google/callback 5. Copy the Client ID + Client Secret, pass them to this tool After successful creation, call integration_oauth_initiate with the matching provider_slug; the route will auto-pick this new oauth_app. Verify with integration_test once OAuth completes.

tools.name: oauth_app_delete
tools.description: Hard-delete an OAuth client registration. Existing email_connections / ppc_connections / seo_connections rows that referenced this app will have oauth_app_id set to null and lose their refresh path — those connections must re-run integration_oauth_initiate (which can then fall back to platform-default if available). Use with care; prefer oauth_app_update for rotations.

tools.name: oauth_app_get
tools.description: Fetch one OAuth client registration by id. Returns the same shape as oauth_app_list. client_secret is never returned — to verify the secret is right, run integration_oauth_initiate + finish the consent flow + integration_test.

tools.name: oauth_app_list
tools.description: List the per-account OAuth client registrations this account has created (Google / Microsoft / Meta). Returns each app's id, provider, name, client_id (full + masked preview), products it's enabled for, created_at. The client_secret is never returned. Use this to (a) discover an oauth_app_id to pass to integration_oauth_initiate, (b) audit which OAuth client is wired for a given product, (c) decide whether to oauth_app_create a new one or oauth_app_update an existing.

tools.name: oauth_app_update
tools.description: Update an OAuth client registration. Use to rotate the client_secret after a leak, fix a wrong client_id, add/remove products on an existing app, or rename. Provider cannot be changed (delete + create instead). **Extending products without overwriting:** the common case is "we already have a Google Cloud OAuth Client used for GSC, and we want to use the SAME app for Gmail + Calendar + Meet." Use `add_products: ['crm_email_calendar']` — this MERGES into the existing array without you having to fetch + resend the whole list. Use `products: [...]` only when you intend to replace. After rotating credentials, any existing connections that referenced this app keep working only after the user re-runs integration_oauth_initiate for that provider.

tools.name: on_page_content_parsing
tools.description: This endpoint allows parsing the content on any page you specify and will return the structured content of the target page, including link URLs, anchors, headings, and textual content.

tools.name: on_page_instant_pages
tools.description: Using this function you will get page-specific data with detailed information on how well a particular page is optimized for organic search

tools.name: onboarding_create_pm_task
tools.description: Create a PM task tied to the onboarding (e.g. "Set up E911 addresses", "Connect GHL").

tools.name: onboarding_link_website_project
tools.description: Link an existing website_project to the onboarding (writes to account_onboardings.website_project_id).

tools.name: onboarding_read
tools.description: Read the active onboarding for the account (returns the orchestrator's onboarding state machine snapshot + step summary).

tools.name: onboarding_write_department_memory
tools.description: Seed memory entries for a specific department from onboarding intake (skills, rules, identity).

tools.name: optimize_images
tools.description: Shrink a WEBSITE PROJECT's images so pages load fast — especially on mobile. Full-resolution PNG/JPEG heroes are the #1 cause of slow sites (a 1.8MB blog PNG becomes a ~60KB webp, -97%). Deployed Hiveku sites do NOT run a runtime image optimizer on the native-VCS path, so the ONLY fix is optimizing the source images — this tool does that. What it does per image: resize to a sane max width + re-encode. OPAQUE PNGs are converted to webp (biggest win) — a NEW foo.webp is written, the ORIGINAL foo.png is KEPT, and code references foo.png -> foo.webp are rewritten (so a missed reference still loads the working original — never a broken image). Everything else (JPEGs, truly-transparent PNGs) is recompressed in place with NO reference change. It NEVER rasterizes SVGs, NEVER flattens animated GIFs, preserves real transparency, and never makes a file bigger. ALWAYS call with dry_run:true FIRST (the default). That returns the exact plan — every image, its projected size, and every code reference that would change — and writes NOTHING. Show it to the user, then call again with dry_run:false to apply. Originals are always kept (no deletion). Proactive use: after you add/generate/upload images to a project, run this (dry_run first) to keep the site fast. To target specific files pass `paths`; otherwise it sweeps the biggest images first (bounded per call — re-run if assets_remaining > 0). After applying, deploy_site to ship the smaller assets.

tools.name: outbound_add_sales_asset
tools.description: Add a sales asset (pricing sheet, calendar link, case study, one-pager) the agent can reference when drafting replies.

tools.name: outbound_create_campaign
tools.description: Create a new outbound email campaign with optional sequences

tools.name: outbound_create_lead
tools.description: Add a new lead to an outbound campaign

tools.name: outbound_health_status
tools.description: Outbound system health: readiness score, blockers, warnings, reply-SLA coverage, per-mailbox health. Use for daily briefings and pre-launch checks.

tools.name: outbound_leads_bulk_create
tools.description: Enroll up to 100 leads in an outbound campaign in ONE call (SmartLead batch cap; 400 above it). Replaces looping outbound_create_lead per lead. Emails are deduped case-insensitively within the batch. COUNTS-ONLY contract: SmartLead returns { uploaded, not_uploaded } with no per-lead outcomes, so which specific leads were rejected (duplicates, block list) is unknowable until the next stats sync reconciles the pending_sync placeholder rows — never present per-lead status as known. Local rows are written only after SmartLead accepts; an upstream failure records nothing. settings supports ignore_global_block_list, ignore_unsubscribe_list, ignore_duplicate_leads_in_other_campaign.

tools.name: outbound_list_campaigns
tools.description: List outbound email campaigns with status and search filters

tools.name: outbound_list_inbox
tools.description: List cold-email inbox threads (BDR reply queue). Filter by thread_status (needs_reply, replied, archived, snoozed), sentiment, or campaign.

tools.name: outbound_list_leads
tools.description: List outbound leads with filters for campaign, status, interest, and reply status

tools.name: outbound_list_objections
tools.description: List known objection patterns with counter-responses and success rates. Consult BEFORE drafting replies.

tools.name: outbound_list_reply_drafts
tools.description: List AI-generated reply drafts (pending by default) awaiting BDR review.

tools.name: outbound_list_sales_assets
tools.description: List sales assets available for reply drafting. Returns all statuses unless is_active='true' is passed to exclude retired assets.

tools.name: outbound_list_sequence_learnings
tools.description: List recorded sequence-performance learnings (winners/losers per campaign step).

tools.name: outbound_log_objection
tools.description: Log a prospect objection (and optionally the counter-response used). Duplicate objection text within the same type increments its seen-count instead of creating a new row.

tools.name: outbound_push_lead_to_crm
tools.description: Create or update a CRM contact from an outbound lead, carrying over profile, company, custom fields, tags, and the full email history. Idempotent — safe to re-run; re-pushes append only new emails.

tools.name: outbound_record_sequence_learning
tools.description: Record or refresh a performance-learning snapshot for a campaign sequence step (subject/body, stats, winner/loser verdict, notes). Upserts per (campaign, step, variant).

tools.name: outbound_save_reply_draft
tools.description: Save a drafted reply for an inbox thread as a PENDING draft for BDR review. This does NOT send email — a human approves and sends from the inbox Drafts tab. One pending draft per thread (re-calls return the existing one).

tools.name: outbound_update_lead
tools.description: Update an outbound lead — status, interest flag, internal notes

tools.name: outbound_update_objection
tools.description: Update an objection pattern: refine the counter-response, record an outcome, approve it for drafting use, or bump counters.

tools.name: outbound_update_sales_asset
tools.description: Update a sales asset (edit fields, deactivate, or bump its usage counter after referencing it in a reply).

tools.name: pages_create
tools.description: Create a page. page_type must be one of: page | blog_post | landing_page | contact | about | privacy | terms | custom.

tools.name: pages_delete
tools.description: Delete a page.

tools.name: pages_get
tools.description: Get one page by UUID.

tools.name: pages_list
tools.description: List the project's website pages (nav-tracked).

tools.name: pages_set_homepage
tools.description: Promote a page to be the project homepage. Clears the previous homepage atomically.

tools.name: pages_update
tools.description: Update a page. Only the fields you provide are changed.

tools.name: pdf
tools.description: 🕷️ CRAWL4AI: Extract text from a PDF URL (Firecrawl-backed via parsers:pdf)

tools.name: pm_milestones_close
tools.description: Mark a milestone complete (status=completed, completed_at=now). Convenience over pm_milestones_update.

tools.name: pm_milestones_create
tools.description: Create a milestone on a project.

tools.name: pm_milestones_delete
tools.description: Delete a milestone (does NOT delete tasks attached to it — they stay with milestone_id=null).

tools.name: pm_milestones_get
tools.description: Fetch one milestone.

tools.name: pm_milestones_list
tools.description: List milestones for a project (or across all projects). Filter by status.

tools.name: pm_milestones_update
tools.description: Update a milestone. Auto-sets completed_at when status flips to completed.

tools.name: pm_project_dependency_graph
tools.description: Every dependency link in a PM project plus the READY SET: tasks that are not done, not cancelled, and have zero open blockers. Pass ready_only=true for just that list. Also returns each blocked task's open_blocker_count. IMPORTANT: on a project where nobody has drawn a dependency yet this returns the whole open backlog, so check edge_count before treating the ready set as a scheduling answer.

tools.name: pm_projects_create
tools.description: Create a PM project. project_type one of: app_dev | website | seo | marketing | ppc.

tools.name: pm_projects_delete
tools.description: Delete a PM project (cascades to its tasks, milestones, and sections).

tools.name: pm_projects_get
tools.description: Fetch one PM project by UUID.

tools.name: pm_projects_list
tools.description: List PM projects (project_type filters: app_dev | website | seo | marketing | ppc).

tools.name: pm_projects_update
tools.description: Update a PM project. Only the fields you pass are changed.

tools.name: pm_sections_create
tools.description: Create a task section within a PM project.

tools.name: pm_sections_delete
tools.description: Delete ONE task section from a PM project. Tasks in it are UNASSIGNED (section_id set to null), never deleted, and the response returns tasks_unassigned so the count is reportable. To clear every section on a project, stage pm.section_delete_bulk for human approval instead - that is deliberately not a direct tool.

tools.name: pm_sections_list
tools.description: List task sections (column-like groupings) within a PM project.

tools.name: pm_sections_update
tools.description: Rename, reorder or collapse one task section in a PM project. Tasks in the section are never touched.

tools.name: pm_task_attachment_create
tools.description: Attach a file or link to a PM task. Two modes in one call: FILE upload — pass `file_name` + `content` (base64, max 50MB). mime_type inferred from extension if omitted. Goes to S3 under pm-tasks/<task_id>/... LINK — pass `file_url` (https://...) + optional link_title + link_description. No upload, just records the URL (e.g. Figma mockup, Loom recording, Google Doc). Works on subtasks too (just pass the subtask's id). Use pm_tasks_list / pm_tasks_get to find the task UUID first.

tools.name: pm_task_attachment_delete
tools.description: Remove an attachment from a PM task. For file uploads, also purges the S3 object (best-effort — DB row delete proceeds even if S3 fails). For link-style attachments, just deletes the DB row. Doesn't touch the task itself.

tools.name: pm_task_attachments_list
tools.description: List attachments on a PM task (or subtask — subtasks are pm_tasks with parent_task_id set, same endpoint). Returns id, attachment_type (image|video|audio|document|file|link), filename, file_url, file_size, mime_type, link_title/description, created_at.

tools.name: pm_task_claim
tools.description: Claim a PM task for an agent. Only tasks in status 'todo' or 'queued' can be claimed; anything else returns 409, as does a task another agent already holds. Atomically sets status to in_progress, stamps the agent codename, and mints branch olympus/task-<task_number>.

tools.name: pm_task_comments_list
tools.description: List a PM task's comment thread (oldest first). Each row: content, created_at, and the author as author_name/author_email (humans + review-link guests), agent_codename (agent-authored, null for humans), or user_id. parent_comment_id links threaded replies; attachments is an array of {name, url, type, size}. Companion read for pm_tasks_comment (which only appends). Accepts `id` or `task_id`.

tools.name: pm_task_dependencies_list
tools.description: Both directions of a PM task's dependencies: blocked_by (tasks that must finish first) and blocking (tasks waiting on this one), each with task_number, title, status, is_done and the dependency_id needed to remove the link. Also returns is_blocked_by_dependencies and open_blocker_count for the task itself. NOTE: a task can be blocked by dependencies without having status 'blocked' - the two are separate signals, and this one is computed from the graph rather than stored.

tools.name: pm_task_dependency_create
tools.description: Record that a PM task cannot start until another one is done. Both tasks must be in the SAME project. Only finish_to_start is supported; start_to_start, finish_to_finish and start_to_finish are reserved and rejected, because PM has no gantt or scheduler to act on a date shift. Refuses self-links (400), duplicates (409) and any link that would close a cycle (409). Adding a dependency does NOT change either task's status and does not stop anyone moving the task - dependencies advise.

tools.name: pm_task_dependency_delete
tools.description: Remove ONE dependency link between two PM tasks. Deletes only the link; neither task is modified or deleted. Get dependency_id from pm_task_dependencies_list.

tools.name: pm_task_get_mc_link
tools.description: Reverse lookup: given a pm_task id, return the Mission Control card linked to it (if any). An agent working a pm_task uses this to pull the decision context — the original mc card body usually carries the WHY behind the work, plus the decision_answer if the human picked a structured option. Returns null in mc_task when nothing is linked. Surfaces multiple_linked: true + all_linked[] if (rarely) more than one card points at the same pm_task.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_create
tools.description: Create a recurring PM task template. On every cron match, the materializer spawns a NEW parent pm_task (status='queued') plus a child task for each entry in subtask_templates. Use this when work repeats on a cadence — weekly status reports, monthly billing, daily standup checklists, quarterly reviews. Cron is standard 5-field (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). Examples: '0 9 * * 1' → every Monday 9am (timezone-adjusted) '0 0 1 * *' → 1st of every month at midnight '*/15 * * * *' → every 15 minutes '0 9 * * 1-5' → 9am on weekdays on_overlap='skip' (default) refuses to spawn when a prior occurrence is still open (avoids stacking 'weekly status report' when last week's isn't done). on_overlap='spawn' fires every time regardless — use for monthly invoices where each occurrence is a distinct unit of work. Subtasks are cloned from subtask_templates on each fire — each entry needs at minimum a `title`; description / priority / ai_instructions / estimated_hours / tags / labels are optional and inherit sensible defaults from the parent template when omitted. Max 50 subtasks per recurrence. After creating, the first occurrence fires on the NEXT cron match (could be tomorrow morning). Call pm_task_recurrence_run_now to spawn one immediately for testing.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_delete
tools.description: Delete a recurrence. Spawned tasks REMAIN (their recurrence_id is set to null) — only future cron fires are stopped. Use pm_task_recurrence_pause for a reversible stop.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_get
tools.description: Fetch one PM task recurrence by id.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_list
tools.description: List PM task recurrences for the account. Optionally filter by project_id or active_only=true. Returns each recurrence with its cron, timezone, last_fired_at, total_occurrences, on_overlap policy, and the parent + subtask templates.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_pause
tools.description: Pause a recurrence (is_active=false). Existing spawned tasks keep working; only future cron fires are suppressed. Idempotent — safe to call on an already-paused row.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_resume
tools.description: Resume a paused recurrence (is_active=true). The next cron match fires normally. Does NOT backfill occurrences missed while paused — call pm_task_recurrence_run_now after resume if you want a one-off catch-up. Idempotent.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_run_now
tools.description: Spawn one occurrence right now, off-schedule. Useful for testing a freshly-created recurrence, backfilling a missed fire after a worker outage, or kicking the loop while keeping the regular schedule. Respects on_overlap unless force=true is passed.

tools.name: pm_task_recurrence_update
tools.description: Update a recurrence. Any subset of fields can be patched; subtask_templates fully replaces the array when supplied (pass the complete intended set). Changing `cron` takes effect on the NEXT cron tick — already-fired occurrences are not retroactively rescheduled. Pausing? Prefer pm_task_recurrence_pause for the explicit semantics.

tools.name: pm_task_release
tools.description: Release a PM task an agent can no longer finish. Only 'in_progress' or 'blocked' tasks can be released. Resets status to queued, clears the agent codename and branch name, and zeroes progress.

tools.name: pm_task_submit_for_review
tools.description: Hand finished agent work to QA. Only 'in_progress' or 'qa' tasks are accepted. Sets status to qa, NOT done - use pm_tasks_complete for the human-final done state. It stamps completed_at even though the task is not complete, so judge completion by status and never by completed_at.

tools.name: pm_task_time_log_create
tools.description: Log time against a PM task. Requires EXACTLY ONE of user_id (a member of this account, for a human timesheet entry) or agent_codename (to record work an agent did) - never both, because the row records one actor and attributing agent hours to a person puts them on that person's billable timesheet. MONEY IS IN DOLLARS, not cents: hourly_rate 75 means $75/hr. total_cost is computed server-side. hours_logged is capped at 24. This RECOMPUTES the task's actual_hours as the sum of all its time logs, overwriting any value set directly.

tools.name: pm_task_time_logs_list
tools.description: Time entries logged against a PM task: hours, date, description, billable flag, hourly rate and total cost, plus the rolled-up task_actual_hours and billable/total sums. Each entry says whether a person or an agent logged it. MONEY IS IN DOLLARS, not cents.

tools.name: pm_tasks_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a PM task. Author codename defaults to 'olympus'. Accepts both `id` and `task_id` for the task identifier (older agent docs use task_id); accepts both `content` and `body` for the comment text.

tools.name: pm_tasks_complete
tools.description: Mark a PM task done. Sets status='done', completed_at=now, progress_percentage=100. Optional `summary` adds an audit comment on the task. Use pm_tasks_uncomplete to reverse.

tools.name: pm_tasks_create
tools.description: Create a PM task. task_number auto-increments per project. Field is `title` (NOT `name` — that's pm_projects_create). The route also accepts `name` as a forgiving alias if you forget.

tools.name: pm_tasks_create_bulk
tools.description: Bulk-create PM tasks (up to 500 per call). Each task must include project_id + title (or `name` as alias). task_number is auto-assigned per project. Validates ownership of every project_id before any insert — one bad project_id blocks the whole batch.

tools.name: pm_tasks_delete
tools.description: Delete a PM task.

tools.name: pm_tasks_get
tools.description: Fetch one PM task by UUID. Response `data` includes an `annotations` array (+ `annotation_count`) — the browser annotations reviewers dropped on the live preview, each carrying its SCREENSHOT. Per annotation: { id, annotation_type, priority, annotation_text, page_url, page_title, coordinates, screenshot_url, screenshot_key, screenshot_status, capture_method, viewport_size, created_by_name, created_by_email, created_at, resolved_at }. `screenshot_url` is a directly-fetchable public PNG. `screenshot_status` = ready | capturing | failed | none; "capturing" + null url means the async screenshot is still being generated, re-fetch shortly.

tools.name: pm_tasks_list
tools.description: List PM tasks. Filter by project_id / status / assigned_to_id / parent_task_id (for subtasks) / section_id / milestone_id.

tools.name: pm_tasks_reassign_bulk
tools.description: Reassign many PM tasks at once (single updateMany — fast).

tools.name: pm_tasks_subtasks
tools.description: List subtasks of a parent task. Shorthand for pm_tasks_list with parent_task_id.

tools.name: pm_tasks_uncomplete
tools.description: Reopen a completed task. Clears completed_at, resets status (default 'in_progress'), resets progress_percentage (default 0). Use this instead of pm_tasks_update — the update PATCH allow-list doesn't include completed_at, so it can't fully undo a completion. Optional summary records a reopen comment on the task.

tools.name: pm_tasks_update
tools.description: Update a PM task — only the fields you pass are changed.

tools.name: ppc_account_settings_get
tools.description: Account-level settings — currency, time zone, auto-tagging, conversion-tracking status + id, customer name, manager/test-account flags, tracking_url_template, final_url_suffix. The 'is this account configured correctly?' snapshot. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_ad_group_create
tools.description: Create an ad group inside an existing campaign. Starts ENABLED (campaigns start paused; ad_groups inherit the campaign's effective state). default_bid is the CPC bid for keywords in this ad_group that don't have their own — only matters under Manual/Enhanced CPC. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_ad_group_list
tools.description: List PPC ad groups. Filter by campaign_id / status.

tools.name: ppc_ad_list
tools.description: List PPC ads. Filter by ad_group_id / status.

tools.name: ppc_ads_discover_customers
tools.description: List Google Ads accounts for a connection. Without manager_customer_id: the customers the OAuth user can log in as, each enriched with name + is_manager (agency users typically see MCC manager accounts here — campaigns NEVER live on an MCC, so don't bind one as customer_id). With manager_customer_id: the ENABLED client accounts under that MCC. Requires a developer_token (412 with hint if missing). Bind a direct account with ppc_connection_update {customer_id}; bind an MCC client with {customer_id: '<client id>', manager_id: '<mcc id>'} — manager_id is sent as login-customer-id on every sync call. Status auto-flips to connected.

tools.name: ppc_anomaly_check
tools.description: Compares yesterday's per-campaign cost / clicks / conversions vs the prior 7-day average. Flags any campaign that moved by more than threshold_pct (default 50%) in either direction. Use as a daily 'did anything blow up?' check — catches runaway spend, tracking breakage, sudden traffic drops. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_asset_attach
tools.description: Attach an existing asset to a campaign / ad_group / customer (account-wide). Pass exactly ONE of campaign_id, ad_group_id, or customer_level=true. field_type matches the asset (SITELINK for sitelinks, CALLOUT for callouts, etc.). Returns the link resource_name — capture for asset_detach if needed. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_asset_create
tools.description: Create an Asset (modern extensions API) at account level. Returns the asset's resource_name — use ppc_asset_attach to link to a campaign / ad_group / customer (account-wide). Per asset_type, `asset` shape: • sitelink: {link_text, final_url, description1?, description2?} • callout: {text} • structured_snippet: {header (e.g. 'Brands' / 'Services'), values: [...]} • promotion: {promotion_target, final_url, percent_off? | money_amount_off? | promotion_code?} • call: {country_code, phone_number} • business_name: {business_name} GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_asset_detach
tools.description: Remove an asset-link by its resource_name (returned by ppc_asset_attach). Removes the LINK, not the underlying Asset (it stays in the account library and can be re-attached). Route infers scope from the resource_name shape (campaignAssets / adGroupAssets / customerAssets). GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_auction_insights
tools.description: Auction Insights — who else competes in your auctions. Returns per-competitor-domain impression_share + overlap_rate + outranking_share + position_above_rate. Use to understand competitive pressure and identify domains worth monitoring. For low-impression-volume campaigns the report may be empty (Google requires sufficient volume).

tools.name: ppc_audience_attach
tools.description: Attach an existing audience (user_list / custom_audience / user_interest) to an ad_group as a TARGETING criterion (the audience must match the user for the ad to show). For 'observation' mode (no targeting restriction, just data collection + bid modifier), use ppc_bid_modifier_update with target_type='audience' instead. Optional bid_modifier (1.0 = no change). Audience resource_name is detected by path shape — userLists, customAudiences, or userInterests. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_audience_detach
tools.description: Detach an audience criterion from an ad_group or campaign — the inverse of ppc_audience_attach (Google Ads). Address it either by the exact criterion_resource_name (returned by attach) or by scope (ad_group_id XOR campaign_id) + audience_resource_name, which looks up the live criterion. Deliberately does NOT change the entity's observation/targeting mode: detaching the last audience from a targeting-mode entity makes it serve broadly — decide that explicitly.

tools.name: ppc_audience_ops
tools.description: Unified CRM-audience sync ops across ad platforms (Meta Custom Audiences / Google Customer Match / LinkedIn Matched Audiences / TikTok Custom Audiences — platform inferred from the connection). operation: 'list' (platform audiences [{id, name, size?}]) | 'create' (params.name — creates the platform audience, returns platform_audience_id; structured failures: meta_ca_tos_not_accepted (+tos_url), google_customer_match_not_eligible (+hint), linkedin_dmp_create_forbidden) | 'process-pending' (params.sync_id, optional params.max_batches — drains the audience sync ledger: pending adds/removes upload in platform-sized chunks with per-chunk commits, so re-invoking resumes safely; returns processed_adds/processed_removes/remaining. TikTok removals flip locally only — note 'tiktok_removals_add_only'; TikTok also creates the audience on first flush when the sync row has none) | 'stats' (params.sync_id or params.platform_audience_id — {matched_count} where the platform reports one, else null). | 'delete' (params.sync_id or params.platform_audience_id, optional params.force — removes the PLATFORM audience. REFUSES with audience_has_active_sync while a live CRM sync feeds it, and on Google additionally with audience_attached_to_criteria while live ad group/campaign criteria target it; force=true overrides and disables the orphaned sync rows. Destructive — platform-side deletion is not reversible) | 'update' (params.name and/or params.description — masked rename; LinkedIn/TikTok support name only). Identifier hashes are pre-computed on the sync ledger; never pass raw PII.

tools.name: ppc_audience_performance
tools.description: Performance of audiences attached to ad groups (user lists / in-market / custom intent / demographics). Returns audience_type + audience_ref + per-audience metrics + current bid_modifier. Use to decide: keep & expand bid modifier (high conversions, low CPA), demote (high cost no conversions), or drop entirely. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_bid_modifier_update
tools.description: Set a bid modifier on a device / geo / audience target at the campaign OR ad_group level. bid_modifier = 1.0 means no change; 1.2 = +20%; 0.8 = -20%. target_type one of: • device — target_value MOBILE | DESKTOP | TABLET (campaign-level only) • location — target_value is a geo_target_constant id (e.g. '2840' for United States) (campaign-level only) • audience — target_value is a user_list resource_name (works at both campaign + ad_group) Use after ppc_audience_performance / ppc_segment_report identifies a segment that's converting well (or poorly). GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_bidding_strategy_update
tools.description: Switch a campaign's bidding strategy. Common workflow: after the campaign accumulates ~15+ conversions/month on manual_cpc, switch to target_cpa or target_roas to let Google's ML optimize. Smart-bidding strategies enter a ~7-day LEARNING phase after the switch where performance is unstable — surface that warning to the user. target_cpa / target_roas require their respective numeric targets.

tools.name: ppc_billing_summary
tools.description: Billing-setup snapshot — payments accounts linked, billing status, start/end dates. NOTE: detailed invoice/spend breakdowns aren't in the Ads API; this surfaces what's queryable. For full invoices use the Ads UI Billing section or the separate Cloud Billing API. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_bing_ad_extension_associate
tools.description: Attach existing Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) ad extensions (ids from the create lanes / ppc_bing_ad_extension_list) to a campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). THIS is the step that makes an extension serve. Max 20 per call. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_ad_extension_list
tools.description: READ ad extensions on the Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) account. Default types SitelinkAdExtension + CalloutAdExtension; override with extension_types (comma-separated Microsoft type names). Max 100 per read (Microsoft's cap).

tools.name: ppc_bing_ad_schedule_add
tools.description: Dayparting on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). schedules is an array of {day, from_hour (0-23), to_hour (0-24), from_minute?, to_minute? (0/15/30/45), bid_adjustment_percent?}. WARNING: adding ANY schedule restricts serving to the listed windows — unlisted hours STOP serving. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_audience_associations_list
tools.description: READ every audience attached to one Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id), split targeted vs excluded, with the entity's audience_mode (bid_only vs target_and_bid — the only way to see an entity is serving ONLY to its audiences). Returns the criterion_ids that ppc_bing_audience_criterion_remove takes. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_audience_criterion_add
tools.description: Associate an existing audience (id from ppc_bing_audience_list) with a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id) — bid boost, or exclude=true. Whether targeting restricts reach depends on the entity's target-and-bid mode (Microsoft defaults to bid_only = reach unchanged) — check ppc_bing_audience_associations_list. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_audience_criterion_remove
tools.description: Detach audience criteria (targeted OR excluded) from a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group by criterion_id (from ppc_bing_audience_associations_list; exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). Refuses any id that is not an AUDIENCE criterion — use ppc_bing_criterion_delete for geo/schedule/device/demographic. Removing an exclusion WIDENS reach. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_audience_list
tools.description: READ every audience the Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) account can target (remarketing, in-market, custom, similar, customer lists...) with the audience_type that ppc_bing_audience_criterion_add requires. Audience CREATION/upload is deliberately not exposed (PII policy) — this reads what already exists.

tools.name: ppc_bing_audience_target_setting_set
