tools.description: Switch a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id) between bid_only (Microsoft's default — audiences adjust bids, reach unchanged; the SAFE fix for an accidentally narrowed entity) and target_and_bid (serves ONLY to its targeted audiences — reach collapses to their size). Exclusions are unaffected. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_callout_extension_create
tools.description: Create callout extensions ('Free Estimates', '24/7 Service') on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) account: array of strings <=25 chars, max 20 per call. Created NOT serving — associate via ppc_bing_ad_extension_associate to show them.

tools.name: ppc_bing_conversion_goal_create
tools.description: Create a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) conversion goal against an existing UET tag (tag_id from ppc_bing_uet_tag_list / ppc_bing_uet_tag_create). goal_type: url (needs url_expression + url_operator) | event (needs >=1 of event_category/action/label) | duration (minimum_duration_seconds) | pages_viewed_per_visit (minimum_pages_viewed). goal_category is REQUIRED on url/event goals (purchase, signup, contact, submit_lead_form, book_appointment, request_quote, subscribe, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, get_directions, outbound_click, page_view, other). Created ACTIVE by design — a goal never serves or spends, and a paused goal records nothing; it DOES change what smart bidding optimizes toward. Unblocks conversion-based strategies in ppc_platform_bidding_strategy_update.

tools.name: ppc_bing_conversion_goal_list
tools.description: READ every conversion goal on the Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) account (type, status, tracking status, revenue settings, exclude-from-bidding).

tools.name: ppc_bing_conversion_tracking_status
tools.description: READ the Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) conversion-readiness diagnostic: UET tags + install state, conversion goals + recording state, ready_for_conversion_bidding flag, and a plain-language verdict. Run BEFORE switching any campaign to max_conversions/target_cpa/target_roas.

tools.name: ppc_bing_criterion_delete
tools.description: Remove Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) targeting criterions by id (from ppc_bing_criterions_list; exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id) — the undo for the location/radius/schedule/device/demographic add lanes. The criterion type is resolved by reading the entity first, so a transposed id fails loudly instead of deleting the wrong lane. Max 100 ids. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_criterions_list
tools.description: READ every targeting criterion (location, radius, location intent, ad schedule, device, age, gender) plus audience criterions on ONE Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). Flags has_location_targeting=false — i.e. the entity serves everywhere the account allows. Criterion ids here feed ppc_bing_criterion_delete. Needs prior ppc_sync (ownership mirror).

tools.name: ppc_bing_demographic_criterion_add
tools.description: Age and/or gender bid adjustments on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). age_ranges: 18-24 | 25-34 | 35-49 | 50-64 | 65+ | unknown; genders: male | female | unknown. At least one of the two. There is no exclude flag — Microsoft expresses a demographic exclusion as bid_adjustment_percent=-100. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_device_criterion_set
tools.description: Set the bid adjustment for one device class (computers | smartphones | tablets) on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). bid_adjustment_percent -100..900 is REQUIRED; -100 removes the device class entirely. Updates the auto-created Device criterion in place. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_impression_share_report
tools.description: Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign impression-share report (async; LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-23 with real production rows): impression_share, lost_to_budget, lost_to_rank per campaign, plus summary.scaling_headroom — budget_limited (>=10% lost to budget: raise-budget candidates) and rank_limited (>=20% lost to rank: raise bids / fix quality score) — and impressions-weighted avg_impression_share. days default 30; limit caps returned rows.

tools.name: ppc_bing_keyword_performance
tools.description: READ Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) keywords (id, text, match type, status, bid, editorial status) for one ad group, or for every locally-synced ad group when ad_group_id is omitted (run ppc_bing_pull_ad_groups first in that case). This is where Bing keyword_ids for ppc_platform_keyword_bid_update / ppc_platform_keyword_match_type_change come from — keywords are NOT mirrored locally.

tools.name: ppc_bing_location_criterion_add
tools.description: Target (or exclude=true) Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) location ids (from ppc_bing_location_search) on a campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id). Max 100 ids per call. Optional bid_adjustment_percent -100..900 (not allowed with exclude). Pair with ppc_bing_location_intent_set — Microsoft defaults to in_or_searching, which leaks budget to out-of-area searchers. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_location_intent_set
tools.description: Set a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign/ad group's location-intent (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id): people_in (physically in the area — the usual local-service fix), searching_for, or in_or_searching (Microsoft's leaky default). Updates the auto-created criterion in place. Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_location_search
tools.description: READ. Resolve a place name or postal code ('Dallas', '75201', 'Texas') to Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) location ids for ppc_bing_location_criterion_add. Optional country_code (ISO) and location_types (comma-separated, e.g. 'City,PostalCode') filters.

tools.name: ppc_bing_pull_ad_groups
tools.description: Sync Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) ad groups into the local mirror (ppc_ad_groups) for every synced campaign. Run ppc_sync first so campaigns exist locally. Required before ad_group-scoped ppc_bing_* writes on large accounts — ownership checks read this mirror.

tools.name: ppc_bing_pull_ads
tools.description: Sync Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) ads into the local mirror (ppc_ads) for every synced ad group. Run ppc_sync + ppc_bing_pull_ad_groups first. Ad ids from this mirror feed pause/enable at resource_type=ad.

tools.name: ppc_bing_push_campaign
tools.description: Create a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) Search campaign shell — created PAUSED (never auto-spends) with the given daily budget, EnhancedCpc, all languages. Add ad groups (ppc_platform_ad_group_create), keywords and RSAs, plus location targeting (ppc_bing_location_criterion_add — a fresh shell serves EVERYWHERE the account allows), then enable via ppc_platform_enable_resource. Budget guardrail applies.

tools.name: ppc_bing_quality_score_report
tools.description: Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) keyword quality-score report (async): per-keyword QualityScore with component scores (ExpectedCtr / AdRelevance / LandingPageExperience), plus a low_quality summary (QS <= 5 with the weak components named and spend at risk) and avg_quality_score. days default 30; limit caps returned rows.

tools.name: ppc_bing_radius_criterion_add
tools.description: Target a radius around a lat/lon point on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign or ad group (exactly one of campaign_id OR ad_group_id) — the local-service shape ('20 miles around the shop'). radius_unit miles (max 500) or kilometers (max 800). Needs prior ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_bing_search_terms_report
tools.description: Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) search-terms report (async submit/poll/download; LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-23): per-query impressions/clicks/spend/conversions/ctr/cpc sorted by spend, plus a wasted_spend summary (queries with spend and zero conversions — the negatives-mining feed; add negatives via ppc_platform_negative_keyword_add). days default 30 (1-365); optional campaign_id scopes; limit caps returned rows (summaries always computed over the full report).

tools.name: ppc_bing_shared_negative_list_associate
tools.description: Associate a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) shared negative list with a campaign — from that moment every term on the list stops triggering that campaign's ads. Needs prior ppc_sync (campaign ownership check).

tools.name: ppc_bing_shared_negative_list_create
tools.description: Create a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) shared negative keyword list (name <= 255 chars), optionally seeded with keywords (strings default phrase match, or {text, match_type: exact|phrase|broad}; max 200). A fresh list blocks NOTHING until ppc_bing_shared_negative_list_associate attaches it to a campaign.

tools.name: ppc_bing_shared_negative_list_items_add
tools.description: Add negatives to an existing Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) shared list (shared_list_id from ppc_bing_shared_negative_list_list; keywords as strings or {text, match_type}, max 200). Every campaign already associated with the list starts blocking these terms IMMEDIATELY.

tools.name: ppc_bing_shared_negative_list_list
tools.description: READ the Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) account's shared negative keyword lists (id, name, item count).

tools.name: ppc_bing_sitelink_extension_create
tools.description: Create sitelink extensions on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) account: array of {text (<=25 chars), final_url (http/https), description1?, description2? (<=35 chars)}. Max 20 per call. Created NOT serving — nothing shows until ppc_bing_ad_extension_associate attaches them to a campaign/ad group.

tools.name: ppc_bing_uet_tag_create
tools.description: Create a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) UET tag (name <= 100 chars). A UET tag never serves or spends — it's the measurement snippet. The returned tracking_script must be installed on every page of the client's site before anything records; conversion goals on an uninstalled tag report zero.

tools.name: ppc_bing_uet_tag_list
tools.description: READ every UET tag on the Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) account with its tracking status and snippet. A tag not 'recording' means the site snippet is missing/broken — the #1 reason a Bing account reports zero conversions.

tools.name: ppc_budget_update
tools.description: Set a campaign's daily budget in the account currency. Returns old_daily_budget + new_daily_budget for confirmation. Note: if the budget is a SHARED budget (explicitly_shared=true), the change affects every campaign using it — the response carries an explicit `warning` field and `explicitly_shared` flag. Confirm with the user before applying shared-budget changes. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_bulk_edit
tools.description: Multi-resource STATUS edits in ONE round-trip via the Ads API mutate endpoint (max 100 operations per call). Supported ops: - {mutate_op: 'campaign_status', campaign_id, status: 'ENABLED'|'PAUSED'} - {mutate_op: 'ad_group_status', ad_group_id, status} - {mutate_op: 'keyword_status', ad_group_id, criterion_id, status} Budget changes are NOT allowed here (refused with code budget_op_in_bulk_edit) — use ppc_budget_update per campaign, which enforces the step-cap guardrail. Use bulk_edit for 'pause everything in campaign X' patterns — one API call instead of N. The response counts applied + skipped_unknown so you can verify everything took. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_campaign_create
tools.description: Create a new campaign with an inline (non-shared) budget. ALWAYS starts paused — the caller is expected to add ad_groups + ads + at least one keyword/audience before enabling via ppc_enable_resource. bidding_strategy options: manual_cpc | max_clicks | max_conversions | max_conversion_value | target_cpa | target_roas | target_impression_share. • target_cpa requires the target_cpa arg (in account currency) • target_roas requires the target_roas arg (e.g. 1.5 = 150% ROAS target) • smart bidding strategies need ~15+ conversions/month to perform well — recommend manual_cpc for greenfield campaigns until volume builds. campaign_type: search | display | shopping | video | performance_max | discovery | demand_gen. Geo + language targeting use defaults (all targeted countries); refine via separate criteria mutations after creation. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_campaign_get
tools.description: Fetch one campaign. Pass include=ad_groups,ads,metrics (comma-separated) to inline related data.

tools.name: ppc_campaign_list
tools.description: List PPC campaigns (Google Ads / Meta Ads / LinkedIn Ads / Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) / TikTok Ads) from the local cache. Filterable by platform / status / connection_id.

tools.name: ppc_change_history
tools.description: Recent account changes — who / what / when. Returns timestamp, user_email, client_type (GOOGLE_ADS_UI / GOOGLE_ADS_API / etc.), resource_type, change operation, and the affected campaign / ad_group. Use when something starts behaving differently and you want to know 'what changed?'. Max 30 days back (Google API limit).

tools.name: ppc_connection_create
tools.description: Create a BYOK PPC connection — the customer's own platform app credentials, for accounts not using Hiveku's native OAuth quick-connect. Supported platforms: Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads), LinkedIn Ads, TikTok Ads — plus chatgpt_ads / vibe_ctv / amazon_ads. Per-platform required credentials: google_ads needs developer_token + client_id + client_secret + refresh_token + customer_id; microsoft_ads needs client_id + client_secret + refresh_token + customer_id (plus manager_id, the parent Bing customer id, for campaign calls); meta_ads / tiktok_ads / linkedin_ads need access_token + ad_account_id. Idempotent on (account, platform, customer_id) — re-creating an existing connection returns it with existed:true. A 400 carries a per-platform setup guide. After creating, run ppc_connection_test, then ppc_sync.

tools.name: ppc_connection_delete
tools.description: HARD delete a PPC connection. Removes the ppc_connections row + all linked campaigns / ad_groups / ads / metrics via FK cascade. Use to clean up phantom rows (e.g. unbound placeholder created during OAuth setup) or to release a (account_id, platform, customer_id) unique slot so the connection can be recreated. Not soft-delete — the data is gone. Confirm with the user before calling on a connection with campaign_count > 0.

tools.name: ppc_connection_get
tools.description: Get one PPC connection by UUID.

tools.name: ppc_connection_list
tools.description: List the account's PPC ad-platform connections — Google Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads), TikTok Ads.

tools.name: ppc_connection_test
tools.description: Run a live API test against a PPC connection (verifies OAuth + permissions).

tools.name: ppc_connection_update
tools.description: Update a PPC connection — set developer_token (Google Ads BYOK), customer_id, manager_id (MCC / Bing parent customer), display_name, is_active, or rotate credentials (client_id/client_secret/refresh_token/access_token). When customer_id lands on a google_ads connection (or ad_account_id on meta_ads), connection_status auto-flips from 'pending' to 'connected' so the sync route picks it up. Credential changes reset status to 'pending' — run ppc_connection_test after rotating. GUARDRAIL (daily sweep): settings.monthly_budget_target_cents (integer cents) arms budget monitoring; settings.guardrail.alert_at_pct (default 85) files inbox alerts; settings.guardrail.pause_at_pct (opt-in, number) auto-pauses live campaigns at that % of target. PATCH replaces the WHOLE settings object — read the connection first and merge, or unrelated keys are lost.

tools.name: ppc_conversion_actions_list
tools.description: List every conversion action configured on the account — what counts as a conversion. Returns id, name, status (ENABLED / REMOVED / HIDDEN), category (PURCHASE / LEAD / SIGNUP / etc.), counting_type (ONE_PER_CLICK / MANY_PER_CLICK), attribution model, lookback windows, value settings, type, origin (FIRST_PARTY / GOOGLE_ANALYTICS / etc.), primary_for_goal. Pair with ppc_conversion_tracking_status to detect broken tags. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_conversion_tracking_status
tools.description: Health check: which conversion actions actually FIRED in the last N days? Returns action_count + enabled_count + silent_count, a per-action list, and a `warnings[]` array naming each silent action plus an account-level line when EVERY enabled action recorded nothing. The single fastest 'why aren't we converting?' diagnostic. IT NOW SEES DEAD TAGS. This runs two queries, not one: an unsegmented pass that lists every non-REMOVED action, then a segmented pass that overlays counts. A date-segmented query returns no row at all for an action with zero conversions, so a single query silently omitted exactly the actions worth reporting — a fully dead tag was invisible and the account looked healthy. Expect enabled_count and silent_count to be materially higher than they used to be on the same account; that is the fix working, not a regression. READ THE TWO CONVERSION NUMBERS CORRECTLY. Each action carries `conversions` (metrics.conversions — only actions included in the Conversions column, which is what Smart Bidding optimises on) AND `all_conversions` (every conversion, including actions deliberately excluded from that column). Silence is judged on `all_conversions`, so an action set to not count toward Conversions is NOT reported as broken. An action can legitimately show conversions=0 with all_conversions=50; do not call that a dead tag. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_custom_audience_create
tools.description: Create a CUSTOM AUDIENCE (custom intent / in-market style) from keywords / URLs / place categories / apps. Returns the audience's resource_name — attach with ppc_audience_attach. NOTE: this is for keyword-/URL-driven audience definitions; customer-match (CRM-list) audiences need an upload flow not yet exposed here. Custom audiences take a few hours to fully populate after creation. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_customer_match_upload
tools.description: Upload hashed user identifiers to a Customer Match user_list. Each member must contain at least ONE of: hashed_email (sha256 of lowercased+trimmed email), hashed_phone_number (sha256 of E.164 phone), or address fields (hashed_first_name + hashed_last_name + country_code + postal_code). TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT upload — it returns a dry-run preview (member counts, totals) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to execute. PRE-HASHING IS THE CALLER'S RESPONSIBILITY — DO NOT pass raw PII; members must be PRE-HASHED sha256 hex (raw emails/phones are rejected with code raw_pii_rejected). The route enforces this by requiring the `hashed_*` field names. REQUIREMENTS: (a) MCC must have List status verified by Google (b) user_list must already exist (create in the Ads UI's Audience Manager — API for creating CM lists is limited) (c) explicit GRANTED consent for both ad_user_data and ad_personalization per regional privacy law (GDPR / CCPA). Only pass GRANTED when consent has been collected; default UNSPECIFIED otherwise. Job runs async on Google's side; populated audience size updates take 24–48h.

tools.name: ppc_digest
tools.description: Cross-platform PPC digest in ONE call. For each active platform connection on the account (google_ads / meta_ads / microsoft_ads / linkedin_ads / tiktok_ads / chatgpt_ads / amazon_ads / vibe_ctv), returns: window spend / clicks / impressions / conversions, active+paused campaign counts, last_synced_at, has_stale flag, connection_count, and a per-platform `pacing` block. Plus a `totals` block aggregating across all platforms and a `warnings[]` array calling out stale connections (>25h since sync), platforms with connections but zero data, mixed currencies, and pacing that reads low because of a stale sync. PACING — this is the month-pacing read for ALL platforms (ppc_pacing_summary stays GOOGLE ADS ONLY and per-campaign). Each by_platform[p].pacing is calendar MONTH-TO-DATE, independent of the `days` window param: { mtd_spend, monthly_target, target_source, target_mtd, pace_ratio (>1 = ahead of pace), projected_eom_spend (straight-line mtd_spend / days_elapsed x days_in_month), flag (true when more than 20% off pace either direction), days_elapsed, days_in_month, mixed_currency }. monthly_target sums settings.monthly_budget_target_cents across the platform's connections — the same key the guardrail sweep and ppc_reallocation_plan read (target_source 'connection_target'); when no connection carries a target it derives sum(active campaigns' daily_budget) x days_in_month (target_source 'derived_from_daily_budgets'); with neither, target_source is 'none' and every target-relative number is null — never invented. Mixed budget currencies within a platform set mixed_currency: true and null the target/ratios (skipped rather than blended). A has_stale platform's pacing reads LOW (recent days are missing from the cache) — sync first before acting on pace_ratio. Reads from local DB cache (ppc_campaigns + ppc_campaign_metrics) — no external API calls — so it's fast (under 1s typically). Stale-data warnings tell the agent when to fire ppc_sync / ppc_sync_async before relying on numbers. Best as the FIRST tool an agent calls in a weekly account review — saves 5-10 platform-specific tool calls and gives the cross-channel picture (including budget pacing) in one shot.

tools.name: ppc_disapprovals_list
tools.description: List every disapproved or area-of-interest-only ad with its policy topic entries (the specific reasons Google flagged). Time-sensitive — disapproved ads stop accruing impressions the moment they happen, so this is the first thing to run when traffic drops or conversion volume falls. Returns ad_id + ad_name + ad_type + approval_status + review_status + per-topic flags + the parent ad_group / campaign.

tools.name: ppc_enable_resource
tools.description: Re-enable a previously-paused campaign / ad_group / ad / keyword. Same args as ppc_pause_resource. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_google_ads_read
tools.description: Run a READ action against Google Ads through the marketing agent's own Python implementation — the same code the marketing department agent uses, not a reimplementation. USE THIS when the existing ppc_* tools do not cover what you need: it exposes the underlying CLI's read surface directly. Actions: account-settings, anomaly-check, auction-insights, audience-performance, billing-summary, change-history, conversion-tracking-status, impression-share, keyword-ideas, keyword-metrics, keyword-planner-forecast, linked-accounts, list-conversion-actions, list-disapprovals, list-keywords, list-recommendations, period-comparison, pull-ad-groups, pull-ads, pull-campaigns, pull-metrics, search-terms, segment-report. Get connection_id from ppc_connection_list. Extra flags go in `args`, e.g. { "date-range": "LAST_30_DAYS", "campaign-id": "123" }. READ-ONLY. Campaign, budget, bid and audience WRITES are deliberately not exposed here — they spend money, and the marketing agent applies budget ceilings and a staged-approval flow around them that this path does not reproduce. For those, use the existing ppc_* write tools or talk_to_department({ domain: 'marketing' }).

tools.name: ppc_google_asset_upload
tools.description: Google Ads media assets — the image bytes and YouTube video ids that Display / Demand Gen / Performance Max creative hangs off. operation: 'image-asset-create' (params.name ≤128 chars, params.media_source — an https URL or an s3:// key in Hiveku's asset buckets; fetched through the SSRF-guarded media pipeline with a 5 MB cap, then stored by Google so the source can disappear). Returns suggested_field_types naming the slots the image legally fills (MARKETING_IMAGE 1.91:1, SQUARE_MARKETING_IMAGE and LOGO 1:1, PORTRAIT_MARKETING_IMAGE 4:5). 'youtube-video-asset-create' (params.youtube_video_id — the 11-char id or a pasted watch URL; optional params.name) — the video must already be public/unlisted on YouTube; Google Ads never hosts video bytes. 'assets-list' (optional params.asset_type 'image' | 'youtube_video' | 'text' | 'sitelink' | 'callout' | 'structured_snippet' | 'call' | 'promotion' | 'price' | 'business_name', params.limit ≤1000) — read-only; image rows carry pixel dimensions + suggested_field_types.

tools.name: ppc_google_conversion_actions
tools.description: Google Ads conversion-action CRUD — FIX tracking, not just diagnose it (pair with ppc_conversion_tracking_status / ppc_conversion_actions_list for the read side). operation: 'conversion-action-create' (params.name required; params.category e.g. 'DEFAULT' | 'PURCHASE' | 'SIGNUP' | 'SUBMIT_LEAD_FORM' | 'PHONE_CALL_LEAD' | 'IMPORTED_LEAD' | 'BOOK_APPOINTMENT' | 'REQUEST_QUOTE' | 'CONTACT'; params.type_ (NOTE the trailing underscore) 'WEBPAGE' (site tag, default) | 'UPLOAD_CLICKS' (CRM import) | 'UPLOAD_CALLS' (PBX call import) | 'AD_CALL' | 'WEBSITE_CALL' | 'CLICK_TO_CALL'; optional params.value fixed default value, params.count_type 'ONE_PER_CLICK' (leads) | 'MANY_PER_CLICK' (sales), params.click_through_lookback_days 1-90, params.include_in_conversions_optimization bool (false = reporting-only, out of Smart Bidding), params.status 'ENABLED' | 'HIDDEN', params.phone_call_duration_seconds 1-10000 — call types only; calls shorter than it record NOTHING). Returns the conversion_action_id + tag_snippets to install. 'conversion-action-get-tag' (params.conversion_action_id numeric) — global site tag, event snippet, AW- conversion_id and conversion_label. 'conversion-action-update' (params.conversion_action_id; at least one of params.status 'ENABLED' | 'HIDDEN' (status REMOVED is REFUSED on this lane — removal is permanent and destroys what Smart Bidding optimizes toward, so it stays behind the marketing department's human-approval flow; use HIDDEN to retire from reporting), params.include_in_conversions_optimization bool (changes what Smart Bidding optimizes toward — change deliberately), params.value, params.always_use_default_value bool (CAUTION: true flattens every conversion to the default value and destroys transaction-level revenue reporting — reversible but spend-consequential), params.phone_call_duration_seconds 1-10000).

tools.name: ppc_google_pmax
tools.description: Google Ads Performance Max asset groups — the creative unit a PMax campaign cannot serve without (ppc_campaign_create alone makes a PMax campaign that can never serve). Nothing here can set anything live: groups are created PAUSED with no status argument; enabling the group and the campaign are two separate approvals on the enable lane. operation: 'asset-group-create' (params.campaign_id — must be a PERFORMANCE_MAX / DEMAND_GEN campaign; params.name; params.final_url https; params.headlines [3-15, each ≤30 chars]; params.descriptions [2-5, each ≤90, at least one ≤60]; params.long_headline ≤90; params.business_name ≤25; params.marketing_image_asset_resource_names [1.91:1] + params.square_marketing_image_asset_resource_names [1:1] + params.logo_asset_resource_names [1:1] — each needs ≥1, upload first via ppc_google_asset_upload image-asset-create which names the slot each image fits; optional params.landscape_logo_asset_resource_names, params.youtube_video_asset_resource_names ≤5, params.search_themes ≤25, params.audience_resource_names ≤10 ('customers/X/audiences/Y' paths), params.path1/params.path2 ≤15 chars). ONE atomic write — it refuses to create a group missing anything Google requires rather than building one that can never serve. Created PAUSED; returns servability note. 'asset-group-asset-add' (params.asset_group_id, params.asset_resource_names [≤20], params.field_type 'HEADLINE' | 'DESCRIPTION' | 'LONG_HEADLINE' | 'BUSINESS_NAME' | 'MARKETING_IMAGE' | 'SQUARE_MARKETING_IMAGE' | 'LOGO' | 'LANDSCAPE_LOGO' | 'YOUTUBE_VIDEO') — the repair path for a slot asset-group-list reports missing. CAUTION: on an ENABLED group in an ENABLED campaign the new creative serves immediately. 'asset-group-signal-add' (params.asset_group_id; params.search_themes [≤25, each ≤80 chars] and/or params.audience_resource_names [≤10]) — signals are HINTS, not targeting fences; never narrows delivery, never changes spend. 'asset-group-list' (optional params.campaign_id, params.limit ≤200) — read-only: every group with per-slot asset counts, signals, ad_strength, primary_status, and missing_requirements naming exactly why an idle group cannot serve. 'price-asset-create' (params.price_type 'BRANDS' | 'EVENTS' | 'LOCATIONS' | 'NEIGHBORHOODS' | 'PRODUCT_CATEGORIES' | 'PRODUCT_TIERS' | 'SERVICES' | 'SERVICE_CATEGORIES' | 'SERVICE_TIERS'; params.offerings_json JSON ARRAY of 3-8 rows {header ≤25, description ≤25, amount, final_url, optional unit 'PER_HOUR'|'PER_DAY'|'PER_WEEK'|'PER_MONTH'|'PER_YEAR'|'PER_NIGHT', optional currency_code — omitted falls back to the ad account's currency, refused if unreadable: a wrong-currency price is a real quote to a real customer; optional params.language_code default 'en', params.price_qualifier 'FROM' | 'UP_TO' | 'AVERAGE'). Account-level; shows nowhere until ppc_asset_attach field_type=PRICE.

tools.name: ppc_google_pmax_performance
tools.description: THE Performance Max performance surface (read-only): per-asset-group metrics (impressions, clicks, cost, conversions, conversions_value, ctr_pct, cost_per_conversion, ad_strength, primary_status) PLUS Google's per-channel split of where PMax delivery actually went (segments.ad_network_type: SEARCH, SEARCH_PARTNERS, CONTENT=Display, YOUTUBE, GMAIL, DISCOVER, MAPS, GOOGLE_TV; MIXED=cross-network), per campaign, channels sorted by spend. params.days 1-365 (default 30), optional params.campaign_id to scope to one PMax campaign (a non-PMax campaign_id is refused with a pointer to ppc_metrics). Asset groups with zero traffic in the window are absent — ppc_google_pmax asset-group-list shows every group with its servability diagnostic. If the channel query fails on an old agent image, asset-group rows still return and channel_split_unavailable says why.

tools.name: ppc_google_shared_negatives
tools.description: Google Ads shared negative keyword lists — maintain ONE blocklist and apply it to many campaigns. operation: 'shared-set-create' (params.name ≤255 chars) — empty NEGATIVE_KEYWORDS list; blocks nothing until keywords are added AND it is attached. 'shared-set-keywords-add' (params.shared_set_resource_name, params.keywords [array of strings ≤80 chars, max 200 per call]; optional params.match_type 'exact' | 'phrase' (default) | 'broad'). Takes effect IMMEDIATELY on every campaign the list is attached to; a broad negative blocks any query containing all the words in any order. 'shared-set-attach' (params.campaign_id, params.shared_set_resource_name) — every keyword in the list starts blocking on that campaign immediately. 'shared-set-detach' (params.campaign_shared_set_resource_name from the list op) — WIDENS reach: blocked queries can serve again. 'shared-sets-list' (optional params.shared_set_id to also list that set's keywords, params.limit ≤1000) — read-only: lists with member counts + attached campaigns.

tools.name: ppc_google_targeting
tools.description: Google Ads campaign geo / proximity / language targeting — scope an Olympus-created campaign to a client's city, radius or language. operation: 'geo-target-search' (params.query — place name or postal code e.g. 'Dallas, Texas' or '75201'; optional params.country_code 2-letter ISO e.g. 'US', params.limit ≤100) — resolves names to the geo_target_ids the add op takes, with reach estimates. 'campaign-geo-targets-list' (params.campaign_id) — location + proximity criteria with resource_names; negative=true means EXCLUDED. 'campaign-geo-target-add' (params.campaign_id, params.geo_target_ids [array, max 100]; optional params.negative bool to EXCLUDE, params.bid_modifier 0.1-10.0, not allowed on exclusions). Adding the first positive location narrows the campaign from 'everywhere' to only those places. 'campaign-geo-target-remove' (params.resource_names [array of campaignCriteria resource names from the list op, max 100]). 'campaign-proximity-add' (params.campaign_id, params.latitude, params.longitude, params.radius; optional params.radius_units 'MILES' (max 500, default) | 'KILOMETERS' (max 800)) — radius targeting for service-area businesses. 'campaign-language-targets-list' (params.campaign_id) — no criteria means ALL languages. 'campaign-language-target-add' (params.campaign_id, params.language_ids [array of codes like 'en'/'es' or numeric criterion ids, max 50]) — matches the user's Google interface language. 'campaign-location-settings-update' (params.campaign_id; params.positive_geo_target_type 'PRESENCE' | 'PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST' | 'SEARCH_INTEREST' and/or params.negative_geo_target_type 'PRESENCE' | 'PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST') — PRESENCE stops local budgets leaking to out-of-area searchers.

tools.name: ppc_google_user_lists
tools.description: Google Ads user lists (remarketing audiences). 'user-lists-list' is how you get the user_list_id that ppc_customer_match_upload REQUIRES (no other tool surfaces it); the resource_names it returns also feed ppc_audience_attach. operation: 'user-list-create-rule-based' (params.name required; params.rules_json — JSON array of rules {name: 'url__' (page URL, default) | 'referrer__url__', operator: 'CONTAINS' | 'EQUALS' | 'STARTS_WITH' | 'ENDS_WITH' | 'NOT_CONTAINS' | 'NOT_EQUALS' | 'NOT_STARTS_WITH' | 'NOT_ENDS_WITH', value: string ≤500 chars}, max 20 rules; optional params.description, params.membership_life_span_days 1-540 (default 30), params.rule_operator 'and' | 'or', params.prepopulate bool — backfill last 30 days of visitors). Creates a WEBSITE-VISITOR list that fills from the Google tag on the site — NOT customer match, no customer data uploaded. Needs ~100 members to serve on Search, ~1,000 on Display. 'user-lists-list' (optional params.limit ≤1000) — read-only: every list on the account (including CRM/customer-match lists) with user_list_id, sizes and eligibility.

tools.name: ppc_impression_share
tools.description: Per-campaign search impression-share metrics: search_impression_share, top_impression_share, abs_top_impression_share + the lost-to-budget AND lost-to-rank breakdowns at each tier. The 'where are we losing visibility?' report — high lost_to_budget means raise the budget; high lost_to_rank means raise bids or improve quality score. Open this first when traffic drops. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_keyword_add
tools.description: Add a new positive keyword to an ad group. Optional initial cpc_bid (omit to use the ad-group default). Match types: broad | phrase | exact. Returns the created criterion's criterion_id + resource_name — capture these for follow-up bid / status / match-type changes. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_keyword_bid_update
tools.description: Set the manual CPC bid on a keyword. ONLY effective when the parent ad_group / campaign is on a bidding strategy that honors keyword-level bids (Manual CPC, Enhanced CPC). For target-CPA / target-ROAS / Max Conversions etc. the bid is recorded but not used for ranking — the response carries an explicit note when that's the case. Verify the bidding strategy via ppc_campaign_get before relying on this. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_keyword_list
tools.description: List every positive keyword in the account (or scoped to one campaign / ad_group) with last-N-days metrics, status, match type, CPC bid, and the four quality-score components (overall + creative + landing page + predicted CTR). The prune-or-promote list — pair with ppc_search_terms_report. Negatives are excluded; use a separate report for those. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_keyword_match_type_change
tools.description: Change a keyword's match type. Google Ads doesn't let you mutate match_type in place — it's part of the criterion's identity — so this action removes the existing keyword and creates a new one with the new match_type, preserving the bid (set preserve_bid=false to drop it). Returns the OLD resource_name (now removed) and the NEW one. Common workflow: broad keyword burns too much → switch to phrase or exact.

tools.name: ppc_keyword_planner_forecast
tools.description: Forecast impressions / clicks / cost / conversions / avg CPC / CPA for a keyword set at a given bid + budget. Use BEFORE launching a campaign: 'if we bid $2 broad on these 10 keywords with a $100/day budget, what's the expected daily volume?'. Some MCC setups disable Keyword Planner API access — the response surfaces that error with a hint when it happens. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_linked_accounts_list
tools.description: List product linkages (Google Analytics 4, Merchant Center). Disconnected linkages mean lost cross-product data (audience imports, conversion imports, shopping feed) — check here when those sources go cold.

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_abm_segment
tools.description: LinkedIn ABM company segments. UNVALIDATED-LIVE. operation: • 'company-segment-create' — create an empty COMPANY DMP segment (name required) • 'company-segment-add' — the ABM upload: segment_id + companies (array of objects, each needing at least one identifier: organization_urn (strongest match) / name / domain / website / page_url; optional city, state, country ISO-2, postal_code, stock_ticker refine a match but never make one. CLI accepts up to 20,000 per segment, but a single call carries roughly 1,500-2,000 companies within the 120KB params cap — chunk larger lists across calls (re-invoking is safe; partial/unaccounted rows are surfaced)). Company names/domains are business data — NOT hashed; person-level identifiers (email/hashed_email/names) are REFUSED by policy. Campaigns targeting the segment start reaching the added companies, so the first call previews and executing requires confirm=true. Partial failures are surfaced per-chunk — companies with no per-element result must be treated as unknown, check the segment before resending. (Member/contact uploads are ppc_linkedin_matched_audience_upload — those DO require pre-hashed emails.)

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_audience_segments
tools.description: LinkedIn campaign-side audience (DMP segment) targeting. UNVALIDATED-LIVE. operation: • 'list-audience-segments' — the account's DMP segments (optional limit, default 100) • 'campaign-audiences' — one campaign's current segment include/exclude lists (campaign_id required; optional segment_facet, default 'matched_audience') • 'campaign-audiences-update' — edit a campaign's segment lists: campaign_id + at least one of include_segment_ids / exclude_segment_ids / remove_segment_ids; mode 'add' (merge, default) | 'replace'. This changes delivery on a possibly-LIVE campaign immediately, so the first call previews and executing requires confirm=true.

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_boost_post
tools.description: Boost an organic LinkedIn post — wraps the post (post_urn: urn:li:share:* or urn:li:ugcPost:*) as a DRAFT creative on the given campaign (campaign_id). UNVALIDATED-LIVE. The boosted creative cannot serve until a human launches/enables it in Campaign Manager — no tool can activate a LinkedIn draft.

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_campaign_group_create
tools.description: Create a LinkedIn Campaign Group (the pre-campaign container — required to host new campaigns). ALWAYS created DRAFT — the CLI forces it regardless of the status field (kept for compatibility only); drafts never spend, and no tool can activate a LinkedIn draft — a human launches it in Campaign Manager. Optional total / daily budgets at the group level cap aggregate spend across all child campaigns (guardrailed; the CLI additionally hard-caps every LinkedIn budget write at 100,000). Campaign build-out from here: ppc_linkedin_campaign_push pushes a local draft campaign into a group (DRAFT), ppc_linkedin_creative_create / ppc_linkedin_boost_post add creatives — or drive the full lane through the marketing department (talk_to_department, domain 'marketing').

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_campaign_group_update
tools.description: Update or archive a LinkedIn campaign group (group_id = LINKEDIN group id). operation: • 'update' — change name, start_date, end_date, daily_budget, total_budget (at least one required). Group budgets live ONLY here (the LinkedIn update-budget lane is campaign-level); they are guardrailed and the CLI hard-caps every budget write at 100,000. Status flips stay on ppc_platform_pause_resource / ppc_platform_enable_resource (resource_type 'campaign_group') • 'archive' — IRREVERSIBLE; the group and its campaigns stop serving permanently. First call previews; executing requires confirm=true.

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_campaign_groups_list
tools.description: Pull the account's LinkedIn campaign groups from the API into the local DB and return them (id, name, status, budgets, run schedule). Not covered by ppc_sync (LinkedIn's sync lane pulls campaigns + metrics only) — call this to discover group ids for ppc_linkedin_campaign_group_update / as push targets.

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_campaign_push
tools.description: Push a LOCAL draft campaign (a ppc_campaigns row — campaign_id is the LOCAL row id, NOT a LinkedIn id) to LinkedIn, inside a found-or-created default 'Hiveku' campaign group. ALWAYS created DRAFT — drafts never spend, and NO tool can activate a LinkedIn draft (campaign-update and set-status both refuse DRAFT->ACTIVE by design); a human launches the draft from LinkedIn Campaign Manager. LinkedIn hard-requires a budget AND at least one location targeting facet (urn:li:geo:* in the draft's targeting) at create time — missing pieces come back as a named list instead of guessed values. Budget writes are CLI-capped at 100,000. Write path not yet live-validated.

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_campaign_update
tools.description: Update or archive a LinkedIn campaign (campaign_id = LINKEDIN campaign id). operation: • 'update' — change name, start_date, end_date (YYYY-MM-DD; at least one required). Status flips stay on ppc_platform_pause_resource / ppc_platform_enable_resource; budgets stay on ppc_platform_budget_update (guardrailed). Drafts cannot be activated by any tool — human-only in Campaign Manager • 'archive' — IRREVERSIBLE; the campaign stops serving permanently. First call previews; executing requires confirm=true.

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_conversions
tools.description: LinkedIn conversion tracking — rules + Conversions-API events. UNVALIDATED-LIVE. operation: • 'conversion-rules-list' — list conversion rules (optional limit, default 100) • 'conversion-rule-create' — create a rule: name + conversion_type (LEAD | PURCHASE | SIGN_UP | ADD_TO_CART | DOWNLOAD | INSTALL | KEY_PAGE_VIEW | LANDING | SAVE | START_CHECKOUT | SUBSCRIBE | ADD_BILLING_INFO | BOOK_APPOINTMENT | REQUEST_QUOTE | SUBMIT_APPLICATION | COMPLETE_SIGNUP | PHONE_CALL | JOB_APPLY | TALK_TO_REPRESENTATIVE | OTHER) required; optional conversion_method CONVERSIONS_API (default) | PIXEL, post_click_window_days (1|7|30|90, default 30), view_through_window_days (1|7|30, default 7), attribution_type LAST_TOUCH_BY_CAMPAIGN (default) | LAST_TOUCH_BY_CONVERSION, default_value + default_value_currency, campaign_ids (array to associate) • 'conversion-event-send' — send offline/CAPI events to a rule: conversion_id + events (array, max 500) required. SHA256_EMAIL identifiers must arrive PRE-HASHED (sha256 of the lowercased+trimmed email — caller responsibility, same contract as the matched-audience upload). Batched; a partial response is NOT success — per-element failures are surfaced and failed events must be resent. CONFIRM GATE: conversion data trains LinkedIn's bidding and uploaded conversions cannot be recalled, so 'conversion-event-send' — and 'conversion-rule-create' whenever default_value is set — PREVIEW on the first call (event_count + total_value_by_currency) and execute only when the exact call is repeated with confirm=true. Show the operator the totals before confirming; do not auto-confirm.

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_creative_create
tools.description: Author a single-image Sponsored Content ad end-to-end (image upload -> dark post -> creative) and attach it to a LinkedIn campaign. UNVALIDATED-LIVE. The creative's intendedStatus is FORCED to DRAFT — there is no status argument; a DRAFT creative on a DRAFT campaign means going live still takes human activation in Campaign Manager (no tool can activate a LinkedIn draft). The post is DIRECT SPONSORED CONTENT (a dark post) — it never appears on the organization's organic feed. COVERS single-image sponsored content with a click-through link ONLY — NOT video, carousel, document, text, spotlight/dynamic, message ads, or lead-gen-form creatives (do not claim otherwise). Limits: headline <=200 chars, commentary <=3000, description <=300; media_source is an https URL or s3:// key. organization_urn (urn:li:organization:*) is auto-resolved from the ad account when omitted.

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_creative_disapprovals
tools.description: List LinkedIn ads (creatives) whose review REJECTED them. UNVALIDATED-LIVE. Detects rejection from the creative's review object (status REJECTED + rejectionReasons when the app tier decorates them) OR REJECT-flavoured servingHoldReasons. When LinkedIn returns no rejectionReasons text (tier-dependent), items are status-only (reasons_available=false) and the policy detail lives in Campaign Manager. LinkedIn creatives are unnamed — name is always null; use content_reference / ppc_linkedin_creatives detail for context. Returns {disapproved_count, items:[{id, name, level, status, reasons, serving_hold_reasons, campaign, intended_status, content_reference}]}. Optional campaign_id scopes to one campaign.

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_creatives
tools.description: LinkedIn creative (ad-layer) lifecycle. operation: • 'list' — pull creatives (optionally scoped to campaign_id; enrich=true resolves previews + per-creative stats over `days`) • 'detail' — one creative's full detail + stats (creative_id required; optional days, default 7 (pass days for a wider window)) • 'set-status' — pause or enable ONE creative's serving intent (creative_id + status 'enabled'|'paused'). Enabling can make the ad DELIVERABLE if its parent campaign/group are active, so status='enabled' previews first and requires confirm=true; pausing needs no confirm. Serving also depends on the parents — check servingHoldReasons if it still does not deliver • 'archive' — IRREVERSIBLE (LinkedIn has no hard delete; ARCHIVED is terminal). Previews first; requires confirm=true.

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_demographics_report
tools.description: LinkedIn's signature report — performance broken down by professional attributes. The WHY-LinkedIn diagnostic: 'which job titles converted highest?' / 'which industries spent without converting?'. pivot options: • MEMBER_JOB_TITLE — most actionable for ABM / role-targeted campaigns • MEMBER_INDUSTRY — vertical performance • MEMBER_SENIORITY — IC vs Director vs VP+ performance • MEMBER_FUNCTION — engineering vs marketing vs sales departments • MEMBER_COMPANY_SIZE — SMB vs Enterprise targeting validation • MEMBER_COMPANY — top accounts engaging your campaigns • MEMBER_REGION / MEMBER_COUNTRY_V2 — geo

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_leadgen
tools.description: LinkedIn Lead Gen Form retrieval → feed captured leads into the CRM. UNVALIDATED-LIVE. operation: • 'lead-forms' — list the account's lead-gen forms (optional limit, default 50) • 'lead-form-responses' — pull form responses (optional days default 30, limit default 100, campaign_id to scope to one campaign's leads).

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_matched_audience_upload
tools.description: Upload hashed identifiers to an EXISTING LinkedIn DMP Segment (Matched Audience). hashed_emails entries must be SHA256(lowercased+trimmed) — caller responsibility. google_ids is the Google Advertising ID set for mobile targeting. REQUIREMENTS: • Segment must already exist + must be type=USER (not COMPANY) — create in Campaign Manager UI; the public-API creation path requires a Marketing Solutions Partner-tier permission most accounts don't have • LinkedIn dedupes server-side; member-to-LinkedIn-user match takes 24-48h

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_media_image_upload
tools.description: Upload an image to LinkedIn's media library for ad use (returns urn:li:image:* for creative builds). UNVALIDATED-LIVE. Asset-only — spends nothing and changes no live ad. media_source is an https URL or s3:// key; organization_urn is the owning advertiser org (urn:li:organization:*).

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_targeting
tools.description: LinkedIn targeting discovery + audience sizing. UNVALIDATED-LIVE. operation: • 'targeting-facets' — list the targeting facet URNs (titles, industries, skills, geos, ...). Optional locale_language (default 'en') / locale_country (default 'US') • 'targeting-search' — search entities within one facet: facet required (friendly alias like job_title | company | seniority | industry | skill | job_function | location | company_size | school, or a raw urn:li:adTargetingFacet:* URN), query, limit (default 25) • 'audience-count' — forecast audience size for a targeting criteria object: include required, optional exclude. Use the returned URNs in draft-campaign targeting for ppc_linkedin_campaign_push.

tools.name: ppc_meta_ad_create
tools.description: Create a Meta ad binding an existing creative (ppc_meta_adcreative_create) to an existing ad set. ALWAYS created PAUSED — hardcoded at the wire, no status parameter exists. Even once enabled (ppc_platform_enable_resource, resource_type 'ad') the ad only serves if its ad set and campaign are also active. Write path not yet live-validated.

tools.name: ppc_meta_ad_set_audiences_update
tools.description: Edit the include/exclude custom-audience lists on a Meta ad set — this can change delivery on a LIVE ad set immediately and re-enters the learning phase, so the first call returns a preview and executing requires confirm=true. audience_mode 'add' merges into the current lists; 'replace' makes the lists passed the WHOLE lists (anything omitted is dropped). remove_audience_ids takes ids off both lists (mode 'add' only). Read the current lists first with ppc_meta_audiences_list operation 'ad-set-audiences'. Write path not yet live-validated.

tools.name: ppc_meta_ad_set_create
tools.description: Create a Meta ad set under an existing campaign. ALWAYS created PAUSED — the CLI hardcodes the status at the wire and there is no status parameter to smuggle one through; enabling is a separate explicit ppc_platform_enable_resource call. targeting is the full spec and MUST include geo_locations (JSON object, or a JSON string if your provider drops object args). Budgets are account-currency floats and pass the programmatic spend guardrail (absolute ceilings). promoted_object is required for conversion optimization goals (e.g. {"pixel_id": "123", "custom_event_type": "LEAD"}). Meta does not allow switching an ad set between daily and lifetime budget types after creation. Write path not yet live-validated.

tools.name: ppc_meta_ad_set_update
tools.description: Update a Meta ad set's name, bid_amount (bid cap), or targeting (at least one required). ⚠ TARGETING REPLACES THE WHOLE SPEC: Graph has no partial merge for targeting — whatever is sent becomes the entire spec and anything omitted is DROPPED (geo_locations stays mandatory). Read the current spec first (ppc_meta_audiences_list 'ad-set-audiences' / the synced ad-set row), edit it, send it back WHOLE. Editing targeting on a delivering ad set re-enters the learning phase. Deliberately NOT here: status (enable/pause stays on ppc_platform_enable_resource / ppc_platform_pause_resource — the single audited path) and budgets (ppc_platform_budget_update with budget_level='ad_set' — the guardrailed path). Write path not yet live-validated.

tools.name: ppc_meta_adcreative_create
tools.description: Create a Meta ad creative — a creative alone spends nothing (it becomes an ad only via ppc_meta_ad_create, which is itself created PAUSED). All formats need name, page_id, link (destination URL), message (primary text). format: • 'link' — single image/link card. Optional title, description, image_url OR image_hash (from ppc_meta_media_upload), call_to_action (e.g. LEARN_MORE) • 'video' — video_id required (from ppc_meta_media_upload operation 'video'). Optional thumbnail_image_hash OR thumbnail_url, title, link_description, call_to_action, instagram_user_id (co-publish to Instagram) • 'carousel' — child_attachments required: array of 2-10 cards ({link, name?, description?, image_hash?, picture?, video_id?}). Optional call_to_action; multi_share_optimized=false keeps card order FIXED; multi_share_end_card=false drops the trailing Page profile card. Write path not yet live-validated (CLI marks Meta writes NEEDS-live-validation).

tools.name: ppc_meta_advantage_create
tools.description: Create the two halves of a Meta Advantage+ buy (v25 unified structure). Both are ALWAYS created PAUSED (CLI-hardcoded — no status parameter exists); enabling is a separate ppc_platform_enable_resource call. operation: • 'campaign' — name + objective (OUTCOME_SALES | OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION | OUTCOME_LEADS) required. Optional daily_budget / lifetime_budget (guardrailed), end_time, bid_strategy, bid_amount, special_ad_categories • 'ad_set' — campaign_id, name, optimization_goal, billing_event, geo_locations, promoted_object required. Optional custom_audiences / excluded_custom_audiences (audience-id arrays), start_time, end_time. Targeting beyond geo+audiences stays on Advantage+ automation. Write path not yet live-validated.

tools.name: ppc_meta_advantage_status
tools.description: Read a Meta campaign's Advantage+ posture — whether it runs the v25 unified Advantage+ structure, which automation features are on, and its objective/budget shape. campaign_id is the META campaign id.

tools.name: ppc_meta_archive
tools.description: Archive a Meta campaign / ad set / ad — IRREVERSIBLE through this surface (ARCHIVED at the wire; the entity stops serving permanently). To stop delivery temporarily use ppc_platform_pause_resource instead. First call returns a preview; executing requires confirm=true. operation picks the layer: 'campaign' (campaign_id) | 'ad_set' (ad_set_id) | 'ad' (ad_id).

tools.name: ppc_meta_audience_create
tools.description: Create a Meta audience (audience-only write — spends nothing until attached to an ad set). operation: • 'rule' — rule-based custom audience: name, source_type ('website' pixel-visitors | 'engagement'), rule (flexible rule JSON) required. Optional retention_days (1-180), prefill=false to start empty, description • 'lookalike' — name, origin_audience_id (the seed custom audience), country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) required. Optional ratio (0.01-0.20, default 0.01), starting_ratio (lower band edge), description. Customer-file uploads are ppc_meta_custom_audience_upload (pre-hashed rows). Write path not yet live-validated.

tools.name: ppc_meta_audiences_list
tools.description: Meta audience reads. operation: • 'list-custom-audiences' — the account's custom + lookalike audiences (id, name, type, approximate size) • 'audience-map' — which audiences are attached to which ad sets account-wide (the include/exclude picture) • 'ad-set-audiences' — one ad set's current include/exclude audience lists (ad_set_id required; read this BEFORE ppc_meta_ad_set_audiences_update)

tools.name: ppc_meta_campaign_push
tools.description: Push a LOCAL draft campaign (a ppc_campaigns row created in the dashboard/agent UI — campaign_id is the LOCAL row id, NOT a Meta id) to Meta. ALWAYS created PAUSED on Meta ('never auto-spend on a freshly pushed draft'); build out ad sets + ads, then enable explicitly with ppc_platform_enable_resource. Note ppc_campaign_create (the draft-row creator) is Google-only — Meta drafts come from the dashboard UI or the marketing department agent. Write path not yet live-validated.

tools.name: ppc_meta_campaign_update
tools.description: Update a live Meta campaign's name, stop_time (ISO 8601), special_ad_categories, or bid_strategy (campaign_id = META campaign id; at least one field required). Status flips stay on ppc_platform_pause_resource / ppc_platform_enable_resource; budgets stay on ppc_platform_budget_update (the guardrailed path). Write path not yet live-validated.

tools.name: ppc_meta_conversion_volume
tools.description: Per-conversion volume for Meta — the answer 'is this recording, and when did it last record' that Meta was assumed not to give. Returns each Custom Conversion with attributed_conversions and attributed_value for the window, joined from insights actions[] on the conversion id (offsite_conversion.custom.<id> embeds the node id, so the join is exact). TWO NUMBERS, DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED. attributed_conversions counts only conversions Meta ATTRIBUTES TO ADS under the account's attribution setting — a strict subset. last_fired_time counts EVERY matching event, ad-driven or organic. So a conversion that fired an hour ago with zero attributed is recording perfectly and simply was not ad-driven: that is a MEDIA finding, not a tracking failure, and must not be reported as broken. Every value carries field_provenance naming which platform field it came from. One window per call. Ask twice for a 7-day and 30-day comparison, the same way the Google conversion tools are used. A read that fails returns readability/coverage_gap with a reason classified as permission, token or api_error — three different operator actions — and never zeros.

tools.name: ppc_meta_creative_list
tools.description: List ad creatives in the Meta account — id, name, status, object_type, image_url / video_id, title, body, link_url, call_to_action_type, object_story_spec. Pair with ppc_meta_insights_breakdown(level='ad') to identify which creatives are actually performing and need refresh / scale.

tools.name: ppc_meta_custom_audience_upload
tools.description: Upload hashed identifiers to an EXISTING Meta Custom Audience. Schema fields end in _SHA256 for hashed values (EMAIL_SHA256, PHONE_SHA256) and plain for non-PII (CT=city, ST=state, etc.). Each row is an array of values in schema order. Pre-hashing is caller responsibility — pass SHA256(lowercased+trimmed email) etc. REQUIREMENTS: • Audience must already exist (create in the Ads UI; API for CM-audience creation is gated) • Explicit GRANTED consent for ad_user_data + ad_personalization per regional privacy law (GDPR / CCPA) — only pass GRANTED with documented user consent • Audience populates over ~hours; Meta dedupes server-side

tools.name: ppc_meta_custom_conversions
tools.description: What Meta thinks a conversion IS. Lists the ad account's Custom Conversions with name, the URL RULE (the only place a URL condition exists anywhere in Meta's object graph), custom_event_type, aggregation, default value, retention window, archived state, the owning pixel, and first/last_fired_time. USE THIS BEFORE CONCLUDING A META ACCOUNT CANNOT BE MEASURED. It was long believed Meta exposed no per-conversion detail, so tooling checked it at PIXEL grain only — but one pixel serves every conversion, so a pixel that fired an hour ago cannot tell a dead LEAD from a live PURCHASE. last_fired_time is per conversion and answers that directly. An empty list means this account defines no CUSTOM conversions — standard pixel events (fb_pixel_lead and friends) still record, they simply have no named definition object to read. That is different from a failed read: if the catalogue could not be read, the response says so in readability/coverage_gap and NEVER returns an empty list, because 'no conversions' and 'we could not look' must not render the same way.

tools.name: ppc_meta_disapprovals_list
tools.description: List Meta ads the platform is refusing to serve (effective_status DISAPPROVED) or serving restricted (WITH_ISSUES), with policy reasons from issues_info (error_summary/error_message per issue; empty reasons = Graph attached no detail, not 'no reason exists'). Returns {disapproved_count, items:[{id, name, level, status, reasons, issues, adset_id, campaign_id}]} — same shape as ppc_disapprovals_list (Google). Time-sensitive: disapproved ads spend nothing and silently starve their campaigns.

tools.name: ppc_meta_insights_breakdown
tools.description: Meta's most flexible report — /insights with the `breakdowns` parameter. Common breakdowns: age, gender, country, region, dma, publisher_platform (Facebook | Instagram | Audience Network | Messenger), device_platform (mobile | desktop), placement, impression_device. Combine up to 3 (Meta's hard cap) for pivots. level: account | campaign | adset | ad — controls aggregation grain. Use 'ad' for creative-level pivots like which-ad-by-placement, 'campaign' for higher-level reads.

tools.name: ppc_meta_leadgen
tools.description: Meta lead-gen (instant form) retrieval → feed captured leads into the CRM. operation: • 'forms' — list a Page's lead forms (page_id required; from ppc_meta_pages_pixels list-pages) • 'leads' — pull a form's captured leads (form_id required; optional since_unix to fetch only new leads, optional page_id). Read-only; lead fields arrive exactly as the form collected them.

tools.name: ppc_meta_media_upload
tools.description: Upload an image (operation 'image', cap 30MB) or video (operation 'video', cap 100MB — no chunked upload, so oversized files refuse) to the Meta ad account's media library from an https URL or s3:// key. Asset-only: spends nothing and changes no live ad. Returns image_hash / video_id for ppc_meta_adcreative_create.

tools.name: ppc_meta_pages_pixels
tools.description: List the Meta ad account's Facebook Pages (operation 'list-pages' — page id + name; a page_id is required for every ad creative and for lead-gen forms) or Meta Pixels (operation 'list-pixels' — pixel id + name; a pixel_id feeds promoted_object on conversion-optimized ad sets).

tools.name: ppc_meta_targeting
tools.description: Meta targeting discovery + reach estimation. operation: • 'search' — find targeting options by keyword (query required). search_type family: interests | behaviors | demographics | life_events | industries | income | family_statuses | locations | employers | job_titles | schools (default interests) • 'browse' — walk the full targeting-category tree (no query) • 'delivery-estimate' — estimated audience size for a targeting spec: pass targeting (full spec incl. geo_locations; JSON object or JSON string) + optimization_goal (e.g. LINK_CLICKS, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS) Use the returned ids inside the targeting spec for ppc_meta_ad_set_create.

tools.name: ppc_metrics
tools.description: Daily PPC metrics (Google Ads / Meta Ads / LinkedIn Ads / Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) / TikTok Ads). Provide ONE of campaign_id / ad_group_id / ad_id. Filter by date window (since/until).

tools.name: ppc_negative_keyword_add
tools.description: Add a negative keyword at ad_group OR campaign level (exactly one — pass `ad_group_id` for ad-group scope, `campaign_id` for campaign scope). Match types: broad | phrase | exact. The most common daily PPC action — pair with ppc_search_terms_report to identify what's wasting clicks. Returns the created criterion's `resource_name` (needed for ppc_negative_keyword_remove if you want to undo). GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_negative_keyword_remove
tools.description: Remove a negative keyword by its resource_name (returned from ppc_negative_keyword_add). Resource names look like 'customers/<id>/adGroupCriteria/<adGroupId>~<criterionId>' (ad-group scope) or 'customers/<id>/campaignCriteria/<criterionId>' (campaign scope) — the route infers scope from the path shape. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_offline_conversion_upload
tools.description: Upload offline conversions (CRM sales / SQLs / phone-call appointments). Closes the loop on click → sale attribution. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT upload — it returns a dry-run preview (row counts, value totals) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to execute. Each conversion entry must have: - gclid (preferred, from URL when the user clicked) OR order_id (your dedupe key) - conversion_date_time: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS+HH:MM' - conversion_value (numeric) - currency_code (e.g. 'USD') REQUIREMENTS: the conversion_action_id must exist + be configured as 'Upload' source in the Ads UI (Conversions → New conversion → Import). Partial-failure mode is on — bad rows surface in `results[]` with ok:false; good rows still land. Conversions take a few hours to appear in reports. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_pacing_summary
tools.description: Per-campaign spend pacing for the current calendar month. Returns target_mtd (daily_budget × days_elapsed), actual_mtd, pace_ratio (>1 = ahead, <1 = behind), projected_eom_spend, and a `flag` field on campaigns >20% off pace either direction. The 'are we on budget?' snapshot — run weekly. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For month pacing on ANY other platform — or the whole account in one call — use ppc_digest: its per-platform `pacing` block covers every connected platform against settings.monthly_budget_target_cents (falling back to active daily budgets). This tool remains the per-campaign granular view, Google-only.

tools.name: ppc_pause_resource
tools.description: Pause a campaign, ad_group, ad, or keyword by id. For ad / keyword you must also pass ad_group_id (the parent). Reverses with ppc_enable_resource. Catch-and-pause is one of the most common daily PPC actions — paired with ppc_metrics or ppc_search_terms_report to identify underperformers. GOOGLE ADS ONLY. This tool routes to the Google Ads surface; passing a Microsoft/Meta/LinkedIn/TikTok connection_id returns a wrong-platform error, not an empty result. For those platforms use the ppc_bing_* / ppc_meta_* / ppc_linkedin_* / ppc_tiktok_* tools.

tools.name: ppc_period_comparison
tools.description: Compare two periods on Google Ads at campaign | ad_group | keyword level. Returns winners / losers (by clicks delta) and cpc_climbers / cpc_droppers (by avg-CPC delta). The MoM / WoW / pre-vs-post-launch / algorithm-update report — same shape as seo_gsc_period_comparison. For paired-period budget-pacing reviews, scope to 'campaign'. For finding new opportunities or pruning, scope to 'keyword'.

tools.name: ppc_platform_ad_group_create
tools.description: Create a PAUSED ad group under a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign (connection_id + campaign_id + name, optional cpc_bid). Google: ppc_ad_group_create.

tools.name: ppc_platform_bidding_strategy_update
tools.description: Set a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) campaign bidding scheme (connection_id + campaign_id + strategy: manual_cpc|enhanced_cpc|max_clicks|max_conversions|target_cpa|target_roas). strategy=target_cpa REQUIRES target_cpa (account currency); strategy=target_roas REQUIRES target_roas (a RATIO — 2.5 = 250% return, not a percent). Conversion-based strategies (max_conversions/target_cpa/target_roas) are refused unless the account has an active, bidding-eligible conversion goal — check ppc_bing_conversion_tracking_status first. Google: ppc_bidding_strategy_update.

tools.name: ppc_platform_budget_update
tools.description: Cross-platform daily-budget update — Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads), LinkedIn Ads, TikTok Ads. Per-platform shape: • google_ads: pass campaign_id + daily_budget • meta_ads: CBO campaign budget: campaign_id + (daily_budget OR lifetime_budget). ABO ad-set budget: budget_level='ad_set' + ad_set_id + (daily_budget OR lifetime_budget) — most Meta accounts budget at the ad-set level, so if the campaign-level write refuses with a CBO error, the budget lives on the ad sets • microsoft_ads: pass campaign_id + daily_budget • linkedin_ads: pass campaign_id + (daily_budget OR total_budget); LinkedIn defaults USD for the money-object currencyCode and hard-caps every budget write at 100,000 • tiktok_ads: pass exactly one of campaign_id OR adgroup_id + daily_budget (TikTok supports budgets at both levels)

tools.name: ppc_platform_enable_resource
tools.description: Cross-platform enable — Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads), LinkedIn Ads, TikTok Ads. Same args as ppc_platform_pause_resource. Reverses a pause.

tools.name: ppc_platform_keyword_add
tools.description: Add a keyword to a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) ad group (connection_id + ad_group_id + text + match_type[exact|phrase|broad], optional bid). Google: ppc_keyword_add.

tools.name: ppc_platform_keyword_bid_update
tools.description: Set a keyword CPC bid on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) connection (pass connection_id + keyword_id + bid in account currency). For google_ads use ppc_keyword_bid_update. Bing keyword ids come from ppc_platform-side reads / keyword-performance.

tools.name: ppc_platform_keyword_match_type_change
tools.description: Change a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) keyword match type (connection_id + keyword_id + match_type). Bing may reject in-place edits; if so add a new keyword + pause the old. Google: ppc_keyword_match_type_change.

tools.name: ppc_platform_negative_keyword_add
tools.description: Add a negative keyword on a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) connection at ad_group OR campaign level (exactly one) + text + match_type. Mine ppc_metrics/search terms for waste. Google: ppc_negative_keyword_add.

tools.name: ppc_platform_pause_resource
tools.description: Cross-platform pause — Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads), LinkedIn Ads, TikTok Ads. Works on connections for any platform. resource_type per platform: • google_ads: campaign | ad_group | ad | keyword (ad/keyword require ad_group_id) • meta_ads: campaign | ad_set | ad • microsoft_ads: campaign | ad_group | ad | keyword • linkedin_ads: campaign | campaign_group (LinkedIn API doesn't expose ad-level status) • tiktok_ads: campaign | adgroup | ad Reverses with ppc_platform_enable_resource. For the rich Google-only mutation surface (keyword bid updates, match-type changes, asset attaches, etc.) use the ppc_* tools (40-tool family).

tools.name: ppc_platform_period_comparison
tools.description: Cross-platform period comparison at campaign level — Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads), LinkedIn Ads, TikTok Ads. Fetches each platform's native reporting API for two windows, diffs them, returns winners/losers by clicks delta. Same shape across all platforms; metric availability varies (Bing's reporting API is async-only — the response includes a note suggesting client-side diff from pull-metrics in that case).

tools.name: ppc_platform_responsive_search_ad_create
tools.description: Create a PAUSED Responsive Search Ad in a Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads) ad group. Bing requires >=3 headlines and >=2 descriptions. connection_id + ad_group_id + headlines[] + descriptions[] + final_url (+ path1/path2). Google: ppc_responsive_search_ad_create.

tools.name: ppc_reallocation_plan
tools.description: Cross-platform budget reallocation PLAN — a recommendation engine over the synced local metrics cache (same tables the guardrail sweep and ppc_digest read). Ranks the account's active PPC connections by marginal efficiency (CPA ascending; zero-conversion spenders flagged as reduce candidates; budget-limited connections whose CPA beats the account median as increase candidates) and proposes conservation-balanced monthly moves: [{from_connection, to_connection, monthly_amount_cents, rationale, apply_with}] netting to ZERO against current targets, step-capped at 25% of any connection's monthly target per plan. Also returns per-connection cards {platform, spend, cpa, roas, mtd pace vs settings.monthly_budget_target_cents, impression-share headroom, verdict: increase|hold|reduce, reasons[]}. HONESTY CONTRACT: this tool NEVER applies anything — it is read-only over synced data. Applying a move goes through the guardrailed budget tools it names per move: ppc_budget_update (google_ads) / ppc_platform_budget_update (all platforms), which enforce the programmatic spend ceilings and 2x step cap. `confidence` (high|medium|low) is deterministic and drops when a recommendation rests on weak evidence; `data_gaps[]` lists what the plan could not know: connections without budget targets (excluded from moves), zero-conversion spend that may be a tracking gap rather than waste, sub-10-conversion CPAs (low significance), unknown impression-share headroom (it reads stored data only and never fires live share reports — it names ppc_impression_share / ppc_bing_impression_share_report for that), stale syncs, mixed currencies. Connections without settings.monthly_budget_target_cents get verdict cards but no moves.

tools.name: ppc_recommendation_apply
tools.description: Apply a Google Ads recommendation by its resource_name (from ppc_recommendations_list). Uses Google's auto-generated default parameters for the rec type — same as the 'Apply' button in the Ads UI. Some rec types are gated to UI-only and will return a structured 400 with the reason — surface that to the user. Side effects vary by type (creates / updates resources). Confirm with the user before applying budget / bidding-strategy recs since they affect spend behavior.

tools.name: ppc_recommendations_list
tools.description: List Google Ads' own optimization recommendations for the account — each one includes type, scope (campaign / ad_group), and impact estimate (clicks delta, cost delta, conversions delta if Google has enough data). Sorted by absolute conversion delta. Source of high-leverage cheap wins; pair with ppc_recommendation_apply. Filter by `types` to focus on a category (e.g. ['KEYWORD', 'KEYWORD_MATCH_TYPE'] for keyword tuning, ['BIDDING_STRATEGY', 'TARGET_CPA_OPT_IN'] for bidding moves).

tools.name: ppc_responsive_search_ad_create
tools.description: Create a Responsive Search Ad. Requirements: • 3–15 headlines (each ≤ 30 chars). Mix product features + benefits + CTAs. • 2–4 descriptions (each ≤ 90 chars). Expand on headlines. • final_url (the landing page). Optional path1 / path2 (each ≤ 15 chars) for the display URL paths. Optional pinning: pinned_headlines = { '1': 1 } pins headline at index 0 to position 1 (Google won't rotate that headline out of slot 1). Use sparingly — Google's ML works best with all slots flexible. ALWAYS creates PAUSED — enable via ppc_enable_resource {resource_type:'ad', resource_id:<ad_id>, ad_group_id} after preview.

tools.name: ppc_search_terms_report
tools.description: Pull Google Ads' search_term_view — the exact queries that triggered ads, joined to keyword / ad_group / campaign with clicks / impressions / cost / conversions / CTR / avg CPC. The single most-mined report in any PPC review; source of negative-keyword candidates. Default last 28 days, 1000 rows. Use ppc_negative_keyword_add on any wasteful entries.

tools.name: ppc_segment_report
tools.description: Flexible Google Ads report — pass one or more dimensions and get clicks / impressions / cost / conversions / CTR / avg CPC grouped by the combined dimensions. ONE tool covers many named reports: • ['date'] — daily time series; pair with deploy date for 'did my change help?' • ['week'] / ['month'] — coarser trends • ['device'] — mobile/desktop/tablet split • ['day_of_week'] — when in the week • ['hour'] — dayparting / bid-by-hour candidates • ['geo_target_constant'] — geo breakdown (top spend states/cities/countries) • ['ad_network_type'] — Search vs Search Partners vs Display • ['query', 'page'] equivalents in Ads-land — try ['conversion_action'] for which conversions came from where Combine dimensions (e.g. ['date','device']) for 2-D pivots. Scope with campaign_id or ad_group_id; default is account-wide.

tools.name: ppc_sync
tools.description: Trigger a pull of campaigns + metrics from all active PPC connections — Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Ads (Bing Ads), LinkedIn Ads, TikTok Ads — (or a specific one via connection_id). SYNCHRONOUS — blocks the HTTP call for up to 300s (the client timeout matches the route budget, so long syncs no longer abort at 60s).
