Previews are reaped automatically; call project_vcs_branch_preview_teardown when done to free it sooner.

tools.name: project_vcs_branch_preview_status
tools.description: Check a branch preview started by project_vcs_branch_preview. Returns { status, ready, previewUrl, branch }. Re-probes the container, so a preview that finished compiling since you started it flips to ready here. Poll this instead of starting another preview — starting again spawns a second app. Omit session_id to list every live branch preview for the project.

tools.name: project_vcs_branch_preview_teardown
tools.description: Destroy a branch preview and its isolated app now. Optional — previews are swept automatically once they age out — but tear down when the review is finished so several open previews do not pile up. Irreversible: start a fresh preview to look again.

tools.name: project_vcs_branches
tools.description: List a project's Hiveku-native branches (default `main` first), backed by Supabase. Calling this also lazily initializes the project's VCS (`main` ref + initial commit), so the dev extension calls it right after downloading a project to ensure version control is ready. No GitHub involved.

tools.name: project_vcs_checkout
tools.description: Return a branch's full working tree as { files: [{path, content, encoding}] } so you can materialize it locally (switch branches). For `main` this returns the live project state; for a branch it returns the branch's off-to-the-side content. `encoding` is 'base64' for binary files.

tools.name: project_vcs_commit
tools.description: Hiveku-native commit on `main` — saves file edits/deletions AND records a commit entirely in Supabase (NO GitHub needed). This is the dev-flow equivalent of `git commit && git push`, used by the VSCode extension and by Claude Code working in a downloaded project folder. Works on EVERY project (GitHub-connected or DB-only) — unlike project_commit, which is GitHub-only. It saves the files via the normal versioned path, snapshots the new state as a checkpoint (the commit's content), and advances the project's `main` branch ref. The project's `main` is bootstrapped lazily the first time you commit/list — nothing to set up. When to use: 'commit my local changes back to Hiveku', 'save this edit session with a message'. After committing, trigger a deploy with deploy_site if you want it live. BODY: message (required) + files: [{path, content, encoding?}] (encoding 'base64' for binaries; `file_path` accepted as an alias for `path`). Optionally deletedFiles: [path]. Returns the new commit { id, message, checkpoint_hash, files_committed, files_deleted, created_at }. Revert later via project_checkpoint_restore using the commit's checkpoint_hash.

tools.name: project_vcs_compare
tools.description: Compare two branches' working trees file-by-file (status relative to going from `from` → `to`). Either side may be `main`. Returns { from, to, added, removed, modified, entries: [{path, status}] }. Use to review what a branch changed before merging.

tools.name: project_vcs_history
tools.description: List Hiveku-native VCS commit history (newest first) for a project, backed by Supabase. Each entry: { id, branch_name, message, actor, checkpoint_hash, files_committed, files_deleted, created_at }. `actor` says WHO made the commit — { kind: 'user'|'dashboard_agent'|'mcp_key'|'system', id, label } — derived server-side from the writer's credential at commit time (an MCP/agent commit shows kind 'mcp_key' with the API key's id + name; a dashboard commit shows kind 'user' with the user's id). `actor` is null on commits from before attribution existed — display 'unknown'; it is not inferable. Bootstraps `main` lazily, so even a never-before-committed project returns its initial commit. Use a commit's checkpoint_hash with project_checkpoint_restore to revert.

tools.name: project_vcs_merge
tools.description: Merge a branch into `main` with 3-way conflict flagging. Non-conflicting branch changes are applied to the live project (forming a `merge` commit); files changed on BOTH the branch and main (to different content) are returned in `conflicts` and left for you to resolve — they are NOT overwritten. The branch is not deleted, so you can fix conflicts and merge again. Returns { applied, deleted, conflicts, commit }.

tools.name: project_vcs_prune
tools.description: Prune orphaned branch-tree storage for a project — S3 tree objects not referenced by any branch or commit (accumulated from superseded branch commits). SAFE BY DEFAULT: runs as a dry run and only reports what WOULD be deleted unless you pass dry_run=false. Returns { scanned, referenced, orphaned[], deleted, dry_run }.

tools.name: project_version_log
tools.description: Combined chronological timeline of file edits, checkpoints, restores, and deploys for one project. One call answers 'what happened to this project today?' without juggling four separate endpoints. Each event has the same shape: { type, at, title, subtitle, ref_id, metadata }. Newest-first. Edit events carry metadata.actor = { kind: 'user'|'dashboard_agent'|'mcp_key'|'system', id, label } saying WHO made the edit — derived from the writer's credential at write time; null on rows from before attribution existed (display 'unknown'). Pass the response's `oldest_event_at` as `until` on the next call to paginate older events. Filters: • since / until — ISO timestamps for date-range scoping • file_path — limit to edits of one file (forces type=edit) • types — CSV of event types to include (edit, checkpoint, restore, deploy) • limit — max events (default 100, max 500)

tools.name: redesign_homepage_approve
tools.description: Mark the project's homepage as approved, unlocking the rest of the redesign workflow. Sets website_projects.redesign_homepage_approved_at — until this is set, redesign_start refuses with 409 "Homepage not approved". Call exactly once after the user confirms the homepage looks good.

tools.name: redesign_import
tools.description: Start the background scrape of all selected pages — fires Firecrawl per page and stages results in the 7-day scraper bucket. Returns 202 immediately; poll redesign_status to watch pages transition through scraping → assets_imported. After that, call redesign_promote per page (with the user-approved subset of asset URLs) to move them into durable storage.

tools.name: redesign_promote
tools.description: Move a staged redesign page from the scraper bucket (7-day TTL) into durable project storage. Downloads the agent-approved subset of discovered asset URLs into the project bucket as builder_project_assets rows, S3-copies HTML+markdown into the durable brand-assets/ prefix, and writes .hiveku/redesign/<slug>.json into the project workspace for the agent to read on its redesign turn. Pass assetUrls to filter; omit/null = promote all discovered.

tools.name: redesign_restart
tools.description: Abandon the current redesign session (status → partial_failed with reason="Aborted by user") so the next redesign_start opens a fresh row. Completed sessions cannot be restarted.

tools.name: redesign_select_pages
tools.description: Replace the selection set on a redesign session. Set pageIds to the array of builder_redesign_pages.id values the user chose. Passing an empty array clears the selection and the session falls back to status="pages_discovered".

tools.name: redesign_start
tools.description: Kick off page discovery for a redesign session. Calls Firecrawl /map on the source URL, persists each discovered page as builder_redesign_pages rows, and returns the list for the user to pick from. Refuses with 409 if redesign_homepage_approved_at is null. Returns {session:{id,status,total_pages}, pages:[{id,source_url,path,slug,title,screenshot_url}...]}.

tools.name: redesign_status
tools.description: Get the redesign session + all per-page rows in one call. Use as a polling endpoint while pages are mid-scrape or mid-promote. Without sessionId returns the most-recent session for the project (handy for "where did I leave off").

tools.name: room_async_jobs_await
tools.description: Convenience: poll for completed async jobs in a room. Shorthand for room_async_jobs_list with status='completed'. Use after firing delegate_to_department_background to gather results.

tools.name: room_async_jobs_list
tools.description: List orchestrator async-delegation jobs for a room (jobs fired by delegate_to_department_background). Filter by status / department.

tools.name: room_note_append
tools.description: Append to a room note (creates it if missing).

tools.name: room_note_delete
tools.description: Delete a room note by key. kind defaults to "note" (use "asset" or "resource" for those entry types).

tools.name: room_note_read
tools.description: Read one room note by key.

tools.name: room_note_write
tools.description: Write (replace) a room note.

tools.name: room_notes_list
tools.description: List notes scoped to an agent room (e.g. a marketing-strategy chat thread).

tools.name: room_rename
tools.description: Rename a room (orchestrator session). Truncated to 500 chars server-side. Use sparingly — only when the topic is stable enough that a title would help find it later.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: 🕷️ CRAWL4AI: Capture page screenshot (Firecrawl-backed)

tools.name: seo_add_competitor
tools.description: Add a competitor domain to track for an SEO project.

tools.name: seo_aeo_audit_get
tools.description: Read the LATEST persisted AEO audit results for a domain. No DataForSEO calls — pure DB read from seo_serp_features. Returns per-keyword AI-overview / featured-snippet / PAA presence + whether the domain is cited, plus ai_overview_references (top 20 per keyword: the sources the AI Overview actually cites, each {source, domain, url, title}, with ai_overview_reference_count for the uncapped total) — so 'who is AI citing instead of us' is answerable from stored history without paying for fresh probes. Same summary stats as seo_aeo_audit_run. `since` filters to only rows newer than that ISO date — handy for trend analysis.

tools.name: seo_aeo_audit_run
tools.description: Run an AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) audit for a domain. For each keyword, calls DataForSEO's organic SERP and parses the AI Overview, Featured Snippet, and People Also Ask blocks — records whether each feature is present AND whether the target domain is cited in them. PERSISTS every probe to seo_serp_features (append-only, so history works) and upserts seo_featured_snippets rows for keywords where a snippet exists. Returns a summary (readiness %, top opportunities) plus the per-keyword breakdown. Use this BEFORE recommending AEO changes so you have concrete data. Each keyword = 1 DataForSEO SERP call; cap at ~25 to control cost.

tools.name: seo_aeo_brand_audit
tools.description: Run the multi-provider LLM brand interrogation — asks several AI models about the brand and records how they answer, so you can see how the brand is represented in AI results. Requires a configured aeo_brand_profiles row (400 if none). Shares the SAME per-UTC-day audit budget the dashboard enforces, so it can refuse when the day is spent.

tools.name: seo_aeo_brand_audit_history
tools.description: Read the stored brand-audit history (aeo_brand_audits) — latest audit + up to `history` prior runs (default 12 ≈ a quarter of weekly sweeps, max 100), newest first. Pure DB read, no LLM spend — this is how you trend the core AEO KPI (overall_avg score movement, per-provider recognition/sentiment/share-of-voice dimensions in provider_scores, competitors_mentioned evidence, inaccuracies) without re-running the audit. Run a FRESH audit with seo_aeo_brand_audit (costs real LLM spend, budgeted per UTC day).

tools.name: seo_aeo_brand_profile_get
tools.description: Read the account's AEO brand profile (aeo_brand_profiles) — the audit subject config that gates the entire brand-audit engine: brand_name, domain, category, industry, region, and the competitor set that anchors share-of-voice scoring. Returns { profile: null } when the brand hasn't been configured yet — in that state seo_aeo_brand_audit 400s and the weekly brand-audit sweep cron skips the account, so create the profile with seo_aeo_brand_profile_upsert before any brand-audit work. One profile per account.

tools.name: seo_aeo_brand_profile_upsert
tools.description: Create or update the AEO brand profile — the required setup step for the brand-audit engine (seo_aeo_brand_audit 400s and the weekly sweep cron skips the account until this exists). Same field contract as the dashboard settings form. FULL-REPLACE semantics: brand_name, domain, and category are required on EVERY call (this is not a partial patch — read the current profile first with seo_aeo_brand_profile_get when editing). competitors may be omitted or empty — the first brand-audit run AI-seeds them from the engine's suggestions, and they stay editable here afterwards (max 10, each {name, domain?}).

tools.name: seo_aeo_rankings_sync
tools.description: Track keywords across AI engines. For each (keyword × search_engine) combination, ensures a website_rankings row exists (creates if missing, reuses if present), then queries DataForSEO's LLM Mentions API to populate the current citation position + ai_mentioned + mentions_count + ai_search_volume on each row. After this runs, the dashboard's AI ranking columns light up. Supported engines: • ai_overview — Google's generative SERP (most reliable AEO signal) • chatgpt — DataForSEO platform='chat_gpt' • perplexity — currently routed through 'google' (DataForSEO doesn't have a direct Perplexity platform yet) Each (keyword × engine) costs one DataForSEO LLM Mentions call. To create tracking rows without paying the per-keyword cost upfront, pass skip_sync=true; you can call seo_aeo_rankings_sync again later (or trigger sync via the existing ranking-sync cron) to populate them.

tools.name: seo_aeo_readiness
tools.description: Zero-cost AI-readiness check for a domain: llms.txt, robots.txt AI-crawler directives, homepage JSON-LD / meta / h1, and sitemap. Plain HTTPS fetches — spends nothing and persists nothing, so it is always safe to run first, before any credit-spending AEO audit.

tools.name: seo_audit_get
tools.description: Fetch one audit including issues + crawl summary.

tools.name: seo_audit_list
tools.description: List SEO site audits for a project (most recent first). project_id is required (server enforces).

tools.name: seo_audit_start
tools.description: Start a fresh site audit on a project (queues a DataForSEO crawl).

tools.name: seo_automated_reports
tools.description: List the scheduled/automated SEO reports for a project.

tools.name: seo_backlink_opportunities
tools.description: List backlink opportunities (gap analysis against competitors).

tools.name: seo_backlinks_list
tools.description: List discovered backlinks for a project domain (paginated). project_id is required (server enforces).

tools.name: seo_bing_backlinks
tools.description: Bing backlinks for a property.

tools.name: seo_bing_crawl_stats
tools.description: Bing crawl stats for a property (GetCrawlStats).

tools.name: seo_bing_inspect_url
tools.description: Inspect one URL's crawl/index state in Bing (GetUrlInfo) — the GSC seo_gsc_inspect_url analog.

tools.name: seo_bing_keywords
tools.description: Bing keyword performance for a property (GetKeywordPerformance).

tools.name: seo_bing_list_sitemaps
tools.description: List submitted sitemaps/feeds for a Bing property (GetFeeds).

tools.name: seo_bing_list_sites
tools.description: List the sites verified in this Bing Webmaster account (GetUserSites) — the GSC seo_gsc_list_sites analog. No site_url needed.

tools.name: seo_bing_pages
tools.description: Bing top pages for a property (GetPageStats). Bing's analog of seo_gsc_top_pages. Pair with seo_bing_query_stats to triangulate which queries drive which pages.

tools.name: seo_bing_period_comparison
tools.description: Compare two periods on Bing. Fetches the daily GetRankAndTrafficStats series once, then aggregates each window server-side: total clicks/impressions/CTR, impression-weighted avg position, daily rollups. Use for the same MoM / WoW / pre-vs-post-launch questions that seo_gsc_period_comparison answers, but for Bing traffic. Position deltas are signed Bing-style (lower = better; negative position_delta = improved). Limitations vs GSC: Bing's API has no dimensions param, so this is site-level only (no per-query/per-page diff). The daily_a + daily_b arrays let the agent reconstruct a trend chart, and seo_bing_query_stats / seo_bing_pages give the keyword / page detail if needed.

tools.name: seo_bing_query_stats
tools.description: Bing top user search queries for a property (GetQueryStats). Different from seo_bing_keywords (which is keyword-performance for tracked terms) — query_stats returns the queries Bing's traffic actually came from. Bing's analog of seo_gsc_search_queries.

tools.name: seo_bing_stats
tools.description: Bing rank + traffic stats for a property (GetRankAndTrafficStats).

tools.name: seo_bing_submit_sitemap
tools.description: Submit a sitemap URL to Bing (SubmitSiteMap).

tools.name: seo_bing_submit_url
tools.description: Submit a URL to Bing for re-crawl (SubmitUrl).

tools.name: seo_cannibalization
tools.description: Detected keyword cannibalization (multiple pages competing for the same query). Data source: computed every Sunday by the seo-analysis-sweep cron — queries where 2+ pages of the same domain each drew 50+ impressions (200+ combined) in the last 28 archived days. Empty (with a note) until GSC is connected and the first weekly run completes.

tools.name: seo_citations_audit
tools.description: Run a citation audit for a Google Business Profile connection: pulls the canonical NAP (name/address/phone/website) from the synced GBP listing, runs ONE DataForSEO Business Listings search for the business's public listings footprint, diffs every listing attributable to the business (primary + duplicates) for NAP consistency (normalized: phone digits-only, address tokenized with abbreviation canonicalization, name fuzzy), and checks a fixed major-directory list (Google, Yelp, Facebook, Bing Places, Apple Maps, BBB, Yellow Pages, Foursquare, Tripadvisor where category-relevant) using in-app signals. Returns directories_found / consistent / inconsistent (with per-field their_value vs expected) / missing_major (entries carry a basis field — 'no_signal' means presence is UNVERIFIED, not confirmed absent) and persists the snapshot. SPENDS DataForSEO CREDITS: one Business Listings search per run, metered under the account's monthly SEO research cap (same read-spend class as seo_research — no confirm step). A 24h server-side cooldown returns 429 with retry_at plus the stored audit. AUDIT ONLY — this never writes to any directory (citation submission is not offered). Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). Read the stored snapshot for free with seo_citations_get.

tools.name: seo_citations_get
tools.description: Read the STORED citation-audit snapshot for a GBP connection (canonical NAP, directories_found/consistent/inconsistent with per-field diffs, missing_major with per-directory basis, audited_at). Free, DB-only — never calls DataForSEO. Omit connection_id for a row per active GBP connection (audit: null = never audited; run seo_citations_audit to compute one).

tools.name: seo_competitor_changes
tools.description: Recent changes detected on tracked competitor sites.

tools.name: seo_competitors_list
tools.description: List a project's tracked competitors. project_id is required (server enforces).

tools.name: seo_connection_create
tools.description: Create an SEO data-source connection (BYOK). BING WEBMASTER is the simplest — just { platform: 'bing_webmaster', site_url, api_key } (the key from bing.com/webmasters -> Settings -> API access; no OAuth). GOOGLE SEARCH CONSOLE: { platform: 'google_search_console', site_url, client_id, client_secret, refresh_token } (scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters — the FULL scope, not .readonly, or sitemap submit/delete will 403). GOOGLE BUSINESS PROFILE: { platform: 'google_business_profile', client_id, client_secret, refresh_token } then set gbp_account_id/gbp_location_id via seo_connection_update. After create, call the connection's test/sync (seo_sync) to verify. For a Bing Webmaster site not yet in the tool, the user can one-click 'Import from Google Search Console' at bing.com/webmasters first.

tools.name: seo_connection_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an SEO connection (sets is_active=false). Preserves the row for audit history; downstream tools that filter by is_active will stop finding it. To clean up a phantom or stuck pending row created during OAuth setup.

tools.name: seo_connection_update
tools.description: Update an SEO connection — set the chosen site_url (GSC), gbp_account_id + gbp_location_id (GBP), display_name, or is_active. When the final identifier lands (site_url for GSC; both gbp_account_id + gbp_location_id for GBP), connection_status auto-flips from 'pending' to 'connected' so the sync route picks it up. Credentials reset status to 'pending' on update.

tools.name: seo_connections_list
tools.description: List connected SEO data sources (DataForSEO/GSC/Bing Webmaster/Google Business Profile).

tools.name: seo_content_decay
tools.description: Pages with declining organic traffic (good refresh candidates). Data source: computed every Sunday by the seo-analysis-sweep cron from the permanent Search Console query/page archive (last 28 archived days vs the prior 28; floors 100 impressions + 5 clicks). Empty (with a note) until GSC is connected and the first weekly run completes; rows a human re-statused are preserved across re-runs.

tools.name: seo_content_gaps
tools.description: Find content gap opportunities vs a competitor domain. project_id is required (server enforces).

tools.name: seo_core_web_vitals
tools.description: Core Web Vitals for any URL, field + lab in one call. FIELD = Chrome UX Report real-user p75 LCP/INP/CLS — the numbers Google actually ranks on (GSC's CWV report has no API; this is the only programmatic source). LAB = PageSpeed Insights Lighthouse: performance/accessibility/best-practices/SEO scores plus the top improvement opportunities ranked by estimated savings. Platform API key, no per-account connection — works on any URL including competitors. If field data 404s for an exact URL (thin traffic), retry with origin= for site-level data. include=field skips the slow (~20-60s) Lighthouse run.

tools.name: seo_create_project
tools.description: Create a new SEO project to track a domain with target country/language

tools.name: seo_cro_audit
tools.description: Heuristic conversion-rate (CRO) audit of ONE landing page — v1 is audit only, NOT experiment tracking (run experiments as pm_tasks for now). Fetches the page (SSRF-guarded), then scores five sections 0-100: speed (CrUX real-user p75 + PageSpeed lab), clarity (H1/title/meta, image alt coverage), friction (form field counts, labels, a conversion path existing at all), trust (testimonials, reviews, guarantees, badges, social-proof numbers, visible phone), and cta (action-verb copy + an above-fold heuristic: header/hero or first 35% of the page). Returns named findings each carrying {issue, why_it_costs_conversions, fix} plus a quick_wins shortlist of cheap edits. Pure read: nothing persisted, no credit spend, works on any public URL including competitors. If the web-signals key is missing only the speed section degrades — the rest still audits.

tools.name: seo_deliverable_delete
tools.description: Delete a deliverable.

tools.name: seo_deliverable_get
tools.description: Fetch one deliverable with its full content + recommendations.

tools.name: seo_deliverable_list
tools.description: List saved SEO deliverables (audits, content briefs, strategy docs, etc.).

tools.name: seo_deliverable_save
tools.description: Save (create) a new SEO deliverable.

tools.name: seo_deliverable_update
tools.description: Update an existing deliverable.

tools.name: seo_eeat_scores
tools.description: E-E-A-T (Experience/Expertise/Authority/Trust) scores for the account's top Search Console pages (up to 10/account, re-scored monthly by the Sunday seo-analysis-sweep). Pages are fetched live and LLM-scored (account-metered, budget-gated) with a static-signal fallback — check *_signals.method ('llm' vs 'heuristic_only') for scoring depth. competitor_scores is not computed. Empty (with a note) until GSC is connected and the first sweep completes.

tools.name: seo_entity_check
tools.description: AEO entity audit via the Google Knowledge Graph: does this brand/person/topic resolve to a KG entity? Returns kg_id, canonical name, types, description and resultScore per match. A brand with no entity is a string, not a citable source — that absence is itself an audit finding. Use kg_id + official_url in schema.org sameAs/mainEntityOfPage markup, and compare resultScore against competitors as an entity-strength signal. Platform API key, works for any query.

tools.name: seo_featured_snippets
tools.description: Featured-snippet opportunities (keywords where the snippet is winnable).

tools.name: seo_ga4_admin_scopes
tools.description: Does this Google Analytics connection's token carry the analytics.edit scope? Read-only preflight — call it before a write wave to learn the customer must reconnect, instead of discovering it from a 403 halfway through a change.

tools.name: seo_ga4_conversion_audit
tools.description: START HERE for GA4 conversions. Which key events exist, which URL rules feed them, and which recorded NOTHING in the window. A key event with zero events is a Google Ads conversion action (origin GOOGLE_ANALYTICS) reporting zero with no error shown anywhere — the Ads side looks configured and simply never fires. Many Ads conversions ARE imported GA4 key events, so this is where an 'Ads conversion stopped recording' investigation starts.

tools.name: seo_ga4_data_streams_list
tools.description: List a GA4 property's data streams (name, type, defaultUri, measurementId). Event create rules hang off a STREAM, not the property, so this is the lookup that makes every rule action possible.

tools.name: seo_ga4_event_create_rule_create
tools.description: TURN A URL INTO A CONVERSION. GA4 cannot mark 'a page_view whose URL contains /thank-you' as a conversion — only a whole event name — so the chain is: this rule creates a distinct event, then seo_ga4_key_event_create marks it, then Google Ads imports it. TWO TRAPS THIS TOOL HANDLES FOR YOU. GA4 has NO page_path parameter: the URL lives in page_location, which is the FULL url including host and any ?utm_ query string — so EQUALS never matches a bare path, and CONTAINS is the right default. And a rule with no event_name condition fires on nearly EVERY event GA4 collects; this pins the source event automatically. GA4 never backfills, so a new rule starts at zero. v1alpha, and rules hang off a DATA STREAM, not the property.

tools.name: seo_ga4_event_create_rule_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE. GA4 stops creating the destination event entirely, so any key event on that name — and any Google Ads conversion imported from it — records nothing from that moment on, with no error anywhere. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call does NOT delete; it returns requires_confirm with a preview and issues no write. Repeat with confirm: true (strict boolean). v1alpha.

tools.name: seo_ga4_event_create_rule_update
tools.description: Change a GA4 event create rule's destination event, conditions, parameter copying or mutations. conditions is a REPEATED field — a patch REPLACES the whole list, it does not append, so send every condition you want to keep. Renaming the destination event leaves any key event on the OLD name receiving nothing, silently flatlining its imported Google Ads conversion. v1alpha. TWO-STEP CONFIRM, because unlike GTM (where a write is a draft that serves nothing until publish) a GA4 change is LIVE ON RETURN and propagates into every Google Ads conversion imported from it. The first call writes nothing and returns a preview naming each field's current value, new value and consequence. Repeat with confirm: true.

tools.name: seo_ga4_event_create_rules_list
tools.description: List GA4 event create rules — the URL-driven rules that turn a thank-you-page URL into a distinct event. They live on a DATA STREAM (properties/{p}/dataStreams/{s}/eventCreateRules), NOT the property, and the resource exists only in Admin API v1alpha, so it can change without notice. Sweeps every stream unless data_stream is given.

tools.name: seo_ga4_key_event_create
tools.description: Mark a GA4 event as a key event (a conversion). Google Ads conversion actions imported from GA4 read this. GA4 ACCEPTS A KEY EVENT FOR AN EVENT NAME IT HAS NEVER RECEIVED, and it then records nothing forever with no error — confirm the event actually arrives with seo_ga4_conversion_audit. If the conversion is a page URL rather than an existing event, create the event first with seo_ga4_event_create_rule_create. counting_method matters: ONCE_PER_SESSION for lead forms (a reloaded thank-you page counts once), ONCE_PER_EVENT for purchases. default_value and default_currency must be sent TOGETHER — GA4 rejects a value with no currency. Needs the analytics.edit scope; a connection authorized before it was requested must reconnect.

tools.name: seo_ga4_key_event_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE. Un-marks a GA4 event as a conversion. Any Google Ads conversion action imported from it stops recording immediately and SILENTLY — the Ads conversion action keeps existing and flatlines, and if it sits in a bidding goal, Smart Bidding loses that signal. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call does NOT delete — it returns requires_confirm with a preview and issues no write at all. Repeat the identical call with confirm: true (a strict boolean; the string 'true' only previews).

tools.name: seo_ga4_key_event_update
tools.description: Change a GA4 key event's counting method and/or default value. eventName is IMMUTABLE — renaming means create + delete. Both changes propagate AUTOMATICALLY to Google Ads conversions imported from this key event, shifting reported volume or value without anyone touching Google Ads, which moves CPA and forces Smart Bidding to relearn. Not retroactive. The response names the consequence. TWO-STEP CONFIRM, because unlike GTM (where a write is a draft that serves nothing until publish) a GA4 change is LIVE ON RETURN and propagates into every Google Ads conversion imported from it. The first call writes nothing and returns a preview naming each field's current value, new value and consequence. Repeat with confirm: true.

tools.name: seo_ga4_key_events_list
tools.description: List GA4 key events (the conversions) with countingMethod and defaultValue — the two settings that make an imported Google Ads conversion wrong. GA4 Admin API v1beta properties/{p}/keyEvents. (conversionEvents is the deprecated name for the same thing.)

tools.name: seo_gbp_attributes
tools.description: Location attributes for a GBP connection, in one round-trip: `current` (attributes actually set), `available` (the full catalog Google offers for the location's category), and `audit` (completeness summary + the missing list). Unset attributes are invisible to Google's filtered local searches ('wheelchair accessible', 'outdoor seating') — filling them is usually the cheapest local-visibility win. Live Google call. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). Apply changes with seo_gbp_attributes_update.

tools.name: seo_gbp_attributes_update
tools.description: Patch location attributes on a GBP connection. Changes publish DIRECTLY to the client's live listing — they alter how the business appears in Google's filtered local searches. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT apply — it returns a preview (attribute names + count, connection name) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to apply. Each entry: { name: 'attributes/<id>', values?: [...], repeatedEnumValue?: {...}, uriValues?: [...] } per the Business Information Attributes resource — only the named attributes change (attributeMask derives from them). Discover attribute ids + gaps with seo_gbp_attributes (its audit.missing list). Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile).

tools.name: seo_gbp_discover_locations
tools.description: List Google Business Profile accounts + locations accessible to a connection. Returns an 'accounts' array; each account has a 'locations' array with location_id (resource name) + location_title. After picking, call seo_connection_update with both gbp_account_id AND gbp_location_id — status auto-flips to 'connected' once both are set.

tools.name: seo_gbp_insights
tools.description: Daily Google Business Profile insights: website clicks, call clicks, direction requests, mobile/desktop impressions on Maps vs Search.

tools.name: seo_gbp_listing
tools.description: Full GBP listing snapshot: Listing Score with per-field breakdown, NAP block, verification + duplicate status, and score history. Reads the synced DB snapshot (no live Google call — the 6h sync cron keeps it warm). Get connection_id from seo_connections_list; omit it to return a row per active GBP connection (needs_setup connections return state-only rows).

tools.name: seo_gbp_location
tools.description: Live Business Information read for a GBP connection's location: title, phone, categories, website, address, hours, service area, open status, place metadata. Also refreshes the cached listing snapshot. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). Edit the core listing fields (NAP / hours / categories / description / website) with seo_gbp_location_update.

tools.name: seo_gbp_location_update
tools.description: Edit the core Google Business Profile listing fields — the NAP/hours/categories lane: title (business name), phoneNumbers, profile (description), regularHours, specialHours, categories, websiteUri, storefrontAddress. Changes publish DIRECTLY to the client's live listing, and name/address/category edits can trigger Google re-verification. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT apply — it returns a preview (the fields + values being changed, the connection name, the cached listing title) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to apply. Only the fields present in `updates` change (the PATCH updateMask derives from them); unknown fields are rejected with a 400. Field shapes follow Google's Business Information API Location resource: title and websiteUri are strings; phoneNumbers = { primaryPhone, additionalPhones? }; profile = { description }; regularHours = { periods: [{ openDay, openTime: { hours, minutes? }, closeDay, closeTime }] }; specialHours = { specialHourPeriods: [...] }; categories = { primaryCategory: { name: 'categories/gcid:...' }, additionalCategories? }; storefrontAddress = a postalAddress object. Read current values first with seo_gbp_location. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). For attribute toggles use seo_gbp_attributes_update instead.

tools.name: seo_gbp_media
tools.description: The GBP location's public photo gallery (live read, no DB cache): each item's media_id (feed it to seo_gbp_media_delete), category (COVER / PROFILE / LOGO / EXTERIOR / INTERIOR / PRODUCT / AT_WORK / FOOD_AND_DRINK / MENU / COMMON_AREA / ROOMS / TEAMS / ADDITIONAL), format, googleUrl/thumbnail, dimensions, view count — plus total_media_item_count. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). Add photos with seo_gbp_media_add.

tools.name: seo_gbp_media_add
tools.description: Add a PHOTO to the GBP location's gallery from a public https URL. The photo publishes PUBLICLY on the client's live listing (Google fetches it from source_url). Categories COVER / PROFILE / LOGO REPLACE the listing's primary imagery instead of appending to the gallery — use them deliberately. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT publish — it returns a preview (category, source_url, media_format, whether primary imagery is replaced) with requires_confirm: true; URL and category validation run at this step, so a bad input fails before confirm. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to publish. source_url must be https and resolve to a public host; videos are rejected (photo-only). Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile).

tools.name: seo_gbp_media_delete
tools.description: Permanently remove one media item from the GBP location's live public gallery (deleting a COVER / PROFILE / LOGO item removes the listing's primary imagery). TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT delete — it fetches the live item and returns a preview (category, format, googleUrl/thumbnail, create time, view count) with requires_confirm: true, so you see exactly what is being removed; a bad media_id fails at this step. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to delete. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile); get media_id from seo_gbp_media.

tools.name: seo_gbp_overview
tools.description: Cached GBP dashboard overview for one connection: insights totals + daily trend (last `days`, default 30), review stats (count / average rating / unreplied count), and the cached listing snapshot. DB-only — no live Google call. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile).

tools.name: seo_gbp_review_reply
tools.description: Publish the business-owner reply on a Google Business Profile review. The reply POSTS PUBLICLY on the client's live listing (and replaces any existing owner reply). Max 4096 characters. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT publish — it returns a preview (the reply text + length, the review being replied to, the connection name) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to publish. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile); get review_id from seo_gbp_reviews. Remove a reply with seo_gbp_review_reply_delete. NOTE: GBP POSTS (What's New / offers / events) deliberately have NO direct tool in this lane — publish them via the social lane: social_create_post with platform google_business_profile (goes through the approval queue).

tools.name: seo_gbp_review_reply_delete
tools.description: Permanently remove the public business-owner reply from a GBP review on the client's live listing. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT delete — it returns a preview (the existing reply, the review) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to delete. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile); get review_id from seo_gbp_reviews.

tools.name: seo_gbp_reviews
tools.description: Recent GBP reviews with reply state. Filter by rating range.

tools.name: seo_gbp_services
tools.description: The GBP location's service menu (live Business Information read): serviceItems — structured services (Google-defined serviceTypeId for the category) and free-form services (merchant-defined label under a category), each optionally priced — plus title/categories context for picking valid category ids. Services show publicly on the listing and feed Google's 'services' local-search filters. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). Edit with seo_gbp_services_update.

tools.name: seo_gbp_services_update
tools.description: Replace the GBP location's service menu. This REPLACES the ENTIRE service list on the client's live listing — every current service missing from service_items is REMOVED, and an empty array removes ALL services. The menu publishes publicly. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT apply — it returns a live diff summary (current_count / new_count / added / removed / kept service names) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to apply. Each item has EXACTLY ONE of structuredServiceItem ({ serviceTypeId, description? } — serviceTypeId comes from the category's Google-defined service types) or freeFormServiceItem ({ category: 'gcid:...', label: { displayName, description?, languageCode? } }), plus optional price ({ currencyCode, units?, nanos? }). Read the current list first with seo_gbp_services (it also returns the location's categories for free-form category ids). Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile).

tools.name: seo_generate_sitemap
tools.description: Generate sitemap.xml content from the project's published website_pages (honors show_in_sitemap unless includeNoIndex is set in sitemap_settings). Returns { file_path: 'public/sitemap.xml', content }. Commit via project_commit to save.

tools.name: seo_gsc_delete_sitemap
tools.description: Remove a sitemap from Google Search Console — DELETE /sites/:site/sitemaps/:feedpath. Use during template/structure migrations when an old sitemap URL is no longer canonical.

tools.name: seo_gsc_discover_sites
tools.description: List the GSC-verified sites accessible to a connection's OAuth user. Returns 'sites' (queryable: siteOwner / siteFullUser) and 'restricted_sites' (siteRestrictedUser — appears in /sites but returns 403 on data queries). After picking one, call seo_connection_update with {site_url: '<picked>'} — that flips status to 'connected'. If the user has only delegated read access and 0 sites appear, the hint will tell the agent to use sc-domain:<domain> directly.

tools.name: seo_gsc_get_sitemap
tools.description: Per-sitemap detail for one feedpath — lastSubmitted, lastDownloaded, isPending, isSitemapsIndex, errors[], warnings[], contents[]. Use this when seo_gsc_list_sitemaps shows a sitemap with submitted > indexed to find out what's wrong.

tools.name: seo_gsc_index_coverage
tools.description: Best-available substitute for GSC's Index Coverage report. Google's public API has NO bulk coverage endpoint — this tool fans out URL Inspection per URL and buckets the results by coverage_state (e.g. 'Submitted and indexed' | 'Discovered - currently not indexed' | 'Crawled - currently not indexed' | 'Duplicate without user-selected canonical' | ...). Use to surface index health for a known URL set (sitemap entries, top-traffic pages, new launches). Capped at 50 URLs per call — split into batches for larger sites.

tools.name: seo_gsc_inspect_url
tools.description: Run GSC's URL Inspection on a specific page. Returns indexability + mobile-usability + rich-result analysis. NOTE: Google's public API only inspects the indexed snapshot — there is no liveTest equivalent, and manualActions / securityIssues are not exposed in this response (they're UI-only in Search Console).

tools.name: seo_gsc_list_sitemaps
tools.description: List sitemaps registered in GSC for a property + their submission state.

tools.name: seo_gsc_list_sites
tools.description: List Google Search Console verified sites for the account.

tools.name: seo_gsc_period_comparison
tools.description: Compare two time periods on the same site and return winners/losers + rank climbers/droppers. Fetches both periods, joins on the supplied dimensions, computes click/impression/position deltas. Top use cases: post-launch review (period_b=after, period_a=before), algorithm-update analysis, MoM/WoW reporting. Position deltas are signed Google-style (lower = better; rank_climbers have negative position_delta).

tools.name: seo_gsc_search_analytics
tools.description: Full multi-dimension Search Analytics query — the canonical GSC report tool. Pass dimensions as ANY combination of date | query | page | country | device | searchAppearance (e.g. ['query','page'] answers 'which query drives which page?'). Filters support equals | notEquals | contains | notContains | includingRegex | excludingRegex. Up to 25000 rows per call; paginate with start_row.

tools.name: seo_gsc_search_queries
tools.description: Top queries from GSC for a property (dimensions: query). Default window: last 28 days. search_type: 'web'|'image'|'video'|'discover'|'googleNews'.

tools.name: seo_gsc_submit_sitemap
tools.description: Submit a sitemap to Google Search Console — PUT /sites/:site/sitemaps/:feedpath. Use after a redeploy that added or changed indexable URLs. Idempotent — re-submitting an existing sitemap is fine.

tools.name: seo_gsc_time_series
tools.description: Daily clicks/impressions/CTR/position time series. Convenience wrapper over seo_gsc_search_analytics with dimensions=['date']. Use to answer 'did my change help?' — overlay a deploy date on the trend. Accepts the same filters[] (e.g. {dimension:'page', expression:'/blog/', operator:'contains'} to scope the trend to one section).

tools.name: seo_gsc_top_pages
tools.description: Top pages from GSC (dimensions: page). Same params as seo_gsc_search_queries.

tools.name: seo_gtm_install
tools.description: Install a GTM container's snippet into one tier's site-wide custom code — the <script> block in HEAD and the <noscript> iframe in BODY. GTM needs BOTH; a head-only install silently loses no-JS and some privacy-blocked traffic. STRICT TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (confirm omitted, or anything other than the boolean true) returns requires_confirm with a preview and changes NOTHING. Repeat the identical call with confirm: true to write. NEVER DUPLICATES, BUT DOES REPAIR. It is a no-op only when the container is FULLY installed site-wide (both halves). Otherwise it fixes what is wrong, writing only what is missing and leaving what is present byte-for-byte: a half install gets its missing box added (and the response says which, since an iframe-only install means the container never loads at all, while a script-only one merely undercounts no-JS traffic), and a container living only in page overrides is MOVED site-wide in one transaction. If a page override box holds other code alongside the snippet, the call refuses and names the page rather than splicing customer HTML. SAVED IS NOT LIVE: the write takes effect on the NEXT DEPLOY of that tier, and the preview tier additionally requires run_in_preview (see project_custom_code_preview_toggle).

tools.name: seo_gtm_install_status
tools.description: Is the GTM container the agent is editing actually installed on the site? Reports per tier (preview / development / staging / production), head and body separately: not installed, installed, installed-but-a-different-container, or installed more than once. ALWAYS call this before and after seo_gtm_tag_create / seo_gtm_publish. A published container that is not installed fires on nobody, and every tag call still reports success — that failure is invisible from both ends. The three findings that cost money: WRONG CONTAINER (the site runs a container the agent is not editing; both ids are named, and conversions recorded is zero), DUPLICATE INSTALL (the same container twice on one rendered page, which DOUBLE-COUNTS every conversion — it reads as performance improving and corrupts every downstream CPA and ROAS), and TIER DRIFT (verified on staging, never installed on production). Also flags a head-only install (loses no-JS traffic) and a row that is disabled or over the injection cap — which reads as installed in the UI and ships on no deploy, ever. SCOPE: reads project_custom_code. A container hardcoded in the site's own source is invisible here — use analytics_diagnose_tracking for that. Reports the SAVED state, never the LIVE one.

tools.name: seo_gtm_publish
tools.description: Publish a GTM container version — THE step that CHANGES THE CLIENT'S LIVE SITE: every tag in the version starts serving to real visitors immediately. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT publish — it returns a preview (container name + public id, the version's tags, what is currently live, and the workspace's pending changes with a note that those are NOT in this version) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to publish. Get version_id from seo_gtm_version_create. Requires the Tag Manager publish scopes (tagmanager.edit.containerversions + tagmanager.publish, requested since 2026-08-23) — a connection authorized before then gets a reconnect-Google-Analytics error naming the fix. Remember the documented failure mode this pipeline exists to close: a container whose conversion tags were never published recorded nothing for months. CONTAINER PINNING: the first time a container is used successfully on a connection, that container is claimed from Google's own answer and stored on the connection. A later call naming a DIFFERENT container is refused with a 403 naming both — the connection's Google user can legitimately reach containers belonging to other tenants, so the pin is what stops one account editing another's container. Retrying the same call will not help; either use the pinned container, or clear the pin deliberately with seo_connection_update (gtm_container_path: null) and let the next successful call re-claim it.

tools.name: seo_gtm_status
tools.description: Google Tag Manager status for a Google Analytics connection (GTM rides the SAME seo_connections row — one Google authorization covers both). Without container_path: lists the GTM accounts + containers the connection's Google user can see (container_path + public GTM-XXXXXX id). With container_path: the publish preview for that container — container name, the default workspace's PENDING CHANGES (what the next version would contain), a draft-vs-live tag split (draft_only tags are NOT serving), the currently-live version, and a loud warning when the container has NEVER been published (the documented failure mode: a never-published container silently losing every Ads conversion). Also returns triggers[] — every trigger in the workspace, the live version and the built-ins, each with trigger_id, name, type, filters, load_only and spa_safe, and each tag's firing_triggers[] resolved BY NAME rather than as a bare numeric id. That is what lets you bind a conversion tag to a click trigger a human already built, without creating a duplicate. Also returns variables[] — variable_id, name, type, type_label, reference (the {{Name}} form) and data_layer_key (the dataLayer key it actually reads, which is independent of its display name). variable_id is what seo_gtm_variable_get / _update / _delete take, and nothing else emits it. Built-in variables are excluded because they have no numeric id. Read this before seo_gtm_tag_create and before seo_gtm_version_create / seo_gtm_publish. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_analytics). CONTAINER PINNING: the first time a container is used successfully on a connection, that container is claimed from Google's own answer and stored on the connection. A later call naming a DIFFERENT container is refused with a 403 naming both — the connection's Google user can legitimately reach containers belonging to other tenants, so the pin is what stops one account editing another's container. Retrying the same call will not help; either use the pinned container, or clear the pin deliberately with seo_connection_update (gtm_container_path: null) and let the next successful call re-claim it.

tools.name: seo_gtm_tag_create
tools.description: Create a tag in a GTM container's default workspace — a WORKSPACE DRAFT ONLY: nothing serves until the container is published (seo_gtm_version_create then seo_gtm_publish), and an unpublished conversion tag records nothing however complete it looks in GTM. No confirm gate for that reason. TAG TYPES: 'ga4_event' (measurement_id 'G-XXXXXXXXXX' + event_name), 'ads_conversion' (conversion_id + conversion_label from the Ads conversion action's tag setup), 'bing_uet' / 'bing_uet_event' (uet_tag_id), 'meta_pixel' / 'meta_event' (meta_pixel_id), 'custom_html'. Bing and Meta are emitted as templated Custom HTML because GTM has no first-party type for them; bing_uet and meta_pixel are BASE tags that fire once per document load. CONVERSION VALUE: pass conversion_value + currency_code (+ transaction_id to deduplicate) as a literal or a '{{Variable}}' reference. Omit them and the tag sends NO VALUE — the conversion still records, but every one is worth the same, so tROAS bids against a constant. Create a dataLayer variable with seo_gtm_variable_create and reference it here. FIRING TRIGGERS: pass firing_trigger_ids (existing ids from seo_gtm_status, which now returns every trigger's name/type/filters so you can bind to a click trigger a human already built) OR create_trigger. 'all_pages'; 'page_path' (+ trigger_page_path, e.g. /thank-you), which defaults to trigger_type 'both' — one pageview AND one historyChange trigger, because on a Next.js site a form submit is a client-side route change a pageview trigger never sees while a hard landing is a document load historyChange never sees, and either alone has a silent blind spot; or 'click' / 'link_click' / 'form_submit' (+ trigger_match_on / trigger_match_value) for the click conversions — tap-to-call, WhatsApp CTA, PDF download, booking button. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_analytics); get container_path from seo_gtm_status. CONTAINER PINNING: the first time a container is used successfully on a connection, that container is claimed from Google's own answer and stored on the connection. A later call naming a DIFFERENT container is refused with a 403 naming both — the connection's Google user can legitimately reach containers belonging to other tenants, so the pin is what stops one account editing another's container. Retrying the same call will not help; either use the pinned container, or clear the pin deliberately with seo_connection_update (gtm_container_path: null) and let the next successful call re-claim it.

tools.name: seo_gtm_tag_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Delete a GTM tag from the workspace. It stops working on the NEXT PUBLISH, not immediately, so the damage surfaces later than the action. A deleted conversion tag stops recording — the Google Ads or GA4 conversion it feeds flatlines with no error anywhere. Prefer paused: true on seo_gtm_tag_update, which is reversible. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call does NOT delete — it returns a preview and touches nothing. Repeat with confirm: true (a strict boolean; the string 'true' only previews). Draft-only: the change lands in the workspace and serves nothing until seo_gtm_version_create then seo_gtm_publish. CONTAINER PINNING: the first time a container is used successfully on a connection, that container is claimed from Google's own answer and stored on the connection. A later call naming a DIFFERENT container is refused with a 403 naming both — the connection's Google user can legitimately reach containers belonging to other tenants, so the pin is what stops one account editing another's container. Retrying the same call will not help; either use the pinned container, or clear the pin deliberately with seo_connection_update (gtm_container_path: null) and let the next successful call re-claim it.

tools.name: seo_gtm_tag_get
tools.description: Read one GTM tag in full — every stored field, its fingerprint, and referenced_by (what else in the container depends on it). Read this before any update: an update replaces the entity, so you need to know what is currently there. A GET, so it does not require the write scope. CONTAINER PINNING: the first time a container is used successfully on a connection, that container is claimed from Google's own answer and stored on the connection. needs keyword + location_code) local-finder-serp — local-finder variation SITE AUDIT DEEP DIVE (Tranche C) — most need `target` = a prior site-audit task_id from seo_audit_start: instant-page — fast single-page audit (needs url, no task_id) duplicate-content / duplicate-tags — content + meta dupes redirect-chains / non-indexable — crawl issues internal-links — link graph keyword-density — on-page term frequency BACKLINKS DEEP DIVE (Tranche D, needs target or domain): backlinks-timeseries — link velocity / growth & decay (use date_from + date_to) backlinks-anchors — anchor-text distribution backlinks-competitors — link-overlap-based competitor discovery backlinks-history — long-term link history bulk-page-summary — backlink summaries for many URLs at once (needs targets[]) REPUTATION / CONTENT ANALYSIS (Tranche F): sentiment-analysis — sentiment around a brand/term (needs keyword) content-mention-search — find web pages mentioning a term content-summary — aggregate sentiment + volume MERCHANT + APP DATA (Tranche G): amazon-products / google-shopping-products (needs query) amazon-reviews (needs target = ASIN) google-app-info / apple-app-info (needs app_id — package name for Play, numeric for Apple) AEO/GEO (answer-engine optimization): aeo-audit — multi-keyword feature-presence report (needs keywords[]; tools.name: seo_task_implement

The agent edits the website project, typechecks, test-builds, then STAGES the production deploy behind the approval rail (it never ships on its own; approval happens via agent_approval_approve or the user's SEO workspace). TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) dispatches NOTHING — it returns { requires_confirm: true, preview } with the task title/description, target website project (name + domain), and resolved page anchor. Show it to the user, then repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true (strict boolean) to dispatch the paid agent turn. Only open tasks (todo / queued / blocked / need_info) can be implemented; a running session 409s (never double-dispatches), an already-deployed task 409s. Billing gates match the interactive chat (402 when the AI budget or free daily limit is exhausted). After dispatch, poll seo_task_implement_status.

Performs the same status-sync writes as the dashboard (deployment linking, task auto-complete) — safe to poll.

tools.description: Hub-and-spoke topic clusters (pillar pages + cluster keywords).

tools.name: seo_track_keyword
tools.description: Start tracking a keyword's rank position over time for a target domain — creates the live-tracker row the daily ranking worker checks AND queues the first check immediately (rank data within minutes; read history via seo_rankings_list view=history with the returned ranking.id). ranking_type='local' with business_name tracks the LOCAL PACK position; AI engines (chatgpt/perplexity/ai_overview/claude/gemini) track citation mentions. The route auto-derives a stable goal_id from (account, target_domain) when goal_id is omitted — so all keywords tracking the same domain group together. Pass goal_id explicitly only if you want to subdivide tracking within a domain.

tools.name: seo_tracked_keyword_delete
tools.description: Stop tracking a keyword.

tools.name: seo_tracked_keywords_list
tools.description: List keywords currently being tracked for rank monitoring.

tools.name: serp_locations
tools.description: Utility tool for serp_organic_live_advanced to get list of availible locations.

tools.name: serp_organic_live_advanced
tools.description: Get organic search results for a keyword in specified search engine

tools.name: serp_youtube_locations
tools.description: Utility tool to get list of available locations for: serp_youtube_organic_live_advanced, serp_youtube_video_info_live_advanced, serp_youtube_video_comments_live_advanced, serp_youtube_video_subtitles_live_advanced.

tools.name: serp_youtube_organic_live_advanced
tools.description: provides top 20 blocks of youtube search engine results for a keyword

tools.name: serp_youtube_video_comments_live_advanced
tools.description: provides data on the video comments you specify

tools.name: serp_youtube_video_info_live_advanced
tools.description: provides data on the video you specify

tools.name: serp_youtube_video_subtitles_live_advanced
tools.description: provides data on the video subtitles you specify

tools.name: shopify_admin
tools.description: Invoke a Shopify Admin API action via the builder's named-action proxy (the Admin token stays server-side). admin_action is the named handler (e.g. 'ping', 'get_shop', 'list_products', 'list_installed_apps', 'app_compat_check', 'create_product_draft', 'invalidate_cache'). params is the action-specific body.

tools.name: shopify_article_create
tools.description: Create a blog article. author_name is required because ArticleCreateInput.author is non-null. The schema declares NO default for isPublished, so published is sent explicitly and defaults to false here; published: true puts the article on the storefront at once.

tools.name: shopify_article_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a blog article. Irreversible; returns the deleted article id. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_article_get
tools.description: Fetch one blog article including its full HTML body. Returns null when the id does not exist on this shop.

tools.name: shopify_article_list
tools.description: List blog articles across all blogs, or one blog via blog_id. Uses the top-level articles connection because Blog.articles accepts neither query nor sortKey; blog_id becomes a blog_id: search term.

tools.name: shopify_article_update
tools.description: Update a blog article. Partial, but tags REPLACES the whole tag list. published: true makes it shopper-visible immediately; changing handle changes the live URL unless redirect_new_handle is set.

tools.name: shopify_blog_create
tools.description: Create a blog (a container for articles). A blog has no draft state; comment_policy defaults to the shop setting and MODERATED means shopper comments wait for comment_moderate.

tools.name: shopify_blog_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a blog. Irreversible. The schema documents only that the blog is removed, not what becomes of the articles inside it, so move or export them first. Returns the deleted blog id. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_blog_get
tools.description: Fetch one blog by id (title, handle, comment policy, template suffix, tags). Returns null when the id does not exist on this shop. Use article_list with a blog_id filter for its articles: Blog.articles accepts no query and no sortKey, so it cannot be filtered or sorted from here.

tools.name: shopify_blog_list
tools.description: List blogs (id, title, handle, commentPolicy). commentPolicy is MODERATED, CLOSED or AUTO_PUBLISHED and decides whether new shopper comments need comment_moderate.

tools.name: shopify_blog_update
tools.description: Update a blog. Partial. Changing handle moves every article URL under it, so pass redirect_new_handle and redirect_articles to have Shopify leave redirects behind.

tools.name: shopify_catalog_list
tools.description: List products from the connected store (handle, title, status, totalInventory aggregate, price, featured image). Use this to discover what to build a page around. For per-VARIANT stock counts use shopify_inventory_get. Convenience wrapper over shopify_admin(list_products).

tools.name: shopify_collection_create
tools.description: Creates a collection. Pass rule_set to make it SMART (appliedDisjunctively true = OR, false = AND) or product_ids to make it MANUAL. Two runtime traps the scope check cannot see: collectionCreate is PLAN-GATED and fails on Starter and Retail plans even with write_products granted, and the new collection is NOT visible on any sales channel because publishing needs write_publications, which Hiveku does not hold.

tools.name: shopify_collection_delete
tools.description: Deletes a collection. Irreversible: there is no undelete, the storefront URL 404s immediately, and any navigation menu or template pointing at it breaks. The products themselves are not deleted. Takes a wrapper input { id }, unlike the add/remove/reorder mutations which take bare arguments. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_collection_get
tools.description: Reads one collection by id or by handle, with its first page of member products. ruleSet null means manual, non-null means smart, and the rule READ shape (conditionObject) cannot be fed back into collection_update, which takes conditionObjectId. Publication state is not returned; that needs read_product_listings, which Hiveku does not hold.

tools.name: shopify_collection_list
tools.description: Lists collections (Relay cursor paging, 250 max). ruleSet null means a manual collection, non-null means a smart one; there is no isSmartCollection boolean. sort_key is only ID, RELEVANCE, TITLE or UPDATED_AT (no CREATED_AT, no PRODUCTS_COUNT). Pass query: "collection_type:smart" or "collection_type:custom" to filter by kind. Publication state is not returned; that needs read_product_listings, which Hiveku does not hold.

tools.name: shopify_collection_products_add
tools.description: Adds products to a MANUAL collection via collectionAddProductsV2, never the V1 mutation, which aborts the whole batch on a single already-present product. Shoppers see the change as soon as the job runs; it is undone by collection_products_remove, which is why this is not confirm gated. Returns a Job: empty userErrors means Shopify ACCEPTED the work, not that it finished, so re-read the collection to confirm. Adding to a smart collection is refused by Shopify because its membership comes from its rules.

tools.name: shopify_collection_products_remove
tools.description: Removes products from a MANUAL collection. Shopify does NOT validate that the products are in the collection or that they exist at all, so empty userErrors proves nothing about what was removed; re-read the collection to confirm. Returns a Job: empty userErrors means ACCEPTED, not finished.

tools.name: shopify_collection_products_reorder
tools.description: Reorders products inside a collection. Only works when the collection sortOrder is MANUAL; on any other sort order Shopify rejects it. new_position is ZERO-BASED and is evaluated AFTER the earlier moves in the same call, so positions shift as the list is rebuilt. Sent as an UnsignedInt64 string. Returns a Job: empty userErrors means ACCEPTED, not finished.

tools.name: shopify_collection_update
tools.description: Updates a collection, including converting it to smart by sending rule_set (appliedDisjunctively true = OR, false = AND). rule_set REPLACES the whole rule list, so send the full desired set. product_ids is REFUSED here: Shopify accepts CollectionInput.products only on collectionCreate, so sending it would return success having changed no membership; use collection_products_add / collection_products_remove instead. Changing a smart collection rule_set re-evaluates membership ASYNCHRONOUSLY, so a read straight afterwards can still show the old members. Changing handle moves the live storefront URL; redirect_new_handle leaves a redirect behind. A rule_set read from collection_get cannot be resent unchanged, because the read exposes conditionObject and the input takes conditionObjectId.

tools.name: shopify_comment_list
tools.description: List shopper comments on blog articles with their moderation status (PENDING, UNAPPROVED, PUBLISHED, SPAM, REMOVED). Author email and commenter IP are protected customer data and are not returned.

tools.name: shopify_comment_moderate
tools.description: Moderate one article comment: approve PUBLISHES it publicly on the storefront under the article, spam hides it, not_spam un-marks spam and returns it to the pending queue without publishing. Not confirm gated because every decision is reversible by another decision: approve is undone by spam. There is no comment_delete here; deletion is the one irreversible move and it is deliberately not exposed.

tools.name: shopify_connect_start
tools.description: STEP 1 of connecting a store. Generate a Shopify authorize URL the USER opens in their own browser to approve the connection (you can't approve it for them — it's the merchant's Shopify consent screen). Prereq: the account needs a Shopify OAuth app (bring-your-own from the customer's Shopify Partners dashboard). Find one with oauth_app_list(provider='shopify'); register one with oauth_app_create(provider='shopify', products=['shopify_storefront'], client_id, client_secret) if none. Returns 412 code='no_oauth_app' if missing. intent_type: shopify_project_connect (bind to one project — pass project_id; this is the Ecommerce-tab case), shopify_account_connect (account default), or shopify_reconnect (re-auth an existing connection — pass connection_id). Returns data.setup_url (hand to user) + data.callback_url (must be in the Shopify app's Allowed redirection URLs). After the user approves, poll shopify_connection_status until the store appears.

tools.name: shopify_connection_status
tools.description: STEP 2 (poll). List the account's Shopify connections — the target after shopify_connect_start. Pass shop_domain to filter to one store; poll until a row appears with disconnected_at=null (that means the user finished approving). Returns sanitized rows only (shop_domain, shop_name, shop_id, scope, purpose, installed_at, disconnected_at, is_dev_store) — never tokens.

tools.name: shopify_customer_create
tools.description: Create a customer. Email marketing consent requires email and SMS consent requires phone in the same call. Addresses are not settable here, CustomerInput has no address field. Shopify sends the shopper nothing; no invite or activation email is triggered.

tools.name: shopify_customer_get
tools.description: One customer with addresses, amountSpent, tags, tax exemptions and email marketing consent. Name, email, phone and address need Shopify Level 2 protected customer data approval and are null without it. Returns null when the id does not exist.

tools.name: shopify_customer_list
tools.description: Page the customer list (Relay cursor, 250 max, no offset). Name, email, phone and address are protected customer data: without Shopify Level 2 approval they come back null with no error. Orders are not included, that needs read_orders.

tools.name: shopify_customer_marketing_consent_set
tools.description: Set a customer's email and/or SMS marketing consent through the dedicated mutations customerEmailMarketingConsentUpdate and customerSmsMarketingConsentUpdate. Split out of customer_update deliberately: this writes a CONSENT RECORD about a real person and can overwrite an opt-out, so it is confirm gated while ordinary profile edits are not. Only the settable states are accepted (NOT_SUBSCRIBED, PENDING, SUBSCRIBED, UNSUBSCRIBED); REDACTED and INVALID are states Shopify assigns itself. marketingState is NON-NULL on both consent inputs, so an opt-in level sent without a state is a validation error, not a partial update. Sends only the half you supply, and returns the resulting consent for each. It does NOT email anyone: nothing in this registry puts a message in a shopper inbox. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_customer_update
tools.description: Update a customer. tags REPLACES the whole tag list, use tagsAdd/tagsRemove for an incremental change. Setting email or SMS marketing consent changes what a real shopper receives, and the matching email or phone must already be on the record.

tools.name: shopify_eject_manifest
tools.description: READ-ONLY. Returns a structured migration plan for moving this project off the Hiveku Shopify storefront to a stand-alone Hydrogen + Oxygen repo: what would be transformed, and where. It changes NOTHING -- the plan is computed on demand from the current code versions, nothing is written, and no eject is performed (the eject runner itself is not built). Use it to show a merchant what leaving would involve.

tools.name: shopify_file_list
tools.description: Lists Shopify Files (content library images, videos and generic files) with an optional Shopify search query. Fields differ by kind, so images, generic files and videos each carry their own extra keys. Relay pagination only, 250 max.

tools.name: shopify_inventory_get
tools.description: Per-VARIANT inventory for the connected store — what you need to build an inventory-aware page/funnel (list_products only gives the product-level totalInventory aggregate). Pass params.handle for one product, or params.first (1-50) for the latest N products. Returns each product's variants with inventoryQuantity, price, sku, title, options. Live read via the store's Admin API (token stays server-side). NOTE: the deployed page reads live quantityAvailable through the scaffolded Storefront client — this tool is for the agent to reason about stock while building.

tools.name: shopify_metafield_definition_create
tools.description: Create a metafield definition for one owner type. Needs write access to that owner (write_products, write_customers, write_content), so the union is declared and the per-owner scope is enforced in the call. `type` is fixed at creation and cannot be changed later, and every metafield stored under this namespace/key must match it.

tools.name: shopify_metafield_definition_delete
tools.description: Delete a metafield definition by id. With delete_all_associated_metafields true this also destroys EVERY metafield stored under that definition on every owner, permanently and with no undo, which is why it is confirm gated. The definition is read first so the owner type is known: it needs write access to that owner (write_products, write_customers, write_content), the union is declared and the exact scope is enforced before the delete runs. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_metafield_definition_list
tools.description: Metafield definitions for ONE owner type, Relay paged. ownerType is required by Shopify and there is no all-owners listing, so call this once per owner type. The definition needs read access to its owner type, so the read union is declared and the exact scope is enforced per call.

tools.name: shopify_metafield_definition_update
tools.description: Update a metafield definition, identified by owner_type plus namespace and key rather than by id. `type` is NOT updatable and is not accepted here. Needs write access to the owner type (write_products, write_customers, write_content), declared as a union and enforced per owner in the call. Tightening validations returns a validationJob: existing metafields are re-checked asynchronously, so an empty userErrors means accepted, not finished.

tools.name: shopify_metafields_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete metafields by owner id, namespace and key. The values are gone: there is no undo and no version history, so this is confirm gated. Like metafieldsSet it carries no scope of its own and needs write access to the OWNER (write_products, write_customers, write_content), enforced per call. Returns one result PER REQUESTED metafield with deleted true or false, plus deleted_count and not_found_count: Shopify reports a metafield that did not exist as a null in position, NOT as an error, so a call that deleted nothing otherwise looks identical to one that deleted everything. ORDER, DRAFTORDER, DISCOUNT, LOCATION, MARKET and COMPANY owners are refused because Hiveku never requests those write scopes. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_metafields_get
tools.description: Metafields on one owner (PRODUCT, COLLECTION, CUSTOMER, PAGE, ARTICLE, BLOG), Relay paged, 250 max per page. Metafields carry no scope of their own, so the owner type decides the scope (products/collections read_products, customers read_customers, pages/articles/blogs read_content). The exact one is enforced per call and named in the error, so nothing is declared statically. An EMPTY result can mean another app owns them: app-reserved namespaces are invisible to every other app regardless of scope.

tools.name: shopify_metafields_set
tools.description: Create or overwrite up to 25 metafields on owners of one type (metafieldsSet is hard capped at 25 per call). `type` is required and must match any existing definition exactly or Shopify refuses the write in userErrors. metafieldsSet has no scope of its own: it needs write access to the OWNER (write_products, write_customers, write_content), and the one that applies is enforced per call and named in the error; ORDER, DRAFTORDER, DISCOUNT, LOCATION, MARKET and COMPANY owners are refused because Hiveku never requests those write scopes. Omitting namespace stores the value in the app-reserved namespace, where no other app can see it.

tools.name: shopify_order_fulfillments
tools.description: Shipments for one order: status, tracking company/number/url, origin address and the fulfilled line items. Fulfillment and FulfillmentTrackingInfo are readable under read_orders; the FulfillmentOrder objects behind them are NOT - those need the fulfillment-order scopes Hiveku does not hold - so this shows what shipped, never what is assigned or holdable. read_orders reaches ONLY the last 60 days and an older order comes back null with no error; older orders need read_all_orders (Partner Dashboard approval, not held) and the truncation is SILENT. Customer name, email, phone and shipping/billing address are protected customer data needing Level 2 approval and can be null even with the scope granted. Fulfillment location and fulfillment service are omitted (read_locations / the fulfillments scope family). Accepts a numeric id or a full gid.

tools.name: shopify_order_get
tools.description: One order with line items, totals, shipping line and the customer block. read_orders reaches ONLY the last 60 days, so an order older than that returns null rather than an error: older orders need read_all_orders (Partner Dashboard approval, not held) and the truncation is SILENT. Customer name, email, phone and shipping/billing address are protected customer data needing Level 2 approval and can be null on a call that fully succeeded. Accepts a numeric id or a full gid. Line items are Relay-paginated at 250 max; lineItems.pageInfo.hasNextPage true means the order has more lines than were returned. Fulfillment orders, returns and inventory are NOT included - they need scopes Hiveku does not hold.

tools.name: shopify_order_list
tools.description: List orders with totals, status and customer block. read_orders reaches ONLY the last 60 days; older orders need read_all_orders (Shopify Partner Dashboard approval, not held) and the cut-off is SILENT, so a short list is not proof an order is missing. Customer name, email, phone and shipping/billing address are protected customer data needing Level 2 approval and can be null even though the scope is granted. The query argument takes Shopify order search syntax: financial_status:paid|pending|refunded|partially_refunded|authorized|voided, fulfillment_status:fulfilled|unfulfilled|partial|restocked, status:open|closed|cancelled, created_at:>2026-01-01, updated_at:<2026-02-01, tag:vip, plus name:, email:, sku:, AND/OR/NOT. Relay cursors only (max 250 per page, no offset): pass the returned endCursor as the after argument.

tools.name: shopify_order_transactions
tools.description: Payment transactions and refunds for one order, with the amounts captured, refunded and still outstanding.
