OrderTransaction and Refund are both covered by read_orders alone. read_orders reaches ONLY the last 60 days, so an older order returns null rather than an error - older orders need read_all_orders (Partner Dashboard approval, not held) and the cut-off is SILENT. Customer name, email, phone and shipping/billing address are protected customer data needing Level 2 approval and can be null even with the scope granted. Card and gateway payloads (paymentDetails, receiptJson) and the transaction location are NOT returned. Accepts a numeric id or a full gid.

tools.name: shopify_page_create
tools.description: Create an online store page. Created as a DRAFT unless you pass published: true. Shopify itself does the opposite: PageCreateInput.isPublished defaults to TRUE when no publish date is given, so a page created through the raw API is live the instant the call returns. This action always sends the field explicitly and defaults it to false, so an agent cannot publish to a client storefront by omission. Pass published: true to go live; page_update flips it back.

tools.name: shopify_page_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete an online store page. Irreversible; returns the deleted page id. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_page_get
tools.description: Fetch one online store page including its full HTML body. Returns null when the id does not exist on this shop.

tools.name: shopify_page_list
tools.description: List online store pages (id, title, handle, isPublished, publishedAt). Relay cursor paging only, 250 max per page, no offset.

tools.name: shopify_page_update
tools.description: Update an online store page. Partial: only the fields you pass change. Changing handle changes the live URL, so pass redirect_new_handle: true to have Shopify leave a redirect from the old one.

tools.name: shopify_product_create
tools.description: Create a product. ProductCreateInput accepts no variants, images or ProductInput fields; Shopify ALWAYS auto-creates one standalone variant, so real variants need a following productVariantsBulkCreate with strategy REMOVE_STANDALONE_VARIANT or the product keeps a junk variant. The new product is on NO sales channel: publishing needs write_publications, which Hiveku does not hold.

tools.name: shopify_product_delete
tools.description: Delete a product permanently, with its variants and media. Irreversible; requires confirm: true. Runs synchronously so the deleted id comes back on this call. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_product_duplicate
tools.description: Duplicate a product under a new title. The copy defaults to DRAFT unless new_status says otherwise, and is on NO sales channel: publishing needs write_publications, which Hiveku does not hold. Image copying returns a Job, so imageJob.done false means the images are still copying.

tools.name: shopify_product_get
tools.description: One product by id or by handle (exactly one), with options and the first page of variants. Publication state is NOT returned: resourcePublications needs read_product_listings, which Hiveku does not hold, and selecting it would fail the whole query.

tools.name: shopify_product_media_add
tools.description: Attach images, video or 3D models to a product from a PUBLIC https URL. Uses productUpdate(product:{id}, media:[...]) because productCreateMedia is deprecated in favour of productUpdate/productSet. Ingest is ASYNC: no error means accepted, not processed, so re-read Media.status until it is READY (FAILED carries mediaErrors). A file that is not publicly reachable cannot be uploaded here, because the stagedUploadsCreate flow needs a multipart byte POST this JSON proxy cannot make.

tools.name: shopify_product_media_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete media from a product. Reports failures on mediaUserErrors, not userErrors. Irreversible and shopper-visible, so it requires confirm: true. Non-image media ids must be passed as a full gid. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_product_media_reorder
tools.description: Reorder a product's media. The mutation argument is id, not productId, and newPosition is UnsignedInt64 which must be sent as a JSON STRING. Returns a Job: empty mediaUserErrors means ACCEPTED, not finished, so poll job.done or re-read the media order. Position 0 is the featured image, so this is shopper-visible.

tools.name: shopify_product_media_update
tools.description: Update alt text or the preview image of existing product media. Reports failures on mediaUserErrors, not userErrors (the userErrors field on this payload is deprecated). A changed previewImageSource is re-ingested ASYNC, so re-read Media.status. Non-image media ids must be passed as a full gid, since a bare number is assumed to be a MediaImage.

tools.name: shopify_product_option_update
tools.description: Rename, reposition or edit the values of ONE option. The mutation is productOptionUpdate, singular, and takes exactly one option. variantStrategy MANAGE lets Shopify create and delete variants to match the new value set, so deleting a value with MANAGE DELETES ITS VARIANTS; LEAVE_AS_IS refuses the change instead. Confirm gated for that reason: its siblings product_options_delete and variants_bulk_delete are gated and this destroys variants just as permanently. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_product_options_create
tools.description: Add one or more options (Size, Color) to a product. variantStrategy LEAVE_AS_IS keeps the existing variants and only defines the option; CREATE expands the catalog into every new combination, which can multiply the variant count and is shopper-visible at once.

tools.name: shopify_product_options_delete
tools.description: Delete options from a product. strategy DEFAULT destroys the variants that used the option, POSITION keeps the first value, NON_DESTRUCTIVE refuses rather than losing variants. Irreversible and shopper-visible, so it requires confirm: true. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_product_options_reorder
tools.description: Reorder a product's options and, optionally, the values inside each one. Order is shopper-visible: option 1 is the first selector on the product page. Identify each option by id or by name, and pass the full ordered list.

tools.name: shopify_product_set
tools.description: Create or fully replace a product in one call. FULL REPLACE: anything omitted is deleted, so send the complete desired state. Target an existing product with product_id or handle; omit both to create. ProductSetInput carries NO id field, so identity comes from the identifier argument. Requires confirm: true. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_product_update
tools.description: Update a product by id. ProductUpdateInput accepts no variants, images or options. tags REPLACES the entire tag list, so use tags_add / tags_remove for incremental tag changes.

tools.name: shopify_scaffold_compat
tools.description: Pre-flight a storefront scaffold BEFORE writing files: reports the project's router type, path aliases, Tailwind presence, and any route collisions for the given feature. Call this before shopify_storefront_scaffold to avoid clobbering existing routes.

tools.name: shopify_segment_create
tools.description: Create a customer segment from a ShopifyQL segment query, for example email_subscription_status = 'SUBSCRIBED'. segmentCreate takes bare name and query arguments, not an input wrapper. A bad query comes back as a userError, not a crash.

tools.name: shopify_segment_delete
tools.description: Delete a customer segment. Irreversible: the segment and its query are gone and every campaign or automation targeting it loses its audience. Customers themselves are not touched. Requires confirm: true. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_segment_list
tools.description: Page customer segments (Relay cursor, 250 max, no offset). Each segment carries its ShopifyQL query string. Segments hold no customer data themselves, but the members behind them are protected customer data and need Level 2 approval to read.

tools.name: shopify_segment_members_list
tools.description: Page the customers currently in a segment, plus the segment total. A plain read: customerSegmentMembers accepts segmentId directly at 2025-10, so no customerSegmentMembersQueryCreate call is needed. Each node id is a CustomerSegmentMember gid, not a Customer gid. Name, email, phone and address are protected customer data and are null without Shopify Level 2 approval.

tools.name: shopify_segment_update
tools.description: Rename a segment or replace its ShopifyQL query. Both are optional; omitting one leaves it alone. Replacing the query silently changes who every campaign pointed at this segment will reach, since membership is evaluated at send time.

tools.name: shopify_status
tools.description: Get the project's effective Shopify connection (override or account default), with optional catalog sample.

tools.name: shopify_storefront_scaffold
tools.description: STEP 3 — write storefront feature files into the project (builder_code_versions) so the page can render live products + inventory. Idempotent (existing files skipped unless overwrite=true); pass dry_run=true first to preview the file plan + compat. Features: 'storefront-client' (the live Storefront API client exposing quantityAvailable — scaffold this first), 'product-detail-route' (full PDP flow: client + revalidate + reviews), 'cart', 'sitemap', 'revalidate-route' (cache-bust receiver for product/inventory webhooks), 'customer-account', 'reviews', 'subscriptions'. After scaffolding, the coder/deploy pipeline picks up the new files; use preview_sync / deploy to make them live.

tools.name: shopify_tags_add
tools.description: Add tags to a taggable Shopify object WITHOUT replacing the existing list (product_update and the other update actions REPLACE the whole tag list, which is why this exists). The scopes array is empty because the scope Shopify checks is the WRITE scope of whatever owner_id points at, which is not known until the call: it is enforced per call instead, and the error names the one missing scope. Products and collections need write_products, customers write_customers, pages/articles/blogs write_content. Orders, draft orders and companies are taggable in Shopify but unreachable here, because Hiveku never requests write_orders, write_draft_orders or write_companies; passing such a gid is refused with that named. Pass owner_id as a full gid, or as a numeric id plus owner_type.

tools.name: shopify_tags_remove
tools.description: Remove tags from a taggable Shopify object, leaving its other tags alone. Tag removal is CASE-INSENSITIVE but tags are stored with their original casing, so a read-back compared against the string you sent can differ. The scopes array is empty because the scope Shopify checks is the WRITE scope of whatever owner_id points at, enforced per call with the missing one named: products and collections write_products, customers write_customers, pages/articles/blogs write_content. Orders, draft orders and companies are taggable in Shopify but unreachable here and are refused by name. Pass owner_id as a full gid, or as a numeric id plus owner_type.

tools.name: shopify_theme_file_delete
tools.description: Permanently deletes one file from a theme (themeFilesDelete), one file per call. The theme ROLE IS READ BEFORE THE DELETE: if it is MAIN, the published theme, the call is REFUSED unless you pass allow_live_theme: true, because the deletion is live to every shopper at once and can break the storefront. Theme-code writes also need a Shopify- granted app exemption on top of write_themes and whether Hiveku holds it is UNVERIFIED, so this can 403 while a scope audit reads green. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_theme_file_get
tools.description: Returns one theme file by exact filename, body included. The body union is normalised to { type, text, base64, url }: large or binary files come back as BASE64 or as a short-lived URL the caller must fetch itself, not as text.

tools.name: shopify_theme_file_list
tools.description: Lists the files of one theme (filename, content type, size, md5). Pass include_body to also return each file body, normalised from its three-member union into { type, text, base64, url }; it is off by default because a page of liquid bodies is megabytes. Relay pagination only, 250 max.

tools.name: shopify_theme_file_upsert
tools.description: Creates or OVERWRITES one file in a theme (themeFilesUpsert), one file per call. The theme ROLE IS READ BEFORE THE WRITE: if it is MAIN, the published theme, the call is REFUSED unless you pass allow_live_theme: true, because that edit is live to every shopper at once with no undo. Target an UNPUBLISHED or DEVELOPMENT theme; theme_list shows the roles. Needs a Shopify-granted app exemption on top of write_themes and whether Hiveku holds it is UNVERIFIED, so this can 403 while a scope audit reads green. Returns a Job: no userErrors means ACCEPTED, not finished. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_theme_list
tools.description: Lists online store themes with role, processing state and timestamps. Exactly one theme has role MAIN and that is the published, shopper-visible one. Relay pagination only, 250 max.

tools.name: shopify_variant_search
tools.description: Find variants across the whole catalog by SKU, barcode, title or product. Relay pagination only, 250 max per page, no offset. inventoryQuantity is included; per- location inventory is not (read_inventory is not granted).

tools.name: shopify_variants_bulk_create
tools.description: Create variants on a product. productCreate always auto-creates one standalone variant, so pass strategy REMOVE_STANDALONE_VARIANT on the first real batch or the product keeps a junk variant. Per-location stock cannot be set here (write_inventory is not granted), and new variants are not visible on any sales channel until the product is published (write_publications is not granted).

tools.name: shopify_variants_bulk_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete variants from a product. The Shopify argument is spelled variantsIds, not variantIds. Irreversible and shopper-visible, so it requires confirm: true. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_variants_bulk_update
tools.description: Update existing variants on a product. allowPartialUpdates defaults to FALSE, so one bad variant rolls the whole batch back; pass allow_partial_updates true to keep the good ones. Every variant entry must carry its id.

tools.name: shopify_variants_reorder
tools.description: Reorder the variants of one product. Positions are 1-based and shopper-visible immediately, since position drives which variant a product page selects first.

tools.name: shopify_webhook_create
tools.description: Create a shop-scoped webhook subscription delivering one topic to an https callback URL. Refuses, by name, any topic whose scope Hiveku does not request or this store did not grant, since Shopify permits a topic only when the app holds its scope. The created subscription is shop-scoped, so it is invisible to any app-scoped subscription declared in the app TOML and vice versa: an empty webhook_list does NOT mean no webhooks are running. Shopify also silently DELETES subscriptions whose scope is later revoked, so a scope downgrade kills this subscription with no error anywhere. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_webhook_delete
tools.description: Delete one shop-scoped webhook subscription by id, after reporting the topic and endpoint it was serving. CONFIRM-gated: deleting one of Hiveku's own standard topics breaks order ingest and the review-request flow (orders/create, orders/updated), storefront cache invalidation (products/create, products/update, products/delete, collections/update) or uninstall detection (app/uninstalled), with no error anywhere. Only shop-scoped subscriptions are deletable here, so an app-scoped subscription declared in the app TOML survives this and keeps delivering; equally, Shopify silently DELETES subscriptions whose scope is later revoked, so a subscription can vanish without anyone calling this. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_webhook_list
tools.description: List the shop-scoped webhook subscriptions on the connected store (topic, delivery endpoint, format, filter, API version), optionally filtered by topic. Returns ONLY shop-scoped subscriptions, never the app-scoped ones declared in the app TOML, so an empty result does NOT mean no webhooks are running. Shopify also silently DELETES subscriptions whose scope is later revoked, so a scope downgrade kills live webhooks with no error anywhere and they just vanish from this list.

tools.name: site_clone
tools.description: Duplicate a website project so you can experiment without affecting the original. Copies the current file tree (every is_current builder_code_versions row), project assets, settings, and navigation. The new project starts in draft status with a fresh subdomain — use preview_start on the returned project_id to spin up its Fly preview. What's NOT copied: the Supabase database, CloudFront / Cloudflare DNS / S3 hosting bucket / ACM cert, GitHub connection, custom domain. Each of those needs to be provisioned separately on the clone if the experiment needs them. copy_assets modes: • "reference" (default) — clone's asset rows point at the SAME S3 objects as the source. Cheap + instant. Best for short-lived experiments. Caveat: deleting an S3 object orphans the other side. • "duplicate" — re-uploads every asset under the clone's prefix. Slower + uses 2x storage, but the clone is fully independent. Use cases: try a risky refactor on the clone first, A/B variants, sandbox a destructive prompt, hand a clone to a different agent without touching production work.

tools.name: site_create
tools.description: Create a new website project. Three flavors: • BLANK: `{name, project_type?: "nextjs"|"vite"|"static-html", creation_mode: "blank"}` — bare Next.js+Tailwind scaffold (includes the premium section kit). • TEMPLATE: `{name, creation_mode: "template", template_id: "<id-from-templates_list>"}` — seeds the project with the template's sections, components, and example pages. • IMPORT: `{name, creation_mode: "import", project_type}` — for BRINGING AN EXISTING APP. The preview container seeds NOTHING (no starter kit, no section files that would break your build); push the code with project_import_presign → PUT tarball → project_import_finalize, then preview_start. Call templates_list first to see what template IDs are valid. Unknown template_id returns 400. The project's subdomain is auto-generated from the name + a random suffix; the live preview becomes available at hvk-<12-hex>.preview.hiveku.com (check sites_list for the canonical URL once created). Default project_type is "nextjs" when omitted.

tools.name: site_create_external
tools.description: Register an EXTERNAL website with Hiveku for analytics + visitor tracking only — Hiveku does NOT host or deploy this site. Use this when the customer's site lives on WordPress, Shopify, a static export, or any other host, but they want Hiveku's analytics, CRM event capture, marketing automation, and visitor intelligence to run on it. What happens: • A 'project' row is created with project_type='external', status='published' (no deploy/preview needed). • A subdomain in the form `ext-<slug>-<hex>` is allocated (no real DNS — internal ID only). • A verification_token + tracking_token are minted. The tracking_snippet field in the response is a <script> tag the customer pastes into their site's <head>. Once it fires, verification_status flips to 'verified' automatically. • If ASKSQUID_BEARER_TOKEN is configured on the builder, an AskSquid integration is provisioned (SDK + webhooks) so visitor intelligence works out of the box. Failure here is non-fatal. For a Hiveku-HOSTED site (one Hiveku builds + deploys + previews), call `site_create` instead. The two flows are intentionally separate: external sites can't be deployed, edited via the file APIs, or previewed; hosted sites can't carry an external_website_url.

tools.name: site_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE — fully delete a website project AND every external resource it owns: Supabase database (drops billing!), Lambda function, ECR repo, ACM cert, CloudFront distributions (production + staging), Cloudflare DNS, S3 hosting bucket, project assets in S3, AWS Secrets, dev containers, Fly preview, EAS project (archive). Then the DB row. Best-effort cleanup: each step logs + continues on failure so a flaky external dependency cannot orphan the row. A nightly orphan-sweep cron deletes any Supabase projects left behind by silent failures, but reach out to ops if you see one stuck. This is the same chain the dashboard delete button runs. Use ONLY when the user has explicitly confirmed they want the project gone — there is no undo. Accepts `id` or `project_id`.

tools.name: site_reanalyze
tools.description: Re-detect a project's framework from its CURRENT files and heal the stored labels (project_type + detected_project_type). **Call this after converting a project's framework** — e.g. you rewrote a Vite site as Next.js and pushed the new code — so Hiveku's label matches the code. Context so you don't over-worry: the deploy tiers AUTO-DETECT the framework from files on every build (a stale label does not break deploys), and the Fly preview self-heals project_type on the next preview_start. What never self-heals is detected_project_type (it drives SPA-vs-MPA redirect rewrites on static-origin tiers) and the label shown in sites_list/project_get until a preview runs. This tool fixes both immediately. Also returns leftovers[] — previous-framework artifacts that CAN confuse the build analyzers (a lingering vite.config.ts, or "vite"/"next" still in package.json deps of the other framework). Clean those up (delete the file / fix package.json via bulk_save) as part of the conversion. dry_run:true reports what would change without writing. Detection returning null (unrecognizable file set) never overwrites the existing labels.

tools.name: sites_list
tools.description: THE one-call "what can I edit" tool for code-editing agents. Returns every buildable website_project on the account with: • `environments.{development,staging,production}.{url,status,deployment_type}` — the three SERVERLESS tiers (Lambda + CloudFront). ★ A tier `url` is null until that tier is deployed; `status` then reads "not deployed". That is normal, not a failure. • `live_preview.{url,container_status,last_activity_at}` — the Fly preview CONTAINER, and the only URL that exists before anything is deployed. ★ This is what "the preview URL" means; it is NOT the development tier. fly.io hostnames are rewritten to the canonical preview.hiveku.com proxy form so no infra is exposed. • GitHub connection state from builder_project_settings (not pm_projects): connected, connection_type (app/oauth/none), repo full name, default branch, auto_deploy flags per environment, branch mappings per environment, last_sync_at, last_deployed_at. • Dev container status: running / stopped / unknown — if stopped, call preview_start before preview_sync. • Project type (nextjs / vite / static-html / internal). • staging_enabled flag. A `summary` block aggregates totals (with_github, with_production, by_project_type) so you can quickly see "this account has 7 buildable sites, 2 connected to GitHub, 3 with production deploys." Call this BEFORE asking the user "which project do you want to edit?" — the response usually answers half the follow-up questions (github state, preview URL, container status) on its own.

tools.name: social_account_analytics
tools.description: Get daily account-level analytics rows (followers, reach, engagement rate) for ONE connected social account. Requires social_account_id from social_list_accounts. Paginated, newest day first.

tools.name: social_account_get
tools.description: One connected social account: platform, display name, follower count, granted scopes, capability flags and crucially connection_status plus last_error. Read this before blaming a publish failure on the post -- an expired or errored connection is the usual cause. Never returns tokens.

tools.name: social_analytics_best_times
tools.description: Suggested posting times computed from THIS account's own engagement history, returned as concrete future timestamps ready to pass as scheduled_at. Returns an empty list on a new account or one with too few samples: that is the honest answer, not a failure, and means schedule by the calendar instead.

tools.name: social_analytics_followers
tools.description: Follower growth per connected account over `period` days, with a daily series and a rolled-up summary of gained, lost and net change. Reads STORED snapshots, so an account whose last_synced_at is old reports stale growth rather than an error -- check last_synced_at before reading a flat line as a flat audience.

tools.name: social_analytics_summary
tools.description: Get social media analytics summary — total posts, engagement, reach across all platforms

tools.name: social_analytics_sync
tools.description: Refresh post analytics for this account from the platforms, capped at 50 post versions, and return the run report. It only refreshes posts that are DUE, so calling it twice reports zero synced the second time -- that is correct, not a failure. To force one specific post use social_post_sync_analytics.

tools.name: social_analytics_timeseries
tools.description: Get daily social analytics time series across the account: engagement deltas, follower growth, top posts, best-time heatmap, and per-platform totals. NOTE: the backing builder route ships in a later deploy — until then this returns 404; metrics appear once analytics sync is enabled for the account.

tools.name: social_calendar_create
tools.description: Create a social calendar event. Can link to an existing post (linked_post_id) or campaign (linked_campaign_id).

tools.name: social_calendar_delete
tools.description: Delete a social calendar event by ID.

tools.name: social_calendar_get
tools.description: Get one social calendar event with its linked post and content pillar. Use after social_calendar_list to see what a slot actually holds before rescheduling it.

tools.name: social_calendar_list
tools.description: List social calendar events (planned posts, campaigns, holidays) with optional date-range, event-type, and status filters. Paginated, ordered by start date.

tools.name: social_calendar_update
tools.description: Update a social calendar event — title, dates, type, status, recurrence, links, tags, or platforms. Only provided fields are changed.

tools.name: social_comment_get
tools.description: Get one comment from the engagement inbox with its post, the connected account it arrived on, our own reply if any, and any threaded replies. reply_content plus replied_at is the record that a reply was actually published; a comment with neither is unanswered.

tools.name: social_comment_reply
tools.description: PUBLISHES A PUBLIC REPLY to a comment on Facebook, Instagram or LinkedIn, then records it against the inbox row. Outward-facing and immediate: there is no draft mode and no undo. The platform call happens first, so a failure means nothing was posted AND nothing was recorded. A response with recorded:false means the reply IS live but the local write failed -- re-read the comment, never retry, because a retry posts a second public reply. 409 with code reconnect_required means the connection lost the reply scope. X, TikTok and Google Business Profile have no reply API and return 400.

tools.name: social_comment_update
tools.description: TRIAGE ONLY -- nothing here reaches the platform. Sets workflow state on a comment: status, sentiment, requires_response, ai_category, and ai_suggested_response (a DRAFT reply, stored and never sent). To actually publish a reply call social_comment_reply. Passing reply_content here is rejected with 400: it used to be accepted, recorded as sent, and posted nowhere.

tools.name: social_comments_list
tools.description: List social comments received across all published posts, with status, sentiment, requires-response, and text-search filters. READ-ONLY for now — replying to comments via this surface is not yet supported; reply/dismiss actions live in the dashboard.

tools.name: social_create_post
tools.description: Create a new social media post targeting specific platforms and accounts

tools.name: social_delete_post
tools.description: Delete a social media post by ID

tools.name: social_get_post
tools.description: Get a single social media post by ID with versions and analytics

tools.name: social_hashtag_get
tools.description: Get one tracked hashtag with its stored usage and performance counters. Returns what has been recorded for it, not live platform volume.

tools.name: social_hashtag_update
tools.description: Update a tracked hashtag's classification flags. The route accepts exactly four fields -- category, is_branded, is_favorite, is_trending -- and silently ignores anything else, so the tag TEXT cannot be edited here: delete the row and create it again.

tools.name: social_hashtags_create
tools.description: Register a hashtag for tracking on a platform. Upserts — calling again for the same hashtag+platform updates category/flags instead of duplicating. A leading "#" is added if missing.

tools.name: social_hashtags_delete
tools.description: Delete a tracked hashtag by ID (from social_hashtags_list).

tools.name: social_hashtags_list
tools.description: List tracked hashtags with performance metrics (times used, avg engagement, avg reach). Filter by platform, trending/branded/favorite flags; sort by engagement, used, reach, or trending rank.

tools.name: social_linkedin_comment_add
tools.description: PUBLISHES A PUBLIC TOP-LEVEL COMMENT on a LinkedIn post as the connected page or profile, immediately. Outward-facing, no draft mode, no undo. This is for commenting on someone else's post; to answer a comment on our own post use social_comment_reply, which records the reply against the engagement inbox so it is not re-surfaced as unanswered.

tools.name: social_linkedin_comment_delete
tools.description: PERMANENTLY DELETES A COMMENT FROM LINKEDIN. Destructive, outward-facing and irreversible: LinkedIn keeps no copy and offers no restore. It can remove someone else's comment from a page you administer, so treat it as moderation and confirm with a human first. Deleting a comment does NOT remove the stored row in the engagement inbox.

tools.name: social_linkedin_comment_list
tools.description: LIVE comment thread on ANY LinkedIn post URN the connection can see, including posts Hiveku never published. The engagement inbox only covers our own posts and only refreshes every 2 hours. For a post Hiveku did publish, prefer social_post_comments_sync -- it stores what it finds so replies can be tracked.

tools.name: social_linkedin_follower_stats
tools.description: LIVE organization follower composition: organic vs paid, broken down by association type (employee, member) and by job function. This is WHO follows the page, not a follower count over time -- for the trend use social_analytics_followers. Breakdown arrays come back null when LinkedIn withholds them below its minimum audience size, which is not an error. ORGANIZATION CONNECTIONS ONLY.

tools.name: social_linkedin_member_stats
tools.description: LIVE creator analytics for a PERSONAL LinkedIn profile: impressions, likes, comments, shares, clicks and engagement rate per post, plus the follower count. The organization endpoints refuse personal connections, so this is their only analytics surface. Pass post_urn to scope to one post. Needs the member analytics scopes on the LinkedIn app; an app without them returns 502 however the connection was made.

tools.name: social_linkedin_organization_get
tools.description: LIVE LinkedIn organization detail: name, vanity name, description, website, logo and follower count. org_id is the bare numeric id (1234567), not a URN. Returns 502 when this connection does not administer that organization -- LinkedIn refuses the read rather than returning an empty record.

tools.name: social_linkedin_organization_list
tools.description: LIVE from LinkedIn: the organizations this connection administers, with the ACL role granting it. This is what LinkedIn believes now, not what social_accounts has stored -- use it to find the organization id of a page that is not connected yet, or to confirm an admin was not removed from the page behind our back. A personal-profile connection returns an empty list, not an error.

tools.name: social_linkedin_page_stats
tools.description: LIVE organization PAGE traffic: page views split by tab (all, overview, careers) and unique visitors. This is profile traffic, NOT post reach -- someone who saw a post in the feed is not counted here. ORGANIZATION CONNECTIONS ONLY. Supply from_date and to_date together for a per-day range.

tools.name: social_linkedin_post_list
tools.description: The connected page's or profile's ACTUAL LinkedIn timeline, read live. social_list_posts only knows about posts Hiveku published; this is the only way to see posts made on LinkedIn directly. Returns the post URN, which is what the reactions, comments and member-analytics tools take. limit caps at 50 (LinkedIn's own maximum); page with start.

tools.name: social_linkedin_profile_get
tools.description: LIVE LinkedIn profile of the MEMBER who authorized this connection, even when it posts as an organization page -- the token always belongs to a person. Use it to confirm a token is still live and whose consent it carries.

tools.name: social_linkedin_reaction_add
tools.description: PUBLISHES A PUBLIC REACTION on a LinkedIn post as the connected page or profile, immediately. Outward-facing, and this route offers no undo. Use it to engage from the brand account on a partner or employee post, not on your own content.

tools.name: social_linkedin_reaction_list
tools.description: LIVE reaction counts on a post broken down by type (LIKE, CELEBRATE, SUPPORT, LOVE, INSIGHTFUL, FUNNY). The stored analytics snapshot flattens all of these into one like count, so this is the only way to see that a post got INSIGHTFUL rather than LIKE. An older post whose reactions LinkedIn no longer serves returns an empty object, not an error.

tools.name: social_linkedin_share_stats
tools.description: LIVE organization share statistics: impressions, unique impressions, clicks, likes, comments, shares and engagement for the page as a whole, with organic-only figures alongside the totals so paid amplification does not read as organic reach. ORGANIZATION CONNECTIONS ONLY -- a personal profile returns 400, use social_linkedin_member_stats. Supply from_date and to_date TOGETHER for a per-day breakdown; one alone is rejected.

tools.name: social_list_accounts
tools.description: List connected social media accounts with optional platform and status filters

tools.name: social_list_posts
tools.description: List social media posts with filters for status, platform, content type, date range, and AI generation flag

tools.name: social_meta_post_list
tools.description: The connected Facebook Page's or Instagram account's ACTUAL feed, read live from the Graph API. social_list_posts only knows what Hiveku published; this shows everything on the profile, including posts made in the Meta apps. Facebook returns message, permalink and like/comment/share summaries; Instagram returns caption, media_type, permalink, like_count and comments_count -- Graph exposes no share count for Instagram, so that field is simply absent rather than zero. The returned id is the platform post id the analytics surfaces take. Page with the returned paging.after cursor.

tools.name: social_pillar_create
tools.description: Create a social content pillar — a recurring content theme with posting targets, example topics, hashtags, and guidelines.

tools.name: social_pillar_delete
tools.description: Delete a content pillar. Posts assigned to it are unlinked (pillar_id set to null), not deleted.

tools.name: social_pillar_get
tools.description: Get one content pillar with its targets, example topics, hashtags and guidelines. Read it before drafting so a post lands on the theme the account actually committed to.

tools.name: social_pillar_list
tools.description: List social content pillars (recurring content themes the account posts about) with per-pillar post counts, ordered by sort order.

tools.name: social_pillar_update
tools.description: Update a content pillar — name, targets, topics, hashtags, guidelines, active flag, or sort order. Only provided fields are changed.

tools.name: social_post_analytics
tools.description: Get per-post metrics for one social post: aggregated totals (impressions, reach, engagements, likes, comments, shares, saves, clicks, video views, engagement rate) plus a per-platform-version breakdown with each version's platform URL, account, and latest analytics snapshot.

tools.name: social_post_comments_sync
tools.description: Pull a post's comments from its platforms RIGHT NOW and return them, including the ones just ingested. The engagement inbox only refreshes every 2 hours, so call this before replying or the thread will be stale. Covers Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn; platforms with no comment API return the stored rows with sync.synced 0 rather than an error. A resync never clobbers reply or triage fields.

tools.name: social_post_reject
tools.description: Reject a post that is HELD for approval: returns it to draft with approval_status 'rejected' and records the reason. Safe and reversible -- the post can be edited and staged again. Fails with 404 if the post is not currently awaiting approval, and 409 if someone approved it first. There is deliberately no matching approve tool: releasing a held post is a human decision, made in the dashboard approval queue.

tools.name: social_post_sync_analytics
tools.description: Pull fresh engagement metrics for a post from the platform's API.

tools.name: social_provider_list
tools.description: Every social platform Hiveku can connect, each with its OAuth redirect URI, required scopes, setup guide, and hiveku_native telling you whether a Hiveku app is configured on this deployment (false means the customer must register their own app). Read this before telling someone a platform is unsupported: usually the platform is fine and only the native app is unconfigured.

tools.name: social_publish_post
tools.description: Publish a social media post to the post's configured target accounts. GOVERNANCE GATE: publishing requires the post to be approved in the dashboard first. Calling this on an unapproved post does NOT publish — it moves the post into the approval queue and returns { pending_approval: true }; a user must approve it in the dashboard SocialApprovalQueue before it goes out. Posts with approval_status "pending" or "rejected" return an error.

tools.name: social_schedule_slot_create
tools.description: Create a recurring posting slot. Creating a slot schedules NO posts -- it only defines a time that social_schedule_slot_next_open will offer. weekday is 0-6 with 0 = Sunday, minute_of_day is 0-1439 local to the given timezone (so 9:30am is 570). timezone must be a valid IANA name such as America/Chicago.

tools.name: social_schedule_slot_delete
tools.description: Delete a recurring posting slot. Posts already scheduled at that time KEEP their scheduled_at and still publish -- deleting a slot only stops it being offered in future. To stop a post, unschedule the post.

tools.name: social_schedule_slot_list
tools.description: List the account's recurring posting slots (weekday + minute of day + IANA timezone). A slot with social_account_id null applies to every connection; one with it set applies only to that connection. Slots describe WHEN the account wants to post; they do not schedule anything themselves.

tools.name: social_schedule_slot_next_open
tools.description: Next OPEN slot occurrences over a 14-day horizon: defined slots with no post already scheduled into them. Call this before scheduling instead of picking a time and hoping it is free. Returns an empty list when the account has defined no slots -- that is not an error, it means schedule by hand.

tools.name: social_schedule_slot_update
tools.description: Update a recurring posting slot. Only supplied fields change. Setting social_account_id to null widens the slot back to every connection. Returns 404 for a slot id that is not this account.

tools.name: social_update_post
tools.description: Update a social post's editable content: title, body, target platforms and schedule. It CANNOT change status or approval state. It previously advertised `status` and `approval_status`, but the PATCH route forwards neither, so those returned 200 with nothing changed. That silent success is worse than an error: a caller setting `approval_status: 'approved'` was told it worked while the post stayed held. Both fields are removed rather than implemented, because approval is the client decision and must not be settable through a content-edit tool. To schedule, set `scheduled_at`; approval happens in the dashboard approval queue.

tools.name: stock_photos_download
tools.description: Fetch a stock-photo URL and save it to a project's assets (S3 + builder_project_assets row). save_path is the file path inside the project (e.g. 'public/images/hero.jpg').

tools.name: stock_photos_pixabay_search
tools.description: Search the Pixabay catalog. This is the ONLY Pixabay source here: stock_photos_search calls Unsplash and Pexels only, and Pixabay is the one of the three that also carries illustrations and vectors. Returns { assets: [...], pagination: { total, totalHits, currentPage, perPage, totalPages } }. Each asset has fileUrl, width, height, tags[], title/altText/description (all three are the SAME Pixabay tag string, not a caption) and a pixabay block with photographer, page_url, type, urls.{preview,webformat,large,fullHD,vector} and a ready-to-paste attribution line - carry that attribution onto whatever you build. SILENT FAILURE: every error path ALSO returns assets: [] with a populated pagination block, so an empty array is NOT 'no photos matched'. Branch on the HTTP status or on the top-level error field. 412 with reason 'not_configured' means PIXABAY_API_KEY is unset and no retry will ever clear it; 429 comes from one platform-wide Pixabay key shared by every tenant, so one caller looping this rate-limits everybody. NOTHING IS PERSISTED - no DB write, no media library row, and ids like 'pixabay_1234567' are catalog handles, not asset ids. To keep an image, pass its fileUrl to stock_photos_download (saves into a website project) or media_library_register_external_url (creates a media_assets row). Traps: per_page is clamped to 3..200 inside the lib, so asking for 1 returns 3 rows; createdAt is stamped at search time and is meaningless as a sort key; mimeType is always image/jpeg and filename always <id>.jpg even for vector and illustration hits, so read pixabay.type and pixabay.urls.vector to tell what the bytes really are; when largeImageURL is absent fileUrl falls back to a webformatURL that expires after 24 hours, so download promptly or re-search. safesearch is hardcoded on and cannot be disabled through this tool.

tools.name: stock_photos_search
tools.description: Search Unsplash + Pexels for free stock photos. Returns merged results with { url, thumbnail, photographer, source, attribution }. Use the url with stock_photos_download to save into a project.

tools.name: supabase_auth_config_get
tools.description: Fetch the project's Supabase Auth config (signup, email confirmation, JWT, password policy, OAuth flags). NOTE on smtp_pass: in every response it appears as Supabase's ENCRYPTED stored form (a 64-hex blob). It never matches the literal password, its not-changing is NOT evidence the write failed or was substituted, and it must never be fed back as a password. To change it, send the new literal value; the echo will still be the encrypted form.

tools.name: supabase_auth_config_update
tools.description: Update arbitrary Supabase auth config fields. config is the Management API PATCH body. NOTE on smtp_pass: in every response it appears as Supabase's ENCRYPTED stored form (a 64-hex blob). It never matches the literal password, its not-changing is NOT evidence the write failed or was substituted, and it must never be fed back as a password. To change it, send the new literal value; the echo will still be the encrypted form.

tools.name: supabase_auth_user_create
tools.description: Admin-create a Supabase Auth user. Provide email OR phone (one required). password optional — if omitted, user must use a magic-link / OAuth flow to sign in. email_confirm / phone_confirm default true (skip the verification email). user_metadata is user-editable; app_metadata is admin-only and shows up in JWTs.

tools.name: supabase_auth_user_delete
tools.description: Delete an Auth user by UUID. Cascades to RLS-owned rows depending on FK config. Irreversible.

tools.name: supabase_auth_user_generate_link
tools.description: Generate an auth action link (magic link, password recovery, invite, email-change confirmation). type values: 'signup' | 'magiclink' | 'recovery' | 'invite' | 'email_change_current' | 'email_change_new'. Returns the action URL. Useful when you want to email the link yourself instead of letting Supabase send the templated email.

tools.name: supabase_auth_user_get
tools.description: Read one Auth user by UUID. The user_id is the value of auth.users.id (a UUID), NOT the email.

tools.name: supabase_auth_user_update
tools.description: Update one Auth user. Any of: email, phone, password, user_metadata, app_metadata, role, ban_duration. Set ban_duration='24h' / 'none' to ban/unban.

tools.name: supabase_auth_users_list
tools.description: List Supabase Auth users for the project (paginated). These are the END-USERS of the project's app — NOT Hiveku account members. Returns email, phone, created_at, last_sign_in_at, banned_until, and the user_metadata / app_metadata blobs.

tools.name: supabase_configure_hiveku_smtp
tools.description: Convenience: point Supabase Auth emails at Hiveku Email infra (SES + verified sender). Only sender_email needed.

tools.name: supabase_configure_oauth
tools.description: Enable/disable a Supabase OAuth provider with client_id + client_secret (github, google, apple, etc.).

tools.name: supabase_configure_smtp
tools.description: Point Supabase Auth emails (confirmation, magic links, password reset) at a custom SMTP server.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_delete
tools.description: Delete an edge function by slug.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_deploy
tools.description: Deploy one or more edge functions. functions is an array of { slug, source, import_map?, verify_jwt? }.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_get_source
tools.description: Fetch the source bundle for one edge function by slug.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_invoke
tools.description: Invoke an edge function. payload is JSON sent as the request body.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_list
tools.description: List edge functions deployed on the project.

tools.name: supabase_edge_functions_set_secrets
tools.description: Set project-level secrets visible to edge functions. secrets is a {KEY: value} map (strings only).

tools.name: supabase_gen_types
tools.description: Generate TypeScript types for the project's database schema. Returns a `types` string ready to drop into the project as e.g. lib/database.types.ts.

tools.name: supabase_migration_apply
tools.description: Apply a database migration. name is a short identifier (e.g. "add_user_preferences"), query is the full SQL. Migrations are recorded in Supabase's migration history so you can roll forward predictably. For ad-hoc/exploratory writes use database_execute instead.

tools.name: supabase_migrations_list
tools.description: List applied database migrations on the project.

tools.name: supabase_policies_list
tools.description: List Row-Level Security policies on the project DB via pg_policies. Pass `schema` and/or `table` to scope. Returns {schemaname, tablename, policyname, permissive, roles, cmd, qual, with_check}. Call this BEFORE policy_create to confirm whether a policy with the same name already exists on the target table.

tools.name: supabase_policy_create
tools.description: Create a new RLS policy via CREATE POLICY SQL on the project's Postgres. command is SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|ALL. roles is the list of pg roles (default ['authenticated']). `using` is the USING expression (read predicate); `check` is the WITH CHECK expression (write predicate). For SELECT use `using`; for INSERT use `check`; for UPDATE/DELETE you usually need both. schema, table, and each role must be plain pg identifiers (no spaces, no special chars beyond underscore). using/check expressions are inlined verbatim into the SQL — they ARE trusted input; agents authoring policies are expected to construct safe predicates from user_id / auth.uid() / known column comparisons. Errors come back with the original Postgres error message.

tools.name: supabase_policy_delete
tools.description: Drop an RLS policy by name + table via DROP POLICY IF EXISTS. Irreversible. No-op (success) if the policy doesn't exist.

tools.name: supabase_policy_update
tools.description: Replace an existing RLS policy. Postgres only allows partial ALTER POLICY changes — to give you a clean "update everything" surface, this runs DROP+CREATE inside a single transaction. Pass `name` + `table` to identify the existing policy and the new field values as you would in policy_create. Use `new_name` to rename.

tools.name: supabase_storage_create
tools.description: Create a Storage bucket. is_public=true makes objects readable without auth. The bucket-name param is `bucket` (not `bucket_name`).

tools.name: supabase_storage_delete
tools.description: Delete an EMPTY Storage bucket (call supabase_storage_empty first if there are objects). The bucket-name param is `bucket` (not `bucket_name`).

tools.name: supabase_storage_empty
tools.description: Delete all objects in a Storage bucket (bucket itself stays).

tools.name: supabase_storage_list
tools.description: List Supabase Storage buckets for the project.

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_copy
tools.description: Copy an object to a new path inside the same bucket.

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_delete
tools.description: Delete a single object from a Supabase bucket. Permanent — no recycle bin.

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_download
tools.description: Download an object from a Supabase bucket. Returns {bucket, path, mime_type, file_size_bytes, content: <base64>, encoding}. Use for read-back smoke tests, content inspection, etc. Not the primary serve path — public buckets should be linked directly.

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_move
tools.description: Move/rename an object inside the same bucket. from + to are the object keys (paths inside the bucket).

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_signed_url
tools.description: Create a time-limited signed URL for a private bucket object. Default expires_in is 3600s (1h); max 7 days.

tools.name: supabase_storage_object_upload
tools.description: Upload a file to a Supabase Storage bucket. content is base64-encoded bytes (data:URI prefix accepted and stripped). Set upsert=true to overwrite an existing object at the same path. 25MB cap through MCP — use multipart uploads for larger files.

tools.name: supabase_storage_objects_list
tools.description: List files inside a Supabase Storage bucket (paginated). Use this in file-manager apps to enumerate the user's files. Pair with the bucket tools (supabase_storage_list/create) when you need to manage buckets themselves.

tools.name: supabase_sync_redirect_urls
tools.description: Set Supabase site_url + URI allow-list. Call after deploying so OAuth redirects + magic-link emails work.

tools.name: supabase_table_row_delete
tools.description: Delete rows matching filters. UNFILTERED DELETE IS REFUSED — always pass at least one filter. Returns the deleted rows.

tools.name: supabase_table_row_insert
tools.description: Insert one or more rows. `rows` may be a single object or an array of objects. Returns the inserted rows (representation).

tools.name: supabase_table_row_update
tools.description: Update rows matching filters. filters and patch are both required. filters={pk: value} for a single-row update.

tools.name: supabase_table_rows_list
tools.description: Read rows from a table via PostgREST. Safer than database_query for simple ops — no SQL injection surface, structured response. Use filters={col: value} for eq matches; for more complex predicates, fall back to database_query.

tools.name: survey_create
tools.description: Create a DRAFT survey. Omit `questions` to get the canonical starter set for the type — for nps and csat that is the standard wording, and changing it breaks comparability of the score, so prefer the default unless the user asked for something specific. Creating does not send anything: the survey lands in draft. Activate it with survey_update({status:"active"}), which requires at least one active question, then deliver with survey_send.

tools.name: survey_get
tools.description: Get one survey with its active questions.

tools.name: survey_list
tools.description: List the account's surveys with rollups (delivery counts, response counts, and the headline NPS/CSAT metric). Start here to find a survey_id.

tools.name: survey_results
tools.description: Aggregate results: delivery funnel, the NPS/CSAT metric, bucket breakdown, and the latest completed responses INCLUDING free-text answers — use those verbatim quotes as real customer language for copy rather than inventing testimonials.

tools.name: survey_send
tools.description: SENDS THE SURVEY FOR REAL to the named recipients (email or SMS). Not a preview — confirm with the user before calling. Supply contact_ids (from the crm_* tools) and/or raw emails. Applies the same guards as a dashboard send: the survey must be active, the throttle window is enforced, duplicates are deduped, SMS respects quiet hours, and a single call is capped at 200 recipients. channel defaults to "auto" (SMS when a mobile is on file, else email).

tools.name: survey_update
tools.description: Update a survey: rename, activate/pause, adjust the re-ask throttle, or edit the delivery copy. Setting status="active" is what makes a survey sendable and REQUIRES at least one active question — it 400s otherwise. throttle_days is the re-contact guard: a contact surveyed within that window is skipped by survey_send rather than surveyed again.

tools.name: talk_to_department
tools.description: Chat with a specific department identity the same way a user would in the Hiveku dashboard AI chat. The department runs with its own persona, skills, rules, memory, and specialist tools (e.g. SEO has DataForSEO, Content has CMS tools, Social has platform APIs, Analytics has traffic/conversion-tracking and attribution data). Use this for specialist work: strategy, analysis, copywriting, audits. For simple CRUD on account data prefer the direct tools (crm_list_contacts, seo_list_keywords, etc.). Returns the final assistant response, the tool calls the department made, and a session_id that can be passed back in to continue the same conversation.

tools.name: template_get
tools.description: Fetch one template's full metadata by slug. Same shape as templates_list entries — id, name, description, category, tags, preview_image, preview_demo_url (live URL), featured, usage_count, has_overlay_family. Use when you already have a slug (e.g. from a previous templates_list call or a stored user preference) and want the live demo URL without re-paging the whole catalog. 404 if the slug isn't published.

tools.name: templates_list
tools.description: Browse the published website-project template catalog used by site_create. Templates live in the builder_gallery_templates table (status='published'); the docker/template-overlays/ folders on disk are authoring inputs only — a freshly-added overlay won't appear here until scripts/publish-template.ts has run. Currently 70+ templates across categories like healthcare-clinic, podcast-media, b2b-marketplace, restaurant-cafe, online-course, etc. Each entry carries: • `id` — what to pass to site_create as `template_id` • `name`, `description` — pitch to the user when offering choices • `category`, `tags[]` — discovery filters; bridge to facets.categories / facets.tags • `preview_image` — static thumbnail; good for a card grid, NOT for visual study (it's a single frame) • **`preview_demo_url` — LIVE URL of the rendered site**. For real visual study (does this look right for the customer's industry, does the layout match their brand voice, etc.) OPEN THIS URL IN A BROWSER TOOL — that's what it's there for. Recommend a template only after looking at the live demo, not from the name alone. • `featured` — editorial flag; bias toward featured templates when the user hasn't expressed strong preferences • `usage_count` — popularity signal (real production usage) • `has_overlay_family: true` — template pulls extra source sections from the starter (e.g. climate-tech components for climate-hardware) The response also returns: • `total` — pre-pagination match count • `facets: { categories, tags }` — across the FULL catalog so you can navigate without a second round-trip • `blank_option` — describes the no-template path (pass `creation_mode: "blank"` or omit template_id from site_create) WORKFLOW: filter by category/tag/search → for each candidate, OPEN `preview_demo_url` in a browser tool → narrow to 2–3 based on actual rendered design → present those to the user with the live URLs so they can pick. Filters compose with AND. With no filters, ordering is featured → usage_count → name, paginated 100 at a time.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Update a task — change status, priority, progress, due date, description, tags, etc.

tools.name: verify_lint
tools.description: Run `eslint . --max-warnings=0` inside the project's preview environment. Returns exit code + lint output.

tools.name: verify_run_tests
tools.description: Run the project's test script (npm test / pnpm test / etc.) inside its preview environment.

tools.name: verify_typecheck
tools.description: Run `tsc --noEmit` inside the project's preview environment. Returns exit code + stdout/stderr. Use BEFORE declaring a code change done. If the failing line is in a file you didn't touch, mention it but don't try to fix it unless asked — it's likely pre-existing.

tools.name: voice_audit_export_csv
tools.description: Exports this account's voice audit trail as CSV: every audit_logs row whose action is namespaced 'voice.', newest first, capped at 10,000. Columns: timestamp, action, actor_name, actor_id, details_json. The raw CSV body comes back inline as the tool result, not as a file, and an empty result is the header line alone. Read-only: no writes, no carrier call, no money, nothing sent to a person, and no credentials appear because the voice audit helper only ever stores event metadata, never SIP passwords or API keys. It does disclose staff PII, since each row names the actor by full name or email, plus caller-supplied names and numbers inside details_json. READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING IT AS A COMPLETE RECORD: work done through Olympus tools is largely ABSENT. A service key has no builder profile, so voice mutations call the audit helper with a null actor and the helper skips the row outright (audit_logs.user_id is nullable now and carries actor_type/actor_label, but the helper was never updated to use them), and several twins, including the voicemail read flip and the call wrap-up, never call it at all. What you get is essentially the dashboard's human actions. Traps. action REPLACES the 'voice.' prefix filter with an exact match rather than narrowing it, so a partial suffix like 'cdr' matches nothing while 'cdr.exported' matches; a wrong suffix returns the bare header, indistinguishable from a genuinely empty trail. actor must be the internal users UUID: a Clerk id or any other non-UUID goes straight into a uuid column and raises a Prisma error the route does not catch, so you get a 500, not an empty file. from and to are passed to new Date() with no validity check, so an unparsable date also 500s. Unlike the CDR export, to is NOT bumped to end of day here, so to=2026-08-01 stops at that day's midnight and silently drops the whole day; pass a full timestamp. The 10,000 row cap truncates newest-first with no marker, so the OLDEST events vanish quietly. Rows written by a system, cron or service actor come back with BOTH actor_name and actor_id empty, and although the query does load actor_type and actor_label the CSV never emits them, so there is no way to tell which non-human wrote the row. Cells are formula-guarded, so a value starting with = + - @ tab or carriage return arrives with a leading apostrophe. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_blocked_numbers_add
tools.description: Adds one number to this tenant's CALL blocklist and returns { blocked_number: row }. Reads exactly three fields: e164 (required), reason (max 280 chars, nullable), direction ('both' default | 'inbound' | 'outbound'). Anything else you send is dropped silently. This closes a path against a real person, and THE NUMBER THAT GETS BLOCKED MAY NOT BE THE ONE YOU SENT. The server rewrites the value before writing it: any input whose digits count is exactly 10 is stored as '+1' plus those digits, EVEN IF you sent a leading '+' (so '+1234567890' is stored as '+11234567890'); 11 digits starting with 1 get a '+'; otherwise the value is kept as sent when it already starts with '+', or gets a '+' prefixed to its digits. A 10-digit non-US number is therefore filed as a US number: you block a stranger's US line while the caller you meant still rings through. Pass full E.164 with country code, and read the e164 that comes back to confirm what was actually stored. What each direction enforces is not symmetric. 'inbound' (and the inbound half of 'both') is enforced by voice_server's call_router: the call is rejected with a 603 Decline BEFORE any extension rings, so there is no ring, no recording, no voicemail, no missed-call autoresponder and no missed-call SMS. Block a real customer and they hear a decline while your side gets no missed call to follow up on. 'outbound' (and the outbound half of 'both') is enforced in exactly ONE place, the server-side click-to-call route, which answers 403 blocked_number. The browser softphone dials by direct SIP INVITE and voice_server has no outbound blocklist check at all, so an outbound block does NOT stop a user dialling that number from the browser dock, and it does not touch SMS at all. Silent misses to expect on the inbound side: the matcher compares the caller's presented number in +form, bare-digit form and, for an 11-digit 1-leading number, the 10-digit forms, but it never ADDS a country code, so a row stored under the wrong prefix never matches. A withheld or blank caller ID skips the blocklist entirely, so blocking cannot stop an anonymous caller. On a database error the router fails OPEN and lets the call through by design. 409 already_blocked means (account_id, e164) is already on YOUR list, not a server fault: do not retry. 422 invalid_body when e164 fails ^\+?\d{8,15}$, reason exceeds 280 chars, or direction is not one of the three values. 402 is either voice_not_enabled or account_past_due. blocked_by is written NULL over this API, so nothing records that an agent did this: put who asked and why into `reason`. Unlike the dashboard route, this one enforces no per-user role permission, so the service key alone is the gate.

tools.name: voice_blocked_numbers_list
tools.description: Returns { blocked_numbers: [...] }, every row of this tenant's CALL blocklist newest-first: id, e164, reason, direction, blocked_by, created_at. No filters, no pagination, no cap: the whole list comes back in one response, so a tenant with thousands of rows returns thousands. `e164` is the SERVER-NORMALIZED value, not the string whoever added it typed, so always match on the value this returns rather than on what you think was submitted. `direction` is per row ('both' | 'inbound' | 'outbound') and the two halves are not enforced equally: see voice_blocked_numbers_add. Nothing in a row tells you whether it is actually stopping anything. `blocked_by` is a profiles UUID and is NULL for every row added over this API (an API key has no profile behind it), so this list cannot tell you who blocked a number; `reason` is nullable and is the only audit trail that exists. There is no expiry column, so every row is permanent until deleted. CALL blocklist only. It is not the SMS opt-out list (voice_sms_opt_outs), so a number absent here can still be STOP-suppressed for texting and a number present here can still be textable. An empty array means the blocklist is empty, not that call blocking is off. Two different failures both answer 402: error 'voice_not_enabled' (the Voice add-on is off on this account) and error 'account_past_due' (billing). Read the error key, not the status code.

tools.name: voice_blocked_numbers_remove
tools.description: Permanently deletes one blocklist row by id and returns { ok: true }. UNBLOCKING RE-OPENS A PATH SOMEBODY CLOSED ON PURPOSE. A block is how a tenant silences a harasser, a robocaller, or a number staff must not dial; removing it lets that number ring the team again on the very next inbound call and lets staff dial it again, immediately, with no cooldown, no expiry, no notification to anyone and no record that it happened. This is a human decision for the account owner, not an agent's judgement call: the row carries no author (blocked_by is NULL for anything added over the API) and often no reason, so the context that produced the block is usually invisible to you. Confirm with a person before calling. This route enforces no per-user role permission the way the dashboard one does, so nothing but the service key stands between the call and the delete. Hard delete, no soft delete, no undo: e164, reason and created_at go with the row. Re-adding later creates a new row with a new id and a new created_at, so the original block date is lost for good. Tenant-scoped before it deletes: the id is looked up with (id, account_id) first, so an id belonging to another tenant is a 404 rather than a cross-tenant delete. A 404 also means the row was already gone, which is not a retryable error. It does NOT lift a texting opt-out. STOP requests live in a separate table (voice_sms_opt_outs) behind its own route; nothing here re-enables SMS to somebody who asked you to stop, and this tool is never a substitute for that decision. 402 is either voice_not_enabled or account_past_due.

tools.name: voice_call_disposition_set
tools.description: Saves an operator wrap-up (an outcome chip plus notes) against a just-ended call. It finds the CDR row by account plus the last 7 digits of peer inside a plus/minus 120 second window around startedAtIso, then either merges metadata.user_disposition / user_notes into that call's existing crm_activities row or creates a new 'call' activity keyed external_id=call_uuid and links it back onto voice_calls.crm_activity_id. Returns { ok, activity_id, created }, where created false means it merged. Real-world effect: a CRM write only. It never dials, never ends a call, spends no money and sends nothing to a person, but what it writes is read by humans on the contact timeline and the activity page, and OVERWRITING a previous user_disposition or user_notes is not reversible because neither is versioned. Slow on purpose: the CDR lands a beat after hangup, so the handler tries the lookup up to 3 times and sleeps 2.5 seconds after EVERY failed attempt including the last one, so a miss blocks roughly 7.5 seconds before answering 404 call not found yet. Traps. THE DISPOSITION STRING IS NOT VALIDATED. Any text is stored, and the CRM picker only has labels for connected, left_voicemail, no_answer, busy, wrong_number, callback_requested, not_interested, qualified and unqualified, so anything else renders as an unstyled chip with a BLANK label, which reads as a broken UI rather than as a bad value. This also does NOT touch voice_calls.disposition, the phone system's own answered/voicemail/missed/ai_handled/abandoned signal, so call lists, filters and voice_calls_export_csv never reflect what you set here. direction is optional and matters more than it looks on the create path: omit it on an outbound call and the activity is titled 'Inbound call' and the contact is resolved from the CALLER leg, which is your own DID, so the wrap-up links to the wrong contact or to none. The peer match is a last-7-digit contains ordered newest-first, so two calls with the same person inside that 4 minute window resolve to the newest one and you can tag the wrong leg. 422 nothing to save when neither a truthy disposition nor a non-blank notes is supplied (an empty string or whitespace-only notes counts as absent); 422 peer and startedAtIso required when peer holds fewer than 7 digits or startedAtIso is unparsable. Sending only notes leaves any existing disposition intact and vice versa, but a supplied notes REPLACES the old note wholesale, it does not append. Asymmetry worth knowing: on the CREATE path notes is written to BOTH metadata.user_notes and the activity's body column and the subject picks up the resolved contact name, while on the MERGE path only metadata changes and the existing subject and body are left alone. Because a service key has no builder profile the created activity has owner_id null, and rep-scoped CRM views (leaderboard, My Queue, contact filters) silently skip owner-null call activities. Unlike the dashboard PATCH /api/crm/activities/[id] this route writes no user_disposition_at, user_disposition_by or user_notes_updated_at, so the wrap-up shows up with no author and no timestamp, and it calls no audit helper, so nothing records that an agent set it. Safe against retries: the create is keyed on call_uuid and linked back onto the call, so a second identical request merges instead of duplicating, and the later recording worker deliberately copies user_disposition and user_notes forward, so what you write here survives post-processing. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_call_get
tools.description: One call by voice_calls.id, for a deep link into a call older than the newest page voice_calls_list returns. Returns { call: { id, direction, from_number, to_number, peer_name, contact_id, started_at, answered_at, ended_at, duration_seconds, hangup_cause, recording_url, has_recording, recording_transcript, status } }. Three traps answer 200 having told you nothing true: recording_url is HARDCODED null on every response (has_recording is the real signal, and playable audio only comes from voice_recording_url_get), recording_transcript carries voice_calls.ai_summary, an AI-written prose summary, NOT the transcript (use voice_call_transcript_get for the actual words), and status is derived, so a call still ringing (no disposition, no ended_at) reads 'failed' while an ai_handled call reads 'completed'. from_number/to_number coerce a NULL number to the empty string, not to null, so an anonymous or missing caller ID reads as ''. This projection also drops most of the row: voice_calls_list returns raw DB rows with from_e164/to_e164 plus billable_seconds, ai_sentiment, spotted_keywords, attribution_json, utm_campaign, tracking_source, call_uuid, project_id, pool_session_id, queue_id, crm_activity_id and voicemail_read_at, none of which appear here. peer_name/contact_id come from a last-7-digit CRM match against non-deleted contacts, so two numbers sharing a tail attach the same contact and an archived contact reads as no match. The response carries PII: the far-party number, a named CRM contact, and an AI summary of a recorded conversation. 404 not_found is also the cross-tenant answer, since the lookup is scoped to the key's account. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, even though voice_calls_list answers fine on the same account because that route carries no plan gate.

tools.name: voice_call_tracking_diagnose
tools.description: The call-tracking doctor: one structured verdict on whether phone-call conversions are actually reaching Google Ads, and what to fix first. Returns seven checks, each with status ok|warn|fail|unknown, a plain-language explanation and one concrete next action, plus an overall verdict and an ORDERED fix_first list. Read fix_first rather than the check array: the checks are diagnostic, the order is the answer. Read-only, but not free: it makes outbound Google Ads READ calls and one HTTP GET of the tenant's deployed page. Pass skip_google and skip_site_fetch to stay entirely inside the database when either is slow or the connection is broken; both then report `unknown` rather than `ok`, and an `unknown` is NOT a pass. project_id is a selector inside the bound account, never a tenant argument: omit it and the doctor picks the most recently updated non-archived project, which on a multi-site account is very likely not the one you meant. days clamps to 1..365 (default 30). To prove number swapping actually works you need voice_call_tracking_live_probe, because that writes a row and cannot be reached from this read path.

tools.name: voice_call_tracking_live_probe
tools.description: Same verdict as voice_call_tracking_diagnose, but additionally asks the number pool for a DID exactly the way a visitor's browser does, which is the only way to PROVE number swapping works end to end. HAS A SIDE EFFECT, which is why it is a separate tool and not a flag on the read path: the probe writes a voice_pool_sessions row and HOLDS a tracking DID for the sticky window, so that number is unavailable to a real visitor until the window expires. On a pool with few active DIDs, repeated probing can starve live traffic. Run it to confirm a fix, not on a schedule. live_probe must be sent true to get the probe; without it this is just the read-only doctor with an extra round trip. Everything else behaves as in voice_call_tracking_diagnose.

tools.name: voice_call_tracking_outbox
tools.description: Row-level view of voice_conversion_uploads: which call conversions were queued, uploaded, failed or skipped, one row at a time, with the originating call joined on and each error_code translated into plain language. This is the companion to the doctor's aggregate verdict; use it once the doctor says uploads are failing and you need to know WHICH ones and why. Nothing in the product read this table before the route existed. The enqueue path wrote rows and the dispatch tick drained them, so a conversion that never reached Google left no visible trace. An empty result therefore means one of two very different things: nothing was ever enqueued (a tracking problem, ask the doctor) or everything uploaded cleanly. Filter status='failed' first. status and error_code accept a repeated param or a comma list; an unknown status is a 400 naming the valid set rather than a silent empty page. from/to filter created_at and a bad date is a 400. limit clamps to 1..200 (default 50), offset floors at 0, order is created_desc (default) | created_asc | oldest_queued. Account scope comes from the key binding, never from a parameter.

tools.name: voice_call_tracking_setup
tools.description: One idempotent operation that wires call-conversion tracking for a project end to end: number pool, tracking DIDs, per-project phone-tracking config, tenant conversion-upload policy, and the Google "Hiveku - Phone Call" conversion action. Returns per-step results plus an overall state, so success never has to be inferred from a bare 200. Safe to re-run: each step reports already_configured instead of duplicating work. SPENDS MONEY, but only one field does it. `did_count` is the ONLY thing here that can buy phone numbers. Omit it or send 0 and this provisions nothing on the carrier. When set, it buys only the shortfall between the pool's current active size and that target, at most 5 per run, and only after the E911 address checks out; a missing or unvalidated E911 address comes back as a `blocked` step naming the human action, so it never half-buys and never fails opaquely. Numbers, once bought, bill monthly until released. Use dry_run: true first on any account where you are not certain what already exists. The account comes from the key binding; a body-supplied account is neither read nor honoured.

tools.name: voice_call_transcript_get
tools.description: Full transcript for one call as { transcript: '<text>' }, read server-side out of the KMS recordings bucket rather than handed back as a URL. What comes back is the entire stored object body inline as one string, exactly as the post-process worker wrote it: no speaker array, no timestamps, no truncation and no pagination, so a long call returns a large payload in a single response. This is a verbatim record of a real conversation. Names, addresses, card and account numbers, health and financial detail all appear unredacted, and the handler applies NO redaction, NO consent check, NO retention check and no two-party-consent gate of any kind; the only thing it verifies is that the call belongs to the key's account. The id is voice_calls.id, the same id voice_recording_url_get takes. Silent failures: 404 no_transcript when transcript_s3_key is null, which is the normal state until the recording uploads and post-process runs, and a PERMANENT state when the extension has transcription switched off; 404 transcript_unavailable when the object cannot be read, which is byte-identical to what you get when HIVEKU_RECORDINGS_BUCKET is unset in that environment or the S3/KMS read is denied, because the reader swallows every non-NoSuchKey error to null, so a misconfigured deploy, an access-control failure and a swept object are indistinguishable (unlike voice_recording_url_get, this route never answers 503). The query selects ai_summary and then never returns it; read the summary from voice_call_get's recording_transcript field. 404 not_found for a call in another account; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_calls_export_csv
tools.description: Exports this account's call detail records as CSV, one row per call, for diffing against a CallRail or ad-platform export. Columns: call_uuid, direction, from, to, disposition, started_at, answered_at, ended_at, duration_seconds, billable_seconds, tracking_source, ai_sentiment, ai_summary, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, keyword, ad_group, click_id_type, landing_url, repeat_caller, environment.
