THERE IS NO FILE AND NO DOWNLOAD LINK: the raw CSV body comes back inline as the tool result, so an unbounded call can drop up to 50,000 rows of caller numbers and full AI call summaries straight into the conversation. Always bound it with from and to. Read-only: no carrier call, no money, nothing sent to a person, but the payload is bulk PII, including AI summaries of recorded conversations and the landing pages callers came from. Traps. Truncation is SILENT: the cap is 50,000 rows and the file carries no marker, so if you count exactly 50,000 data rows assume it was cut and narrow the window. An unrecognised disposition or direction value is DROPPED rather than refused, so one typo silently exports every call in the period instead of the slice you asked for; the UI's Missed chip is three dispositions, which is what missed_any means (missed, abandoned, voicemail). sort outside the allowlist falls back to started_at and only the exact string 'asc' flips the order, so with the row cap desc keeps the newest calls and asc keeps the oldest. to is bumped to end of UTC day so the last day is included, while an unparsable from or to is silently ignored rather than refused. q searches ai_summary, plus a digits match on both numbers when it holds 3 or more digits, plus up to 50 non-deleted CRM contacts by first or last name matched against BOTH legs (the voicemail inbox matches the caller leg only, so the same q can return different sets there). Blank utm columns do NOT mean direct traffic: a call whose attribution sweep looked and found nothing is stored as an {unmatched:true} sentinel that is rendered exactly like never-processed. keyword prefers the Google Ads click_view enrichment and falls back to utm_term. click_id_type is the LABEL of whichever click id the session carried (gclid, gbraid, wbraid, fbclid, msclkid, ttclid), never the value. repeat_caller is 'true' or empty and never 'false'. Cells are formula-guarded, so a value starting with = + - @ tab or carriage return arrives with a leading apostrophe. COMPLIANCE NOTE: the dashboard version of this export writes a voice.cdr.exported audit row; this one calls the audit helper with a null actor, and that helper console-warns and returns without writing, so an export taken through this tool leaves NO entry on the voice audit page and will not appear in voice_audit_export_csv. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_calls_list
tools.description: List call history. Filterable by direction, disposition, time window.

tools.name: voice_default_greetings_get
tools.description: Returns { account_name, defaults: { ivr, did, whisper, voicemail } }: the account's display name plus the four pre-canned greeting TEMPLATES filled in with it. These are suggestions, not configuration. Nothing here reads the IVR, DID, whisper or voicemail greetings the account actually has, so this can never tell you what callers hear today, it returns the identical four strings whether or not any greeting exists, and receiving a string changes nothing until you save it through the relevant IVR or voicemail route. The trap is that these strings are read ALOUD to callers once saved, and the name is seeded from accounts.name, the internal workspace label, NOT accounts.company_name (which exists and is not consulted). An account signed up as 'Psgi' produces 'Thanks for calling Psgi.' Check the name against the real trading name before writing it into a greeting. Second silent case: when accounts.name is empty or whitespace, account_name comes back as an empty string while the templates substitute the word 'us' ('Thanks for calling us.'). Read both fields, because that fallback is invisible if you only look at defaults. 402 is either voice_not_enabled (Voice add-on off) or account_past_due (billing): read the error key, not the status code.

tools.name: voice_diagnose_setup
tools.description: Snapshot of an account's voice provisioning state — tenant_provisioned, active DIDs, DIDs missing E911, extensions / ring_groups / IVRs / verified E911 addresses counts, plus a `blocking_issues` array of human-readable problems. First-resort tool when an admin asks 'is my phone system set up?' or 'why aren't my numbers working?'.

tools.name: voice_e911_addresses_list
tools.description: List the account's E911 addresses (registered + pending verification).

tools.name: voice_extension_create
tools.description: Provisions a REAL SIP endpoint on the tenant's FusionPBX/FreeSWITCH box and THEN writes the row, returning { extension: { id, extension, display_name, endpoint_type, user_id, phone_model, mac_address, sip_username, presence_state, e911_address_id, created_at } }. This is a live phone-system change, not a draft: the number is dialable internally immediately, a handset or softphone can register to it, and any DID, IVR option or ring group later pointed at it will ring it. No carrier order, no number purchase, no money. The SIP password is returned by the phone system exactly once, encrypted before the insert, and appears NOWHERE in this response, so the device itself can only be set up from the dashboard. THE ORDER CAN ORPHAN. The PBX endpoint is created BEFORE the database insert, so a failed insert leaves a live SIP endpoint with no builder row and an unrecoverable password. The usual cause is a unique collision, and the 409 can name the wrong thing: the handler returns extension_taken for any P2002 whose reported target contains the substring 'extension', and this table carries two more unique constraints, per-account sip_username and one endpoint per (user, endpoint_type, device), whose Postgres constraint names both contain 'voice_extensions'. So a second softphone_mobile for the same person surfaces either as 'Extension 1005 is already in use on this account' or, if the target comes back as field names instead, as a bare 500 internal_error. Neither message is the truth, and both leave the PBX endpoint behind. Check voice_extensions_list before retrying. SILENT 200s to expect. (1) endpoint_type 'external_number' with no external_target_e164 is ACCEPTED here and creates a black hole: the call router finds no target and the caller hears nothing. The update twin refuses that combination (422 forward_target_required); this route does not, so always send both together. (2) external_target_e164 is discarded to null unless endpoint_type is exactly 'external_number'. (3) e911_address_id is stored with no check that the address belongs to this account or is verified, this route makes no carrier call, and nothing in the phone system reads an EXTENSION's e911_address_id at all: every emergency path keys on the DID (voice_numbers.e911_address_id), which is where the hard E911 gate lives. Treat this field as a label, never as an emergency registration. (4) the personal-ring-group reconcile, which is what makes the owner's other phones ring this new endpoint, is best-effort and this response has NO warning field, so a failed reconcile is invisible: confirm with voice_ring_groups_list. phone_model and mac_address are deliberately NOT exposed. The route would persist them and never push them to the phone system (syncExtensionDevice is called only by .../[id]/phone, which has no Olympus twin), so the database would badge a desk phone provisioned while the handset's boot request is served nothing. Device provisioning stays a dashboard action. Errors: 422 invalid_body with zod issues (extension must be 2-6 digits, display_name 1-120 chars); 409 not_provisioned when the tenant has no FusionPBX domain yet, which means voice was never enabled for this tenant and is not a server fault; 409 extension_taken; 403 not_a_member when user_id is not a member of THIS account (deliberately stricter than the dashboard route, which does not check); 403 account_suspended; 402 is either voice_not_enabled (Voice add-on off, or the account has no billing row at all) or account_past_due, so read the error key and not the status; 404 / 409 / 422 / 502 extension_provision_failed when the phone system refuses. This twin does NOT enforce the dashboard's per-user voice 'extensions' permission, so the API key is the only gate. The only undo is voice_extension_delete, which is irreversible and refuses while anything routes to the extension.

tools.name: voice_extension_delete
tools.description: Tears the SIP endpoint down on the phone system and deletes the row, returning { id, deleted: true, upstream_cleaned: boolean }. THIS TAKES A PHONE OFFLINE AND IS IRREVERSIBLE. The stored SIP password dies with the row, so the handset or softphone can never register again: recovery means creating a NEW extension and re-provisioning the device from the dashboard, which no Olympus tool can do. upstream_cleaned false means the row had never been provisioned to the PBX and only the local row was removed; true means the phone system confirmed the teardown. Confirm with a human before calling. It will not strand a live call path, but the guard is narrower than it looks. It refuses with 409 extension_in_use, naming them, while any number routes to this extension (inbound target type extension or voicemail) or any ring group lists it as a member. It does NOT check IVR menu options, ring-group no-answer fallbacks, or queues, so a phone-tree digit pointing here is silently orphaned: voice_ivr_walk will afterwards report that option as resolved.type 'unknown' while the menu still answers 200 and looks healthy. Walk the trees before deleting. The 409 you are most likely to hit is invisible in the dashboard: any user with two or more registering endpoints (desk phone or softphones) has an auto-managed PERSONAL ring group that the ring-group editor deliberately hides, and its member row blocks the delete. It appears in the message as '<Person> (personal) (8001)'. Re-point or thin the group first. PARTIAL TEARDOWN ON FAILURE: the AI receptionist's transfer config is pruned FIRST (this extension is removed from transfer_directory and from human_transfer_extension) and that prune is never rolled back. If the phone system then refuses (502 or 422 delete_failed) the extension still exists and still rings, but the AI can no longer transfer callers to it, and nothing in the response says so. Re-run the delete, or re-add the transfer target. Voicemail: the route does nothing to preserve the mailbox or the messages in it, and a number pointed straight at this extension's voicemail blocks the delete rather than being re-pointed, so re-point that DID yourself first. After the row is gone the owner's personal ring group is reconciled so their remaining phones re-bundle; that is best-effort and a failure only logs, with no warning in the response. This twin does NOT enforce the dashboard's per-user voice 'extensions' permission, so the API key is the only gate. 404 not_found for an unknown id or one owned by another tenant, which also means it was already deleted and is not retryable; 500 internal_error for anything that is not a phone-system refusal; 402 is voice_not_enabled or account_past_due.

tools.name: voice_extension_get
tools.description: Reads one extension by UUID and returns { extension: { id, extension, display_name, endpoint_type, user_id, phone_model, mac_address, sip_username, presence_state, e911_address_id, created_at } } and NOTHING ELSE. It is a narrow select, and the omissions are the trap: external_target_e164, ring_timeout_seconds, every voicemail_* field (enabled, PIN, greeting text, greeting source, transcribe, email-on-receipt), both outbound caller-ID columns and fusionpbx_extension_uuid are all absent, so this can never tell you where a PSTN-forward extension actually rings, whether voicemail is on, what greeting callers hear, or what number the seat presents on outbound calls. voice_extensions_list returns the whole row and is the read for those. presence_state is the stored column, not a live SIP registration probe, so 'offline' may just be stale. Because fusionpbx_extension_uuid is not selected, an extension that was never provisioned to the phone system, and therefore cannot register at all, looks identical here to a healthy one. 404 not_found covers both an unknown id and an id belonging to another tenant, so it is never a cross-tenant read. Gated on the Voice plan: 402 voice_not_enabled means this cannot even confirm an extension exists on an account with the add-on off, and 402 also carries account_past_due, so read the error key. voice_extension_status covers most of the same ground from the diagnostics route, has NO plan gate, accepts the dial number as well as the UUID, answers 200 { data: { found: false } } instead of 404, and DOES return external_target_e164; prefer it for lookups, and use this tool when you specifically need e911_address_id (which voice_extension_status omits) or a hard 404 to confirm an id.

tools.name: voice_extension_status
tools.description: Status of a specific extension — who owns it, endpoint type, registration state. `q` accepts either the dial number ('1003') or the extension UUID.

tools.name: voice_extension_update
tools.description: Edits one extension in place and returns { extension: { id, extension, display_name, endpoint_type, user_id, phone_model, mac_address, sip_username, presence_state, e911_address_id, outbound_caller_id_number_id, outbound_caller_id_anonymous, fusionpbx_extension_uuid }, warning?: string }. ALWAYS READ warning. The row is saved locally first and every push to the phone system afterwards is best-effort, so a 200 carrying a warning means the database and the PBX now disagree about the display name, ring timeout, voicemail toggle or PIN, caller ID, greeting audio, or which phones ring. Re-saving is the retry. IT SPENDS MONEY AND REACHES CALLERS. Once the row ends up with voicemail_greeting_source 'tts' plus greeting text plus a voice id (from this patch or already stored), the audio is rendered through Cartesia, billed per character, written to the voice_tts_renders ledger and rolled into the monthly period. Callers hear the new greeting as soon as it lands on FreeSWITCH. A re-save whose text hash is unchanged reuses the existing render and costs nothing. CALLER ID IS CARRIER-FACING: it changes the number the called party sees on EVERY future outbound call from this seat. outbound_caller_id_number_id must be a DID owned by this account and active, else 422 invalid_caller_id; a toll-free DID is refused with 422 toll_free_caller_id because a 911 call would then present a number with no dispatchable address. That toll-free test only recognizes NANP +1 8xx numbers (800/833/844/855/866/877/888), so a non-US toll-free is not caught. outbound_caller_id_anonymous true presents CLIR (the callee sees Blocked) and WINS over the number id, and it also skips the ownership branch entirely, so an outbound_caller_id_number_id sent alongside it is written with no account check at all: another tenant's DID id is stored on your row, and an id matching no row at all trips the database foreign key in an update that has no try/catch, so the request dies as an unhandled 500 with nothing saved. null on outbound_caller_id_number_id means fall back to the tenant default. SILENT NO-OPS, every one of them a clean 200. (1) The caller-ID push only happens when the row already has a FusionPBX uuid, and that path adds NO warning, so a caller-ID-only save on a never-provisioned extension returns clean and changes nothing on the phone system. (2) ring_timeout_seconds: null and voicemail_pin: null are written to the database but are excluded from the push by an explicit not-null guard, so FreeSWITCH keeps the previous timeout and the mailbox keeps its old PIN. (3) Clearing voicemail_greeting_source to null nulls the greeting pointers but deliberately does NOT delete the rendered greeting_1.wav from FreeSWITCH, so callers keep hearing the greeting the UI now reports as gone. (4) A 'tts' mode without BOTH text and voice, or 'upload' with no key ever uploaded, renders nothing and only returns a warning. (5) voicemail_transcribe, voicemail_email_on_receipt and voicemail_email_to are database-only here and are read later by the voicemail-uploaded ingest handler, never by the PBX. (6) e911_address_id is stored with no ownership or verification check and no carrier call, and no emergency path reads it off an extension. The response is a narrow select and never echoes external_target_e164, ring_timeout_seconds, any voicemail_* field or the greeting state, so you cannot confirm those from the reply: read them back with voice_extensions_list, which returns the whole row. Refusals: the body schema is strict, so any unknown key is 422 invalid_body; phone_model and mac_address get their own 422 use_phone_route because saving them here would change the database without changing the phone system, and their route has no Olympus twin. endpoint_type 'external_number' with no forward target, in this patch or already on the row, is 422 forward_target_required; sending external_target_e164 on any other endpoint type is 422 not_a_forwarding_extension; switching AWAY from external_number clears the stored target so a stale number cannot go live later. Changing endpoint_type or user_id rewrites the personal ring group in FusionPBX for the old AND the new owner, which is literally which phones ring, and a failure there is only a warning. user_id must be a member of this account (403 not_a_member); user_id null clears the owner and is always allowed. 404 not_found for an unknown or another tenant's id; 402 is voice_not_enabled or account_past_due. This twin does NOT enforce the dashboard's per-user voice 'extensions' permission, so the API key is the only gate.

tools.name: voice_extensions_list
tools.description: List the account's extensions (seat phones / softphones / external-number forwards).

tools.name: voice_ivr_create
tools.description: Creates AND provisions a working auto-attendant. Not a database write: it reserves a free extension from this account's 6000-6999 IVR pool, inserts the voice_ivrs row, then calls voice_server, which renders the greeting and every per-option announcement through CARTESIA (a paid TTS vendor, real money per render), writes the MP3s to S3 and to the PBX filesystem, and installs live FreeSWITCH dialplan rules on the shared EC2 box. From the moment it returns, any DID already pointed at this IVR plays it to real callers. RETURNS { ivr, tts_cost_cents, renders, warning? }: the saved row including the assigned extension and fusionpbx_ivr_uuid, the Cartesia spend in cents (cache hits on unchanged text plus voice cost nothing and are not ledgered) and the COUNT of renders billed into voice_tts_renders and voice_usage_periods.tts_cents. Refusals: 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, which is a plan refusal and not an empty account; 409 not_provisioned when the account has no voice tenant yet (voice must be enabled on the PBX first); 409 no_extension_available when 6000-6999 is exhausted on this account; 409 extension_race when a concurrent create grabbed the same slot, which is retryable and re-scans for the next free number (pickIvrExtension is a best-effort scan, not a lock); 422 invalid_body. SILENT FAILURES, none of which error. greeting_tts_text with no greeting_voice_id renders NOTHING: the provisioner builds a greeting only when it has both text and a voice, so the menu answers callers with silence and the save still reports success. The same applies to every option's announcement_tts_text, which uses the IVR-level greeting_voice_id and never one of its own. An option whose target_id does not resolve in this account is NOT refused: it resolves to null and that digit is provisioned with no destination. The after-hours target is dropped the same way, leaving no after-hours route at all, and this route sends NO department with it, so an after-hours ai_agent always lands on the generic receptionist even when your menu options route to a specialist. business_hours is honoured open or closed PER DAY but the phone system supports only ONE shared open/close window, so when the submitted days disagree the response carries a `warning` naming the day whose window now applies to all of them. If FreeSWITCH provisioning fails you get 500 or 502 ivr_provision_failed WITH the saved row and a warning: the IVR exists, the extension stays reserved, nothing answers, and you fix it with voice_ivr_update rather than by creating a second one. Because an Olympus key has no builder profile the audit write is SKIPPED entirely (audit_logs.user_id is a NOT NULL FK), so this create leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_ivr_delete
tools.description: PERMANENTLY removes an auto-attendant and its call routing. IRREVERSIBLE and not database-only: voice_server drops the FreeSWITCH dialplan rules and DELETES the S3 audio objects (the greeting plus every option announcement), then the row is deleted and its 6xxx extension returns to the pool for reuse. There is no undo and the recorded prompts are gone; recreating the menu means paying Cartesia to render every prompt again. This route DOES refuse rather than orphan: 409 ivr_in_use while anything still routes here, and the message names each blocker - phone numbers whose inbound target is this IVR, ring groups falling back to it, queues overflowing to it, and OTHER IVRs whose menu digit or after-hours target points at it. Re-point those first. An option on THIS menu pointing at itself (press 9 to repeat) does not block its own deletion. WHAT THE GUARD DOES NOT COVER: it queries voice_numbers, voice_ring_groups, voice_queues and voice_ivrs only. A call-tracking DID pool whose voice_did_pools.inbound_target_id is this IVR, and a pending carrier order in voice_number_orders that will adopt into it, are both invisible to the check and are silently orphaned; every number that later joins that pool inherits a destination that no longer exists, and a DID left resolving a dead extension gives callers a fast busy while the dashboard still shows it as routed. RETURNS { id, deleted: true, warning? }. The warning is the partial-delete case: if voice_server does not confirm teardown the Hiveku row is STILL deleted, so the dialplan rule and the S3 audio can survive on the PBX for a menu Hiveku has forgotten (that orphan self-heals only if something re-provisions the same extension). A 200 with a warning is not a clean delete. An IVR that never reached the PBX (no voice tenant, or a null extension) is deleted with no teardown call and no warning at all. Also 404 not_found for an id on another account, and 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so nothing records who deleted it.

tools.name: voice_ivr_update
tools.description: Edits an existing auto-attendant and RE-PROVISIONS it end to end on every call, even a rename. voice_server re-renders any CHANGED greeting or option announcement through CARTESIA (paid TTS, real money per render), rewrites the MP3s in S3 and on the PBX filesystem, and re-installs the live FreeSWITCH dialplan rules, so callers hear the new menu immediately. RETURNS { ivr, tts_cost_cents, renders, warning? }: the persisted row, the Cartesia spend in cents and how many renders it paid for. Unchanged text plus voice is a hash cache hit and costs nothing. THE EXPENSIVE MISTAKE: the hash is over text PLUS voice, so changing greeting_voice_id alone invalidates the greeting AND every option announcement and a one-field save re-renders the entire menu at full price. PARTIAL BY DESIGN: a field you omit is not written. Omitting `options` keeps the stored menu and re-provisions from it; SENDING `options` REPLACES the whole menu, so a digit you leave out of the array is DELETED. Refusals: 404 not_found, which is also the answer for an IVR on another account; 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off; 409 not_provisioned when the account has no voice tenant; 422 invalid_body; and 409 menu_option_unresolvable, which happens only on a save that OMITS `options` while a stored option's target_type is not one of the seven canonical values. That refusal changes NOTHING at all and returns invalid_digits, so you repair those digits by sending a full `options` array once (the refusal is deliberate: guessing 'disconnect' for a broken option once made it permanently a hang-up as a side effect of renaming the IVR). SILENT FAILURES: greeting_tts_text or announcement_tts_text with no greeting_voice_id renders nothing and that prompt is simply silent; an option target_id that does not resolve in this account provisions that digit with no destination rather than erroring; an unresolvable after_hours_target_id is dropped, leaving no after-hours route; per-day business_hours windows collapse to ONE shared open/close window, reported as a `warning` naming the day that won. If voice_server fails you get 500 or 502 ivr_provision_failed with the ALREADY-UPDATED row plus a warning: Postgres moved, FreeSWITCH did not, and the two stay out of step until a later save succeeds. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this edit leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_ivr_walk
tools.description: Read one IVR phone tree with every menu target pre-resolved a single level deep, so you can narrate what a caller actually hears without a round-trip per option. Returns {ivr:{id,name,extension,greeting:{text,voice_id,rendered},options,invalid_input_max_attempts,business_hours,after_hours}}. options is keyed by digit, each {digit,target_type,target_id,label,announcement_tts_text,announcement_voice_id,resolved}; resolved is a union where extension carries extension+display_name, ring_group carries strategy plus its full member roster in priority (ring) order, ivr carries a sub-IVR stub of {id,name,extension} and DOES NOT recurse further, ai_agent carries only the account-wide ai_agent_enabled flag, and repeat/disconnect carry nothing. after_hours runs through the SAME resolver, so it degrades the same way. A deleted or missing target does NOT error: it becomes {type:'unknown',reason}, so a tree whose every option points at a deleted extension still answers 200 and looks healthy at a glance. Read every resolved.type before reporting that the menu works. A target_type outside extension/voicemail/ring_group/ivr/ai_agent/repeat/disconnect also comes back unknown with reason 'unsupported target_type: X', which means this route cannot name it, not that the menu is broken. A voicemail option with a null target_id is NOT a real mailbox lookup: it returns the synthesized literal display_name 'Default voicemail' with id and extension null. SILENT DROPS: only single-character keys matching [0-9*#] survive the loop, so menu_json's documented 'default' fallback key and any multi-character key are absent from options entirely and the fallback branch is invisible here. greeting.voice_id NEVER comes back null because it falls back to a hardcoded Cartesia default (a0e99841-438c-4a64-b679-ae501e7d6091), so a non-null voice is not evidence anyone chose one, while announcement_voice_id has no fallback and is just the IVR's own greeting_voice_id or null, so the two disagree on the same IVR; greeting.rendered false means the text was never synthesized to S3. invalid_input_max_attempts reports 3 when the column is null. NOTHING in this response reports fusionpbx_ivr_uuid, so a tree that reads perfectly here may never have been loaded onto the PBX and may route zero live calls: confirm provisioning with voice_diagnose_setup. BUSINESS HOURS ARE THE SOFTEST FIELD HERE: business_hours is non-null for ANY object in the column, but timezone and schedule are read only from the {timezone, schedule:{'0'..'6':[openMinute,closeMinute]}} shape (Sunday = 0), so a row stored in another shape reports timezone null and schedule {} and still looks configured; is_open_now is derived only from that embedded timezone (the separate business_hours_timezone column is never read) and is null both when the timezone is absent and when the date math throws, so null means unknown and never means closed. Even a well-formed schedule over-promises: the provisioner emits ONE FreeSWITCH time-of-day window shared across every open day and silently keeps the first open day's window when they differ, so differing per-day hours are narrated here and not enforced on the phone. Read-only: there is no Olympus write twin, because editing a live phone tree is a human action in the dashboard. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row); 404 not_found for an unknown id or one owned by another account.

tools.name: voice_ivrs_list
tools.description: List the account's IVR menus.

tools.name: voice_number_cnam_set
tools.description: WRITES THE CALLER-ID NAME TO THE CARRIER. The change goes to Telnyx, which pushes it into the national CNAM databases, so every person this tenant calls sees the new name on their handset once it propagates: typically 12 to 24 hours, up to 72. It is not instantly reversible, because clearing it is a second carrier write with the same delay. It places no calls and costs no per-use money, but it changes how this business is identified to the public. Worth doing: an unregistered number shows bare digits and carrier analytics at Verizon, T-Mobile and AT&T are far likelier to label it Potential Spam, so CNAM is one of the few reputation levers a tenant controls. Returns { number: { cnam_name, cnam_enabled, cnam_updated_at } } and NOTHING ELSE, not the rest of the number row. cnam_name is what the CARRIER returned, falling back to your name uppercased, so the stored value routinely differs in case from what you sent. THE SILENT FAILURE: cnam_updated_at is stamped when the carrier ACCEPTED the write, not when handsets show it. Never report the new name as live off that timestamp; it only means the request landed. Refusals, all before the carrier call so nothing is half-done: 422 invalid_body for a name over 15 characters or containing anything but letters, numbers and spaces (no ampersand, no punctuation, no accents), and for enabled true with a blank or whitespace-only name; 422 cnam_not_applicable_toll_free because CNAM is a geographic-number registry and toll-free NPAs 800, 833, 844, 855, 866, 877 and 888 are not in it; 422 not_provisioned when the row has no carrier id yet, which is the normal state for a half-provisioned or still-porting number; 404 not_found, which is also the cross-tenant answer. Any failure after that point is 502 cnam_failed: the usual case is a carrier rejection with nothing persisted, which is the safe direction, but the same 502 covers a carrier write that landed and whose response or local mirror write was lost, so verify with voice_number_get rather than assuming a 502 was a no-op. enabled false ignores cnam_name entirely and clears the local name to null. NO AUDIT ROW: the audit helper is called with a null user because a service key has no builder profile, which is its documented anonymous path, so it console-warns and writes nothing to audit_logs. This public-facing carrier change leaves no entry on the voice audit page. The per-user communications.numbers permission that guards the dashboard is not applied on this surface. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_number_get
tools.description: One DID by voice_numbers.id, for the detail voice_numbers_list does not carry. Returns { number } as the ENTIRE unprojected row (findFirst with no select): e164, provider, provider_number_id (the Telnyx phone-number id), label, purpose, tracking_source, tracking_campaign_id, inbound_target_type, inbound_target_id, inbound_ai_department, geo_routing_json, e911_address_id, is_active, campaign_name, whisper_message, greeting_message, greeting_voice_id, greeting_audio_s3_key, greeting_text_hash, greeting_rendered_at, the four whisper_* equivalents, recording_enabled, forward_to_e164, telnyx_messaging_profile_id, messaging_profile_attached_at, tf_verification_status, cnam_name, cnam_enabled, cnam_updated_at, created_at and updated_at. Fields that answer with something other than what they look like: is_active true does NOT mean calls arrive, because routing lives in inbound_target_type plus inbound_target_id and the FusionPBX side of that pair is pushed best-effort by voice_number_update, so this row can describe a route FreeSWITCH never received. cnam_name and cnam_enabled are a LOCAL MIRROR written only after a successful carrier write, and cnam_updated_at is the carrier ACCEPT time, not the moment handsets show the name (12-24h typically, up to 72h), so a fresh timestamp is not evidence the name is live. tf_verification_status null means never submitted, not rejected. greeting_audio_s3_key and whisper_audio_s3_key are S3 object keys, not URLs, and nothing here plays them. recording_enabled null means inherit the tenant default, which is not the same as false. purpose 'pool' is the legacy spelling of 'did_pool' on old rows. geo_routing_json is raw JSON and null when no location rules were ever set. What is NOT here: pool membership. A pooled DID's routing, whisper and greeting are also configured on its pool and the router lets the per-number value win, so a value on this row can silently beat the pool page that claims to own it; check voice_pools_list. 404 not_found is also the cross-tenant answer, since the lookup is scoped to the key's account. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, even for a number that exists. Read-only: no carrier call, no cost, nothing reaches a person.

tools.name: voice_number_lookup
tools.description: Resolves a raw phone number to a CRM contact for an in-call contact card: { contact: { id, name } | null, last_call_at }. It is a phone-number-to-identity oracle scoped to the targeted account, so treat the result as PII. contact carries ONLY id and name (name falls back to the stored phone string, then to the literal 'Contact', when both name fields are empty), so no email, phone, company or owner comes back and anything richer needs a CRM tool. Matching is last-7-digits contains, deliberately looser than the screen-pop matcher: two different numbers sharing their final seven digits resolve to the same contact, duplicate CRM rows for one number resolve to whichever is seen first, and soft-deleted contacts never resolve at all, so an archived customer reads as no match. SILENT FAILURES: when number is omitted, empty, or has fewer than 7 digits once non-digits are stripped, the route answers 200 with { contact: null, last_call_at: null } without querying anything and never returns 400, so malformed input is indistinguishable from a genuine miss; and because the result map is keyed on the CONTACT's own last 7 digits while the read uses the query's last 7, a stored number whose tail differs (an extension suffix such as '555-1234 x99') matches the database filter and still resolves to contact: null. last_call_at is the started_at of the newest call on this account touching that same 7-digit tail, in either direction and at any disposition, so an unanswered outbound attempt sets it and it can even come from a different number sharing the tail; it is not evidence of a conversation. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_number_release
tools.description: PERMANENTLY GIVES THE PHONE NUMBER BACK TO THE CARRIER. This is irreversible: no undo, no grace period, no confirmation argument. The DID returns to Telnyx inventory and CANNOT BE RE-BOUGHT: it can be sold to a stranger, inbound calls to it stop, and every place it is printed stops working, including vehicle wraps, business cards, signage, the Google Business listing, ad call extensions and email signatures. Only ever call this after a human has explicitly confirmed this exact number, by digits. Returns { id, e164, released, destination_removed, soft } on the carrier path, or { id, released: false, soft } when the row carried no provider_number_id, in which case NOTHING is sent to the carrier and the local row is simply removed. THE SILENT FAILURE: released is echoed straight from the voice server and the local row is deleted (or, with soft, cleared) REGARDLESS of its value, because the delete runs unconditionally once the release call resolves. A 200 carrying released:false means Hiveku has forgotten a number Telnyx may still own and still bill for, and there is no local row left to retry from. Check released on every response. PARTIAL TEARDOWN, none of it rolled back: BEFORE the carrier call the handler releases the FusionPBX inbound route (failure only console.warned), deletes this number's DNI pool membership, and clears the DID off every extension presenting it as caller ID on the PBX and here. If the carrier release then fails you get 502 release_failed with the local row intact, but the number is already out of its pool, off every extension's caller ID and NO LONGER TAKING INBOUND CALLS. Retrying is the only way forward and the number is unusable in between. There is no warning field on any response: a partial PBX teardown is invisible to the caller. NO DEPENDENCY GUARD ANYWHERE: this handler has no 409 at all. Nothing checks whether this is the account's only DID, its purpose 'main' business line, a tracking campaign's destination, a pool's last member or a number a workflow depends on. soft is NOT a safe mode and NOT a dry run: the carrier release happens either way, and soft only keeps the row for audit with is_active false and provider_number_id nulled instead of deleting it (a soft-released row still appears in voice_numbers_list unless you filter on is_active). soft must be the exact STRING '1', because the route compares searchParams.get('soft') === '1'; a boolean true serializes as 'true' and silently takes the HARD DELETE path. Per-extension caller-ID cleanup is best-effort and never throws, so a phone whose cleanup failed keeps presenting a number the account no longer owns, which fails STIR/SHAKEN attestation and becomes spoofing if the carrier re-sells the DID. This route writes NO audit row at all, so a permanent release leaves no entry on the voice audit page, and the per-user communications.numbers permission that guards the dashboard is not applied on this surface. 404 not_found is the missing-row and cross-tenant answer; a carrier-side 404 also comes back as HTTP 404 but with error release_failed, and any other carrier failure is 502 release_failed. An unexpected exception is 500 internal_error. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on. To take a number out of service reversibly, use voice_number_update with is_active false instead; that keeps the DID.

tools.name: voice_number_update
tools.description: CHANGES A LIVE PHONE LINE. Editing inbound_target_type, inbound_target_id, inbound_ai_department or forward_to_e164 rewrites the FusionPBX inbound route, so the very next inbound call rings somewhere else. Editing e911_address_id calls Telnyx and changes the street address emergency services are dispatched to on a 911 call from this number. Editing greeting_message or whisper_message with a matching voice id renders new audio through Cartesia, which COSTS MONEY per render (hash-compared, so an unrelated field edit does not re-render). Returns { number }: the row as written by the single update, captured BEFORE the audio render and BEFORE the PBX push, so greeting_audio_s3_key, greeting_text_hash, greeting_rendered_at and the whisper equivalents in the response are the PRE-render values and are stale on any call that rendered audio. Re-read with voice_number_get. THE SILENT FAILURE: the FusionPBX push is best-effort. A failure is console.errored and this route still answers 200 with the new row, leaving Hiveku showing one route while FreeSWITCH still rings the old target until a human repairs it. The same 200 comes back when the account has no voice tenant row, because the sync returns early with no fusionpbx_domain and pushes nothing. A TTS failure is swallowed the same way: 200, and callers hear the robotic say:flite fallback instead of the greeting you just set. SECOND SILENT FAILURE: the parse coerces a null e911_address_id to undefined, which Prisma reads as no change, so an attempt to CLEAR E911 answers 200 having ignored that key entirely (and on a toll-free DID that same null is read as 'no E911 sent', so it does NOT trip the toll-free refusal either). Half-applied patch: if the carrier rejects an e911_address_id change you get 502 e911_carrier_sync_failed and ONLY that one column is rolled back, while every other field in the same call is already committed and neither the PBX sync nor the TTS render ever ran. Refusals this route DOES enforce, all before any write: 422 e911_not_applicable_toll_free when a NON-NULL e911_address_id is sent on a toll-free DID; 422 e911_required when activating a non-toll-free DID that has no E911 address, and 422 e911_address_invalid when that address is not on this account or carries no carrier registration (RAY BAUM's Act); 422 inbound_target_unroutable when a routing change names a target that is missing, on another account, or has no dial extension, because the sync would otherwise RELEASE the inbound route and leave the row claiming a number is routed while it is dead; 422 geo_rule_target_invalid for the same problem inside a location rule; 409 managed_by_pool listing the fields, when this number sits in a pool that ACTUALLY manages them (a pool owns routing only once it has a destination, whisper only when whisper is enabled with a template, greeting only when it has greeting text), though clearing a managed field to null and re-sending an unchanged value are both deliberately allowed; 422 number_in_pool when setting purpose 'main' on a number that still rotates between website visitors. is_active false is a partial release: it clears this DID off every extension presenting it as caller ID, on the PBX as well as here, best-effort per extension, so a failed clear is only logged and that phone keeps presenting a number this account no longer presents. The body is strict, so an unknown key is a 422 that writes nothing: cnam_name and cnam_enabled are NOT settable here (use voice_number_cnam_set), nor are tf_verification_status or the audio-cache columns. This route calls NO audit helper at all, so a routing change made here leaves no entry on the voice audit page, and the per-user communications.numbers permission that guards the dashboard is not applied on this surface. 404 not_found is also the cross-tenant answer. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_numbers_list
tools.description: List the account's DIDs (E.164 phone numbers). Filter by is_active.

tools.name: voice_numbers_search
tools.description: Searches Telnyx carrier inventory for buyable phone numbers. SEARCH ONLY: it places no order, RESERVES NOTHING and spends no money, so a number listed here is still on the open market and another buyer can take it between this call and any purchase. Returns { results: [ { e164, locality, state, monthly_cost_cents, setup_cost_cents, features, number_type } ] }; locality, state and both cost fields can each be null. features is a string array such as voice and sms, and a result without sms cannot text. monthly_cost_cents is a RECURRING carrier charge and setup_cost_cents a one-time one, nonzero on premium prefixes, so a shortlist handed to a human carries real cost. DEAD END BY DESIGN: there is no Olympus route that buys a number (no POST exists under /api/olympus/voice/numbers), so nothing on this tool surface can complete the order. Present the shortlist and let a person buy it in the dashboard; never tell anyone a number has been ordered or reserved. Refusals: 422 missing_filter when a LOCAL search names none of area_code, locality or state, because an unbounded 'every DID in North America' request just burns a Telnyx call; 422 invalid_body when number_type toll_free is combined with any geographic filter, since toll-free inventory is non-geographic and Telnyx would return zero rows, and equally when toll_free_prefix is sent under local mode. 800 is deliberately missing from toll_free_prefix and cannot be searched at all: premium carrier pricing with no billing pass-through makes it unpurchasable at every layer. THE TRAP THAT IS NOT A CLIENT ERROR: 503 voice_server_update_pending on a toll-free search whose results are not all toll-free. That is a deploy-window guard, not a bug: a voice server predating toll-free support ignores the field, runs a LOCAL search and hands back geographic numbers, and buying one of those as toll-free would land a local DID with NO E911. The builder auto-deploys in about 35 minutes while the voice server is a manual deploy, so this window is real. Retry later, do not fall back to a local search and call it toll-free. Other traps: an empty results array on a 200 means no matching inventory, not a failure; there is NO cursor and NO pagination, so limit (1 to 50, default 20) is the entire result set you can ever get; area_code must be exactly three digits with no +1 and state must be a two-letter code, which the route uppercases for you; any voice-server 5xx surfaces as 503 voice_server_error while a non-carrier exception is rethrown as a 500. Each call is one outbound Telnyx API request billed to this account's carrier relationship, so do not loop it to page through inventory. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_pools_list
tools.description: List every tracking-DID (dynamic number insertion) pool on the account with its call handling, its member DIDs, and where each member DID actually sends an inbound call. Returns {pools:[{id,account_id,name,description,sticky_minutes,conversion_sticky_days,exhaustion_policy,is_active,inbound_target_type,inbound_target_id,forward_to_e164,created_at,updated_at,whisper_enabled,whisper_template,greeting_text,caller_id_mode,attribution_model,whisper_voice_id,greeting_voice_id,tracking_source_mode,tracking_source_rules,member_count,members:[{voice_number_id,e164,label,purpose,routing:{type,target_name,forward_to_e164}}]}]}. THE CALL-HANDLING BLOCK CAN BE FICTION: whisper_enabled, whisper_template, greeting_text, caller_id_mode, attribution_model, whisper_voice_id, greeting_voice_id, tracking_source_mode and tracking_source_rules come from a SECOND read wrapped in a try/catch that swallows P2022, so if those columns are not pushed on this deployment every pool silently reports the same hardcoded defaults (whisper_enabled false, caller_id_mode 'caller', attribution_model 'first_touch', tracking_source_mode 'all', the rest null) and NOTHING in the payload says the read failed. Never report those as a tenant's configured settings without corroborating in the dashboard. The POOL-LEVEL destination is returned raw and un-resolved: inbound_target_type and inbound_target_id come back as a bare type string and a bare UUID with no name, and only the per-member routing block is name-resolved. member_count counts raw membership rows while members[] skips any row whose DID is missing from the account-scoped number lookup, so member_count greater than members.length means the DID was deleted or belongs to another account, not that the page was truncated. Member rows also DROP voice_pool_members.weight, which is what biases rotation, so you cannot see why one DID is served more often than another from this response. In routing, a non-null type with target_name null means the target was deleted or belongs to another account; type null returns the LITERAL synthesized string 'Account default routing' as target_name, which is a label this route invents and not a real target; routing.forward_to_e164 is populated only for external_number extensions, so a null there is not proof the call stays on the platform. PII: this response carries live E.164 tracking numbers, and when a seat-assigned extension has a blank display_name the label falls back to the linked user's first/last name and then to their raw EMAIL ADDRESS, so a staff member's email can appear in routing.target_name. No pagination and no filters: inactive pools come back too, so filter on is_active yourself. tracking_source_mode and tracking_source_rules gate NEW session mints only, so tightening the rules does nothing to a visitor already inside a sticky window (sticky_minutes, extended by conversion_sticky_days once they call), and a pool whose DIDs are all held by sticky sessions falls back per exhaustion_policy ('swap_fallback' shows the tenant's main DID and flags the call, 'reject' keeps the number the page already rendered). Read-only: the source route also exports POST (create a pool), not twinned here. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_get
tools.description: Read one number-port order by id. Returns {port_order:{...}} in the same masked shape as voice_port_orders_list, resolved with an account-scoped findFirst, so an id belonging to another tenant is a 404 and never a cross-tenant read of someone else's porting paperwork. This is the only way to reach an order older than the 100-row window voice_port_orders_list caps at, and you need the id from elsewhere: support_key is a field on the row, not a lookup key here. SAME PII WARNING: only losing_pin and losing_account_number are masked, and the account number still shows its real last four digits; the billing street address, the billing telephone number, the authorized signer, the full E.164 list, the LOA and bill S3 keys, and the unmasked authorization_json / end_user_location_json blobs all come back verbatim. THIS IS THE LOCAL MIRROR, NOT THE CARRIER. status, status_raw, foc_date and exception_details_json are whatever the last carrier webhook or the porting-status poll cron wrote; this route performs no refresh, so a freshly changed order can read stale, and an unknown carrier token updates status_raw ONLY and leaves status frozen. The local vocabulary also runs one step ahead of the carrier by design, so 'submitted' can sit on an order the carrier still holds as an unconfirmed draft: read action_status (draft_only|details_set|submitted|activating|cancelled) for what the carrier actions actually did. last_notified_status and last_notified_comment_at are notification watermarks advanced by the sweep cron, not port state, and reading last_notified_status as the status will report the wrong thing. SUCCESS THAT IS NOT SUCCESS: adoption_state_json is the per-e164 adoption ledger {adopted_at, provider_number_id, route_created, messaging_attached} and adopted_at is set only once EVERY number on the order is adopted, so status 'ported' with adopted_at null means the transfer completed at the carrier while the DIDs are not yet usable on the platform. 'exception' means the losing carrier flagged a fixable problem, with its codes verbatim in exception_details_json (ACCOUNT_NUMBER_MISMATCH, LOA_ILLEGIBLE and similar); pair it with voice_port_order_requirements. Read-only: the source route also exports PATCH (mutating the order's local fields), not twinned here. 404 not_found for an unknown or foreign id; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_requirements
tools.description: Ask the carrier what this port order still needs (an LOA, a recent bill, a verification code) before it can be confirmed, so a confirm is not filed with unmet requirements that bounce back as an exception days later. Returns {requirements:[{field_type,name,description,acceptance_criteria,met}]}; the raw carrier payload is deliberately NOT returned, because it carries the end-user admin block holding the account number and PIN that are masked everywhere else. THE EMPTY LIST IS THE TRAP AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF READING THIS CAREFULLY: an order that has never reached the carrier (telnyx_order_id null, which every draft is) short-circuits to 200 with requirements: [] without calling out at all, and a carrier payload whose requirements key is not an array produces the identical empty result. An empty array therefore means 'nothing was ever asked' exactly as often as it means 'nothing is outstanding'. Confirm the order actually has a telnyx_order_id via voice_port_order_get before reading an empty list as all-clear, and note that having a telnyx_order_id still does not mean the order was confirmed (check action_status). met is Boolean(field_value): it says a value was SUBMITTED, not that the carrier ACCEPTED it, so an illegible LOA or a mismatched account number reads met true here and only surfaces as an exception on the order days later. LITERAL FALLBACKS MASQUERADING AS DATA: name falls back to record_type and then to the literal string 'Requirement', field_type falls back to the literal string 'document', and description and acceptance_criteria come straight from the carrier and are frequently null, so a vague-looking entry may be a payload this route could not name rather than a vague requirement. This is a LIVE NETWORK CALL out through the voice server to the carrier, not a local read: expect real latency and a real failure mode. The order is resolved account-scoped BEFORE its telnyx_order_id is handed to the carrier lookup, precisely because that carrier call would otherwise be a cross-tenant read of another account's port paperwork. Errors: {error:'carrier_error',message} at the carrier's own status code, collapsed to 502 when the carrier returned 5xx, and {error:'internal_error'} at 500 otherwise. Read-only: uploading the LOA or the bill, and confirming or cancelling the order, are legal acts under a signed authorization and are not exposed here. 404 not_found for an unknown or foreign order id; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_orders_list
tools.description: List the account's number-port orders (moving a phone number in from a losing carrier), newest first. Returns {port_orders:[...]} of voice_port_orders rows: status, status_raw, action_status, support_key (PORT-XXXXXX), batch_key, losing_carrier_name, billing_name, billing_phone_number, billing_address_json, authorized_signer, phone_numbers, requested/actual/foc dates, telnyx_order_id, exception_details_json, adoption_state_json, adopted_at, rejection_reason, notes. THIS RESPONSE IS CUSTOMER PII AND LEGAL PORTING PAPERWORK. EXACTLY TWO FIELDS ARE MASKED AND NOTHING ELSE IS REDACTED: losing_pin returns as bullets, and losing_account_number returns as bullets plus the REAL LAST FOUR DIGITS, which the route decrypts on purpose to produce, so this call does disclose the tail of the losing carrier's account number (if decryption throws, the tail is silently empty and looks identical to a short number). The billing street address, the billing telephone number (the BTN), the authorized signer's name, the full E.164 list and the S3 keys of the signed LOA and the carrier bill all come back verbatim. authorization_json and end_user_location_json are ALSO returned untouched and are documented in the schema as {authorized_person, billing_phone_number, account_number, pin_passcode} and the end user's street address, so the masking is not a defence for them; nothing in this platform writes authorization_json today, which is why it reads null, but the sanitizer would not cover it if anything ever did. Do not paste this response into a channel, a ticket or a document. HARD CAP: take 100, with no pagination, no cursor and no filter, so an account with more than 100 orders can never reach the oldest ones through this tool and the cut is silent; use voice_port_order_get with a known id to reach past it. STATUS TRAPS: the LOCAL vocabulary deliberately runs one step AHEAD of the carrier, so 'submitted' means filed with OUR side and being validated while the carrier order may still be raw draft and unconfirmed, and 'pending_carrier' means it sits with the LOSING carrier; the carrier's own raw token 'submitted' maps to pending_carrier, so the two vocabularies collide on the same word and status_raw is what answers what the carrier thinks. action_status (draft_only|details_set|submitted|activating|cancelled) is the sub-state of the carrier action calls and is the honest answer to 'was this actually confirmed'. An unrecognised carrier token normalizes to NULL and the local status DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MOVE (only status_raw is updated), so an order that looks stuck may have advanced at the carrier under a token this platform does not know. 'cancel-pending' collapses into 'cancelled', so an in-flight cancellation reads as finished unless you check status_raw. One submission can appear as several rows because the carrier auto-splits a create by country/type/SPID; siblings share batch_key. Read-only: the source route also exports POST, which FILES a real port order with the carrier. Filing, confirming and cancelling a port are legal acts against a losing carrier under a signed LOA and are deliberately not exposed to an agent. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_presence_get
tools.description: Live BLF lamp state for the account's extensions: { extensions: [{ extension, registered, state, direction, other_party }], channels_ok }, where state is offline | idle | ringing | in_call | hold and other_party is the far-party number of the call in progress. Treat the payload as PII: it says who is on the phone right now and with which number. It is a point-in-time snapshot proxied from voice_server, not a subscription, so two consecutive calls legitimately disagree. THE SILENT FAILURE: the body { extensions: [], channels_ok: false } is returned both when the tenant has no fusionpbx_domain provisioned (voice never set up) and when the voice_server call threw and was swallowed into a console.error, and it is also what a genuinely idle or empty account returns whenever channel state is down. The route emits no 5xx, so an empty list must never be read as 'nobody is on a call'. When channels_ok is false but the list is non-empty, FreeSWITCH channel state was unavailable and every lamp degrades to registered/offline: ringing, in_call and hold can never appear no matter what is really happening. Second trap: this Olympus twin is deliberately stricter than the dashboard. An Olympus key carries no system_role, so the handler takes the restrictive branch UNCONDITIONALLY and extensions owned by a saas_owner or saas_user are always filtered out, meaning an extension voice_extensions_list shows can be legitimately absent here. FusionPBX-side registrations with no matching voice_extensions row for the account are dropped silently too. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off. Takes no parameters.

tools.name: voice_queue_delete
tools.description: PERMANENTLY deletes an ACD call queue. IRREVERSIBLE: the mod_callcenter queue, its agent tiers and its dialplan rule are torn down on the PBX, then the voice_queues row is deleted and its agent rows cascade. The 5xxx extension returns to the pool and can be claimed by something else, so recreating the queue may not get the same number back. RETURNS { id, deleted: true, warning? }. THE WARNING IS A PARTIAL DELETE, NOT A NOTE: teardown runs first but a failure is only reported, never aborted, so the row is deleted regardless and a live queue and dialplan rule can survive on the phone system for a queue Hiveku has forgotten. The warning says to run a tenant repair if calls still reach it, and that is literal - callers can still land in an unmanaged queue. Compare with voice_ring_group_delete, which aborts and deletes nothing when teardown fails. It DOES refuse with 409 queue_in_use while any phone number still routes here, naming how many, because that DID would otherwise start silently failing live calls. That number count is the ONLY dependency it queries. It is also the only pointer the routing schema models for a queue (an IVR menu digit and a ring-group fallback cannot target a queue), with two exceptions nothing checks: a call-tracking DID pool whose voice_did_pools.inbound_target_id is this queue, and a pending carrier order in voice_number_orders that will adopt into it, are both silently orphaned along with every number that later joins that pool. Also 404 not_found for a queue on another account, and 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so nothing records who deleted it.

tools.name: voice_queue_update
tools.description: Edits a live ACD call queue and re-provisions it. voice_server is called BEFORE the database write and REPLACES the mod_callcenter queue row, its agent tiers and its dialplan rule WHOLESALE on every save, including a pure rename, and re-places the hold-music audio; callers already waiting in the queue and callers arriving next are routed by the new config immediately. No TTS and no carrier spend. RETURNS { queue, warning? }, the queue re-read after the write with its members[] included. A 200 DOES NOT MEAN THE PHONE SYSTEM AGREED: a provisioning failure is caught, the edit still saves, and the only signal is `warning` saying the phone system did not pick up the change; a queue with no voice tenant or no extension saves with a different warning and pushes nothing at all. PARTIAL, with two different null rules. abandon_target_type, abandon_target_id, moh_s3_key, greeting_tts_text and greeting_voice_id are read by KEY PRESENCE, so sending null CLEARS them and omitting keeps the stored value; every other scalar falls back to the stored value. `members` REPLACES the roster wholesale and every extension_id must belong to this account (422 invalid_member); omit the key to leave agents alone, or send an empty array to leave the queue with no agents. THE ABANDON TARGET IS NOT HARD-VALIDATED, unlike a ring-group fallback. An abandon_target_id that is not in this account, or a ring group or IVR whose extension is NULL, resolves to nothing and the queue is provisioned with NO timeout action while the row happily stores the target: the dashboard shows an overflow destination and callers who exhaust max_wait_sec are dropped instead. Verify the target resolves before relying on it. Only voicemail, extension, ring_group and ivr are accepted (voicemail and extension take a voice_extensions uuid); ai_agent and external_number are 422 invalid_body even though the column allows them, and the abandon_target_external_e164 column cannot be set through this tool at all. MEDIA TRAPS. moh_s3_key is forwarded to the PBX only when it is an S3 key whose first segment is ivr-audio, did-audio or voicemail-greeting AND whose second segment is exactly this account's uuid, at most 512 chars, with no '..', no leading slash, no empty segment and none of the characters FreeSWITCH or the XML renderer would reinterpret; anything else, an https URL included, is STORED but never sent and the response tells you callers hear the default hold music. greeting_tts_text is stored copy only: the provisioning call is never handed the text or the voice, only a greeting_s3_key that NO path in this product ever writes, so the 'entry greeting did not land ... Re-save to retry' warning can never clear no matter how many times you retry. Sending greeting text with no voice (neither sent nor already stored) is 422 greeting_voice_required. skills on a member is persisted and never sent to mod_callcenter; callback_enabled and sla_answer_seconds are persisted and never sent either, so no callback is offered to anyone and no SLA is enforced. Also 404 not_found for another account's queue, 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, and 422 invalid_body from a STRICT schema that rejects unknown keys. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this edit leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_queues_list
tools.description: List the account's ACD call queues (mod_callcenter), newest first, with no pagination, no filter and no cap: every queue with every member row comes back in one response. Returns {queues:[<full voice_queues row> + members:[...]]}: name, strategy (longest_idle|round_robin|top_down|agent_with_least_talk_time|random), extension, music-on-hold keys, greeting text/voice, announce_position, announce_frequency_sec, max_wait_sec, sla_answer_seconds, callback_enabled, the abandon target (abandon_target_type / abandon_target_id / abandon_target_external_e164, the last being a PSTN number an abandoning caller is pushed to), fusionpbx_queue_uuid, and each member's {id,queue_id,extension_id,skills,tier,position,timeout_seconds,created_at}. TWO NULLS MEAN THE QUEUE DOES NOT WORK AND NEITHER IS REPORTED AS AN ERROR: fusionpbx_queue_uuid null means the queue exists in Postgres but was never loaded into FreeSWITCH, so it answers nothing (the dashboard renders a 'not provisioned' banner for exactly this state; an API caller sees only a null); extension null means no 5xxx dial number was ever allocated, and every routing path in this system (a DID, an IVR option, a ring-group timeout) resolves its target down to a numeric extension string, so a queue with a null extension is unreachable even when it is provisioned. Check both before telling anyone their queue is live. Member rows carry extension_id UUIDs and NO dial number and NO display name, so you cannot say who staffs a queue from this response alone: join against voice_extensions_list. moh_local_path null means the queue falls back to the system default hold music no matter what moh_s3_key says, so a set moh_s3_key is not proof branded hold music plays. position is mod_callcenter's tier_position and only affects ring order under top_down (longest_idle and random ignore it), so reordering members changes nothing under those strategies. voice_queue_members has no account_id column of its own and is reached only through the account-scoped queue relation. Read-only by design: the source route also exports POST, which creates the queue AND provisions it on a SHARED PBX box, and that was deliberately not twinned. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_recent_calls
tools.description: Recent calls + dispositions for diagnosing call-flow issues. Used to investigate "calls aren't coming through" or "goes to voicemail too fast".

tools.name: voice_recording_url_get
tools.description: Issues a presigned S3 GET for a call's recorded audio: { url, expires_in_seconds: 300 }. DANGER, read before calling: the returned URL is an unauthenticated, shareable download of a real conversation. The AWS signature rides in the query string, so ANYONE who receives the link can stream or save the audio with no Hiveku login, no account and no further check for the next 5 minutes (RECORDING_URL_TTL_SECONDS = 300, not adjustable per call and NOT revocable once issued). Pasting it into a ticket, a chat message, a log line or an agent transcript republishes the recording to everyone who can read that surface, and it keeps working there until it expires. The route enforces no consent, retention or redaction check, so two-party-consent obligations rest entirely with the caller, and the presign is signed by pinned HIVEKU_ADMIN credentials rather than by the tenant. Prefer voice_call_transcript_get when you only need what was said. Silent failures: despite the /recordings/ path the id is voice_calls.id, NOT call_uuid and not an id from any recordings table, so the FreeSWITCH uuid 404s forever; 404 no_recording when recording_s3_key is null, which is the normal answer for the minutes after hangup while the EC2 uploader lands the file, and permanent for calls that were never recorded; 503 misconfigured when HIVEKU_RECORDINGS_BUCKET is unset; a 200 does NOT prove the object exists, because the presign is a local signature with no S3 round trip, so a swept or missing object still returns a happy URL that 404s at S3 when opened; 404 not_found for a call in another account; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off. The us-east-2 KMS bucket has no CORS, so the URL plays in an audio element or a direct download but a browser fetch or XHR against it is blocked.

tools.name: voice_ring_group_create
tools.description: Creates a ring group and makes it live. It provisions the PBX FIRST (the FusionPBX ring-group row, one destination per member and the dialplan rule on the shared EC2 box) and only then writes the Hiveku rows in one transaction, so on success dialling the group's extension immediately rings real desk phones and softphones, and any DID later pointed at it sends live callers there. No TTS and no carrier spend on this call itself. RETURNS { ring_group } carrying the saved row plus fusionpbx_ring_group_uuid, member_count and member_destination_uuids. THE EXTENSION IS YOURS TO PICK AND NOTHING CROSS-CHECKS IT. `extension` is a 2-6 digit number you supply (7xxx is the convention); it is not allocated and it is not compared against the IVR 6000-6999 pool, the queue 5000-5999 pool, user extensions from 1001 up, or the 8001-8999 personal ring-group pool. Two dialplan rules matching the same digits are resolved by order, silently, which is how a live misroute happens. The only real guard is the unique index on (account_id, extension), and it fires AFTER the PBX provision: a duplicate is not caught as a 409, it falls through to the generic handler and comes back as 500 internal_error with the FusionPBX group ALREADY CREATED and no Hiveku row to manage it. Pick a free number with voice_extensions_list and voice_ring_groups_list first. Refusals: 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off; 409 not_provisioned when the account has no voice tenant; 422 members_not_found listing extension ids that are not on this account; 422 timeout_target_id_required, timeout_target_not_found (also the answer for a non-UUID id, and for a target row that exists but has a NULL extension) and timeout_target_external_e164_required; 422 invalid_body, and the schema is STRICT so an unknown or renamed key is rejected rather than dropped. The fallback is hard-validated on purpose: a group saved with a fallback type and no resolvable target renders as configured while FreeSWITCH has no post-bridge action at all, so unanswered callers hear silence and then get hung up on. A voice_server failure maps to 404, 422, 409 or 502 ring_group_provision_failed and writes no Hiveku row. MONEY: timeout_target_type 'external_number' forwards every unanswered call out to the PSTN through Telnyx, which bills carrier minutes on each one and is subject to the toll-fraud cap and caller-id rules; only the E.164 shape is checked here, tenant ownership and fraud rules are enforced by voice_server at apply time.

tools.name: voice_ring_group_delete
tools.description: PERMANENTLY deletes a ring group and the routing that depends on it. IRREVERSIBLE: the FusionPBX group, its member destinations and its dialplan rule are torn down and the Hiveku row is deleted, with member rows cascading. There is no undo; recreating it means re-entering every member and fallback, and the freed extension can be claimed by something else in the meantime. This is the SAFEST-ORDERED of the three routing deletes: teardown runs FIRST and a failure returns 502 ring_group_teardown_failed having deleted NOTHING, so a failed call here is safe to retry (the IVR and queue deletes behave differently and delete the row anyway). It also REFUSES rather than orphaning: 409 ring_group_in_use while a phone number routes to it, another group falls back to it, an IVR menu digit or after-hours target points at it, or a queue overflows to it, and the message names each blocker so you can re-point them first. That guard exists because an IVR menu digit renders as a plain transfer in FreeSWITCH, so a deleted group turns that keypress into dead air with no error recorded anywhere. WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK: only voice_numbers, voice_ring_groups, voice_ivrs and voice_queues are queried. A call-tracking DID pool whose voice_did_pools.inbound_target_id is this group, and a pending carrier order in voice_number_orders that will adopt into it, both pass the guard and are silently orphaned, including every number that joins that pool later. RETURNS { id, deleted: true } with no warning key, because the only failure mode is the 502 that changes nothing. A group that never reached the PBX is simply deleted. Also 404 not_found for an id on another account, and 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_ring_group_get
tools.description: One ring group with its member rows, which voice_ring_groups_list does not return. RETURNS { ring_group: { ...row, members[] } } ordered by priority ascending. The row carries name, strategy, ring_seconds, extension, the three timeout_target fields, fusionpbx_group_uuid, rr_cursor (the persistent round-robin pointer the voice server increments per call, never written by the builder) and is_personal / personal_user_id, so the auto-created personal groups from the 8001-8999 pool show up here alongside real teams. Members carry extension_id, priority, weight, delay_seconds and timeout_seconds. READ THE TWO NULLS. fusionpbx_group_uuid null means the group exists only in Postgres and has never reached FreeSWITCH, so it cannot ring anyone no matter how correct the row looks, and an edit to it will report a clean 200 while changing nothing on the phone system. A null extension means nothing can dial or transfer to it, and it also disqualifies the group from being another group's fallback. members[].extension_id is a voice_extensions UUID, not a dial number; resolve the actual phones with voice_extensions_list. members[].timeout_seconds is stored per leg but any edit through voice_ring_group_update re-pushes every leg at the group-level ring_seconds, so a per-member value here is not necessarily what FreeSWITCH is using. Read-only, no spend, nothing changes. 404 not_found is also the answer for a group on another account, so it does not distinguish deleted from foreign. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, which is a plan refusal rather than a missing group.

tools.name: voice_ring_group_update
tools.description: Edits a live ring group: who rings, in what order, for how long, and where an unanswered call falls through to. It COMMITS the Hiveku rows first and then pushes to voice_server, which rewrites the FusionPBX group and its timeout action and replaces the member destinations, so the set of phones that ring for real inbound calls changes immediately. No TTS and no carrier spend on the call itself. RETURNS { ring_group, warning? } where ring_group is the DATABASE row, not the phone system's state. TWO WAYS THIS ANSWERS 200 HAVING NOT CHANGED THE PHONES. First, when the group has no fusionpbx_group_uuid (never provisioned) the route updates Postgres, SKIPS FreeSWITCH entirely and returns a clean 200 with NO warning at all; check that field with voice_ring_group_get before trusting a save. Second, a voice_server failure is a SOFT warning on a 200: the DB committed, the dialplan is one edit behind, and the response says so in `warning` rather than failing. PARTIAL, with two wholesale exceptions. Omitted fields are left alone, but member_extension_ids REPLACES the entire membership, and an empty array is accepted and drops every member, leaving a group that rings nobody. Sending ring_seconds alone also OVERWRITES timeout_seconds on every member row and re-pushes the members, because the live bridge dialstring is built from those rows. A THIRD THING NOTHING TELLS YOU: whenever members are pushed, every leg is sent with the group-level ring_seconds as its timeout, so per-member timeout_seconds is persisted and displayed but never reaches FreeSWITCH from this tool; only delay_seconds survives per member. The fallback is resolved from EFFECTIVE values (the field you sent, else the stored one) whenever ANY of the three timeout fields is present, so a partial body like timeout_target_id on its own is fully validated; a name-only save deliberately does not re-validate stored timeout state, so a legacy broken target cannot block a rename. Sending timeout_target_type null clears the fallback and nulls the id and E.164 with it. Refusals: 422 timeout_target_not_found (also when the target row has a NULL extension, which would otherwise make voice_server CLEAR the FreeSWITCH fallback while this row claims one is set), 422 timeout_target_self because a group falling back to itself ring-loops until the caller or the carrier gives up, 422 timeout_target_id_required, 422 timeout_target_external_e164_required, 422 members_not_found listing ids not on this account, 422 invalid_body (the schema is STRICT, so a renamed key fails loudly instead of being dropped), 404 not_found which is also the answer for another account's group, and 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off. MONEY: switching the fallback to external_number bills carrier minutes on every unanswered call from then on.

tools.name: voice_ring_groups_list
tools.description: List the account's ring groups (parallel-ringing strategies).

tools.name: voice_settings_get
tools.description: Read the account's single voice_tenant_config row, the phone system's guardrails and post-call policy, and the mandatory read before voice_settings_update. Returns { settings } carrying fusionpbx_domain, carrier_mode, concurrent_call_cap, daily_outbound_cap_cents, recording_enabled, recording_retention_days, hipaa_mode, ai_agent_enabled, missed_call_autoresponder_enabled, missed_call_autoresponder_body, conversion_upload_enabled, conversion_upload_disposition, conversion_upload_min_duration_sec, conversion_upload_value, conversion_upload_currency, ga4_upload_enabled, keyword_spotting_enabled, keyword_spotting_terms and provisioned_at. SILENT FAILURE: settings is NULL on a 200 when the account pays for the Voice add-on but the PBX tenant was never provisioned. Null is not an error and it is not a row of defaults, it means there is no row at all, and voice_settings_update against that account comes back as a bare 500 while voice_tenant_healthcheck returns the single failed check tenant_config_present. TRAPS. conversion_upload_value is a Prisma Decimal(12,2) and Prisma's Decimal serializes through toString, so it arrives as a QUOTED STRING like '12.50' rather than a JSON number; null there means upload with no value, so the Google conversion action's own defaultValue applies. keyword_spotting_terms is a bare nullable Json column, so null (never configured) is a distinct state from an empty array. recording_enabled is only the TENANT default: voice_numbers.recording_enabled is a per-DID override that beats it and this response cannot see those, so recording_enabled false is not proof that any given number is unrecorded. daily_outbound_cap_cents here is the cap the toll-fraud guard actually enforces, and it is a DIFFERENT column from account_credits.voice_daily_outbound_cap_cents reported by voice_usage_get, so the two can disagree and only this one stops calls; voice_toll_fraud_state reads this same column and adds today's spend against it. hipaa_mode is readable here but cannot be changed by any API key. ai_agent_enabled and provisioned_at are readable here and appear in NO write path on this route. Read-only, no cost, nothing reaches a person, no carrier is touched. 402 voice_not_enabled (carrying subscription_plan) without the paid Voice add-on; the key needs olympus:voice:read.

tools.name: voice_settings_update
