tools.description: RECONFIGURES A LIVE PHONE SYSTEM'S GUARDRAILS. Writes only the keys you send onto the one voice_tenant_config row for this account. No carrier API is called and no PBX write happens here, but every value is read by a service that spends money, deletes recordings or texts a customer. Returns { settings } with the updated row. RESPONSE GAP: the PATCH select omits ga4_upload_enabled, ai_agent_enabled and provisioned_at even though ga4_upload_enabled IS written here, so a successful ga4_upload_enabled change is simply absent from the reply. Do not read that as a dropped write; confirm with voice_settings_get. CONSEQUENCES, each verified in the handler and its consumers. daily_outbound_cap_cents is the toll-fraud ceiling: voice_server's toll_fraud_guard polls every 30 minutes, sums today's outbound voice_calls.billable_seconds at a deliberately conservative flat 1 cent per minute, and over cap it flags the tenant and uuid_kills NEW outbound channels. Raising it raises the real Telnyx spend absorbed before a compromised extension is stopped, which is a money decision for a human, not a fix for 'outbound calls are being rejected'. Cap state lives in voice_server memory and is re-evaluated on the next poll, so a change takes up to 30 minutes to land and lowering it never drops calls already in progress. The range is 100 to 100000 cents; the guard treats 0 as never auto-cap but this route's floor of 100 makes disabling it impossible here. recording_retention_days causes IRREVERSIBLE DELETION: the daily 08:40 UTC pruner deletes the S3 recording AND transcript objects of calls older than the window, nulls both pointers and clears the CRM timeline's play button, 200 calls per tick oldest first, and nothing restores them; ai_summary and the CRM activity text survive. Cutting 365 to 30 destroys eleven months of call audio on the next tick. 0 means keep forever and those tenants are never scanned. recording_enabled is only the tenant default and a per-DID voice_numbers.recording_enabled override beats it, so setting false does not stop recording on a DID carrying its own override; it also silences the two-party-consent announcement, which is usually the opposite of what a compliance request wants. missed_call_autoresponder_enabled makes future missed inbound calls TEXT THE CALLER a real SMS that costs money per segment; the send goes through dispatchAccountSms, which does screen the do-not-text list and run the reputation governor. SILENT NO-OP: both senders require enabled AND a non-empty missed_call_autoresponder_body, so enabling with the body still null texts nobody, forever, with no error anywhere. conversion_upload_enabled starts pushing attributed calls into the connected Google Ads account as offline conversions every 5 minutes, which changes reported performance and can move automated bidding; ga4_upload_enabled does the same over the GA4 Measurement Protocol. TRAP: the dashboard disables those two controls until an ads connection exists, but THIS ROUTE CHECKS FOR NO CONNECTION AT ALL, so enabling them with nothing connected is accepted, answers 200, and uploads nothing. keyword_spotting_terms REPLACES the stored array wholesale, so sending one term deletes the other ninety-nine and [] clears them; every term is trimmed, lowercased and deduped by the schema, so the stored value will not match your casing. NOT EXPOSED ON PURPOSE: hipaa_mode is accepted by the zod schema and then silently dropped for every API-key caller (a key has no builder profile so it is never staff) while the route answers 200 echoing the OLD value, so this tool deliberately cannot send it; flipping HIPAA mode is a staff action in the dashboard. ai_agent_enabled is not in the write schema either, so this cannot turn the AI receptionist on or off. REFUSALS: 422 invalid_body with a zod issues array, which writes nothing; 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid add-on; 403 without olympus:voice:write; 401 on a bad key. SILENT FAILURES: an account with no voice_tenant_config row hits an unhandled Prisma P2025 and returns a bare 500 rather than a clean 404, so call voice_settings_get first and never PATCH when settings is null; an empty body parses fine, writes only updated_at and answers 200 unchanged. NO AUDIT ROW IS WRITTEN: the route logs the before/after diff through logVoiceAudit with a null user id, which is that helper's documented anonymous path, so it console-warns and persists NOTHING because audit_logs.user_id is a non-nullable FK. A cap raise or a retention cut made here leaves no entry on the communications audit page and no attributable actor. Tell a human exactly what you changed.

tools.name: voice_sms_brand_feedback_get
tools.description: The stored carrier feedback explaining why the account's 10DLC brand was rejected. Returns `feedback`, the brand_feedback_json snapshot already on the row, whose categories (TAX_ID, ADDRESS, and so on) name the EXACT brand fields the carriers refused, so a correction can be targeted instead of guessed. Read-only: it returns what the status cron captured when the brand went FAILED, and does NOT fetch anything fresh from the registry. `feedback: null` therefore means no failure snapshot is stored, NOT that the brand is healthy; read the brand's status for that. An account with no brand at all is a 404 `no_brand`. Fixing the named fields and calling voice_sms_brand_submit again is a fresh, fee-bearing carrier filing, not an edit.

tools.name: voice_sms_brand_submit
tools.description: Create or update the account's single 10DLC brand and FILE IT WITH THE CARRIERS. Not a draft. IRREVERSIBLE AND FEE-BEARING. It submits the legal entity (legal company name, EIN, entity type, registered address, contact email and phone) to Telnyx, which forwards it to The Campaign Registry and the US carriers for vetting. Vetting is a paid third-party review. Once submitted it CANNOT be withdrawn or un-filed from here: the identity data now sits with the registry and the carriers, a brand-vetting fee may already be incurred, and a later correction is a RE-VET (another review, another fee), never a deletion. A wrong EIN or legal name typically returns as a FAILED brand with TCR feedback and has to be re-filed. Get the EIN and legal name right the first time; this is a filing about a real company, and it wants a human decision rather than an agent's inference. One brand per account: calling again updates the existing row and re-submits, and an existing telnyx_brand_id routes to update-and-revet rather than creating a duplicate. Returns `brand` plus `submission_error`: a Telnyx failure does NOT block the local save, so `submission_error` non-null means the row persisted but the carriers never saw it, and READING ONLY THE 200 WOULD TELL YOU IT WORKED. Retry after fixing the cause. Read voice_sms_brand_feedback_get first when re-filing a rejected brand: it names the exact fields the carriers refused.

tools.name: voice_sms_campaign_carriers_get
tools.description: Live per-carrier (MNO) verdict for ONE 10DLC campaign, read straight from Telnyx on every call (no cache). Returns {registered, campaignStatus, tcrStatus, carriers} where each carrier is {mno, networkId, status:'approved'|'review_pending'|'not_qualified'|'unsupported', supported, qualified, reviewPending, tpm, mmsTpm, brandTier, dailyCap}, sorted AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon Wireless, US Cellular, then alphabetical. This is what answers 'T-Mobile is filtering us but AT&T is fine' and 'what throughput did each carrier grant'. campaign_id is the HIVEKU voice_sms_campaign UUID (brand.campaigns[].id from voice_sms_registration_get), NOT telnyx_campaign_id: the lookup is findFirst by primary id scoped to the account, so passing the Telnyx id (the id printed all over the carrier report) returns 404 campaign_not_found rather than anything more helpful. TRAPS, all of which look alike: a campaign that never reached Telnyx answers 200 with registered:false and carriers:[], meaning 'not submitted', not 'every carrier refused'; carriers:[] on a 200 with registered:true means Telnyx has published no mnoMetadata yet, again not a refusal; and a Telnyx failure answers HTTP 502 with registered:true, error 'carrier_status_unavailable', the raw upstream message and empty carriers. That 502 is deliberate fail-soft, so report 'carrier breakdown unavailable' and keep the canonical verdict from voice_sms_registration_get rather than telling anyone their campaign broke. campaignStatus and tcrStatus here are Telnyx/TCR RAW strings (ACTIVE, TCR_ACCEPTED, MNO_PENDING) taken live from the vendor, never the canonical vocabulary; the campaign's stored canonical status is read by this handler and deliberately not returned, so never test these fields the way can_send tests for ACTIVE. Reads TELNYX_API_KEY on the builder web service, which must stay in sync with the voice_server key: a rotated or unset key 502s every call with 'TELNYX_API_KEY is not configured' while the campaign itself is perfectly healthy. Read-only, no cost, nothing is sent to a person and nothing changes carrier-side. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_sms_campaign_draft
tools.description: Draft a carrier-compliant 10DLC campaign from the account's own business context and brand guide, streamed back field by field: campaign name, use case, description, message flow, sample messages and keyword sets. Optional `prompt` steers it. DRAFTS TEXT ONLY. No campaign row is created, nothing reaches Telnyx, The Campaign Registry or the carriers, and there is nothing to withdraw. The irreversible, fee-bearing step is submitting the draft through the campaign-create route afterwards. Requires the account's brand to be VERIFIED first, the same precondition the create route enforces; on an unverified brand this refuses rather than drafting something that could not be filed. Pass the result through voice_sms_cta_preflight before submitting it: the drafter writes a plausible message flow, but only preflight checks that the opt-in page it names actually contains the required disclosures.

tools.name: voice_sms_campaign_resubmit
tools.description: Retry lane for a 10DLC campaign row that never reached Telnyx. The create route persists locally even when the submit fails, leaving telnyx_campaign_id null; this re-files that row. THIS FILES THE CAMPAIGN and is fee-bearing at the registry. It sends the use case, description, message flow, sample messages and opt-in/opt-out keywords to Telnyx, then The Campaign Registry and the carriers. Not reversible from here. The body is OPTIONAL. Send nothing to re-file the row exactly as stored. Send a body and it must be the COMPLETE campaign payload, the same schema as create, not a patch: the row's editable fields are overwritten from it before re-submitting, so omitting a field you previously set CLEARS it. The usual flow is to fix the description a reviewer flagged and retry. Run voice_sms_cta_preflight on the message_flow before retrying. Resubmitting the same flow that was rejected buys another rejection.

tools.name: voice_sms_cta_preflight
tools.description: Check a 10DLC campaign's message flow the way a carrier will, BEFORE you pay to file it. Fetches each opt-in URL the flow names with NO JavaScript, exactly as the reviewer's crawler does, and reports which required CTA elements are actually present in the returned HTML. Returns a `report` of found/missing elements. Run this first, always. It files nothing, writes no row, contacts no registry, and leaves nothing to withdraw, so a missing disclosure costs a re-check here instead of a rejection fee and roughly a week of carrier review. A CTA rendered only by client-side JavaScript will pass in a browser and FAIL here, which is the single most common reason a campaign is rejected. Caller-supplied URLs go through an SSRF guard. message_flow is capped at 4096 characters and a missing or empty one is a 422 naming the field.

tools.name: voice_sms_number_assign_campaign
tools.description: Register one of the account's DIDs to a specific approved 10DLC campaign. For an account running more than one campaign this is how you choose which campaign a number sends under; with a single campaign the assignment is automatic and this is unnecessary. CARRIER PAPERWORK, NOT A LOCAL PREFERENCE. It files the number-to-campaign assignment with Telnyx, which passes it to The Campaign Registry and the carriers as that DID's sending identity. Once accepted the number is on that campaign at the registry, so moving it later is another filing rather than an edit. telnyx_campaign_id is the REGISTRY id, not the local campaign row UUID; read it from voice_sms_registration_get. Assigning a number to the wrong campaign misrepresents the sending identity to the carriers, which is the kind of mismatch that gets traffic filtered rather than merely rejected.

tools.name: voice_sms_opt_out_add
tools.description: Add one E.164 number to this account's do-not-text list (voice_sms_opt_outs, source 'manual') so every outbound SMS path refuses it: dispatchSms calls isOptedOut before handing anything to the carrier and returns error 'opted_out' with 'They must reply START to re-subscribe'. Returns {ok:true, e164, already_present}. Use it to honour a stop request made by phone, email or in person; a texted STOP is already written automatically by the voice server ingester with source 'auto', and this route deliberately never downgrades such a row to 'manual' because the sending-reputation rate counts source='auto' only. SILENT NO-OP: if a row already exists the route writes NOTHING and still answers 200 with already_present:true, so your note is discarded and the stored reason, source and opted_out_at are left exactly as they were. This tool can never correct, re-date or re-note an existing opt-out. NOT PERMANENT: an inbound message from that number whose FIRST WORD is 'start', 'unstop' or 'yes' DELETES the row in hiveku_voice_server's sms_ingester, and 'yes' is the exact word the chat-to-SMS handoff asks customers to reply with, so a later unrelated 'yes' (even 'yes please') silently re-enables texting. NARROW SCOPE: this suppresses SMS only, for this account only, matched on the literal e164 string - it does not touch email suppression, sequence suppression or CRM lifecycle, and a differently formatted number is a different row. For a known CRM contact prefer crm_set_dnc, which suppresses email and SMS, flips lifecycle and exits sequences in one transaction. e164 must match ^\+\d{8,15}$ and a note over 200 characters is a 422 invalid_body that writes nothing; a blank or whitespace-only note is stored as the literal 'manual'. NO audit_logs row is written on this route: an Olympus key has no builder profile id and audit_logs.user_id is a non-nullable FK, so logVoiceAudit takes its anonymous path and only console-warns. There is no add-then-remove: removing an opt-out is not exposed to agents at all, so treat this call as one-way. Two concurrent adds of the same number can collide on the unique (account_id, e164) index and surface as a 500 rather than a clean already_present. Accounts without the paid Voice add-on get 402 voice_not_enabled.

tools.name: voice_sms_registration_get
tools.description: The account's 10DLC brand plus every campaign on it, and the single 'can this account send SMS at all?' verdict. Returns {brand, can_send, has_toll_free_numbers, toll_free, blocking_reason}; brand is null when the account has never registered. can_send is true only when the brand is canonical VERIFIED AND a campaign is canonical ACTIVE AND that campaign carries telnyx_messaging_profile_id, OR at least one toll-free DID is verified - so can_send can be true on toll-free alone with no brand at all. Key on can_send instead of re-deriving the rule. blocking_reason is null when can_send, else 'no_brand', 'brand_unverified', 'campaign_pending' (submitted to Telnyx, carriers still reviewing), 'no_active_campaign' (brand verified, nothing submitted yet) or 'no_messaging_profile' (ACTIVE campaign never provisioned; the status cron's repair phase fills it in). TRAP: a campaign that reached Telnyx is NOT approved. TCR_ACCEPTED and TELNYX_ACCEPTED both normalize to PENDING on purpose in src/lib/voice/tendlc-status.ts, because a campaign has been observed going TCR_ACCEPTED then TELNYX_FAILED, so reading a raw 'accepted' as approval reports something that does not exist. Sending on an unregistered brand is the expensive failure: dispatchSms refuses locally with 'sms_not_enabled', and any traffic that does reach the carriers is filtered as spam while the API call still looks successful. TRAP: the toll_free block is computed fail-closed, so empty numbers and verified_count 0 can equally mean the column or table is not deployed yet; that reads as unverified, can hold can_send at false, and is never evidence of data loss. PRIVACY: brand is the FULL row, including ein (US tax ID), legal_company_name, contact email and phone, street/city/state/postal_code, stock_symbol and brand_feedback_json, and each campaign carries description, message_flow and sample_messages verbatim plus its Telnyx ids. Nothing is masked, so do not paste this into customer-facing copy. Every campaign is returned newest first with no pagination and no cap. Read-only: there is no Olympus route that creates, submits or appeals a registration, because that is a signed legal submission a human makes in the dashboard. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_sms_send
tools.description: SENDS A REAL TEXT MESSAGE to a real person's handset within seconds. It costs money per segment, there is no draft state, no queue to inspect first and no recall once it is away. Send only wording a human has approved. Starts or reuses the thread between tenant_e164 and peer_e164 (an existing thread is reused and its last_message_at bumped), writes the outbound row, and dispatches through voice_server to Telnyx. RETURNS { thread } ONLY: the upserted thread row, with NO message id and NO telnyx id, so you cannot confirm the outcome from this response. Read it back with voice_sms_thread_messages_list on the returned thread id. Refusals this route DOES enforce: 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off; 403 not_your_number when tenant_e164 is not an is_active DID on this account; 409 opted_out when peer_e164 is in voice_sms_opt_outs, meaning that person texted STOP, and only their own START or YES re-subscribes them, so deleting that opt-out row to force a send is a TCPA decision for a human and never an agent's; 422 invalid_body. What it does NOT enforce: there is no 10DLC brand or campaign registration check anywhere in this route or in the shared send path. Only toll-free senders are gated, and an unverified toll-free DID surfaces as 502 send_failed. Unregistered US A2P traffic from a local number is accepted here and then filtered or blocked by the carriers, T-Mobile most aggressively, while your stored row still reads 'sent'. Silent failure: a 200 means TELNYX ACCEPTED the message, not that it arrived. The row is stamped 'sent' and only the later carrier delivery receipt flips it to delivered or failed on the same row. A 502 send_failed is NOT a no-op: the thread and a delivery_status 'failed' message row are already committed, so blind retries leave a trail of failed rows and can double-send if the first attempt actually reached the carrier. The shared reputation governor can also refuse before the carrier (sms_sending_paused kill switch, carrier-prohibited content screen, daily cap of 100/day on free and trial, 500 on hosting, 2000 by default, and a per-minute velocity cap) and it surfaces as the same 502 send_failed with the governor's human-readable reason in message and on the row: that is a policy refusal, so retrying immediately will not help. body may be empty only when media_urls is present (body max 1600 chars, max 10 URLs, and Telnyx fetches those URLs itself, so a private, signed or expiring URL fails at the carrier rather than here); a caption-less MMS is dispatched with a single-space placeholder while the stored body stays empty. Because an Olympus key has no builder profile, sent_by_user_id and assigned_user_id are left null and the audit write is SKIPPED entirely (audit_logs.user_id is a NOT NULL FK), so this send appears in the inbox with no sender and leaves NO entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_sms_send_to_contact
tools.description: SENDS A REAL TEXT MESSAGE to a CRM contact's handset and bills per segment (MMS costs more, and Telnyx fetches each media URL itself). No draft, no recall, no idempotency key anywhere: two identical calls are two texts. The recipient comes from crm_contacts.phone ONLY, never from your input. Refusals it DOES enforce: 402 voice_not_enabled; 404 contact_not_found (scoped to the account with deleted_at null); 409 no_contact_phone; 403 opted_out read from voice_sms_opt_outs, a hard refusal and 403 HERE where the thread routes return 409 for the same condition, so key on the error string and not the status; 404 template_not_found; 403 not_your_number; 409 no_sending_number. WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK, never assume otherwise: NO 10DLC brand or campaign lookup exists on this path or inside sendSms, so unregistered US A2P traffic from a local DID is accepted here and then filtered by carriers while your stored row still reads 'sent'; NO quiet-hours rule exists in src/lib/voice at all and crm_contacts.timezone is never read, so scheduled_for is an absolute UTC instant that can land at 3am local; consent is checked ONLY against the opt-out table, never lifecycle_stage or any CRM DNC column (the CRM DNC route writes into voice_sms_opt_outs, which is why the one check suffices). An explicit from_e164 is checked for is_active on this account but NOT for toll-free verification, so an unverified toll-free sender clears the 403 and then dies INSIDE sendSms as a 502; omitting it is safer, because the auto-pick takes purpose 'main' then the oldest active DID, admits local plus VERIFIED toll-free only, and fails closed on any read error. PHONE PARSING: '214-555-1212 x5' parses to 11 digits not starting with 1 and is refused 409 no_contact_phone, while a value already starting with '+' is passed through with NO length check straight to the opt-out lookup, the thread key and the carrier. TEMPLATE TRAP: merge vars render ONLY when your body.trim() exactly equals the stored template body.trim(); any other body is sent VERBATIM, so an edited body still holding {contact_first_name} arrives as literal braces. An API key has no profile, so {sender_first_name} and {sender_last_name} render EMPTY while {business_name} resolves from accounts.name. SCHEDULED BRANCH: scheduled_for defers only when it is more than 30 SECONDS ahead; anything nearer or in the past SENDS NOW. When it does defer it writes delivery_status 'scheduled' and returns without calling the carrier, and /api/cron/sms-scheduled-tick dispatches later (50 rows per tick across ALL accounts, opt-out re-checked at dispatch, tenant_e164 read off the thread without re-verifying the DID is still active) - but that path writes NO crm_activities row, fires NO webhook and never bumps template usage, so a scheduled send is invisible on the contact timeline, and there is no tool or route here to list or cancel one. Success returns { message_id, thread_id, from_e164, to_e164 } plus scheduled_for when deferred, with NO telnyx id and NO delivery status: a 200 means Telnyx ACCEPTED it, never that it arrived. 502 send_failed returns { error, message, thread_id, message_id } and is NOT a no-op, because the thread upsert and a delivery_status 'failed' row are already committed, so a blind retry can double-send. The shared governor inside sendSms surfaces as that SAME 502 carrying a human reason (voice_tenant_config.sms_sending_paused kill switch, a carrier-prohibited content regex, a UTC daily cap of 100 on free and trial, 500 hosting, 5000 premium, 10000 business, 50000 enterprise and 2000 on any unrecognized plan unless daily_sms_cap_override raises it, and a per-minute velocity cap); those are POLICY refusals that an immediate retry cannot clear. Two mislabels on the success path: the fan-out event is named 'sms.delivered' but fires at carrier ACCEPT, and both the crm_activities row and the webhook payload store your RAW input body rather than the rendered text, so a merge-var send shows the UN-rendered template on the CRM timeline while the customer got the rendered version. NO AUDIT TRAIL: logVoiceAudit is called with userId null, its documented anonymous path, which console-warns and SKIPS the row because audit_logs.user_id is a NOT NULL FK, and sent_by_user_id, assigned_user_id and crm_activities.owner_id are all null, so this send has no attributed sender anywhere in the product.

tools.name: voice_sms_template_create
tools.description: Saves a reusable SMS snippet on the account. Returns { template } with id, name, body, category, shortcut, usage_count, last_used_at and created_at. NOTHING IS SENT: this writes one database row, reaches neither Telnyx nor a person, and the text only becomes a message when a send route renders it. Limits, each a 422 invalid_body carrying a Zod issues[] with nothing written: name 1 to 120 chars, body 1 to 1600, category up to 60, shortcut up to 32 matching /^[a-z0-9_-]*$/i. SHORTCUT TRAP: that regex ends in * so an EMPTY STRING passes validation, and the route stores it as a real value rather than null (it writes shortcut ?? null, and '' is not nullish). The unique index is (account_id, shortcut), so the SECOND template created with shortcut '' comes back 409 shortcut_taken, while OMITTING shortcut stores NULL, which Postgres treats as distinct and never collides. Omit the field rather than sending ''. 409 shortcut_taken is the P2002 answer and always means taken on YOUR account, never a cross-tenant leak. NO DEDUPE on name or body: calling twice creates two identical templates, and this library has no merge or cleanup tool, only voice_sms_template_delete one id at a time. created_by is hardcoded null because an Olympus key has no builder profile, so nothing in the product can ever show who added this template. Merge vars are substituted only at SEND time and only for contact_first_name, contact_last_name, contact_phone, sender_first_name, sender_last_name and business_name, matched lowercase-and-underscore only; NOTHING validates placeholders here, so a typo like {firstName} is accepted silently and later reaches a real handset as literal braces. Under an API key sender_first_name and sender_last_name always render EMPTY. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_sms_template_delete
tools.description: Permanently removes one saved SMS snippet. Returns { ok: true }. IRREVERSIBLE: voice_sms_templates has no soft-delete column and no version history, so there is no undo and no restore tool anywhere in this library, and the body text is gone unless you read it with voice_sms_templates_list FIRST. It does NOT unsend anything and it cannot reach a person: every message already sent stored its own rendered body and keeps it, and a scheduled message stored its text when it was scheduled, so it still goes out. NO DEPENDENCY GUARD, so this never refuses with a 409: nothing checks whether the template is referenced before deleting. voice_sms_messages.template_id is a plain nullable uuid with NO foreign key and no relation, so nothing cascades and nothing is nulled; historical rows are left pointing at an id that no longer resolves, and any usage report that joins on template_id silently goes blank for them. A /shortcut a human types into the composer every day simply stops expanding, with no warning to them. 404 not_found covers both an already-deleted template and one on another account, which are indistinguishable. The destructive statement is a deleteMany scoped to account_id, so a row that disappears between the existence check and the delete still answers 200 ok having removed ZERO rows: a 200 proves the row is absent, not that this call is what removed it. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_sms_template_update
tools.description: Edits one saved SMS snippet in place. Only the fields you send are written, alongside a refreshed updated_at. Nothing is sent to a person by this call. SILENT NO-OP: every field is optional, so an empty object PARSES and the route answers 200 having changed nothing but updated_at, and the Zod parse STRIPS unknown keys, so usage_count, last_used_at, created_by or account_id are discarded without an error and also answer 200. Confirm an edit by reading the returned row, never by the status code. RESPONSE SHAPE DIFFERS from every other template tool: the update carries no select, so this returns the FULL Prisma row including account_id, created_by and updated_at, while voice_sms_templates_list and voice_sms_template_create return an eight-field projection. Do not write a caller that assumes the two shapes match. Pass category or shortcut as null to CLEAR that column; omitting them leaves the stored value alone. Passing shortcut as '' does NOT clear it: the regex /^[a-z0-9_-]*$/i admits '', so an empty string is stored and then collides with any other empty shortcut, since the unique key is (account_id, shortcut). 409 shortcut_taken is the P2002 answer and always means taken on YOUR account. 404 not_found covers both a deleted template and one belonging to another account, which are indistinguishable here. Any OTHER Prisma error is rethrown uncaught and surfaces as a bare Next 500 with no error key to read. Limits are name 1 to 120, body 1 to 1600, category 60, shortcut 32; a violation is 422 invalid_body with issues[] and no write. Editing body cannot reach anything already sent OR already queued: each voice_sms_messages row stored its own rendered text when it was created, including a scheduled row waiting on the cron, so a correction here does not fix a message that is already on its way. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_sms_templates_list
tools.description: Every reusable SMS snippet on the account in one response. Returns { templates: [...] }, each row id, name, body, category, shortcut, usage_count, last_used_at and created_at; account_id, created_by and updated_at are deliberately NOT selected, so this projection is NARROWER than the full row voice_sms_template_update returns. Read-only: nothing here reaches Telnyx or a person, and a template only becomes a message when a send route renders it. ORDERING TRAP: the sort is last_used_at DESC then name ASC, emitted as a bare DESC, and Postgres sorts NULLS FIRST on DESC, so every NEVER-USED template leads the list ahead of the one sent an hour ago. Do not read position 0 as 'most used'; sort on usage_count yourself if that is the question. COUNTER TRAP: usage_count and last_used_at move only when an IMMEDIATE send carried template_id and cleared the carrier, and the bump is fire-and-forget with its own swallowed catch (lib/voice/sms-templates.ts bumpTemplateUsage console.warns and returns). A scheduled send never bumps them, because /api/cron/sms-scheduled-tick does not call the bumper at all; a failed send never bumps them; and a send whose body was edited away from the stored body still bumps them, since the bump keys on template_id alone. These counters both undercount and mislead. NO filters, NO pagination, NO cap and no cursor: an account with hundreds of templates returns hundreds in one payload. body is the RAW template with placeholders unexpanded. Only contact_first_name, contact_last_name, contact_phone, sender_first_name, sender_last_name and business_name ever substitute, matched by /\{([a-z_]+)\}/, lowercase letters and underscores only, so {Contact_First_Name} or {var2} can never match, and any unknown placeholder is left INTACT rather than blanked, which is how literal braces reach a handset. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, which is a plan refusal and not an empty library.

tools.name: voice_sms_thread_messages_list
tools.description: Transcript for ONE SMS thread, newest first. Returns { thread, messages[], next_cursor }, where thread carries tenant_e164, peer_e164, contact_id, assigned_user_id, archived, last_message_at and the PRE-reset unread_count, and each message carries id, direction, body, media_urls, delivery_status, error_message, sent_by_user_id, sent_at and telnyx_message_id. delivery_status is nullable, so a null means never reconciled, not failed, and 'sent' only means Telnyx accepted it. NOT READ-ONLY despite being a GET: opening a thread RESETS its unread_count to 0, so a polling agent silently clears the unread badge a human was working from. Pass mark_read: 'false' for a background sync, and note that only that exact string disables the reset; any other value, including omitting it, clears the badge. The reset is best-effort and swallows its own error, so a reset that fails is invisible and the badge just reappears on the next poll. limit is clamped to 1 through 200 (default 50) and a non-numeric limit is not coerced back to the default. An unresolvable cursor is a HARD 400 invalid_cursor here, deliberately unlike voice_sms_threads_list which ignores a bad cursor and replays page one; the cursor must be a message id from inside THIS thread. A thread id belonging to another account returns a plain 404 not_found, indistinguishable from a deleted thread. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off, which is a plan refusal and not an empty transcript. The output is the full conversation text plus MMS media URLs: treat all of it as customer PII.

tools.name: voice_sms_thread_reply
tools.description: SENDS A REAL TEXT MESSAGE inside an existing thread. Same money per segment and the same real handset as voice_sms_send, with no draft and no recall; use it only on wording a human approved. Appends the outbound row to thread_id, bumps the thread's last_message_at, and dispatches through voice_server to Telnyx. Both the recipient and the sending DID are read off the stored thread, not from your input. RETURNS { message } with id, direction, body, media_urls, sent_at, an OPTIMISTIC delivery_status of 'sent' and telnyx_message_id: that is the created row with two fields overwritten in the response, so 'sent' means Telnyx accepted it and never that it was delivered; the carrier receipt lands on the same row later. Refusals: 402 voice_not_enabled; 404 not_found for a thread id outside this account, indistinguishable from a deleted thread; 409 opted_out, re-checked on EVERY reply even deep inside an open conversation, because a STOP still applies in the thread it was sent in, and re-enabling that person by deleting the opt-out row is a TCPA decision for a human, not an agent's judgement; 422 invalid_body. Asymmetry you must know: unlike voice_sms_send this path does NOT re-verify that the sending DID is still yours or still active. It reads tenant_e164 straight off the stored thread and never queries voice_numbers, so a reply on a released or deactivated number is attempted and fails at the carrier instead of being refused here. last_message_at is bumped BEFORE dispatch, so even a failed send jumps the thread to the top of the inbox. A 502 send_failed is not a no-op: the message row is already committed with delivery_status 'failed' plus the error text, so a blind retry can double-send. The reputation governor (paused sending, carrier-prohibited content, plan daily cap, per-minute velocity) and the missing 10DLC brand and campaign registration check described on voice_sms_send apply identically here, since both tools share one send funnel; a governor refusal arrives as the same 502 carrying its human-readable reason, and retrying it immediately will not help. body may be empty only with media_urls (max 1600 chars, max 10 public HTTPS URLs that Telnyx fetches itself, so no auth and no expiry); a caption-less MMS ships a single-space placeholder and stores an empty body. sent_by_user_id is left null and the audit write is skipped, so this reply has no attributed sender and leaves NO entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_sms_threads_list
tools.description: Paged SMS inbox for the account, newest first by last_message_at. Returns { threads[], next_cursor, search_truncated }; each thread carries id, tenant_e164 (your DID), peer_e164 (the customer), last_message_at, unread_count, archived, contact_id, assigned_user_id, and preview { body, direction, sent_at, delivery_status, has_media } or null when the thread has no messages yet. Read-only: this is the one tool in the SMS group that changes nothing. Every row is customer PII, real phone numbers and real message text. Traps. Voice is a paid add-on, so the whole route answers 402 voice_not_enabled when account_credits.voice_enabled is false, which is a plan refusal and NOT the same answer as an empty inbox. limit is clamped to 1 through 100 (default 50), so asking for 500 silently returns 100, and a non-numeric limit is not coerced back to the default, so pass a real number. cursor is a THREAD id and an unresolvable or foreign cursor is SILENTLY IGNORED here: the filter is simply not applied and you get page one again, so a pager that keeps feeding a stale cursor loops forever (the messages tool deliberately 400s on the same mistake). unread_only and archived are compared against the literal strings 'true' and 'false'; any other value, including 'True' or '1', applies NO filter instead of erroring, so an unread-only sweep can quietly return the whole inbox. Omitting archived returns archived and active threads mixed together. q scans at most 2000 message rows for a body match and ORs in a digits substring match on the two phone numbers only when the query holds 2 or more digits; when neither side matches it returns an EMPTY thread list rather than falling back to unfiltered, and search_truncated: true means the scan hit the 2000-row cap so the result is partial, not exhaustive. preview.body is cut to the first 200 characters, so a search hit deeper in a long message will not be visible in the preview; open the thread to read it. delivery_status inside preview is nullable, where null means never reconciled rather than failed.

tools.name: voice_sms_toll_free_verification_get
tools.description: Toll-free SMS verification state for the account. Returns {numbers, requests, verified_count, total_count}: numbers is one entry per ACTIVE toll-free DID {id, e164, label, status} where status is 'pending'|'in_review'|'action_needed'|'verified'|'rejected' or null, requests is the newest 50 submissions {id, e164s, status, status_raw, use_case, submitted_at, last_error, status_history}, and verified_count counts only numbers whose status is exactly 'verified'. The submitted business_payload is deliberately not selected. This is the second way an account can be sendable when 10DLC is not ready: a toll-free number may not carry SMS until the business behind it passes verification, carriers hard-block unverified toll-free senders, dispatchSms refuses an explicit unverified toll-free 'from' with 'toll_free_unverified', and the auto-picker never selects one - so a wrong read here decides whether messages reach anybody. TRAP: every read here FAILS CLOSED. A missing table or column during a deploy window degrades to empty numbers, empty requests and verified_count 0, and one fallback path returns the numbers with status null on all of them (which also zeroes verified_count). An empty or all-null answer means 'cannot prove anything is verified', never 'nothing exists' and never data loss. TRAP: only is_active toll-free DIDs are listed, and toll-free is decided by NPA (800, 833, 844, 855, 866, 877, 888); 822 is reserved-but-unassigned and excluded on purpose, so a +1822 DID is invisible here and absent from total_count. requests is hard-capped at the newest 50 with no cursor, so a long submission history is silently truncated; status_history is raw vendor JSON echoed verbatim. READ-ONLY BY DESIGN: the session route's submit POST is not twinned here, because resubmitting a number OVERWRITES the existing vendor-side approval and takes a working number off the air until it is re-reviewed. That is a human decision made in the dashboard, not an agent call. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_tenant_healthcheck
tools.description: Runs voice_server's per-tenant consistency battery for THIS account and returns { account_id, ok, checks: [{ id, ok, detail }] }, the data behind the Diagnose button on the communications settings page. ok is true only when every check passed. The checks compare Hiveku's rows against what is actually in FusionPBX and include db_pools_open, tenant_config_present, domain_unique, carrier_gateway_enabled, outbound_rule_in_tenant_context, outbound_rule_no_dupes, no_empty_xml_orphans, outbound_rule_targets_current_gateway, active_dids_have_verified_e911, extensions_have_user_context, outbound_regex_accepts_plus_prefix, ring_group_destinations_enabled, ring_groups_have_dialplan_rule, dids_have_resolvable_targets, extension_caller_id_matches_builder, routed_dids_have_inbound_rules, ring_group_extensions_unique, provisioned_ivrs_have_dialplan_rule, ivr_audio_files_exist_on_disk, provisioned_queues_exist_in_runtime and did_ring_groups_have_fallback; each detail is human-readable and names the offending numbers or extensions. This is the ONLY tool that can see the PBX side, so it is what catches a DID that looks perfect in the dashboard but has no inbound dialplan rule, or a ring-group DID with no no-answer fallback whose missed calls hang up instead of reaching voicemail. Pair it with voice_diagnose_setup, which counts Hiveku rows only and cannot see FusionPBX at all. SILENT FAILURE, read this before reporting: the battery SHORT-CIRCUITS in two cases and returns exactly ONE element. If either database pool is closed you get only db_pools_open with ok false; if the account has no voice_tenant_config row you get only tenant_config_present with ok false and the detail that there is no row for this account. A one-element checks array therefore means nothing else was inspected, never one problem out of twenty, so never report the other twenty as healthy. Real-world effect: none. It is DB-only by its own contract, places no call, writes nothing, touches no carrier and spends nothing, so it is safe to poll. It also REPAIRS NOTHING: voice_server has a separate repair endpoint that writes FusionPBX config, but this route calls only the read, so a red row stays red until a human or the dashboard repair button acts. The tenant inspected is always the authenticated account; there is no parameter and no way to check another tenant. ERRORS: any voice_server 5xx, an unreachable host, or the 15-second client timeout comes back as 503 voice_server_error with the upstream message; other upstream statuses pass through as-is; anything unexpected is 500 internal_error. A 503 means the PBX diagnostic service is down, which is NOT evidence that the tenant is broken. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_toll_fraud_state
tools.description: Current daily-outbound billable seconds vs the toll-fraud cap. Used when admin asks "why are my outbound calls being rejected?".

tools.name: voice_tts_voices_list
tools.description: The curated English Cartesia voice catalog used by the IVR and greeting pickers. Returns { voices: [{ id, name, language, gender, description, is_default }] }, where id is the value the IVR and greeting TTS fields take as their voice, and is_default marks the one production default (force-inserted at the top if Cartesia omits it). gender, language and description are nullable. There are no parameters: no search, no paging, no language filter and no way to force a refresh. Reading it costs nothing, provisions nothing and generates no audio, but choosing a DIFFERENT voice for an announcement that already exists forces a fresh paid Cartesia render, billed into voice_tts_renders.cost_cents and rolled onto the month's voice_usage_periods.tts_cents, so do not reshuffle voices casually. SILENT FAILURE, the one that matters: a ONE-ENTRY response named 'Default voice' is the OUTAGE shape, not a one-voice catalog. voice_server returns exactly that entry whenever its Cartesia key is unset or the Cartesia call throws or answers non-200, and it returns it as a normal HTTP 200, so this route caches it for five minutes and hands it back with NO warning field. Check the length and the description text (it reads either that the API key must be set to load the full catalog, or that the Cartesia catalog is unavailable and a fallback is in use) before telling anyone the account has one voice. The warning field appears only on the OTHER failure, voice_server unreachable while this process still holds a cached catalog, in which case the stale list is served with warning 'voice_server unreachable; serving cached catalog'; with no cache at all the route is 503 voices_unavailable. TWO INDEPENDENT CACHES: this route caches for 5 minutes per builder process, so consecutive calls served by different Render workers can disagree, and voice_server caches Cartesia's answer for one hour per process and deliberately does NOT cache the fallback, so it keeps retrying Cartesia while this side still serves the stale fallback. A newly published voice can take roughly an hour plus five minutes to appear and nothing here can hurry it. TRUNCATION: Cartesia is queried with limit=100 and the result is then filtered to English (en, en-us, en-gb, en-au), so a voice someone saw at Cartesia may simply sit past the cap or be non-English rather than missing. The cache is intentionally global rather than per-account because the catalog is product metadata carrying no tenant data, and the plan gate still runs before any cached value is served. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_usage_get
tools.description: Voice usage snapshot for the CURRENT UTC calendar month. Returns { period, limits, period_start }, where period is the whole voice_usage_periods row (id, account_id, period_start, period_end, minutes_included, minutes_used, seats_included, did_count, overage_minutes, overage_cents, tts_cents, reconciled_at, created_at, updated_at) or null, limits is the plan projection from account_credits (voice_seats_limit, voice_seats_used, voice_minutes_limit, voice_minutes_used, voice_did_count_limit, voice_overage_rate_cents_per_minute, voice_daily_outbound_cap_cents), and period_start is the ISO first instant of this UTC month. There are NO parameters, so no earlier month and no history is reachable through this tool. THE COUNTERS ARE NOT WHAT THEY LOOK LIKE. In this build the only writer of voice_usage_periods anywhere in the workspace is the TTS billing helper recordIvrRenders: it increments tts_cents when an IVR or greeting render is billed and, when it has to create the row, hardcodes minutes_included 0 and seats_included 0. Nothing increments minutes_used, overage_minutes, overage_cents or did_count, and no reconciler stamps reconciled_at. So period: null does NOT mean zero calls, it means no TTS render created a row this month; minutes_used 0 beside hours of real calls is the norm; and minutes_included 0 records the create-time constant, never the plan. account_credits.voice_minutes_used and voice_seats_used are read-only columns in this repo too, so treat them the same way. Use voice_recent_calls or voice_calls_list for real call volume, and remember the invoice is computed independently by summing voice_calls.billable_seconds against account_credits.voice_minutes_limit, not from this row. tts_cents IS live and is the one number here that tracks real spend. FURTHER TRAPS: limits.voice_daily_outbound_cap_cents is a DIFFERENT column from the voice_tenant_config cap the toll-fraud guard actually enforces, so quote voice_settings_get or voice_toll_fraud_state for the enforced ceiling and never this field; voice_seats_limit 0 means unlimited, not zero seats; the period boundary is UTC, so for a tenant west of UTC the month rolls over hours before local midnight. limits is effectively never null because the plan gate already resolved the same account_credits row. Read-only, writes nothing, calls no carrier, costs nothing. 402 voice_not_enabled (carrying subscription_plan) without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_voicemail_mark_read
tools.description: Marks one voicemail heard or unheard by stamping or clearing voice_calls.voicemail_read_at. The real-world effect lands on the humans, not the phone system: marking read CLEARS THE UNREAD BADGE someone is triaging from and drops the message out of every unread_only sweep, so do not use it to tidy an inbox you are only reading. No carrier call, no money, nothing sent to anyone. Returns { id, read }: the id from the path and the boolean you sent, echoed back. It does NOT return the row or the new read_at, so a 200 tells you a row was written but not what the timestamp says; read it back with voice_voicemails_list. Reversible by sending the opposite value, with one loss: read false NULLs the column and the previous heard-at timestamp is not versioned anywhere, so when it was first heard is gone for good. Traps. read must be a real JSON boolean; the string 'true' is a 422 invalid_body carrying the Zod issues, and so is an unparsable body. 404 not_found collapses three different situations into one answer, because the write is an updateMany scoped by account_id AND disposition in the same statement: an unknown id, an id belonging to another account, and a real call on THIS account that is not a voicemail all look identical. A 200 does prove exactly one row matched and was written. Nothing audits this: the route never calls the voice audit helper, so no record exists of who marked the message heard and it will not appear in voice_audit_export_csv. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, which is a plan refusal rather than a missing message.

tools.name: voice_voicemails_list
tools.description: Paged voicemail inbox for the account, newest first. A voicemail is not its own table: it is a voice_calls row with disposition='voicemail', so nothing else appears here. Returns { voicemails[], total, limit, offset, next_cursor }; each row carries id, from_number, to_number, peer_name, contact_id, received_at, duration_seconds, audio_url, has_audio, summary, transcript_text, has_stored_transcript, transcript, read, read_at. Read-only: no write, no carrier call, nobody contacted. It does hand back credentials though. audio_url is a 5-MINUTE PRESIGNED S3 LINK to the recording of a real person's voice, minted per row, and anyone holding that URL can fetch the audio for those 5 minutes with no Hiveku login, so do not paste it into a ticket, a log or a transcript; pass audio_urls 'false' to skip the presign entirely. audio_url comes back null while has_audio is true whenever the recordings bucket is unconfigured or the presign throws, because per-key errors are swallowed to null. Prefer this over voice_calls_list for voicemail work: voice_calls_list can filter disposition='voicemail' but returns raw rows with no presigned audio, no contact name, no search and no date range, and it carries NO plan gate, so it can answer 200 on an account where this route answers 402. Traps. 402 voice_not_enabled is a PLAN refusal (Voice is a paid add-on, and an account with no account_credits row answers the same way), NOT an empty inbox. limit defaults to 200, not 50, and is clamped to 1 through 200; a non-numeric limit falls back to 200 rather than erroring. total is counted BEFORE the cursor narrows the window, so it is the size of the whole match set and does not shrink as you page: stop on next_cursor null, never on a running count reaching total. cursor is honoured ONLY on the default sort 'received_at' with dir 'desc'. Send any other sort or dir and the cursor is SILENTLY IGNORED, giving you page one forever, and a cursor id that is not a voicemail on this account is dropped the same way; next_cursor is still returned under every sort, so the value you are handed can be one the next call will ignore. When the cursor branch runs, any offset you sent is ignored and the echoed offset is 0. unread_only and has_audio act only on the literal string 'true', and audio_urls only on the literal 'false'; any other value applies no filter at all, so an unread-only sweep can quietly return the entire inbox. from and to are UTC dates and to covers the whole day, but an unparsable date is silently skipped instead of refused, so one typo widens the range to everything. to_e164 is exact equality on the DID, not a prefix. q searches ai_summary text, plus a digits substring on both numbers when the query holds 3 or more digits, plus up to 50 non-deleted CRM contacts matched on first_name/last_name only (not company, not email) whose numbers are then matched against the CALLER leg only; it NEVER reads the stored S3 transcript, so words spoken on a call whose transcript lives in S3 cannot be found here. ai_summary carries one of two different artifacts: when it begins 'Voicemail transcript: ' the row holds a raw Deepgram transcript, so summary is null and transcript_text holds the words; otherwise summary holds an AI-written summary and transcript_text is null. The legacy transcript field is transcript_text falling back to summary, so reading transcript can hand you a summary labelled as a transcript. Read summary and transcript_text instead. has_stored_transcript true means the real transcript is in S3; fetch it with voice_call_transcript_get. peer_name and contact_id come from a last-7-digit match against non-deleted contacts, so two numbers sharing a tail attach the same contact and an archived contact reads as no match. from_number coerces a NULL caller ID to '' rather than null. Everything returned is customer PII. Flip read state with voice_voicemail_mark_read.

tools.name: web_actions
tools.description: Execute browser actions (click / input / scroll / screenshot / wait / executeJavaScript) at a URL before scraping. Use when a page requires interaction (clicking a search button, scrolling to load more content, dismissing a modal) before the content of interest is visible. Returns `data.actions.screenshots[]` for any screenshot actions, plus the final scrape output.

tools.name: web_crawl
tools.description: Crawl multiple pages of a site and return both URLs and scraped content. Supports v2.1 options: `sitemap` ("include"|"only"|"skip"), `crawlEntireDomain` (great for "redesign every inner page of this domain"), `webhook` (POST a completion payload to your URL instead of polling), plus standard `scrapeOptions` (formats, maxAge, parsers, onlyMainContent). `wait` defaults to true and blocks until completion; set false to get a job id back and poll via /v2/crawl/:id. Heavy operation — credits scale with page count.

tools.name: web_extract
tools.description: LLM-based structured data extraction across one or more URLs. Pass a JSON Schema (`schema`) or a free-text `prompt` describing what to pull out. Firecrawl scrapes each URL and runs the LLM extraction in a single call. Returns `data` matching the schema.

tools.name: web_map
tools.description: Fast sitemap discovery. Returns up to `limit` URLs for the given domain via Firecrawl /v2/map. Combines sitemap.xml entries and crawled internal links. Returns `data.links` as a normalized string[] of absolute URLs. Use this when you want a list of "what pages exist on this site" before deciding which to scrape.

tools.name: web_scrape
tools.description: Scrape a single URL and return its content. Formats can include "markdown" (default), "html", "rawHtml", "links", "branding" (Firecrawl-extracted brand identity: colors/fonts/logo), "summary" (LLM summary), "images" (image URL list with alt text), or a screenshot object {type:"screenshot",fullPage?,quality?,viewport?}. Set parsers:["pdf"] when the URL might be a PDF. maxAge (ms) returns a cached scrape if one ran within the window — use this for repeat scrapes to save credits. ALWAYS check `scrape_failed` on the response before reading `data` — when true the body looked like a Cloudflare/captcha challenge or hit an HTTP error and downstream code must NOT fabricate content from it.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Web search via Firecrawl /v2/search. Returns search results with optional inline scraping of each hit (set scrapeOptions). Useful for "find live information about X" tasks where you don't have a URL upfront.

tools.name: web_search_brave
tools.description: Web search over the live internet via Brave Search. Returns a ranked list of { title, url, description, age, language }. Use for current events, "what is X", competitor research, or to find authoritative sources before generating copy. Pair with fetch_url to actually read a result. Caps at 20 results per call. Choosing between the two search tools: use this one for a plain ranked list of links, and `web_search` (Firecrawl) when you want the result pages scraped inline via scrapeOptions.

tools.name: workflow_bind_form
tools.description: Wire a workflow's webhook URL into a Hiveku project's form component IN ONE CALL. Replaces a 4+ MCP call dance (workflow_triggers_list → project_file_get → parse → project_secrets_set → preview_sync). The server: reads the form file from builder_code_versions, parses it for the NEXT_PUBLIC_*_WEBHOOK_URL env var + the form fields (name attributes on <input>/<textarea>/<select>), looks up the workflow's webhook URL, sets the project secret (which auto-rebuilds via the NEXT_PUBLIC_* path). Returns {project_id, form_file_path, env_var, webhook_url, form_fields[], secret_set, preview_synced, warnings}. Pass dry_run=true to preview without writing.

tools.name: workflow_bulk_provision_for_project
tools.description: End-to-end form wiring for a whole project in ONE call. Scans the project for form components (-form-island.tsx + others matching the convention), and for each form: instantiates a workflow from the canonical template, looks up the freshly-provisioned webhook URL, and sets the project's NEXT_PUBLIC_*_WEBHOOK_URL secret (which auto-rebuilds the preview). Returns per-form result with workflow_id + webhook_url + env_var + warnings, plus skipped (no env var found, not a form) and errored (template failed, etc.) lists. The 63-site migration drops from ~15 MCP calls per site to 1. Template-level overrides apply to ALL forms (e.g. RECIPIENT_EMAIL: 'sales@acme.com'). For per-form overrides (different recipient per form), call workflow_create_from_template + workflow_bind_form per form individually. Pass dry_run=true to scan + report without writing.

tools.name: workflow_clone
tools.description: Clone a workflow's definition into a new workflow. Defaults: same account, name suffixed '(copy)', is_enabled=false (so the clone is dormant until reviewed). Pass `overrides` to literal-replace strings in the cloned JSON before save — handy for swapping recipient emails or source labels when fanning the same shape across sister sites. To clone CROSS-ACCOUNT pass `target_account_id`; the caller's Olympus key must be a service key (customer `olp_*` keys are tenant-pinned and will get 403). Auto-provisions webhook triggers on the clone so its webhook URL goes live immediately if is_enabled=true.

tools.name: workflow_create
tools.description: Create a new automation workflow. The `definition` is a ReactFlow-style graph: { nodes: [{id, type, data, position}], edges: [{id, source, target, sourceHandle?, targetHandle?}] }. `node.type` must be a valid type from workflow_node_types_list (260+ options across triggers/actions/flow/data/notifications/etc.). Every workflow needs exactly one trigger-category node (e.g. manualTrigger, webhookTrigger, scheduledTrigger) as its entry point. Prefer building incrementally with workflow_node_add + workflow_edge_add — it auto-generates ids, validates connections, and snapshots every change to workflow_versions. Use this tool only when you already have a complete known-good graph (e.g. from workflow_duplicate or workflow_version_get).

tools.name: workflow_create_from_template
tools.description: Instantiate a canonical template (from workflow_templates_list) with per-site overrides. The server substitutes every `{{var.NAME}}` token in the template definition with the caller's `overrides[NAME]` value, then creates the workflow + auto-provisions webhook triggers in one call. The 63-site batch migration becomes truly autonomous. Returns {workflow_id, definition, webhook_url, webhook_triggers[]}. Missing required variables fail-fast with 400.

tools.name: workflow_dashboard_url
tools.description: Get the human-facing dashboard URLs for a workflow — editor, runs-list, and a deep-link to the latest run. Use this when handing off to a human reviewer ("go inspect this in the editor") so the agent doesn't have to know Hiveku's URL layout. Returns `{ workflow_id, workflow_name, is_enabled, editor_url, runs_list_url, latest_run: {id, status, started_at, completed_at, url} | null }`.

tools.name: workflow_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE — permanently delete a workflow and cascade its triggers, schedules, versions, runs, and dead-letter rows. Linked AI chat sessions are unlinked (their workflow_id is nulled) so the historical chat content is preserved. There is no soft-archive — this is a hard delete. Accepts `id` or `workflow_id`. Use ONLY when the user has explicitly confirmed they want the workflow gone.

tools.name: workflow_delete_schedule
tools.description: Remove the scheduledTrigger node from a workflow, disabling all scheduled execution. Other nodes that referenced the trigger will be orphaned (their edges to/from the trigger are also removed) — the response includes a warning when this happens. Webhook and manual triggers are unaffected.

tools.name: workflow_disable
tools.description: Disable a workflow so it stops firing on triggers and schedules. Workflow data remains intact — use workflow_enable to reverse, or workflow_delete to remove. Thin wrapper over workflow_update — flips is_enabled=false. Accepts `id` or `workflow_id`.

tools.name: workflow_duplicate
tools.description: Clone an existing workflow as a new draft in the SAME account (clone starts disabled; new_name defaults to "<source> (copy)"). Alias of workflow_clone, which additionally supports cross-account targeting and string overrides.

tools.name: workflow_edge_add
tools.description: Connect two nodes. Validates that both nodes exist and that this exact source→target+handles combination isn't already an edge. For most nodes leave sourceHandle empty (defaults to 'output'). For a `conditional` source, sourceHandle MUST be 'true' or 'false'. For `switch`, use a handleId from the switchConfig.cases array. Returns the new edge with its server-assigned id (format: edge_<8hex>).

tools.name: workflow_edge_delete
tools.description: Remove a single edge by id. Nodes are unaffected. Version-snapshots before the delete.

tools.name: workflow_enable
tools.description: Enable a workflow so it fires on its triggers and schedules. Thin wrapper over workflow_update — flips is_enabled=true. Accepts `id` or `workflow_id`. Use workflow_disable to pause without deleting.

tools.name: workflow_event_trigger_types_list
tools.description: Enumerate every event-driven workflow trigger node — the ones that fire when something happens INSIDE Hiveku (CRM contact created, deal stage changed, PM task created/updated, helpdesk ticket assigned/resolved, billing invoice paid, Shopify order placed, form submitted, etc.). Returns the full matrix grouped by domain (crm / pm / helpdesk / deploy / shopify / billing / booking / email / email_marketing / form) with each entry showing: - node_type (snake_case canonical) + node_type_camel (alias the engine also accepts) - object_type (what changed) + event_type (what happened) - description (one-liner) - output_shape_keys (what's in `trigger.output` for templating) Use this BEFORE workflow_node_add when wiring an event-driven trigger so you pass the right `type` string. Distinct from workflow_trigger_types_list — that one covers infrastructure-shaped triggers (webhook + scheduled + database row-change).

tools.name: workflow_get
tools.description: Get a single workflow including its definition graph ({nodes, edges}), associated workflow_triggers rows, workflow_schedules, and the top-5 most recent workflow_versions. Accepts `id` or `workflow_id`. For the full version history, use workflow_versions_list. For per-node config schemas, call workflow_node_types_list — the definition.nodes entries reference type strings cataloged there.

tools.name: workflow_get_schedule
tools.description: Read the current cron schedule for a workflow. Returns null if the workflow has no scheduledTrigger node configured. Includes next_run_at and whether the workflow itself is enabled (the schedule will not fire if the workflow is disabled).

tools.name: workflow_list
tools.description: List automation workflows with optional enabled/search filters

tools.name: workflow_node_add
tools.description: Add a single node to a workflow's definition. The server reads, mutates, version-snapshots, and writes atomically — no need to round-trip the whole definition. Returns the new node with its server-assigned id (format: <type>_<8hex>). The agent should: (1) call workflow_node_types_list to pick a valid `type`, (2) read that type's `fields` to know which `data` keys to set — honouring `options` and `optionsEndpoint`, (3) call this tool, (4) call workflow_edge_add to connect it. The response reports config gaps rather than letting you find them at run time: when required fields are unset it carries `config_incomplete: true` and `missing_required_fields: [{key,label}]`. That is ADVISORY: the node IS added, so adding then configuring via workflow_node_update is fine. But do not enable a workflow while any node still reports it.

tools.name: workflow_node_delete
tools.description: Remove a single node. CASCADES: every edge whose source or target is this node is removed too — the response lists the removed edge ids. Version-snapshots before the delete. Returns { deleted_node_id, removed_edge_ids[] }.

tools.name: workflow_node_types_list
tools.description: Discover every workflow node type available. Returns the full catalog: 401 node types with category, label, description, required/optional `data` fields, and outgoing-handle shapes (most nodes emit 'output'; conditional emits 'true'|'false'; switch emits per-case handle ids). The agent MUST call this before building a workflow — it's the only way to know which node `type` strings the engine accepts. Categories include: triggers, ai, crm, helpdesk, pm, seo, ppc, social, marketing, analytics, builder, email, calendar, cms, knowledge, notifications, database, http, cache, files, data, flow, utilities. READ THE FIELD METADATA, do not guess values: - `options` lists the ONLY legal values for that field. A field with options and no matching value fails at run time (helpdeskSetStatus.status accepts open/pending/on_hold/resolved/closed and nothing else). - `optionsEndpoint` names an account-scoped GET returning { options: [{value,label}] }. The value is an id you cannot invent: a PPC connection UUID, a form id, a DID. 13 of these sit on REQUIRED fields. - `commonFields` at the top level documents fields shared by many nodes (currently `on_error`, which every action node accepts). A field carrying no `description` is documented there, not undocumented. It rode 326 nodes and was hoisted to keep the payload down. - Node types accept BOTH camelCase and snake_case; the catalog is keyed by camelCase.

tools.name: workflow_node_update
tools.description: Patch a single node's `data`, `position`, or `type` without resending the whole workflow. `data` is shallow-merged into the existing data (set a key to null to clear it). Each call snapshots the prior workflow version. Returns the updated node.

tools.name: workflow_normalize_payload
tools.description: Preview the case-insensitive aliasing that the webhook trigger ingest auto-applies. When a Webflow/Squarespace/other source form posts mixed-case field names (Webflow's default is lowercase `name` but Title-Case `Email`/`Subject`/`Message`), the engine adds lowercase aliases recursively so `{{trigger.output.payload.email}}` works regardless of source casing. Original keys are preserved alongside. This tool runs the SAME algorithm on an arbitrary payload so you can verify what `trigger.output.payload` will look like before wiring the workflow. Returns: - normalized_payload (the aliased version) - added_aliases[] ({path, original_key, alias_key}) — every alias that was added, so you know which template forms will work - summary {aliases_added, depth} Aliasing rules: only lowercase aliases are added (never uppercase), only when the lowercase form isn't already a key on the same object, and the original key is always preserved.

tools.name: workflow_provision_webhook
tools.description: One-shot helper for the canonical 'webhook in → action out' wiring. Replaces the 3-call dance of workflow_create + workflow_node_add(webhookTrigger) + workflow_trigger_create + workflow_triggers_list. Pass `name` (+ optional `definition` and `http_method`/`authentication`) and you get back `{workflow_id, webhook_url, trigger_id}` in one shot. If `authentication='bearer'`, a one-time `bearer_token` is returned — record it, it will not be shown again. If you omit `definition`, the response scaffolds a barebones workflow with a single webhookTrigger node that you can extend with workflow_node_add. The created workflow defaults to `is_enabled=true` so the URL goes live immediately.

tools.name: workflow_resolve_short_id
tools.description: Resolve a short workflow id (the 8-char hex prefix the dashboard shows, e.g. 'a1b2c3d4') to a full UUID. Scoped to the caller's account. Returns 404 if no match, 409 with `candidates[]` if multiple workflows share the prefix (pass more characters). Use this when a user gives you the short id from the dashboard but you need the full UUID for the rest of the workflow API.

tools.name: workflow_resume
tools.description: Clear an auto-pause on a workflow and reset its failure counter so it accepts triggers again. Hiveku auto-pauses a workflow when its circuit breaker trips (repeated failures) or it detects a cascade loop. While paused the webhook KEEPS ACCEPTING deliveries — they are stored and never processed — so resuming is only half the job: call workflow_stranded_list afterwards to see what piled up, then workflow_stranded_replay to actually run it. Fix the cause first. Resuming a workflow that is still broken just trips the breaker again.

tools.name: workflow_run
tools.description: Trigger a workflow run — works for BOTH test runs during development AND production invocation. Sets triggered_by="manual" on the run row, which the executor handles identically to a real trigger firing. Accepts `id` or `workflow_id`. Two modes: (1) SYNC (default) — waits for completion, returns final status (completed | error), output, and error. Use for short workflows (under ~25s) and for test runs where you want immediate feedback. (2) FIRE-AND-FORGET — set fire_and_forget=true to return 202 with a run_id; use for long workflows. After any run, call workflow_run_get with the returned run_id to inspect per-node step_states (input/output/error per node) — that's your primary debug surface. **`test_mode: true` is the safe dry-run flag.** When set, the engine: (a) skips the run-quota burn + cascade detection + run-row creation (transient, doesn't pollute history); (b) short-circuits every SIDE-EFFECTING node before it fires (no real emails, Slack posts, CRM writes, HTTP requests, helpdesk tickets, DB writes, deploys, etc.). Each skipped node returns a mock NodeExecutionResult with `__dry_run: true`, `action: '<nodeType>'`, and `would_have: { ...the args it would have sent }`. Pure handlers (data transforms, array ops, flow control) STILL run for fidelity. Downstream nodes that reference `{{nodeId.output.X}}` see either the would_have payload or a synthetic field (e.g. messageId for sendEmail) — so the workflow's structural correctness is testable even though no real side effect fires.

tools.name: workflow_run_get
tools.description: Get one workflow run with the full per-node execution detail. Returns: status (pending|running|completed|failed), input_data, output_data, error_message, and step_states — a map of { nodeId: { status, input?, output?, error? } } showing exactly what each node received, produced, or failed on. This is the agent's primary debug tool: after workflow_run, fetch this to see which node tripped and why, then call workflow_node_update to fix and re-run. (Alias of workflow_run_status — same payload, clearer name.)

tools.name: workflow_run_logs
tools.description: Return the per-node lifecycle log lines captured during a workflow run — the engine's structured trace (config / starting / handler invoked / retry / timeout / completion / soft-fail) per node, NOT raw stdout. Complements workflow_run_get (which shows step_states.X.error/output) by showing the timeline of WHAT happened during execution, not just the final state. Response: `{ logs: [{node_id, node_status, ts, level, msg}], summary: {total, by_level: {info,warn,error}, by_node: {<id>: count}} }` sorted by timestamp. Capped at 50 lines per node (longer-running handlers truncate the tail). Filter via `node_id` (one node only) or `level` (info|warn|error). Use to: - Verify a node was reached + how long it took - See retry attempts before a final failure - Confirm soft-fail (on_error=continue) fired as expected - Audit dry-run / test_mode short-circuits

tools.name: workflow_run_status
tools.description: Get the status and full execution detail of a workflow run. Returns: status (pending|running|completed|failed), input_data, output_data, error_message, triggered_by, started_at, completed_at, AND step_states — a per-node map of { nodeId: { status, input?, output?, error? } } showing exactly what each node received, what it produced, and which one (if any) failed. This is the agent's primary debugging surface: after workflow_run, fetch step_states to see which node tripped, then workflow_node_update to fix and re-run. workflow_run_get is an alias for this tool.

tools.name: workflow_run_summary
tools.description: Aggregate run summary for a workflow over a configurable window. Returns: total counts by status (succeeded/failed/running/pending), success_rate (0..1), latency_ms percentiles (p50/p95/p99/mean), up-to-5 most-recent failures with error_message, and pointers to the most recent success + failure (`last_succeeded_at`, `last_failed_at`, `last_failed_run_id` — drill into the latter with workflow_run_get when something looks off). Caps at 1000 runs in the window; narrow the `since` to look at a tighter slice.

tools.name: workflow_runs_list
tools.description: List recent runs of a workflow (paginated). Same route as workflow_run_status/workflow_run_get for a single run.

tools.name: workflow_runs_recent
tools.description: Account-wide recent-runs feed across ALL workflows. Highest-value when debugging a form that's not landing: filter status=failed + since=last 10 min and you see exactly which workflow tripped, no need to iterate every workflow_id. Each entry includes workflow_name, status, triggered_by, error_message, started_at, completed_at, and duration_ms. Default window: last 1 hour. Use this BEFORE workflow_runs_list when you don't yet know which workflow is broken.

tools.name: workflow_set_recipient
tools.description: Rewrite the `to` field on every (or a subset of) sendEmail node in a workflow. Common per-site operation during migrations — replaces a full workflow_update payload with a one-line call. Defaults `mode` to 'expression' (the sendEmail field mode that supports templating); pass 'literal' for a hardcoded address. Snapshots a workflow_versions row before writing so the change is reversible via workflow_version_restore.

tools.name: workflow_set_schedule
tools.description: Set or update the cron schedule for a workflow (upsert). Patches the workflow's scheduledTrigger node in place — does not touch other nodes/edges. cron_expression is a 5-field cron string (e.g. "0 9 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 9am). Supports *, */N, ranges (1-5), comma lists (1,3,5). Set enabled=false to pause the schedule without disabling the whole workflow.

tools.name: workflow_stranded_list
tools.description: Submissions a workflow RECEIVED while it was paused and never processed. Read-only — always call this before replaying. This is the failure mode that looks like nothing happened: a paused workflow still accepts its webhook, so payloads are stored in trigger_runs but produce no CRM record and no notification. The leads are not lost, they are invisible. Returns the pause window, the count, and the stored submissions.

tools.name: workflow_stranded_replay
tools.description: SENDS REAL NOTIFICATIONS. Re-runs stored submissions through the workflow's CURRENT definition. Requires confirm:true. Call workflow_stranded_list first and show the user what would run — these submissions can be days old, so replaying emails someone about a form they filled in last week. Capped at 25 per call; pass trigger_run_ids to replay a specific subset instead of everything. Resume the workflow first (workflow_resume) or the replay just strands them again.

tools.name: workflow_templates_list
tools.description: List the canonical agent-instantiable workflow templates. Returns slug, label, description, the variables each template needs (with type/required flags), and the raw definition (with `{{var.NAME}}` placeholders). Pair with workflow_create_from_template to instantiate. 16 templates ship: the 3 form/newsletter migration defaults plus 13 marketing delivery playbooks (weekly search-terms-to-negatives for Google AND Bing, disapproval triage, impression-share review, lost-backlink alert, tech-audit regression, rank-drop response, content-decay refresh, monthly AEO visibility, GBP review SLA + weekly post draft, CWV watch) — every PPC write in them stages to approval, never auto-applies.

tools.name: workflow_templating_syntax
tools.description: Returns the workflow templating language reference: which `{{...}}` expressions the executor resolves at run-time, what the `trigger.output.payload`/`headers`/`query` scopes contain, how to reference upstream node outputs, the `{mode, value}` field modes used by sendEmail, and worked examples. Read this BEFORE you write any node `data` that interpolates a value — the alternative is guessing from another workflow's JSON.

tools.name: workflow_test
tools.description: Run a workflow as a SAFE DRY-RUN. Functionally identical to `workflow_run` with `test_mode: true`, but the named tool makes it discoverable — agents shouldn't have to remember the flag.
